descriptions.NUR17757: The complex system of structures comprising water sources and water-collecting features, with ingenious channels, and a rectangular building in isodomic masonry.
descriptions.NUR12187:
Megalithic structure consisting of a funerary corridor bordered by two parallel rows of orthostats.

The roof is composed of a single large, quadrangular slab finely finished, which rests against the lateral walls at the end of the tomb.

To enhance the monument's value and accessibility, the surrounding property area has been enclosed and connected to the municipal road network via a path bounded by dry stone walls.
descriptions.NUR12839:
Dolmenic burial with an apsidal corridor.

Located in the territory of the comune of Narbolia (OR)
descriptions.NUR11634: An allée couverte is also present at the site of Chinzana. It is a tomb composed of a rectangular corridor with a remaining length of 5.20 m and a width of 0.95 m, formed by slabs set in a coltello fashion, seven of which still remain in situ; the covering slabs are missing. Around the tomb, on the north-west, south-east, and south sides, some stones of the peristalite project.
descriptions.NUR11655: Different tomb nucleus scattered along the islet.
descriptions.NUR21176: The anterior section has collapsed, while the posterior part is preserved to a considerable extent. The rectangular burial corridor is bordered by a single slab, whereas the lateral walls are composed of a series of blocks upon which smaller stones are placed. The remaining height is about 130 cm. The entire upper surface is covered by a multitude of small hollows (cavities with magical-sacred functions).
descriptions.NUR17997: A kind of ceremonial altar of uncertain period. Located in the immediate vicinity of the nuraghe and the homonymous Nuragic village.
descriptions.NUR11890: The entire area between the domus de janas necropolis and the church of Santo Stefano is rich in weathered stones adapted to niches and recesses, where it is often difficult to distinguish between natural and human intervention. In particular, around the church five sites with carved stones can be identified:
descriptions.NUR12989: Sacred area, probably pre-Nuragic in date. It consists of a stone bench with niches, hollows, and artificial recesses. The summit of the hill is covered by stones fallen from a nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR14262: Stone worked with hammers on the outer surface. Probably a prehistoric altar.
descriptions.NUR17166: Rock bench with stairs and cupolas.
descriptions.NUR10720: The site might relate to a courtyard for animals used in the last centuries; however, an even earlier origin cannot be ruled out.
descriptions.NUR17782: Village, giants' tomb, menhir and remains of a nuraghe in the middle of the agricultural farm
descriptions.NUR16330: Within the archaeological area are Nuragic period burial circles located at 990 m a.s.l., as well as constructions from a later period, including ancient cow pens and ancient sheepfolds known as "Pinnetus".
descriptions.NUR13547: Sacred area consisting of several rooms surrounded by an irregularly elliptical enclosure. One of these buildings has a perfectly round plan with a floor composed of calcare slabs joined with absolute precision. The accuracy of the construction and the existence of an original design plan are evidenced by traces of a circular marking on the floor, corresponding to the first row of stones, traced with a kind of compass.
descriptions.NUR2072: The Phoenician settlement arose in the area of a previous Nuragic settlement, as the structures uncovered by excavation show the reuse of various elements from the indigenous settlement. Indeed, currently visible are a megalithic enclosure and a Nuragic structure adapted and incorporated into a wall trace that appears further surrounded by a fortified line.
descriptions.NUR7010: Domus de janas inside the Phoenician-Punic settlement of Pani Loriga, later repurposed.
descriptions.NUR7041: Domus de janas inside the Phoenician-Punic settlement of Pani Loriga, later repurposed.
descriptions.NUR7040: Domus de janas inside the Phoenician-Punic settlement of Pani Loriga, later repurposed.
descriptions.NUR5531: The archaeological area consists of the ruins of a Punic fortress and a complex nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR19529: Archaeological area comprising various remains among which Cart Ruts; menhir; different types of cairns.
descriptions.NUR14933:
It is located within the municipal territory of Donori.

Prehistoric and historical emergencies, the archaeological area is partially damaged with overlapping cultural phases presumably attributable to the Nuragic, Punic, and Roman periods. A large number of cyclopean stones entirely made of grey granite indicate the presence of the village and the cemetery.
descriptions.NUR12223: Several remains of circular constructions, terraces, and robust curtain walls in megalithic technique are visible, while at the highest point stands a complex structure built of granite blocks, featuring a quadrangular tower. The settlement is crossed by the torrential Riu Bidd'e Mores, a tributary of the Riu Gutturu Mannu.
descriptions.NUR19840: Tomb circle built of polyhedral boulders of various sizes. The structure is circular, formed by superimposing one or two rows of polyhedral boulders. The upper part consists of 13 boulders arranged in a circle (diameter about 150 cm), of which: the tallest, placed to the east in the circle, is triangular and stands out from the others; to the south and north of it are two boulders set on edge with their dressed faces visible; seven boulders of various shapes and sizes follow, completing the circle.
descriptions.NUR19842: Circular burial circle formed by the stacking of polyhedral stones of various sizes. The upper part is composed of 10 large stones arranged in a circle, with a diameter of about 150 cm. At the edges, some stones have fallen, likely originally forming part of the structure. The circle is filled with earth and rubble.
descriptions.NUR19844: Circular burial circle made of large lastriform stones, semi-worked and of diverse shapes, mostly triangular. It differs from the others in the size of the slabs. The circular structure is broken off in the north-west area, where presumably three to four stones are missing. Nine stones remain in their original positions, covering three-quarters of the construction. At the edges, some corbelled slabs are present, which very likely originally closed the circle.
descriptions.NUR17839: In this area there are 11 menhirs and one carved stele, most of them made of granite. None of them has retained their original position; almost all are broken, probably they were buried by mechanical equipment during land improvement works.
descriptions.NUR2019: It includes remains of a nuraghe and a village, the entire structure "correctly" transformed into dry stone walls.
descriptions.NUR10791: During excavation, it shows 2 (possibly 3) sacred wells opening onto a large open area paved with slabs, and a hut located within the paved area, which contains a hole through which water can be seen flowing.
descriptions.NUR16216: The area consists of a enclosure enclosing a megaron temple.
descriptions.NUR1049:
The Punta Unossi complex is one of the most important in the Florinas area.

It consists of an extensive settlement within which stands out a large circular building (external diameter 11 m, internal diameter 7.60 m) featuring elements typical of so-called "meeting huts": a circular seat attached to the walls and a central circular base upon which, originally, a baetyl-tower stood.
descriptions.NUR15175:
At the base of the hill, a short distance away, there is a lake basin, an important source of water for the nearby village.

The shores show clear signs of human intervention through the deliberate arrangement of stones and blocks that form a border around the so-called "nuragic lagoon".
descriptions.NUR10128: It is the native area of the menhirs, which are now located at Sa Figu. At this site, they were piled haphazardly, possibly as a result of land improvement works, as reported by the local shepherds.
descriptions.NUR21011: A massive single-tower nuraghe, of imposing diameter, built with large, roughly worked granite blocks. The entrance faces south and is three-quarters covered. The tholos is almost intact. Inside there are as many as three niches, cut into the wall thickness. Moreover, a spiral staircase starts from the wall to the left of the entrance corridor and certainly led to the upper floor, but is unfortunately blocked by collapse; opposite the stairwell there is a further niche.
descriptions.NUR6765: Baetyls placed near the Corbos nuraghe, used as posts for a metal gate.
descriptions.NUR6770: Prof. Ercole Contu reports in 1992 that there are twenty large baetyls placed halfway along the coast on the south-east slope of Monte Cachile. Some geologists have been involved, and in part have ruled out a natural geological origin. The site has been known to the local population for generations, and orally passed down is a legend that women in labour were brought to the site to give birth.
descriptions.NUR6763: Should be brought to the attention of a specialist. They appear scattered in location, and if any had been used, it would not be the one currently in place. It is clear that their function was related to pastoral needs.
descriptions.NUR6771: It is a monolith of brown trachyte roughly shaped and poorly finished, about two metres high. It has the form of a pyramidal prism with holes.
descriptions.NUR19827: It has an irregular pyramidal shape with its face oriented to south-south-east. The stone, although retaining in some areas the natural roughness of the rock from which it was hewn, shows traces of modification. The upper portion, slightly rounded, displays signs of working and smoothing.
descriptions.NUR6772: Baetyl with two concavities almost on the "head". Probably for the attachment of lithic horns.
descriptions.NUR6762: Unfortunately, numerous damages—often unconscious—have been caused by human activity aimed at reclaiming a few square metres of pasture.
descriptions.NUR15631: Two nuraghi (currently no longer extant and/or buried) located in the territory of Ussana and reported by Taramelli (see "Ussana – Discoveries of tombs of uncertain age in the territory of the commune, region of Salomea", in Notizie degli Scavi, 1906, pp. 57–58). The first was probably situated in the centre of the village, at Bruncu Sa Turri, roughly corresponding to the old municipal aqueduct (via Aldo Frau).
descriptions.NUR19860: Hut with enclosure. The structure is built of small and medium-sized polyhedral stones, dry-laid and arranged in fairly regular courses. It is very likely that the hut was modified and reused right up to the last century.
descriptions.NUR17911: Hut of which only the first level of dentilled ashlar blocks is preserved. Near the same-named giants' tomb and a probable village.
descriptions.NUR21134: The hut had already been described by Taramelli: "The remains of a circular structure were evident, and after excavation it appeared as a circular enclosure of a nuragic construction with a diameter of about 8 m… The narrowness of the wall in comparison with the vastness of the internal space does not allow us to claim it was a true nuraghe."
descriptions.NUR10922: Nuragic huts along the south-west coast within the municipality of Arbus. Very little remains visible, but it is an important testimony of this civilization.
descriptions.NUR19659: Nuragic hut with the remaining ground-level circular enclosure. Located at the edge of the plateau above the hill, Monte Crastu, it dominated the area of the probable village of Badde Cannalza.
descriptions.NUR19858: Nuragic hut. It is circular, built of flat stones of various sizes, stacked one on top of another in courses that slope inward toward the centre. The wall is conical: about 150 cm wide at the base, about 70 cm wide at the top, and with a remaining height of about 130 cm. The wall breaks off for about 100 cm in the south-eastern section (possibly the entrance) due to a collapse of the structure, likely caused by olive and mastic trees.
descriptions.NUR9816: A few metres from the two tombs of Sa Perda and s'Altare lie the foundations of a circular hut (diam. 10.70 – thick. 0.50) whose size and structural type suggest a nuragic origin; unfortunately, only the base course remains.
descriptions.NUR10171: The complex, datable between 1600 and 900 BC, includes a sacred well located within an irregular courtyard, a temple of the 'megaron' surrounded by an elliptical enclosure, and a large circular hut featuring an entrance chamber and a burial chamber. It was a communal site, known as the 'meeting hut', typical of Nuragic villages. Usually, the pilgrim would stay here, perhaps to hold a conversation with the priests.
descriptions.NUR10134: The complex, datable between 1600 and 900 BC, includes a sacred well located within an irregular courtyard, a temple of the 'megaron' surrounded by an elliptical enclosure, and a large circular hut featuring an entrance chamber and a burial chamber. It was a communal site, known as the 'meeting hut', typical of Nuragic villages. Usually, the pilgrim would stay here, perhaps to hold a conversation with the priests.
descriptions.NUR10173: The complex, datable between 1600 and 900 BC, includes a sacred well located within an irregular courtyard, a temple of the 'megaron' surrounded by an elliptical enclosure, and a large circular hut featuring an entrance chamber and a burial chamber. It was a communal site, known as the 'meeting hut', typical of Nuragic villages. Usually, the pilgrim would stay here, perhaps to hold a conversation with the priests.
descriptions.NUR12444: Two huts with sacred functions are present. Structure A has a semicircular shape and is considerably larger than structure B.
descriptions.NUR12739: Remains of a nuragic hut near Mount Margherita or the Manu mountains.
descriptions.NUR19642: It is a site featuring the remains of two single-tower (single-tower) nuraghes (huts), with both retaining their bases, each reaching a maximum height of one metre and a diameter of about 6 metres.
descriptions.NUR8047: On the Monte Narcao plateau, the remains of some prehistoric huts, built with large stones, still stand. Around the area, fragments of obsidian are frequently found.
descriptions.NUR8048: Neolithic huts of circular form characterised by large stones up to 1.00–1.20 metres high, resting on the rocky stratum.
descriptions.NUR5528: The Carrarzu Iddia complex nuraghe is situated on a modest elevation bounded by a curtain wall enclosing a proto-nuraghe and a nuraghe that appears to be of tholos type: between the two structures lies a small cluster of circular huts, some of which are still well preserved. A few dozen metres away lies the homonymous dolmen, and slightly further on the Pranu 'e Ruos and Tittiriolos nuraghes.
descriptions.NUR5023:
In the 1990s it was discovered that the Zapata palace had been built over the well-preserved remains of a Nuragic settlement that the archaeologist Giovanni Lilliu named Nuraxi 'e Cresia.

Thanks to an architectural restoration project of great scenic impact designed by the architect Pietro Reali, both the baronial palace and the underlying nuraghe, duly brought to light, have become the seat of a museum complex, inaugurated on 29 July 2006.
descriptions.NUR19423: Su Stampu de su Turrunu o de su Turnu is a unique sinkhole spring, originating from the Rio e Spinedda, whose waters emerge in a cascade from a hole in the rock, falling into the centre of an attractive lagoon.
descriptions.NUR15262: The site marked is called Su casteddu de Adeva, named after the mountain behind it, Monte Adeva or Is concas de Adeva. It is a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe with an external courtyard, surrounded by a wall face that integrates with the tower's structure, located on the top of a rocky spur, partially incorporating natural rock.
descriptions.NUR19829: To the north-northwest, adjacent to the rocky outcrop on which the northern tower of the nuraghe is built, there are two natural semicircular cavities, about 200 cm deep, closed by a roughly elliptical enclosure constructed of polyhedral stones of various sizes.
descriptions.NUR10027: On 10 July 1205, Maria de Thori, wife of the noble Pietro de Maronju and aunt of Comita, judge of Torres, donated the church of S. Maria di Orria piccinna, near Chiaramonti, together with the nearby church of S. Giusta, along with servants, maids, forest dwellings, lands, and animals, to the eremitic community of Camaldoli, and in so doing granted to Prior Martino, and to his successors, the free election of the church rectors and the dismissal of the monks.
descriptions.NUR4723: It is identified as a megalithic circle because it features a single row of uncut ashlar stones arranged in a circle. Diameter about 11 m. Currently it is used as a sheepfold. Nearby, two menhirs are noted.
descriptions.NUR10200: It is the uniqueness of the site in hosting so many ceremonial circles that leads one to believe in an exaggerated construction effort with no specific purpose. It is instead believed that the site's significance stems precisely from the presence of so many ceremonial circles, indicating a substantial population.
descriptions.NUR10345: The ceremonial circle of Sa Ortija appears almost suddenly in its grandeur. It is aligned with the northernmost solstice. It is composed of polygonal stones of small and medium size. In a slightly oval shape, it has a major radius of 33.00 metres. Sacred rites related to initiation took place here, and rituals and events linked to the seasons and the years of men and women were propitiated.
descriptions.NUR3853: At the level of great ruin. The basal circle of rose trachyte is visible, with stones roughly squared. Contrary to what was previously believed, we are not facing a nuraghe but an important fusional sacred circle, of which various forms are evident. One of these, of historical and religious significance, consists of three steps with a basin. Mu
descriptions.NUR20277: At a point on elevated ground relative to a natural depression, a circle of stones is visible, which could be the base of a partially buried nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR19619: Megalithic circle composed of 16/18 large stones placed in an orthostatic position on a natural rocky foundation. Five of them lie obliquely along the perimeter; three are positioned obliquely inside. The stones, covered with moss and lichen, have irregular shapes and clear signs of craftsmanship.
descriptions.NUR19621: A smaller circle, less extensive than the previous one, has an oval shape and is composed of 12 stones of varying sizes, almost all lying on the ground. The stones, covered with moss and lichens, exhibit irregular forms and clear signs of craftsmanship.
descriptions.NUR12836: Large megalithic circle a short distance from the Sacred Well Mitza Salamu.
descriptions.NUR20540: Composed of 10 megaliths in the form of parallelepipedons, placed one next to the other (one eleventh is found at the centre), forming, thus arranged, a semicircle of about 10 metres. Some ceramic fragments found at the site are attributable to the Monte Claro culture, therefore the Neolithic period.
descriptions.NUR9222: Megalithic circle located on Monte Ladu. It is situated near a small allée couverte.
descriptions.NUR9271:
The circle, irregular in shape, has been destroyed by agricultural work that has compromised its original form.

The monument consists of about 40 trachyte boulders of various sizes forming an irregular ellipse with a major axis of 17 m and a minor axis of 15 m. Archaeological excavations have brought to light an unspecified number of polished stone axes that have allowed the circle to be dated to the Late Neolithic, placing it within the Ozieri Culture (4th millennium BC).
descriptions.NUR19814: About 350 m from the menhir Sa Perda de s'Omini there is a circular burial circle with a diameter of about 150 cm, composed of stones of various shapes and sizes arranged in a circle, and three trachyte slabs embedded in the ground, one of which is the highest and has a triangular tip. South of this slab the trace abruptly breaks off, only to resume after about 50 cm—space that very likely originally was occupied by two trachyte slabs lying directly on top.
descriptions.NUR21123: Composed of a pseudo-rectangular trench about 1 m deep, lined with three courses of stones. Closed with a flat band of three slabs of slate, each 25 cm thick. Single burial with Monte Claro ceramics.
descriptions.NUR10886: These are the ruins of a structure built of large blocks, completely buried; only a few remains appear on the surface. Some years ago a farm vehicle removed one of the large surface boulders, revealing an opening through which it was possible to enter the structure. It is, in all probability, a silo for water storage or provisions. The shape is a truncated cone with a bulge at the bottom. Diameter at the base 1.55 m; height 2.73 m.
descriptions.NUR11475:
They are located within the municipal territory of Fonni (NU).

The site includes five tombs, two of which are well preserved. Four tombs are clustered together, while a fifth (in very poor condition) is situated about 400 metres in the north-west direction.
descriptions.NUR6754: There is no direct connection, yet it is identical to the contemporary Mesopotamian temples and embodies the 'orientalising' belief in the union of heaven and earth: sacred areas on hilltops were regarded as the meeting point between humans and the divine. The temple of Monte d'Accoddi, dating back five thousand years, is a ziggurat unique in Europe for the singularity of its architectural types. It was discovered in the mid-20th century by excavating a small hill that appeared 'artificial' in the middle of a plain.
descriptions.NUR5686: It is a proto-nuraghe of the corridor type, located within an area where remains of a larger village are visible.
descriptions.NUR1340:
It is located within the territory of the comune of Montresta (OR).

At the centre of the delimited area, on a rocky outcrop, stands a structure that for a long time was considered a nuraghe. It is more likely, however, to be a quadrangular Carthaginian fortress, with traces of masonry visible at its base that completed the defensive structure.
descriptions.NUR20327: Un censito nuragic area archaeologica, segnalata da Davide Arzu, estesa per tutta la macchia dove non si vedono alberi. Composta da vari nuraghi e capanne.
descriptions.NUR21180: The rock shelter at "Sa Conca Frabica" preserves as many as seven excavation layers that testify to continuous use from the mid-Neolithic until the Iron Age. The site was used for burying the dead, alongside which a funerary assemblage was placed, mainly composed of ceramic objects but also including bronze and oxidized stone items.
descriptions.NUR21181: Possible Nuragic huts near the spring source
descriptions.NUR5399: A very unusual and unique structure in form. Known as the rectangular nuraghe. Situated atop a stratified mass of limestone shaped like a reproductive member, around which the river makes a bend. It could be a temple with buildings serving communal gatherings.
descriptions.NUR4662:
Santa Vittoria constitutes one of the most important ritual complexes of the Nuragic Sardinia. Extending over more than 3 hectares, it is protected by a natural cliff to the S/S-O and by a wall to the N/O following the rocky margin.

The sanctuary features four main groups of buildings: the two temples and the "hut of the priest", the "festive enclosure", the group of the "double baetyl" enclosure, and the eastern-southern-eastern group.
descriptions.NUR11884: Three giants' tombs are present at the site, all built with schist stone.
descriptions.NUR10581: The archaeological complex of Piscina Caboni belongs to the Culture of the Circles of the Arzachena area, which, in earlier years, appeared to affect only the Gallurese region. Site occupation, in the absence of excavation data, dates back to the third millennium BCE.
descriptions.NUR20119: Astronomical megalithic clock, built in the pre-Nuragic period, before 1500–1300 BC. It has a circular form and is constructed with large stones, with open zones allowing sunlight to pass through a central stone covered with white pebbles that enhanced solar ray reflection during different periods—equinoxes, solstices—and during lunar phases, it reflected moonlight in specific directions.
descriptions.NUR2692: Composed of a complex nuraghe and a Nuragic settlement
descriptions.NUR4664: Complex-type nuraghe, consisting of a central tower and four additional towers. The structure, datable to 1400–1000 BC, is located at the border between the municipalities of Oristano and Villaurbana. Surrounded by scrubland and vegetation, it is not easily accessible or visitable.
descriptions.NUR13609: Unfortunately, very little remains, but those few residual ashlar stones are enough to help us understand this temple. It features ritual circular huts, within which along the entire internal circumference are visible seating areas. Numerous parallelipipedal basalt and trachytic tuff stones from T populate the entire site; they are perfectly shaped and finished. In a sudden flash of memory, I am transported back to other Sardinian sanctuaries.
descriptions.NUR2533: Complex nuraghe consisting of a primitive tower and a bastion, perhaps four-lobed. The entire outline of the central tower survives, although hidden by vegetation and collapse. The structures of two chambers belonging to the central tower survive. A curvilinear curtain wall forms the link between two peripheral towers oriented NNW and ENE. The NNW tower is connected by a curtain wall to another tower oriented WSW, of which much of the outer outline survives.
descriptions.NUR739: The complex contains a sacred well with a paved area, a temple on a rectangular plan, a corridor building, and some stretches of cyclopean walls. The nuraghe Cherchizza stands at the western end, along the edge of the plateau. The site would have served as a landmark for the population of a wide surrounding area. Excavations have yielded bronze artefacts, including a figurine of the mother goddess, as well as amber objects.
descriptions.NUR13598:
The complex consists of a nuraghe with a settlement, a giants' tomb, and a well.

The nuraghe, built on a rocky outcrop, belongs to the type of complex structures: it is indeed composed of a central tower to which three secondary towers have been attached on the front and lateral sides.
descriptions.NUR8743:
The Lu Brandali nuraghe is of mixed type, with features of both a corridor nuraghe and tholos nuraghi.

The entrance opens in the north-western part of the latter, its length marked by several watchtowers that make use of rock outcrops.

Outside the curtain wall the village extends; Michele Careddu's 1967 survey recorded 36 huts, mostly circular. Period between the 14th and 10th centuries BC.
descriptions.NUR6200: The Orconale complex features a bastioned tower with a courtyard. The main tower has an ogee profile. Surrounding it are the remains of a large Nuragic settlement, including a megaron temple where a model of a nuraghe was found, possibly belonging to a basin similar to that of Su Monte Sorradile.
descriptions.NUR13080:
The site experienced two main phases of construction: the first during the middle Bronze Age and the second during the transitional period between the Bronze and the early Iron Age.

The complex consists of a megaron temple, about 17 metres long, surrounded by a enclosure known as a temenos and by other cult and residential buildings, among which are actual metalworking workshops; nearby stands a complex nuraghe with a three-lobed plan.
descriptions.NUR3890:
The site experienced two main phases of construction: the first during the middle Bronze Age and the second during the transitional period between the Bronze and the early Iron Age.

The complex consists of a megaron temple, about 17 metres long, surrounded by a enclosure known as a temenos and by other cult and residential buildings, among which are actual metalworking workshops; nearby stands a complex nuraghe with a three-lobed plan.
descriptions.NUR8119: The Romanzesu nuragic complex lies at 750 m above sea level in the locality "Poddi Arvu" (the white poplar), in the cork-oak forest of the Sa Serra granite plateau, in the province of Nuoro. It is a Nuragic village covering more than seven hectares, dating to the Bronze Age, near the source of the Tirso river, and comprises a sacred well, about a hundred huts, two megaron temples, a rectangular temple, a stepped elliptical amphitheatre, and a large labyrinthine structure.
descriptions.NUR13722: Located on a trachytic plateau at 152 m a.s.l., from which a vast expanse of territory can be seen, Monte Baranta is a pre-Nuragic settlement characterised and protected by a enclosure-tower, a long and powerful wall enclosing a group of rectangular huts, separated from a sacred area by menhirs and a megalithic circle.
descriptions.NUR10069: Total ruin. The older inhabitants of the area recall its existence, though only a few basal circles remain. When the fast-moving road between Sassari and Tempio was constructed, excavation work affected more than one site, in total disregarding their immense historical value. mu
descriptions.NUR9836: It is a marvel with so many stones placed in rows of bator trees for trees. And there are channels to drain water or another substance? Probably so. And others still are in circular and oval forms, with one additional stone placed to hold an offering to the god or for reasons of offering to the dead or for the initiation of young people and young girls.
descriptions.NUR7136: It is the prehistoric necropolis that gave its name to the first phase of the Early Bronze Age in Sardinia, known as the Bonnanaro Culture (1800–1600 BC). It consists of seven hypogea, among which the domus I, the most important, is located about 600 metres to the north-west (outside this polygon). Two of the hypogea mentioned are more properly described as cave burials.
descriptions.NUR7179: It is the prehistoric necropolis that gave its name to the first phase of the Early Bronze Age in Sardinia, known as the Bonnanaro Culture (1800–1600 BC). It consists of seven hypogea, among which the domus I, the most important, is located about 600 metres to the north-west (outside this polygon). Two of the hypogea mentioned are more properly described as cave burials.
descriptions.NUR7164: It is the prehistoric necropolis that gave its name to the first phase of the Early Bronze Age in Sardinia, known as the Bonnanaro Culture (1800–1600 BC). It consists of seven hypogea, among which the domus I, the most important, is located about 600 metres to the north-west (outside this polygon). Two of the hypogea mentioned are more properly described as cave burials.
descriptions.NUR10232: Clear traces of hut or circle construction within the area of Su Pagliaco. The heavily anthropized zone features several constructions, strongly interconnected in a unique assemblage not found elsewhere in our territory. mu
descriptions.NUR16436: It could refer to the construction of a giants' tomb or to a nuragic hut associated with the nearby homonymous nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR10295: The subterranean shelters provided ancient humans with a safe refuge for themselves and their clan. The cave was divided into small rooms, and in particular one for the day, located further in, against the rock wall for the night. These rooms often also served as burial sites. Until the 1950s and 1960s, entire family groups lived there, carrying out agricultural and pastoral activities.
descriptions.NUR10296: The subterranean shelters provided ancient humans with a safe refuge for themselves and their clan. The cave was divided into small rooms, and in particular one for the day, located further in, against the rock wall for the night. These rooms often also served as burial sites. Until the 1950s and 1960s, entire family groups lived there, carrying out agricultural and pastoral activities.
descriptions.NUR10582:
The archaeological complex of Piscina Caboni belongs to the Culture of the Circles of the Arzachena area, which, in earlier years, appeared to affect only the Gallurese region.

Site occupation, in the absence of excavation data, begins to be dated to the third millennium BCE.
descriptions.NUR6816:
The complex consists of a "cromlech" and other menhirs. In the surrounding area, an underground necropolis attests to the intensive occupation of the territory in prehistory.

The "cromlech" is made of large rounded boulders (trachyte, grey granite and pure white quartz) transported from considerable distances.

The complex is attributable to the Final Neolithic (3200–2800 BC, Ozieri culture) and the Early and Middle Chalcolithic (2800–2400 BC, Filigosa and Abealzu cultures).
descriptions.NUR20098: It has a slightly elliptical shape, with a diameter varying between 20 and 0 m. Some stones are no longer aligned along the perimeter but are instead positioned inside or outside the circle; nevertheless, most of them remain well aligned with each other, and some are still perfectly upright. It is remarkable to note that, despite the passage of thousands of years, the state of conservation is still relatively good.
descriptions.NUR10394: Until halfway through the last century, remains of various nuraghes could be seen, together with many basaltic ashlar of different shapes and sizes.
descriptions.NUR8642:
The archaeological area of Cuccuru Sa Cresia Arta, in the territory of Soleminis, is located on a hilltop about 40 metres above the level of the field road access, about 250 metres to the south-west of Soleminis, in the inland region of the Cagliari Gulf.

The archaeological excavation works, funded by the municipal administration, are part of a broader initiative to promote the valorisation of Soleminis' archaeological sites, a project previously agreed upon with the Superintendence.
descriptions.NUR7173: Unfortunately, the destructive actions of treasure hunters have put the majority of the sites in the commune of Chiaramonti at risk. The loss of further historical and artistic testimonies further diminishes its cultural heritage. The heritage left by our ancestors must be part of our history, to help us better understand the path we should follow for the future. mu
descriptions.NUR9813:
The dolmen has a circular burial chamber (1.57 x 1.26 x 0.52 m high above the fill) bounded by ten orthostats of various sizes (measurements of two slabs: 0.68 x 0.27 x 0.50 m high – 0.70 x 0.25 x 0.52 m high), while two slabs placed on one side of the entrance, oriented to the north-east, suggest the existence of a short corridor now destroyed.

The capstone is vaguely pentagonal (2.40 x 2.25 m) and has a maximum thickness of 0.55 m tapering to a minimum of 0.48 m.
descriptions.NUR9814: The Arbu Dolmen II is instead composed of a rectangular corridor (1.84 m x 0.78/0.72 m), bounded on the longer sides by naturally occurring rock carefully smoothed and by an orthostat on the head end; above it, a covering slab (1.70 m x 1.22 m x 0.45 m thick).
descriptions.NUR6884:
Small dolmen composed of two vertical slabs upon which rests a well-shaped covering slab.

The back wall is instead formed by two base stones upon which smaller stones are placed to close the chamber.

For the valorisation and access to the monument, the surrounding area has been fenced off and connected to the municipal road network via a fenced path.
descriptions.NUR16988:
Megalithic funerary structure composed of three vertical stone slabs set at right angles to one another.

Archaeologists have interpreted it as a dolmen, although like all the other surrounding monuments, it requires more in-depth scientific investigation.
descriptions.NUR14468: Built of granite as a collective burial and, at the same time, a place of worship, it is a classic example of the megalithic culture that characterised Europe, and the island in particular, during the Copper Age (3rd millennium BC). The dolmen is constructed using the trilithic system (from Greek tri, three, and lithos, stone) – the oldest known architectural scheme – characterised by vertical load-bearing elements that support others laid horizontally.
descriptions.NUR9754:
Partially incorporated into a dry stone wall and retains in situ only three orthostats (0.35x0.22 in thickness – height 0.50; 0.80x0.30 in thickness – height 0.50; 0.60x0.15 in thickness – height 0.50); and the cover slab (1.70 x 1.52 x 0.52/0.40 in thickness); another orthostat is visible beneath the wall.

Numerous slabs scattered around the domus burial indicate the presence of a peristalith, of which now no trace remains.
descriptions.NUR20384: Genetically attributable to the Ozieri culture, dating from 3500–2700 BC, it is a simple burial structure of rectangular plan with an entrance facing east. It features a trapezoidal chamber measuring 2.65 m in length and 2.20 m in width. The lateral walls are composed of a lithic slab topped by a bedding of rubble, while the back wall is formed by a single flat, quadrangular orthostat that projects from the walls by almost half a metre.
descriptions.NUR6863: Simple dolmen, with a rectangular plan and entrance facing north-east. The right wall is formed by a single rectangular slab, while the left wall is composed of two roughly worked stones resting on natural rock. The covering slab is flattened on the lower surface and left natural on the upper surface. EPOCH: Ozierian culture (3500–2700 BC).
descriptions.NUR10595: Likely giants' tomb, dolmenic, completely collapsed
descriptions.NUR17885: It is a small, still intact dolmen.
descriptions.NUR6873: The dolmen is composed of four remaining orthostatic slabs enclosing a polygonal space (1.86 x 1.40 m), bounded at the top by a large slab, roughly shaped, of variable thickness and with a rounded profile.
descriptions.NUR11748: Small dolmen closed on three sides with a single covering slab.
descriptions.NUR6858: The Prunaiola dolmen is an archaeological funerary monument located on a small hilltop in the Torralba area, in western Sardinia. It is situated near the State Road 131 Carlo Felice and in close proximity to the giants' tomb of Cabu Abbas and two domus de janas, in a region rich in archaeological remains that document continuous human settlement from prehistory.
descriptions.NUR12388:
It is of tufaceous trachyte (L 5, W 2.50, H 2.70 m), consisting of a rectangular chamber (4.18 x 1.14 m) bounded on the sides by two orthostats, by a front slab with an entrance hatch with rounded corners facing south-east, and by a flat covering slab.

Inside the western lateral orthostat a rectangular niche opens (L 1.22, W 0.88, D 0.50 m). To the left of the monument's front slab there is a small niche, cut into the thickness of the western orthostat.
descriptions.NUR6903: The chamber, roughly circular with a maximum diameter of about 1.80 m in the north-south direction, is enclosed by four orthostats, but ideally seven can be reconstructed to complete the perimeter with an entrance to the south-east; three of the four remaining orthostats support the covering slab;
descriptions.NUR12361: Composed of stones driven into the ground that support a slab measuring 3 x 2 m, surrounded by an elliptical stone enclosure. The Elcomis dolmen appears to have been constructed about three centuries after Su Laccu, as its orientation (azimuth 161.9; declination –46°75) points consistently towards Alpha of the constellation of the Mosca, but in 2100 BC.
descriptions.NUR14780: Sa Turricula is recognised as the first phase of the Nuragic civilization. The site includes the nuraghe, the village, and at a short distance, in the territory of the comune of Osilo (locality Funtana 'e Casu), a dolmen.
descriptions.NUR6878: The dolmenic tomb stands on a modest rocky rise, about 200 metres north-west of the giants' tomb of the same name and less than 500 metres south-east of the Nuraghe Cherbos. The burial chamber, of a vaguely quadrangular shape, is bounded by five stones set on edge that appear to rest directly on the outcropping rock. The cover consists of a polygonal slab, now slightly tilted by the fall of an orthostat and with widespread chipping, thinner than the supports.
descriptions.NUR14465: The dolmen is made of a row of squared boulders and roughly worked slabs set upright to form a rectangular chamber about six metres long. Above it, at a height of about 2.20 metres, two more slabs laid flat close the burial chamber; one of them is the second largest of its kind in the whole Mediterranean basin: it measures 4.80 x 3.42 m and is about 45 cm thick.
descriptions.NUR15231: General location in the area of Li Casacci
descriptions.NUR14237: Dolmen composed of a large horizontal slab placed on a dry-stone wall of cyclopean masonry.
descriptions.NUR13073: Dolmen composed of a large covering slab supported by three vertical orthostats
descriptions.NUR6901:
The structure consists of a large horizontal basalt slab resting on seven smaller stones that form a polygonal chamber. Around it is a circle of stones that was intended to contain the earth forming the mound cover.

The construction of this funerary monument dates back to the third millennium BCE.
descriptions.NUR6898: Dolmen located near the homonymous nuraghe
descriptions.NUR11650: Dolmen with a lapidary slab on megalithic walls
descriptions.NUR6905:
Remains of a megalithic tomb that, as can be seen, appears to be clearly a dolmen.

Of the monument, only one orthostat remains “in situ” (width 1.52 m – thickness 0.40 m – visible height 1.10 m), while numerous other slabs have been overturned in the area directly in front of the exedra. The covering slab lies broken into several fragments; the presence of a peristalith is evident.
descriptions.NUR7051: Two tombs partially collapsed and eroded beneath a striking natural dolmen
descriptions.NUR6894: The dolmen is located on a basaltic outcrop on the northern bank of the Riu Coraggiu, about 200 metres north of the Nuraghe Nela. The burial chamber is currently enclosed by three orthostats, on which rests a large covering slab.
descriptions.NUR6870:
The dolmen has a burial chamber of a vaguely polygonal shape (1.51 x 1.20 x 0.71 m high) and still preserves six orthostats in their original position, on which the large polygonal covering slab, worked with some care, rests (2.20 x 1.90 x 0.50 m thick).

Around the monument, among numerous overturned stones, three orthostats still in situ can be seen maintaining an alignment parallel to the perimeter of the tomb and forming part of its peristalith.
descriptions.NUR11647: Two small dolmen already described by Taramelli
descriptions.NUR12350: It is located in the municipality of Buddusò. It is situated within an area managed by the Forest Service, known for its scenic landscape.
descriptions.NUR12183: The giants' tomb of S'Ena 'e Sa Vacca is particularly interesting for some architectural features that in the past have led researchers to consider it a dolmenic structure. The special feature of this burial is the large, unworked covering slab that completely covers the burial chamber, giving the monument the appearance of a long dolmen or "allée couverte".
descriptions.NUR15380: One of the numerous dolmen present in the Sardinian territory. Dolmen (from Breton tol-men, "stone table") are funerary monuments erected presumably during the recent Neolithic and early Neolithic (3400–2700 BC).
descriptions.NUR20398: The dolmen is located in the area of Berchiddeddu. The dolmen chamber has a nearly square plan; the covering slab, the one with the largest dimensions, measures about 1.60 x 1.20 m. Nearby, there is also a menhir, together with traces of other destroyed structures and fragments of Ozieri culture ceramics.
descriptions.NUR6895: Also known as S'Aspru, it is located on the southern slopes of Monte Bardia, near the Roccia de Monte Longu, at an elevation of 513 m a.s.l. and overlooks the wide valley facing the centre of Cala Gonone. It is accessible via a short trekking route. It is rectangular in plan, built of limestone slabs, and consists of four parallelipipedal slabs (originally five), which form a large chamber covered by a pentagonal slab.
descriptions.NUR18818: Prehistoric megalithic funerary structure. Of the monument, the part not concealed by vegetation shows only two vertical slabs at right angles to each other.
descriptions.NUR6893: To reach it, one travels for about 4 km along the S.P. 63 from Sindia to Scano di Montiferro, where on the right one sees the beautiful single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe Serrese. The dolmen is located 750 metres north of the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR12362: Sos Monimentos has a circular plan, with a chamber measuring about 1.80 x .100 m, surrounded by a dry-stone wall of granite. At the entrance to the structure two rectangular slabs, about 0.60 m high, rise. On these slabs rests a circular lid slab measuring about 2.50 x 2.25 m. Its possible astronomical orientation has not yet been identified.
descriptions.NUR12363: It lacks the covering slab and is covered by vegetation.
descriptions.NUR6855: Dolmen I is composed of a slab resting on stones that, in antiquity, were likely set in precise cuts to support the roof. Dolmen II preserves only the ceiling slab and a few wall stones. In the same area, about sixty hemispherical cavities are noted, clearly artificial and possibly linked to ancient ritual practices connected with the prehistoric monuments just described.
descriptions.NUR12080: It is a dolmen later adapted by shepherds as a sheepfold. It has a trapezoidal plan (3 m in length, 1.80 m in width, 2.20 m in height).
descriptions.NUR6853: Area around which, besides the dolmen Su Crastu Covaccadu, there is also the giants' tomb Sa Pedra Coveccada, of which only the arched stele remains, broken at the base.
descriptions.NUR12024: The elongated ('allée couverte') dolmen of 'Tramassumele' is probably a monument of transition between Neolithic dolmen and the 'giants' tombs of the Bronze Age.
descriptions.NUR7747: Multicellular domus with a dromos probably collapsed. Inside the main chamber there is a pillar with carved capitals.
descriptions.NUR10025: These are domus belonging to those with complex architecture. The development of the rooms cannot be fully understood as Mother Earth has preserved almost the entire site intact. Access is possible through the collapse of the roof of one of the chambers. Inside, clear construction details, accessories, and petroglyphs are visible. Mu
descriptions.NUR6989: Initially, probable subsoil shelters have become domus de janas as needed, through the addition of related modifications. There are other examples to be noted. The surrounding area is rich in fossils and calcareous formations. Photo Mario Unali
descriptions.NUR7367: They are located on the left bank of the river Oloitti. They extend in an L-shape, consisting of three chambers with antechambers. The photo showing the throne "sa trona de su Re" is nearby and intriguing for its shape, which ergonomically fits the posterior of a commander.
descriptions.NUR7426: It is also known by the name of the adjacent terrain "sas Damas", which I consider to be the older and more appropriate term, as it is closely linked with Sa Domus de sas Fadas, whose extension becomes Dama = lady. It was discovered accidentally during the expansion works of a residential house, currently known as Agriturismo Sas Damas Doneddu-Murgia; the site was rich in domestic artifacts, many of which have been donated to the local museum in Perfugas SS.mu
descriptions.NUR10256: Jewel among the jewels of the archaeological treasure chest of our commune of Chiaramonti. It is a domus whose womb is still intact, preserved by Mother Earth. Visible only is the rich antechamber, adorned with petroglyphs of rare beauty. mu
descriptions.NUR10257: Interesting reading of the representations contained. It is still intact in the womb of Mother Earth. mu
descriptions.NUR7049: Domus de janas with clear signs of its reuse in the 20th century.
descriptions.NUR7269: The entrance is severely collapsed, blocking access to the domus, which is arranged in various rooms surrounding a central chamber.
descriptions.NUR7262: This domus de janas is named after the bas-relief sculpture of a bull's-head protome carved on one of the internal walls. The other notable feature is the dolmenic corridor located in front of the entrance.
descriptions.NUR7502: It is a domus de janas necropolis facing the Gulf of Carbonara, located in the area of Spiaggia del Riso. Of the entire necropolis, only one tomb has remained intact: it is a truly fascinating monument that projects the territory back in time by about six millennia.
descriptions.NUR7313: The cemetery is located along the southern slopes of Monte Corona 'e Teula and consists of 11 domus de janas, characterized by the complexity of their planimetric layouts and decorative patterns. Only one of these is monocellular, while the others are composed of multiple cells arranged according to increasingly complex designs.
descriptions.NUR7408: The cemetery is located along the southern slopes of Monte Corona 'e Teula and consists of 11 domus de janas, characterized by the complexity of their planimetric layouts and decorative patterns. Only one of these is monocellular, while the others are composed of multiple cells arranged according to increasingly complex designs.
descriptions.NUR7344: Single-cell domus de janas especially eroded
descriptions.NUR7722: The domus de janas at Bonorchis is a single-chamber tomb, very small, with a wide and well-crafted entrance portal.
descriptions.NUR7490: The domus de janas of Bruncu s’Allegau or of Sa Domu ‘e s’Orku was probably originally carved out of a natural cavity later adapted for funerary purposes. It consists of a single chamber with horizontal development and an irregular elliptical plan, measuring about 2.65 m in length, 3.9 m in width, and 1.5 m in height from the current floor level; in the vault small parallel grooves and dents from prehistoric stonemasons’ work are still visible.
descriptions.NUR7584: Group of domus de janas situated on the calcareous escarpment overlooking the Bunari valley (Abealzu culture)
descriptions.NUR7079: At certain times of the year, due to high water levels in the reservoir, it becomes inaccessible.
descriptions.NUR7057: This underground tomb, cut from a block of erratic rock, is located about 300 m from the village's sports field. Nearby, other rock blocks with cups can be observed.
descriptions.NUR7076: Single-cell domus de janas on a calcareous massif
descriptions.NUR7067: Single-cell domus de janas on a calcareous massif
descriptions.NUR7093: Single-cell domus de janas on a calcareous massif
descriptions.NUR7297:
The underground chamber is cut into a schist rock, and on the side opposite the entrance—i.e., the northern side—there is a clear indication of a previous excavation, likely from another underground chamber. Access to the domus de janas is via a door with a drainage groove cut into the threshold:

the door is characterized by the presence of a frame surmounted by a lintel, formed by carving the rock, to highlight this architectural element.
descriptions.NUR7626: The cemetery consists of 33 hypogea of domus de janas dug into tuff and divided into two groups. The site, datable to the Neolithic, was used by the peoples of the Ozieri, Abealzu-Filigosa, Monte Claro, the Vaso campaniforme, and Bonnanaro cultures, as well as by the Nuragic people of Iloi in the early Bronze Age, with later medieval reuse.
descriptions.NUR7743: The cemetery consists of 33 hypogea of domus de janas dug into tuff and divided into two groups. The site, datable to the Neolithic, was used by the peoples of the Ozieri, Abealzu-Filigosa, Monte Claro, the Vaso campaniforme, and Bonnanaro cultures, as well as by the Nuragic people of Iloi in the early Bronze Age, with later medieval reuse.

descriptions.NUR7648: The hypogeum is cut into an isolated basalt boulder. The doorway opens at some height above ground level and is surmounted by two deep grooves cut horizontally and parallel in the rock. The doorway still shows a clear rebate for the closing slab. A narrow groove cut into the thickness of the doorway outlines all four sides. The oval chamber is of the oven type. The tomb was explored in 1927 by A. Taramelli, who found it already violated and emptied long before.
descriptions.NUR7466:
The funerary site, datable to the 3rd millennium BC and in use until the early centuries of the 2nd millennium BC, consists of thirteen domus de janas. The artifacts recovered are attributable to the Ozieri, Abealzu-Filigosa, Monte Claro, the vessel with bell-shaped form, and Bonnanaro cultures and are today largely preserved in the Villa Sulcis museum in Carbonia.

On the summit of the hill where the necropolis is located stands a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR4347:
The funerary site, datable to the 3rd millennium BC and in use until the early centuries of the 2nd millennium BC, consists of thirteen domus de janas. The artifacts recovered are attributable to the Ozieri, Abealzu-Filigosa, Monte Claro, the vessel with bell-shaped form, and Bonnanaro cultures and are today largely preserved in the Villa Sulcis museum in Carbonia.

On the summit of the hill where the necropolis is located stands a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR7096: Group of three pruricellular domus de janas
descriptions.NUR7208: Group of three pruricellular domus de janas
descriptions.NUR7085: Group of three pruricellular domus de janas
descriptions.NUR7613: Cemetery composed of three nuclei, one of which contains a tomb decorated internally with a carved spiral.
descriptions.NUR7267: Cemetery composed of three nuclei, one of which contains a tomb decorated internally with a carved spiral.
descriptions.NUR7424: Cemetery composed of three nuclei, one of which contains a tomb decorated internally with a carved spiral.
descriptions.NUR7783: Group of three domus de janas of particular interest. Featuring a carved doorway in the basalt rock and a rectangular exedra situated below ground level.
descriptions.NUR7155: "Domus de janas of Orrilì. On the slopes of Monte Sedda 'e Sos Campos, along the valley of the Rio Orrilì; it has a single chamber carved out of calcareous rock; elongated; at the sides of the entrance there is a kind of niche cut into the wall, possibly a cavity for placing offerings to the deceased. In the territory of Pietro Farris Zumbosu".
descriptions.NUR7310: The hypogeum lies at the southern edge of a small plateau, characterised by dense woodland. The burial is cut into a block of heavily fractured granite, so that part of the antechamber has completely broken away and now lies right next to the entrance. The entrance to the cell is about 0.70 m above ground level; it has jambs and a lintel carved in relief, with carefully finished surfaces.
descriptions.NUR7266: It is a single chamber obtained within a calcareous outcrop of friable rock. In the immediate vicinity, a significant amount of work is visible due to the presence of other outcrops that have been abandoned or where construction has not been completed.
descriptions.NUR7080: In a private plot. There are decorations in the form of probable bull's-head protomes.
descriptions.NUR7107: In a private plot. There are decorations in the form of probable bull's-head protomes.
descriptions.NUR7083:
It is a small artificial cave cut from a single, rounded block of limestone. The entrance, shaped like a forge, faces south-east and leads into a long, linear space divided into multiple chambers, which were likely intended to form the burial chambers of an underground burial.

The tomb shows no decorative elements and has not yielded any funerary goods. It dates to the recent Neolithic and demonstrates human presence in the area from the pre-Nuragic period.
descriptions.NUR7518: 2 domus de janas with architectural façade, typical funerary architecture very present in Sassari.
descriptions.NUR7392: Domus de janas located on the hill facing the Ortali 'e su Monte complex, beneath a smaller nuraghe similarly named.
descriptions.NUR7451: It is a tomb with an architectural façade, greatly modified and reused in medieval and modern times, blending the features of domus de janas and giants' tombs.
descriptions.NUR7658:
The necropolis comprises 18 domus de janas, all multi-chambered with up to 12 rooms, richly adorned with pilasters, panels, false doors, bull's-head protomes, chevrons and other spiral or wolf's-tooth motifs.

Seven tombs reproduce pre-Nuragic dwellings: single- or double-pitched roofs, horizontal or sloping, with or without central beams and side rafters, supported or not by pillars, all carved in the rock. One has an architectural façade with a carved arched stele.
descriptions.NUR7640:
The Sos Laccheddos cemetery is an archaeological site located in the Sassari area, in western Sardinia. It is divided into two groups of tombs situated close to one another, positioned between State Road 127 bis and the new provincial road of Anglona, a few kilometres east of the town centre, heading towards Osilo.

The 32 tombs recorded in the aforementioned study were supplemented by 19 additional tombs identified in more recent investigations.

The 32 tombs recorded in the aforementioned study were supplemented by 19 additional tombs identified in more recent investigations.

descriptions.NUR7299:
It is carved from an erratic limestone block, worked also on the exterior, with a roughly trapezoidal shape. On the main façade, which has an entrance, a "centinata stele" of almost 4 metres in height was erected, originally bearing three small baetyls at its summit. On the rear façade a second small entrance is visible, possibly of earlier date.

The material culture recovered during excavations belongs to the Bonnanaro type (early Bronze Age).
descriptions.NUR7322:
The underground chambers at the site are two: the first tomb is the more interesting one, as it features a series of incisions above the access door; the second is located a little further on, near the edge of the road, and has its internal space almost completely flooded.

Both burials are of the pothole type and date back to about 3000 BC.

descriptions.NUR7545: Situated on the slopes of the Còrongiu Sènes hill. It has a longitudinal layout. Chambers built in progressive heightening from the entrance inwards, consisting of an antechamber and two cells with entrances almost perfectly aligned. The domus is entered through an elliptical opening. The first cell has a sub-rectangular plan, where traces of working consisting of slight vertical grooves are evident. The second cell is sub-elliptical in shape with traces of working.
descriptions.NUR7286: The tomb is dug into a granite outcrop; it consists of a dromos and a chamber in which a small niche has been carved. The underground chamber opens above a gentle slope just a few centimetres above the field level.
descriptions.NUR7549:
The "Domus de Janas" is carved into a modest granite outcrop with an irregular, rounded contour, barely rising above the countryside level.

The plan consists of a single cell of very limited dimensions; the entrance, facing south, is preceded by a short recess cut into the rock, with a sub-trapezoidal shape and lateral walls of decreasing height from north to south.
descriptions.NUR7092: Single-cell domus de janas built within a "trovante"
descriptions.NUR7376: "Domus de janas of Gianna Oria Porru or Solottos; a short distance from the Rio Mannu or Rio Posada trench, on the opposite side of Nuraghe Eritta (no. 5). Two small chambers cut into limestone, each with a low doorway and border. Empty. In the Antioco Sanna ground" (Taramelli, 933).
descriptions.NUR7210: Both burials have entrances oriented to south-west. Inside the first domus, measuring about 5 x 3 m, the remains of two columns that once decorated the chamber are still visible, both in the ceiling and in the floor. The second tomb, similar to the first, features a antechamber with raised steps on either side, and the burial chamber, rectangular in plan, contains two elevated burial couches on the lateral sides.

descriptions.NUR7207: "Domus de jana of Su Adu 'e Sa iana, a short distance from the village, at the crossing of Rio Minori, was formerly an underground chamber, which has disappeared for many years, but the elders of the village still remember it. In the Pasqua Sanna field was Isidoro."
descriptions.NUR7060: Single-cell domus de janas partially collapsed
descriptions.NUR7214: The domus has an entrance oriented ESE and features a plan layout in the form of a cross. The funerary structure consists of a trapezoidal door leading into a sub-rectangular antechamber, then into a rectangular chamber; on three of its sides, three elevated niches are located, oriented SSE to NNO and NNE. Originally, each niche was decorated with pilasters set at the centre.
descriptions.NUR7573: Within the broad and intricate framework of Sardinian subterranean architecture, the magnificent necropolises of Mesu 'e Montes, S'Adde 'e Asile, S'Isterridolzu, Noeddale, Su Littu, and the Tomba di Littos Longos have provided extremely significant data regarding the phenomenon of subterranean burial. The entrance is marked by a long corridor cut into limestone. Inside, bull's-head protomes and other carved decorations are present.
descriptions.NUR7152:
They are located in the territory of the comune of Busachi (OR).

At least 4 domus de janas are visible.

The necropolis should include at least  8 domus de janas.
descriptions.NUR7461:
It is a tomb with an architectural façade, that is, an underground tomb that reproduces in rock the external façade of a Nuragic giants' tomb, featuring a vaulted stele and an exedra.

In the late medieval period it was reused as a rock-cut chapel (its dedication is unknown).
descriptions.NUR7551:
It consists of a series of open spaces on the western flank of a rocky hill. The main nucleus, the result of various transformations related to different phases of use over the centuries, is composed of three large chambers connected together and arranged in sequence from north to south.

The spaces open onto a narrow embankment along the rock face, which features two narrow staircases through which access to the higher plateau is possible.

descriptions.NUR7248: A short distance from the settlement of Sassari, the domus of Oredda reveals its decorative splendour only to those who seek the mystery that defines the domus de janas. We went in search of this jana in a field, where one would expect to find nothing at all—except a ditch—and then entered it, holding one's breath at the concentrated art found within.

descriptions.NUR7588: The complex, chronologically situated between the final Neolithic (Ozieri culture, 3200–2800 BC) and the Chalcolithic, is located on a large outcrop of tuff and consists of 26 domus de janas. The domus, arranged along the cliff at various levels, are multicellular, that is, composed of multiple chambers; most of them have access via a dromos (a corridor carved into the rock), while only a few have direct access.

descriptions.NUR7618: The entrance was later modified by the construction of a wall to form a kind of shelter for domestic animals.
descriptions.NUR7088: Domus de janas with a sacred well placed at the entrance to the park on the south side
descriptions.NUR7359: The Pranu Narbonis cemetery consists of a group of three domus still in excellent conservation, dug out from a single large granite block emerging from the ground.
descriptions.NUR7383: Just outside the village of Irgoli, heading towards Onifai/Orosei, before a small bridge, one turns onto the road leading to Capo Comino. After just 300 metres, at the intersection with the circumvallation road, on the right a paved municipal road begins. Travel along this road for about 5 km until, on the left, two clear granite pillars become visible. Walk until reaching the Domus de Janas Sa Conca 'e mortu.
descriptions.NUR7375:
The necropolis, located along the southern slopes of Monte Corona 'e Teula, consists of 11 domus de janas characterized by the complexity of their planimetric layouts and decorative schemes.

The tomb of the water clocks, on the other hand, comprises 10 rooms, whose walls feature relief geometric motifs.
descriptions.NUR7510: The cemetery consists of eleven domus de janas, both single- and multi-cellular. The largest one was originally composed of five chambers, now reduced to a single room due to the collapse of the dividing walls. It is characterised by two distinct phases of use: the first in the Neolithic period and the second during the Middle Bronze Age (1700–1300 BC), when at least three hypogea were transformed into "domus with architectural façades".

descriptions.NUR7492: It is located in the territory of the comune of San Vito (CA), inside the church of the same name.
descriptions.NUR7530: The domus de janas, existing in the immediate vicinity of the nuraghe, marks the continuity of human occupation of the site over the millennia.
descriptions.NUR7528: Single-cell domus de janas carved out of granite
descriptions.NUR7099:
Three hypogeic tombs on the slope of a small rise (244 m). The first has a single elliptical oven-shaped cell. The second consists of an atrium, an antechamber and a quadrangular burial chamber with a niche on the right-hand wall. On the left a wider raised cell with two small niches and a relief decoration depicting two human faces.

The third tomb, further downhill than the other two, is of the more regular type with atrium, antechamber and cell.
descriptions.NUR7181: The antechamber is quadrangular; the walls are concave, while the ceiling and floor are flat, and the chamber height is almost equal to the door height. In the basal wall is the door that leads to the main chamber, which is sub-quadrangular in shape and placed irregularly within the wall. The main chamber is sub-ellipsoidal (1.80 x 1.24 m); the walls are concave and the ceiling is flat.
descriptions.NUR7396: Single-cell domus de janas located near Riu fruscu
descriptions.NUR7505: The archaeological site dating back to about 3500 B.C. is located near the provincial road and consists of three tombs. The first, isolated, was dug into a rock block rising behind a small structure; the other two, close to each other, are situated further south in a granite monolith along the road. All three domus de janas are of simple type, without antechamber, and feature a notch in the access opening.
descriptions.NUR7366: The archaeological site dating back to about 3500 B.C. is located near the provincial road and consists of three tombs. descriptions.NUR7582: The stone of Sant Eliseo is a large erratic boulder located on the lower slopes of Monte Santu, in the area of Mores. Used across various periods, it was first a prehistoric Neolithic tomb, then adapted by the Romans, and finally became a Byzantine church dedicated to Sant Eliseo. The domus has a ground floor and a first floor, reminiscent of fairy houses (in Sardinian, precisely, domus de janas).
descriptions.NUR7245: Domus de janas with superimpositions on the stele
descriptions.NUR7407: Small domus de janas with two cells
descriptions.NUR7729: The Tracucu Cemetery is a beautiful and extensive archaeological site located about three kilometres from Lotzorai, along the road to Talana. It comprises thirteen domus de janas, marked by wooden signs, which can be admired by following a guided path through the granitic rocks and dense vegetation.

descriptions.NUR7524: The cemetery includes seven very unusual and strikingly beautiful domus de janas, dug into erratic stones, and one in particular, with natural cup-like formations adjacent to the doorway.
descriptions.NUR7260: The cemetery includes seven very unusual and strikingly beautiful domus de janas, dug into erratic stones, and one in particular, with natural cup-like formations adjacent to the doorway.
descriptions.NUR7277: The cemetery includes seven very unusual and strikingly beautiful domus de janas, dug into erratic stones, and one in particular, with natural cup-like formations adjacent to the doorway.
descriptions.NUR20341: A small isolated domus de janas, particularly notable for the presence of a rock-cut terraced basin (ancient vats for pressing grapes to extract wine) carved into the rock.
descriptions.NUR7314: Dug into a calcareous rock outcrop stained pink by iron veins. Single-chamber tomb.
descriptions.NUR7425: The Luzzanas domus de janas are located near the river, and access is possible only from above through a shaft entrance. After descending, we find ourselves in a chamber containing two doorways, leading to two tombs; one of them is composed of a small antechamber plus three recesses, only two of which are accessible. In this domus there is a particularly striking incision depicting a labyrinth, although it could have been made in Roman times.
descriptions.NUR21144: Neolithic burial composed of two chambers connected by a door, which has, above it, a probable bull's-head protome.
descriptions.NUR7111: The domus de janas of Scala Coperta is located a few hundred metres from the Elephant Rock, in the area of Pedra Sciolta. Scavated within an erratic trachyte boulder, it consists of a main chamber and four side chambers arranged in a cross. Outside, above the boulder, there are three holes for the placement of small baetyls; a fourth hole is slightly set back from the others and is now barely visible due to vegetation.
descriptions.NUR7095: The tombs number about ten and vary in form, from the simplest single-cell tombs with an antechamber and a single chamber, to those with circular plan and various recesses, a hearth, and pilasters that separate the small chambers. They are cut into the soft tuff rock. Threatened by unauthorized archaeological excavations.
descriptions.NUR7304:
The domus is partially collapsed, but the incisions and bas-reliefs (with the motif of double horns) decorating the walls are still visible. There are also traces of red painting.

A few metres to the right, another domus is partially buried and equally ruined.
descriptions.NUR7188: Group of two single-cell domus de janas with façade.
descriptions.NUR7205: Group of two single-cell domus de janas with façade.
descriptions.NUR7239:
The domus is cut into a limestone face that is almost sheer above the valley below. It has a façade 2.60 m high depicting a simple stele. On the stele are the three typical recesses.

Like most architectural-façade domus created from scratch, it has a single chamber; this has a semi-elliptical plan. Inside, on the left, a wide niche opens whose function is unclear but which was presumably used for depositing votive objects.
descriptions.NUR7428: Single-cell domus de janas with a façade
descriptions.NUR7385: Single-cell domus de janas with a façade
descriptions.NUR7362: Single-cell domus de janas with a façade
descriptions.NUR9114: Small domus de janas, about a hundred metres from the Nuraghe Orgurù. Nine such structures have been recorded in the area. This small domus is located carved into a natural rock outcrop, not immediately visible as the view is initially blocked by other rocks.
descriptions.NUR12424: Domus carved out of granite. Composed of an access corridor and a central chamber opening into a small cell.
descriptions.NUR12423: Small domus whose entrance was once walled up for use as a sheepfold.
descriptions.NUR20076: Domus de janas to be verified, unnamed
descriptions.NUR11883: Domus de janas on the junction of SS125
descriptions.NUR7728:
Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe built of sandstone blocks. The main chamber features three asymmetric niches.

From the right corridor a staircase with 15 steps leads down. Maximum height of the tower: 9.15 m.

Nearby are the remains of a settlement and two domus de janas.
descriptions.NUR7538:
Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe built of sandstone blocks. The main chamber features three asymmetric niches.

From the right corridor a staircase with 15 steps leads down. Maximum height of the tower: 9.15 m.

Nearby are the remains of a settlement and two domus de janas.
