descriptions.NUR6956: Abandoned mine located in the municipality of Padria. (possibly a domus de janas)
descriptions.NUR7221: The imposing underground chamber of Sas Puntas, dug into a low limestone bench just a short distance from the settlement, fully reproduces a giants' tomb both in its exedra-front facade and internally, with an elliptical burial chamber. The burial belongs to the category of tombs with architectural façade, also known as "nuragic domus", i.e. underground tombs carved into rock, often adapting pre-existing Neolithic domus de janas.
descriptions.NUR6931: A natural cavity adapted into a domus de jana that has hosted games for generations of children from the village of Uri, currently abandoned due to changes in time. Access is from above via a "manoeuvre" that is quite dangerous, and it is situated at a height of about 6 to 7 metres above the ground.
descriptions.NUR14312: It is located in the territory of the comune of Putifigari (SS). Underground tomb (domus de janas) with a notably buried entrance, about two metres below road and field level. It consists of a main cell with pilasters and three smaller lateral cells. The double-slope roof is particularly noteworthy.
descriptions.NUR17350: It is a domus excavated at the base of a trachytic rock outcrop.
descriptions.NUR19963: Domus de janas reported via the Nurnet page by an anonymous contributor. From the photos it appears to be a two-cell tomb, used by the landowner for storing livestock.
descriptions.NUR6933: In the limestone outcrop bordering the Baddenare plateau, two domus de janas of multicell structure have been excavated. Both feature an antechamber, a main chamber, and two secondary side chambers. Access to one hypogeum is via a long corridor, while the other is reached through a raised doorway from the camp level. The domus with the corridor entrance preserves two fine columns in the main chamber and an incised inscription (L M S), likely of Roman or medieval date.
descriptions.NUR20258: Domus de janas reported to the Nurnet editorial office. From the video it appears to be a rocky massif where a larger necropolis may be present.
descriptions.NUR8695: Group of domus de janas immediately beneath the road embankment. It is suspected that other domus de janas may lie beneath or have been destroyed by the works for road construction.
descriptions.NUR7006:
The rock face of this hypogeum has the peculiarity of bearing, above the doorway, a bull sign consisting of a line (1.14 m) incised with its ends turned upwards (height 0.18 m).

It is a representation of the bull deity drawn in an extremely elementary and rough manner, which is nevertheless of considerable interest because it is the only known example in the area. Chamber measurements: depth 1.24 m; width 1/1.18 m; height 0.70/0.94 m.
descriptions.NUR9758: Short antechamber (depth 0.45 – width 0.77) leading to the door (height 0.48 – thickness 0.18 – width 0.40). The chamber measures: depth 0.98 – width 1.16/0.90 – height 0.44/0.80.
descriptions.NUR14943: Domus de janas with a chamber having a collapsed ceiling.
descriptions.NUR7483: A rectangular niche cut into the sedimentary rock, set against a quadrangular space bounded by four large upright stones with dry-stone walls. In the lowest Bell Beaker levels three cist structures were identified, sealed by limestone slabs and containing human skeletal remains attributable to several individuals. Above these lay further deceased individuals accompanied by grave goods such as objects in ceramic, metal, stone, bone and a gold necklace.
descriptions.NUR14663: Domus de janas located inside a granite quarry. Pruricellulare with an internal double pillar.
descriptions.NUR14144: Located at the southern edge of the Corraile plateau (480 m a.s.l.), (San Michele di Ozieri culture). The eight tombs that compose it, together with a small natural cave, show architectural features similar to those of the main cemeteries in the area. Some tombs stand out for their monumental scale and for the presence of symbolic elements closely linked to religious practice.
descriptions.NUR7202: The area, surrounding a small single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe, includes a small necropolis of four domus de janas, some of which feature carved bull's-head protomes.
descriptions.NUR12074: Small underground chamber in an isolated stone.
descriptions.NUR7998: It is a domus de janas, a burial of the "double oven" type, attributable to a period spanning from the third to the second millennium BCE.
descriptions.NUR6957: It consists of four domus de janas.
descriptions.NUR7649: This domus is single-cell with a pseudo-quadrangular plan and curved walls. The domus is located adjacent to the perimeter wall of the cemetery, with an opening facing that wall. The nature of some apparent "reliefs" on the ceiling should be investigated further. Adjacent is a second tomb.
descriptions.NUR7279: It is a pair of hypogea: a two-cell domus and a three-cell domus.
descriptions.NUR7124: Domus de janas with architectural façade, interesting the graffiti.
descriptions.NUR7003: Visible from the road, they are domus with modified entrances set slightly above the countryside level and located within the sheepfold.
descriptions.NUR7717: It consists of four tombs located in Chighizzu, above the galleries along the SS 131, the main road in Sardinia. The gradient of the route and the empty space beneath are truly dizzying, and those who dug these domus were without doubt extremely courageous.
descriptions.NUR7791: It consists of four tombs located in Chighizzu, above the galleries along the SS 131, the main road in Sardinia. The gradient of the route and the empty space beneath are truly dizzying, and those who dug these domus were without doubt extremely courageous.
descriptions.NUR7748: It consists of four tombs located in Chighizzu, above the galleries along the SS 131, the main road in Sardinia. The gradient of the route and the empty space beneath are truly dizzying, and those who dug these domus were without doubt extremely courageous.
descriptions.NUR7139:
It is a two-cell domus, oriented to south-east, with a roof widely collapsed (opening 1.06 x 0.86 m), lacking the diaphragm that once separated the two chambers, which was recently destroyed to create a single, more spacious chamber.

Access to the subterranean level is through a square opening (height 0.44 m – width 0.50 m – thickness 0.22 m), finely carved, featuring a triple molding for the insertion of a door latch.
descriptions.NUR7404: The cemetery consists of two multicellular domus de janas dug into limestone, plus a third one begun (only the dromos has been excavated) and never completed. One of the two tombs opens into the wall near the cemetery, while the second, together with the unfinished tomb, opens along the edge of the plateau to the south-east.
descriptions.NUR7074: They are located on a slight elevation at 184 m. The four grottoes are carved into the sandy rock and each features a single elliptical, barrel-vaulted chamber. Numerous artificial cuts, clearly visible along the rocky wall adjacent to the domus on the right side for a length of 12 m, are clear signs of ancient extractive activity that has largely destroyed the original site configuration.
descriptions.NUR9755: It is a domus carved into a flat rocky outcrop and consists of two rooms with a vaguely circular plan, aligned along the same axis and both opening to the south-east, separated by a partition with a door; the walls are finely finished, while the ceiling is slightly hemispherical.
descriptions.NUR12073: Single-chambered, carved out of a granite monolith.
descriptions.NUR14659: Domus de janas submerged by the Omodeo flood. It preserves a unique bull's-head protome in high relief.
descriptions.NUR7027:
It consists of 18 domus de janas arranged in three groups about 200 m apart. The first group has five hypogea aligned on an east–west axis; the second group, south of the first cluster, has three aligned on a north–south axis; the third group, 250 m to the east, comprises ten small rock-cut chambers that are difficult to reach and interpret.

The burials are of the horizontal-projection type with entrances between east and south. A system of channels cut into the rock protected the tomb interiors.
descriptions.NUR7048:
It consists of 18 domus de janas arranged in three groups about 200 m apart. The first group has five hypogea aligned on an east–west axis; the second group, south of the first cluster, has three aligned on a north–south axis; the third group, 250 m to the east, comprises ten small rock-cut chambers that are difficult to reach and interpret.

The burials are of the horizontal-projection type with entrances between east and south. A system of channels cut into the rock protected the tomb interiors.
descriptions.NUR7039:
It consists of 18 domus de janas arranged in three groups about 200 m apart. The first group has five hypogea aligned on an east–west axis; the second group, south of the first cluster, has three aligned on a north–south axis; the third group, 250 m to the east, comprises ten small rock-cut chambers that are difficult to reach and interpret.

The burials are of the horizontal-projection type with entrances between east and south. A system of channels cut into the rock protected the tomb interiors.
descriptions.NUR15235: It is one of the various domus de janas located in the municipality of Alghero. Inside there is a carved hearth in the stone foundation.
descriptions.NUR7435:
The cemetery includes 11 domus de janas, generally multicellular, some of which are characterized by architectural reliefs.

The most interesting burial consists of 11 rooms arranged in an irregular pattern.
descriptions.NUR7257: On the external wall there is a domus; another one has been carved inside the cave, about 3 m from the entrance on the left side.
descriptions.NUR17859: Two other domus de janas are visible in the vicinity.
descriptions.NUR7042: It consists of three domus de janas partially eroded and in very poor condition.
descriptions.NUR7421:
The extensive excavation work and the architecture of this monumental underground chamber date back to the early period of metal diffusion on the island. In this « domus de janas » the result is an evolution, reflecting the consequences of the emergence of powerful family nuclei subordinate to tribal chiefs, capable of imposing on their dependents a greater volume of labour.

The cells opened at a high level above the flat, accessible rock surface, which could only be reached without a ladder.
descriptions.NUR7026:
On the hill of San Giovanni a Punic fortified complex has been identified on the remains of a pre-existing Nuragic village.

Opposite are the Domus de Janas of Burdaga.

In Giuseppa Tanda's recent publication it is stated that, among the various types of Domus de Janas, there is one characterised by the fact that the necropolis is carved into pre-existing rock shelters, perhaps enlarged by artificial excavation, almost as if the overhang could provide shelter for the sacred remains of the dead.
descriptions.NUR20352: Located within a private property, among the numerous domus of the Ozierese area, they are the largest present in the region and not only; but they are also the only ones to feature symbols of the bull god carved in such a conspicuous manner.
descriptions.NUR7134: Eight domus de janas scattered along the period indicated on the map and a few taphouses.
descriptions.NUR15783: The domus, multicellular, is in a precarious state of conservation and consists of a antechamber and four cells.
descriptions.NUR6990: The domus de janas cemetery is excavated in a basalt outcrop that dominates the Riu Mannu valley, along the provincial road Suni-Pozzomaggiore, in the Planargia region, in north-western Sardinia. The underground complex includes 12 single and multi-cellular burials, all accessed almost always through a vestibule.
descriptions.NUR7086: The two domus, between which a large tree stands, are located about 1 km from the village of Goni and are carved into a rocky formation situated about 4 metres above the walking surface.
descriptions.NUR6959: “Sa Pedraia” consists of five hypogea set close together on a short rock face. One of them has an antechamber with a sloping roof and grooves showing the run of the beams. In the same chamber two bull’s-head protomes have been carved naturalistically to show that the fertility god would guarantee rebirth in the new life. The adjacent domus on the left has a cell with a central pillar and a raised lying-in floor.
descriptions.NUR7380: It is located in the municipality of Florinas and is composed of three hypogea.
descriptions.NUR6951: Subterranean burial with 10 domus de janas. A site worthy of in-depth study, containing 10 convex chambers.
descriptions.NUR7109:
It is known for having given its name to an important Sardinian Neolithic culture, the Filigosa culture, closely linked to that of Abealzu, so that the term "Abealzu-Filigosa culture" is frequently used. The cemetery consists of four pluricellular domus de janas, dug into a tuff hillside and characterized by long access corridors.  

It was in use from the third millennium BCE until the early centuries of the second millennium BCE;
descriptions.NUR6914: The cemetery of Fund'e Monti (or of Tracucu) consists of 15 hypogean tombs, locally known as Domus de Janas (fates' houses). The tombs, single- and multi-chambered, have entrances characterized by a passage (dromos) up to 5 m long or by a small antechamber. The doorways are more elaborately decorated, finely carved and finished with moldings (used to house lithic doorposts) and sloping terraces (for the drainage of liquids).
descriptions.NUR7019:
The necropolis consists of 14 domus de janas, considered among the most beautiful in Sardinia for their architectural design.

Twelve of them are open in the rock in a horizontal series, while the other two are located adjacent to the first. The façades stand out for their monumental scale and the precision of the stone work: in particular, that of tomb 3, a system of channels carved into the rock, still visible today, preserved the burials from infiltration of rainwater.
descriptions.NUR7758:
It has a single chamber.

Another domus de janas should be located nearby.
descriptions.NUR21142: The necropolis includes 4 domus de janas.
descriptions.NUR7234: It is located in the territory of the comune of Buddusò (OT) at a lower elevation than the road passing through the granite quarry.
descriptions.NUR7222:
It is a Neolithic burial cut into a schist ridge near a watercourse.

The burial consists of a single cell with a sub-circular plan. Traces of the entrance hatchway can be seen.

To the right on entering there is a small niche/cupboard. There is no chronological evidence, either because no finds were recovered or because the structure was used several times, even in recent times, and has been completely disturbed; indeed it lacks a floor.
descriptions.NUR7192: It is an enormous rock that contains a funerary hypogeum of the 4th–3rd millennium BC. The site saw an extraordinary continuity of use lasting five thousand years, from the Neolithic to the 19th century. It now houses the museum of the ethnographic traditions of Anglona, which illustrates agro-pastoral culture, the life of local communities, history and archaeology, starting from the Neolithic tomb that forms the oldest level of the Rocca: six cells of varying sizes and shapes, two of which are merged into a single chamber.
descriptions.NUR7187: Prehistoric underground cemetery composed of 6 tombs.
descriptions.NUR7302: This tomb, dug into trachyte, shows — in the antechamber and in the main chamber — a painted ceiling designed to imitate the roof of a hut according to two different typological schemes. Particular attention is drawn to the "lattice" motif appearing along the walls of the main chamber.
descriptions.NUR11879: Multicellular house featuring false windows, defined by incised grooves with traces of red paint, and straight beams in relief in the form of radiating lines on the ceiling to suggest a wooden roof. In the main chamber there is a sub-rectangular pilaster, of which only the lower and upper parts remain, the latter bearing an incised bull's-head protome. In the surrounding area the presence of a Nuragic village is evident.
descriptions.NUR6970:
The area includes a dolmen, a domus de janas, and remains of a megalithic circle.

Particular area defined by the megalithic enclosure within which the dolmen is situated. About 20 m from the dolmen lies the single-chamber domus de janas with a dolmenic corridor, added in a later period to create an additional tomb. Dated between the 3rd and 2nd millennium BC, according to the Municipal Sign.
descriptions.NUR19729:
The domus consists of three main rooms with a sub-rectangular plan, from which five smaller cells open off, each with an elliptical or semicircular plan.

Access to the tomb is through a rectangular vestibule, whose ceiling reproduces a double-pitched roof with a central lintel (20 cm x 5 cm in depth), from which the lateral beams (eight per side) extend, alternating with broad flat bands (20–30 cm wide).
descriptions.NUR15895: Cemetery composed of domus de janas repurposed in the Roman period.
descriptions.NUR6950:
In an initial phase, several villages of square huts were established in the area, belonging to the Ozieri culture, which included a necropolis with hypogean tombs of domus de janas and a probable sanctuary featuring a menhir, stone slabs for sacrifices, and stone spheres.

It consists of 8 hypogean tombs, among which the "Head's tomb" stands out in importance.
descriptions.NUR8002: Domus de janas entirely excavated in shale, consisting of a single chamber with lateral benches.
descriptions.NUR7009: Excavated in an amphitheatre of trachyte rock on the southern flank of the 'silent' hill of sa Pranedda, it consists of over 40 tombs of various sizes and plans, aligned along the rock face in a symmetrical arrangement that appears pre-planned. The necropolis of Montessu is one of the most significant and fascinating pre-Nuragic testimonies on the Island, in use for a millennium and a half, from the Late Neolithic (3200–2800 BC) to the Early Bronze Age (1800–1600 BC).
descriptions.NUR7735: Three domus de janas. Featuring an imposing column inside and carved bull's-head protomes on the walls. Very difficult to locate.
descriptions.NUR7158: On the flank of Monte Cumida. It consists of eight domus de janas, variously articulated and characterised by decorative motifs on the walls. In Tomb VI, which has seven chambers, a false door of trapezoidal shape is carved into the back wall of one of the cells. In Tomb VIII, the main cell has a double-pitched ceiling and, on the front wall above the hatch giving access to one of the secondary chambers, double horns are carved in low relief, now barely legible.
descriptions.NUR14691: The two domus de janas are located in the territory of the comune of Silanus (NU), 40 metres north of the former SS 229, close to the nuraghes Ordari and s’Aspru, which are built on rocky outcrops at a higher elevation.
descriptions.NUR14194: The construction is unique, as it incorporates elements typical of the subterranean context. It is a domus de janas repurposed in the Nuragic period, where a stele and a corridor were built. It represents a distinctive tomb with an architectural façade.
descriptions.NUR7606: They are located within the territory of the comune of Sassari. These are two underground chambers of the Abealzu culture, dug into limestone rock, situated close to one another on the left side of SS131, heading towards Portotorres. The entrances to the domus are barely noticeable to anyone walking along the path that runs beside them and leads into a residential area, as the structures are completely enveloped by natural vegetation.
descriptions.NUR7306:
Two domus de janas, separated by about 2 m. The antechamber has a semi-elliptical plan and an irregularly flat ceiling. In the back wall of the antechamber there is a square opening, also with a recess, providing access to a room with a flat ceiling.

A rectangular light opening with a recess for the shutter provides access to an antechamber with a sub-elliptical plan and a flat ceiling.
descriptions.NUR7022: (very difficult to locate, but it exists)
descriptions.NUR7174: It should include at least five hypogea.
descriptions.NUR7068: Composed of two rooms of square plan dug into compact granite.
descriptions.NUR6998: On the Punta Sas Baddes plateau lies the domus de janas of Funtana 'e Furru, the only one with access via a small well, a single-cell structure with a chamber shaped like a "oven".
descriptions.NUR8033: Domus de janas fractured and covered with debris
descriptions.NUR7035: Domus de janas fractured and covered with debris
descriptions.NUR6932: Cemeteries with nine hypogeic tombs, located in an area with rocks protruding from the surrounding ground. The tombs were accidentally discovered during recent excavation work. It is believed that the site was first used from the recent Neolithic (about 3500 BC).
descriptions.NUR7165:
The underground chamber is located about 750 metres to the south-east of the Nuraghe s'Infurcadu, while about fifty metres to the north-east two menhirs and traces of ancient habitation are found—though these have been erased by uncontrolled land-clearing works.

The domus, excavated in a basaltic rock outcrop, consists of a short pavilion leading into a cell with a niche.
descriptions.NUR7320:
It is located within the territory of the comune of Cagliari.

Final section of a domus de janas (Neolithic underground tomb), near the cave of the same name, destroyed by the limestone quarry.
descriptions.NUR7043: It is two underground chambers of domus de janas.
descriptions.NUR17728: A short distance from the Sant'Andria nuraghe, in the north-west direction, lies the domus de janas, which is carved into a granitic outcrop. The entrance has collapsed, so access to the underground chamber is through an irregular opening; this chamber features a small antechamber from which the entrance to the second chamber opens. Around it, fragments and pieces of lithic material are scattered.
descriptions.NUR7384: On a rocky granite outcrop of irregular shape, two single-cell domus de janas have been excavated. The surrounding area is characterized by a dense forest of oaks. The two subterranean burials, separated by about 1 metre, are respectively dug into the northern and western sides of the granite outcrop.
descriptions.NUR6939: Domus de janas restored and used as a pastoral and agricultural refuge.
descriptions.NUR7066: It consists of two single-cell tombs, side by side, each with a rectangular entrance.
descriptions.NUR7104: The archaeological area includes a village and two domus de janas, situated on a granitic tower partially surrounded by the Tèscere river. The complex nuraghe is characterized by the presence of natural cavities integrated with masonry structures. The two domus are excavated in two large stones. The first, single-chambered, is accessible through an elevated entrance preceded by a short pavilion. The second has a single chamber, collapsed due to the failure of the stone that once formed the entrance.
descriptions.NUR4151: The archaeological area includes a village and two domus de janas, situated on a granitic tower partially surrounded by the Tèscere river. The complex nuraghe is characterized by the presence of natural cavities integrated with masonry structures. The two domus are excavated in two large stones. The first, single-chambered, is accessible through an elevated entrance preceded by a short pavilion. The second has a single chamber, collapsed due to the failure of the stone that once formed the entrance.
descriptions.NUR6934: They are four small underground burials dug out in an isolated rock outcrop.
descriptions.NUR7185: It includes three hypogea, of which the first (with 7 cells) should also be called "Sa Spelunca de Nonna".
descriptions.NUR7169:
Domus de janas necropolis particularly striking, located adjacent to part of a larger site that includes a nuraghe with a village and a dolmen.

One of the most beautiful Domus de Janas, until a few years ago it was entirely still underground. From a small entrance one accesses a large chamber, inside which there are three additional entrances leading to three separate rooms.
descriptions.NUR11474: Domus de janas necropolis particularly striking, located adjacent to part of a larger site that includes a nuraghe with a village and a dolmen. One of the most beautiful Domus de Janas is Sirilò, until recently entirely still buried underground. From a small entrance one accesses a large chamber, within which there are three additional entrances leading to three separate rooms.
descriptions.NUR7059: Domus de janas carved out of granite, particularly striking for its double door set between a pillar.
descriptions.NUR14912: Dug into a basalt wall, the tomb shows an entrance oriented to the west at a depth of 0.80 m below the camp level; it is rectangular and well carved, bordered by a deep recess. The threshold features a drainage groove, while along the wall thickness, near the corner posts, two opposite recesses are present, possibly to facilitate the flow of the doorstop. The chamber, of irregular semicircular plan, has a flat floor and a roof with curved walls.
descriptions.NUR15545: On the slopes of "Monte Santo", three different stones host Neolithic burials along an ascent path. Three erratic boulders in which the tombs have been carved. In the first stone encountered when ascending towards the summit, Su Crastu de Santu Eliseu, which gives the site its name, the domus has been repurposed as a Christian cult site. Then comes Su Crastu de Santu Elia, and finally Su Crastu de Santu Enoch, which features a domus with two fine bull's-head protomes.
descriptions.NUR15543: On the slopes of "Monte Santo", three different stones host Neolithic burials along an ascent path. Three erratic boulders in which the tombs have been carved. In the first stone encountered when ascending towards the summit, Su Crastu de Santu Eliseu, which gives the site its name, the domus has been repurposed as a Christian cult site. Then comes Su Crastu de Santu Elia, and finally Su Crastu de Santu Enoch, which features a domus with two fine bull's-head protomes.
descriptions.NUR7201: Pluricellular, extensively modified and used as a shepherd's shelter.
descriptions.NUR6996: Single-cell domus de janas dug into trachyte
descriptions.NUR7443:
Nearby lies the same-named domus de janas. The nuraghe is heavily eroded.

A short distance from the provincial road Florinas-Banari; a service track leading to a disused sand quarry allows closer approach to the site.
descriptions.NUR3899:
Nearby lies the same-named domus de janas. The nuraghe is heavily eroded.

A short distance from the provincial road Florinas-Banari; a service track leading to a disused sand quarry allows closer approach to the site.
descriptions.NUR18937: It consists of six single-cell domus de janas.
descriptions.NUR19616:
Isolated domus with reuse.

Excerpt from the publication "Archaeological research in Marghine-Planargia" by Moravetti
descriptions.NUR7409: Domus de janas with the particularity of a double door on two opposite sides, with the roof collapsed on the vault.
descriptions.NUR19039: The domus is very deeply buried and entry into it is practically impossible.
descriptions.NUR7241: It is a multicompartments underground chamber.
descriptions.NUR7433: The pre-Nuragic necropolis of S'Elighe Entosu consists of eight very distinctive domus de janas: for example, one preserves in its cell a circular stone hearth carved into the floor, a ceiling carved with a double pitch replicating the timbering of a wooden roof, and on the sides a reproduction of the walls of prehistoric huts. Another, called "delle Sette Stanze", has medieval graffiti along the entrance corridor and seven small cells arranged around the main chamber.
descriptions.NUR6915: The pre-Nuragic necropolis of S'Elighe Entosu consists of eight very distinctive domus de janas: for example, one preserves in its cell a circular stone hearth carved into the floor, a ceiling carved with a double pitch replicating the timbering of a wooden roof, and on the sides a reproduction of the walls of prehistoric huts. Another, called "delle Sette Stanze", has medieval graffiti along the entrance corridor and seven small cells arranged around the main chamber.
descriptions.NUR7638: The complex consists of six hypogeal tombs cut into large isolated blocks of limestone, erratic boulders. Tombs I and IV stand out for their decorative ornaments, represented by spiral motifs carved in relief with the direct pecking technique, and architectural elements typical of contemporary dwellings, such as beams and joists (reproducing a double-pitched roof), frames, pilasters, plinths, steps and false doors, carved in bas-relief.

descriptions.NUR6910: The complex consists of six hypogeal tombs cut into large isolated blocks of limestone, erratic boulders. Tombs I and IV stand out for their decorative ornaments, represented by spiral motifs carved in relief with the direct pecking technique, and architectural elements typical of contemporary dwellings, such as beams and joists (reproducing a double-pitched roof), frames, pilasters, plinths, steps and false doors, carved in bas-relief.
descriptions.NUR1258: Two small domus de janas visible from the road
descriptions.NUR9756:
The underground tomb opens into a shallow outcrop, about 150 metres east of the municipal boundary Borore – Silanus.

The underground chamber, oriented south-west, consists of two sub-circular chambers arranged along the longitudinal axis; the walls are carefully smoothed and the ceiling is slightly hemispherical.
descriptions.NUR9757:
The underground tomb opens into a shallow outcrop, about 150 metres east of the municipal boundary Borore – Silanus.

The underground chamber, oriented south-west, consists of two sub-circular chambers arranged along the longitudinal axis; the walls are carefully smoothed and the ceiling is slightly hemispherical.
descriptions.NUR7469: The evidence for this period dates no earlier than the Final Neolithic. The very simple domus de janas at Campu Estius should belong to the Ozieri culture. "and the handle of a volcanic rock, the smallest of those from Perda Longa (Lilliu, 1975 p. 3; Lilliu, 2003 pp. 98-99), like a sacred rock, witness to the artificial holes made in it and to the finds of stone rings, of green stone and of discs found whole"
descriptions.NUR14950: Domus de janas of which no photographs exist and whose condition is unknown
descriptions.NUR6975: It is located in the territory of the comune of Nuoro. It is a single-cell domus, well finished internally. Difficult to identify due to dense vegetation. It opens onto a low granite bank.
descriptions.NUR7763: The necropolis of Iscala Mugheras consists of six domus de janas. In particular, the fourth, fifth, and sixth have been used as sheepfolds by the landowner in whose territory they are located.
descriptions.NUR7690: The necropolis of Iscala Mugheras consists of six domus de janas. In particular, the fourth, fifth, and sixth have been used as sheepfolds by the landowner in whose territory they are located.
descriptions.NUR7691: The necropolis of Iscala Mugheras consists of six domus de janas. In particular, the fourth, fifth, and sixth have been used as sheepfolds by the landowner in whose territory they are located.
descriptions.NUR7120: The necropolis of Iscala Mugheras consists of six domus de janas. In particular, the fourth, fifth, and sixth have been used as sheepfolds by the landowner in whose territory they are located.
descriptions.NUR7110:
Dug into a tuff cliff and located in a narrow valley gorge fed by a tributary of the Rio Mannu, just outside the village, to the right of the road to Allai.

The domus are situated in a private property, enclosed and secured by a gate; the owner is often seen working in the garden and will readily let you enter and guide you to the site.
descriptions.NUR7290: They are carved from a rock composed almost entirely of white quartz pebbles. The origin of these pebbles can be traced to a fluvial-deltaic environment dating back to about 166 million years ago.
descriptions.NUR17692: The domus consists of three large rooms with a single entrance.
descriptions.NUR15886: It is a small single-chambered underground chamber.
descriptions.NUR6945: Moderate in scale (about 51 metres with a negative elevation drop of 10 metres), easily accessible.
descriptions.NUR13986:
In a wooded area, carved into trachytic rock. The interior is decorated with a false door and a probable bull's-head protome above.

It includes 7 hypogea in total and known.
descriptions.NUR6923: Cemetery consisting of 25 tombs dug into granite. No sculptural decorations are present on the walls.
descriptions.NUR12033: Domus de janas that was begun but never completed, only the entrance and a partial excavation of the interior are visible.
descriptions.NUR6940:
Administratively it belongs to the municipality of Thiesi, province of Sassari, from which it is about 10 kilometres away.

The necropolis consists of four domus de janas cut into a trachyte outcrop on the slopes of Monte Ittiresu. Among them, Tomb III stands out for its importance; also known as the "Painted Tomb", it is considered one of the most interesting testimonies of the Sardinian Neolithic. Because the site has been left abandoned, the frescoes are undergoing continuous and rapid deterioration.
descriptions.NUR12135:
They are two hypogea.

They are located just outside the settlement, about 800 m away. They are accessed via a path between the slopes leading towards Murruzzone and Su Lu'e. Of the two, only one is in good condition, though relatively small, situated on an isolated rocky outcrop, with its opening exposed to the east—this one is shown in the first photo; the other appears severely damaged and overgrown with brambles, as shown in the image below. The two 'oncheddas' are separated by about 100 m.
descriptions.NUR12136: Second domus de janas. in poor condition due to the overgrowth of brambles.
descriptions.NUR7231: The archaeological site, dating to the late Neolithic, consists of 5 domus de janas positioned at different elevations along the mountain slope and is easily accessible by following a path a short distance from the provincial road Nuoro-Siniscola; the first domus opens directly onto the path, while the others are located among the vegetation above it.
descriptions.NUR7114: It consists of four underground chambers. Probable location.
descriptions.NUR7381: The chamber, monochambered, with a sub-elliptical plan and entrance offset to the left relative to the central axis of the chamber, features a flat floor and a curved vault, almost like a oven. It shows two phases of construction: in the original layout, the chamber and the rectangular door were excavated, marked by a groove; in a later phase, a small dolmenic corridor was added.
descriptions.NUR11471:
This domus came to light during the flood of 18-11-2013.  

Until then, it had been covered by vegetation and was likely known to the local herders. Above it lies a road.
descriptions.NUR7263: Once one "slid" inward, the tomb reveals itself in all its splendour: columns, bull's-head protomes in low relief, chambers, antechambers, the door of the beyond, symbols and signs of an ancient devotion that intoxicates body and spirit.
descriptions.NUR7112: Beautiful necropolis of domus de janas consisting of eight domus, four of which are grouped together (5–6–7–8), the fourth is located near the group of four tombs, the third is about 200 metres to the south, and the first and second are situated near each other, about 100 metres east of the third.
descriptions.NUR7232: Beautiful necropolis of domus de janas consisting of eight domus, four of which are grouped together (5–6–7–8), the fourth is located near the group of four tombs, the third is about 200 metres to the south, and the first and second are situated near each other, about 100 metres east of the third.
descriptions.NUR7371: Beautiful necropolis of domus de janas consisting of eight domus, four of which are grouped together (5–6–7–8), the fourth is located near the group of four tombs, the third is about 200 metres to the south, and the first and second are situated near each other, about 100 metres east of the third.
descriptions.NUR1356: It is a small cemetery composed of 5 domus de janas, one of which is barely outlined and hardly visible because hidden by vegetation.
descriptions.NUR12070: There are three isolated tombs in the municipality of Mamoiada.
descriptions.NUR7098: The domus de janas, carved into the basaltic hillside, number five, all attributable to the Ozieri Culture and dating from 3100 to 2900 BC. The pre-Nuragic village, also belonging to the Ozieri Culture, is located at the foot of the hill.
descriptions.NUR20012:
The domus is located within a private garden and is carved out of a massive oval granite outcrop; above it, a small pit has been dug, from which two channels extend.

The domus consists of a forechamber providing access to a large chamber, within which on the right side an entrance leads to an additional chamber.
descriptions.NUR9803:
The underground chamber, oriented to the northeast, is composed of a short rectangular antechamber (depth 0.45 m – width 0.56 m – height 0.66 m) that opens into the burial chamber via a square doorway (width 0.38 m).

The chamber has a vaguely elliptical plan (depth 0.78–1.08 m – height 0.62 m – width 1.70 m) with an irregular profile, walls smoothed with care, and a slightly hemispherical ceiling.
descriptions.NUR7204: It is Domus I, the most significant and easily visible of a necropolis composed of 7 hypogea. The other tombs are located on private land, about 600 metres away in a straight line to the south-east. Two of the hypogea are more accurately described as caves used as tombs. This prehistoric necropolis gave its name to the first phase of the Early Bronze Age in Sardinia (1800–1600 BC), known as the Bonnanaro Culture.
descriptions.NUR7230:
Located between the Sas Pireddas area to the east and Riu Mortu to the south, the Domus of Istiolai is a depression carved into a single granite monolith, consisting of a courtyard and a burial chamber with a rounded base; the latter features a small artificial pit cut into the floor, likely used for votive offerings.

The entrance is oriented north-north-west, and the craftsmanship is particularly precise, especially at the entrance.
descriptions.NUR7292:
The Sas Arzolas de Goi necropolis dates to the Ozieri Culture period (3200–2800 BC).

Five domus de janas have been identified so far; they lie on the slope of a trachyte hill that has been extensively affected by quarrying.

Tomb 1 is particularly interesting because it displays two complete bull's-head protomes, with ears and head, carved above the entrance hatch and on the pillar inside the burial chamber. The horns at the entrance are carved in convex relief.
descriptions.NUR7235: This domus de janas belongs to the larger complex of Abealzu-Calancoi, which includes dozens of domus de janas. It is situated on the half-slope of a limestone hillside, exposed to the south, and is difficult to reach on foot. It is notable for its state of degradation due to limestone weathering and subsequent human use.
descriptions.NUR7429: The site is characterized by a quadrangular courtyard, which originally served as the main chamber now collapsed. Access is provided through a granite arch of rare beauty, from which one reaches what remains of the original domus; two rooms, one quadrangular and aligned with the entrance, the other irregularly shaped to the right.
descriptions.NUR6987:
The tomb belongs to the cemetery of Campu Majore, composed of 24 domus de janas, which are located within private properties and are not accessible without permission.

The entrance to this domus faced the village of Busachi, which during the Second World War was modified with a reinforced concrete wall, adapted by the owners to serve as a shelter against bombings.

Today it is used as a water reservoir.
descriptions.NUR7154: On the edge of the named height: a very ruined tomb, possibly the only underground chamber remaining from a small necropolis.
descriptions.NUR7137: The cemetery of Coroneddu (Bosa – OR) consists of three underground chambers, two adjacent and one more separated. It is situated on a rocky cliff on the southern slope of a calcareous hill that extends into the Modolo valley. Probable location
descriptions.NUR6961: The cemetery consists of six domus de janas in poor state of conservation. One, however, features two pillars carved into the rock with fish-spine decorations. The ceiling is also carved, depicting the roof of the hut.
descriptions.NUR7402: Single-cell domus de janas located near the municipal road
descriptions.NUR6958: It consists of 6 hypogea, of which 4 have been destroyed.
descriptions.NUR7142: Inside there is a pillar on which a bull's-head protome is carved in high relief.
descriptions.NUR7261: Three domus de janas built on a limestone cliff, monocellular, later decorated with carved stelae set against the rock face.
descriptions.NUR7295: Three domus de janas built on a limestone cliff, monocellular, later decorated with carved stelae set against the rock face.
descriptions.NUR7446: Three domus de janas built on a limestone cliff, monocellular, later decorated with carved stelae set against the rock face.
descriptions.NUR7527: Dug in a low trachytic formation, it features a bull's-head protome in the antechamber.
descriptions.NUR6983:
Group of domus de janas, arranged along a channel of about 200 metres in length.

The largest one, located beneath the road embankment, contains: Su laccu: a basin likely used to produce must.

The domus is so spacious that it appears more like a dwelling than a tomb.

Various-sized recesses on the walls. Storage areas of different types and subterranean chambers of lower level, adjacent to the main chamber.
descriptions.NUR7364:
The cemetery is situated within a broader archaeological context that includes a village of dry-stone huts and fortified dwellings – located just a few hundred metres away – and a megalithic circle (diameter 3.00 m) at a distance of about 600 m.

The funerary complex comprises nine domus de janas with variously articulated plan layouts. Tomb I is multicellular and contains eleven successive cells.
descriptions.NUR7116: Six hypogea of the domus de janas type. The immediate proximity to a tuff quarry, with only faint traces of other hypogea found at its edges, suggests the site may have extended beyond its current known boundaries. Of the six domus present, one is almost entirely destroyed; three have been adapted into rustic farmhouses during the historical period, after substantial modifications to their layout; only the last two (Tombs V and VI) have preserved the original structure.
descriptions.NUR7016: The "Domus de janas" are pre-Nuragic underground (subterranean) cemeteries, dated to 3500–3000 BC, composed of one or more rooms and used up to the Nuragic period. On Monte Arìsta, in the municipality of Cardedu, there is a cemetery consisting of ten tombs carefully constructed and in excellent state of preservation. The tombs are carved out of isolated granite blocks. The underground chambers are of two types: single- and double-chambered, and they have a longitudinal development.
descriptions.NUR7255: Multicellular domus de janas containing carved decorations depicting a bull's-head protome. At the centre there is a pillar cut out by removal of rock.
descriptions.NUR7017: On Monte Zara there are nine domus, including two adjacent ones known popularly as Is ogus de monti, or "the eyes of the mountain". A majestic staircase of about sixty steps, entirely carved into the stone, leads to the summit of the mountain from where one enjoys a wide view of the Cagliari coast. Here lies a Nuragic sacred area dating back to the 7th century B.C., featuring an altar and several cisterns for collecting rainwater.
descriptions.NUR7025: On Monte Zara there are nine domus de janas, including two adjacent ones known popularly as Is ogus de monti, or "the eyes of the mountain," a truly fitting nickname. A majestic staircase of about sixty steps, entirely carved into the stone, leads to the summit of the mountain from where one enjoys a wide view of the Cagliari coast. Here lies a Nuragic sacred area dating back to the 7th century B.C., featuring an altar and several cisterns for collecting rainwater.
descriptions.NUR6930: The necropolis of Museddu is located within the park of petroglyphs; it consists of 18 domus de janas, with simple planimetric layouts, either a quadrangular cell preceded by a small pavilion, or two or three cells arranged in longitudinal projection.
descriptions.NUR6974: The well-known necropolis of Noeddale is located at the western edge of a saddle that declines significantly to the west, along the valley of Sae. It consists of six hypogea, three of which were dug into a slightly inclined limestone outcrop, one into a low underlying wall, and two into the front of a higher rock face. Two of the hypogea are preceded by short dromoi.
descriptions.NUR7113: Single-cell domus de janas carved in limestone
descriptions.NUR7278: Single-cell domus de janas carved in limestone
descriptions.NUR6949: The cemetery consists of three domus de janas, among which the tomb I stands out for its size and decorations.
descriptions.NUR7045: Domus de janas built around a central acrocoro on which the traces of a hut or megalithic circle are evident.
descriptions.NUR7033: Large natural cave, on the eastern side of which open several smaller cavities whose morphological features would suggest they should be classified as domus de janas; this hypothesis would be strengthened by the presence of channels and cups on the top of the cave, used both functionally and ritually.
descriptions.NUR7064: The two domus de janas are hard to see from the provincial road because their entrances are hidden by vegetation.
descriptions.NUR6966:
It can be counted among the most extensive of those known and is rich in particular architectural symbolism. Hewn from a rocky plateau of red trachyte, it consists of at least twenty hypogea.

The domus de janas very often reproduce the ground plans and certain details of the dwellings of the living.

In some of them anthropomorphic petroglyphs are carved, known as “capovolti” because they are thought to represent the souls of the dead returning to mother earth.
descriptions.NUR7161: It is a group of six domus de janas tombs, of which five, of the monocellular oven type, are in very poor condition, while the sixth features a sub-square antechamber from which access is gained to an adjacent rectangular chamber.
descriptions.NUR7115: It is one of two hypogea in the Campu Marinu area. In the past, a dolmen (presumably destroyed) also existed at the site.
descriptions.NUR6984: Cemetery consisting of four domus de janas dug into erratic boulders
descriptions.NUR7225: They are three underground cists dug into a low limestone cliff face.
descriptions.NUR6947:
The cemetery consists of 18 domus de janas, excavated on three horizontal levels stacked one above the other, starting from the base of the cliff, for a maximum height of 3 m above the plain level.

The materials recovered during excavations have allowed dating of the burials to a period ranging from the final Neolithic (San Michele culture, 3200–2800 BC) to the early Bronze Age (Bonnanaro culture, 1800–1600 BC).
descriptions.NUR7197: The cemetery consists of five hypogea and numerous cavities that were probably domus de janas, but now appear to have been destroyed or incomplete. One of the domus (the first) features in its main chamber an interesting column.
descriptions.NUR7132: Domus de janas of which no description is available
descriptions.NUR7509: It is located within the territory of the comune of Florinas. It consists of two underground chambers.
descriptions.NUR7089: Next to the village, two single-cell domus de janas dug out in a calcarean cave.
descriptions.NUR7056:
Probable location.

It consists of two underground chambers.
descriptions.NUR11644:
It is a domus in basalt. It consists of a vestibule and an adjacent chamber.

On the right wall of the vestibule, a small niche has been carved. The floor features a "fireplace" of notable craftsmanship.

Located in a low basaltic coastal area shaded by some holm oaks. Easily accessible just a few dozen metres from the road.
descriptions.NUR12034: It is an incomplete domus located within a granite monolith.
descriptions.NUR12071:
The small necropolis of Ovau consists of three small domus de janas. The first one is the one with the largest chamber and the most prominent door frame. The third, on the other hand, is very small inside.

Nearby are two remarkable, superimposed menhirs, very well crafted. The first menhir
descriptions.NUR12649: Group of domus de janas hidden in the undergrowth
descriptions.NUR9770: It is a small single-chamber tomb, of oven type, circular in plan (depth 0.55 m – width 0.62 m), accessed through a finely carved opening (width ….. – height 0.42 m – thickness 0.12 m), preceded by a short antechamber (depth 0.32 m – width 0.75/0.48 m). The orientation is to the south; the walls are perfectly smoothed and the ceiling is slightly hemispherical.
descriptions.NUR15931: The cemetery consists of three domus de janas.
descriptions.NUR14005: Domus de janas on a trachytic cliff, internally decorated with a false door and a possibly carved hearth.
descriptions.NUR7316: Typical single-cell domus de janas with a carved stele facing the limestone.
descriptions.NUR7121: Six domus de janas in the locality of Sas Concheddas de Pianu Edras, carved into a cliff face composed of trachytic tuff, are located within the Prehistoric Subterranean Necropolis of Pianu Edras, among which the Domus delle Cappelle stands out.
descriptions.NUR6962: There are four (but one is destroyed).
descriptions.NUR7539: It consists of a rectangular doorway leading into a small antechamber originally roofed. This is followed by a doorway with four rebates arranged like steps to receive the closing slab. The tomb is single-chambered and the walls are carefully worked. In the small antechamber, on the right-hand wall and in the ceiling of the left-hand side, there are traces of red ochre that must originally have coloured the whole chamber. Copper Age material (Monte Claro culture) comes from this domus de janas.
descriptions.NUR6922: It consists of at least 19 tombs, including one barely outlined.
descriptions.NUR15083: The condition of the tomb is unknown.
descriptions.NUR10541: Group of domus de janas, the most important of which features a checkerboard motif, bordered on one side by a zig–zag band, representing the depiction of textiles found in the dwellings of the living and re-presented in the tombs of the dead.
descriptions.NUR6952: The cemetery includes 21 domus de janas. Visible from the bridge on SS131.
descriptions.NUR20266: During construction a water vein was discovered beneath, allowing the domus to remain full of water even during periods of drought. For this reason it became a temple dedicated to fertility, to such an extent that a female reproductive organ was carved into the rock around the domus entrance, and above it, a male reproductive organ. These are connected by a channel incised into the rock, symbolizing fertilization.
descriptions.NUR7372: Neolithic rock-cut burial, typologically perhaps attributable to the Filigosa culture (about 2500 BC). The monument is hard to read because it is covered by dense vegetation. The burial consists of an entrance corridor (dromos), an antechamber and a chamber. The narrow corridor leads into the roughly circular antechamber. The chamber proper, smaller and roughly rectangular in plan, is reached through a roughly rectangular/trapezoidal doorway.
descriptions.NUR20017:
These are three hypogea cut into a trachyandesite outcrop inside a private property.

Domus I has a short dromos entrance, an antechamber that opens onto two successive cells along the same axis. The Domus has no particular decoration.

Domus II and III: the first is full of water, but its wide entrance can be admired; the second is completely overgrown with vegetation to the point that it was not possible to explore it.

There are probably other hypogea.
descriptions.NUR7327: It lies near the country church of San Pietro, about one kilometre from the village. Its name, S'Acqua 'e is dolus, means "the water of sorrows", from an old folk belief that the water in this small cave has miraculous powers; a legend also tells that during one of his journeys San Pietro took shelter in this artificial grotto and prayed there for so long that the imprint of his knees was left forever in the rock.
descriptions.NUR7318: The complex consists of two domus de janas carved into a rocky outcrop of sandstone exposed to the south, located in a south-eastern position relative to the new church of San Giovanni.
descriptions.NUR7339: The complex consists of two domus de janas carved into a rocky outcrop of sandstone exposed to the south, located in a south-eastern position relative to the new church of San Giovanni.
descriptions.NUR7094: The complex consists of two domus de janas carved into a rocky outcrop of sandstone exposed to the south, located in a south-eastern position relative to the new church of San Giovanni.
descriptions.NUR13966: In a tomb a large bull's-head protome and traces of painting are still visible. Six single-cell domus are identifiable, in poor state of conservation. Two other tombs are located about 500 metres away in the south-east direction.
descriptions.NUR12308:
Domus 1 has a multi-cell layout, featuring a semicircular antechamber from which access is gained to a first trapezoidal cell, which is characterised by a central pillar. On top of this pillar there is an opening leading to a higher level, which includes two superimposed small cells above the previous one.

Domus 2 has a multi-cell layout, featuring a corridor, an elliptical cell, a central sub-rectangular chamber with a niche, and a third quadrangular cell.
descriptions.NUR19989: Domus de janas reported by a hiker.
descriptions.NUR7719: The sculptures of the bull's head can be admired, representing the head of the male god, worshipped by the populations of the Neolithic period, who buried their dead in these artificial caves.
descriptions.NUR12727: The sculptures of the bull's head can be admired, representing the head of the male god, worshipped by the populations of the Neolithic period, who buried their dead in these artificial caves.
descriptions.NUR13691: The context is special because the quarried stone appears "isolated", surrounded by holm oaks that blend it into the surroundings, the entrance faces south-west, the chamber is circular, and the walls feature square niches; the surrounding ground slopes gently, and a striking rocky outcrop is visible a few metres away to the west.
descriptions.NUR7664: Remains of a domus de janas
descriptions.NUR7781: In the countryside of Osilo there is a very large domus de janas, greatly modified, located beneath the foundations of a church now reduced to ruins.
descriptions.NUR7237: The underground chamber is cut into a limestone cliff. "The whole appears carefully organised and balanced in proportion, producing a powerful compositional harmony" (Giuseppa Tanda).
descriptions.NUR7430: The underground chamber is cut into a limestone cliff. "The whole appears carefully organised and balanced in proportion, producing a powerful compositional harmony" (Giuseppa Tanda).
descriptions.NUR7199: Four domus de janas spaced apart
descriptions.NUR6916:
You crawl through that opening; the space is tight, the ceiling low because of all that millennia-old earth, and you go on advancing on your elbows, slowly. It consists of at least 12 hypogea, cut into the limestone and provided with various decorations and bull protomes.

These are domus that move you, because their beauty lies in everything they hold.

Then, in the darkness, a shaft of light illuminates a magnificent triple-framed decoration on a doorway still almost completely buried.
descriptions.NUR6942: The domus de janas that make up this necropolis, one of the most extensive and significant in Sardinia, are carved into the vertical face and the plateau of a trachytic outcrop – about 10 m high and oriented to the south – and are arranged in about twenty burials, mostly situated at a certain height above the countryside level.
descriptions.NUR20041:
The Domus de Janas of Sant'Andrìa are located in the municipality of Mara (Sassari), in the rural area of "Sant'Andrìa, from which they take their name.

They consist of a single "nicchia", set amid thick vegetation.

They are easy to identify; they can be seen from the road to Bonu Ighinu, on the left-hand side, higher up.
descriptions.NUR6968:
A small cemetery with chambers interconnected and with traces still visible of red ochre.

Located on SP 15, towards Sorradile, clearly visible at the junction leading to the lake.

The entrance is very finely carved; the collapses of the antechamber are evident, and there were certainly other chambers, as clear traces remain in the ground immediately in front.
descriptions.NUR12644: The necropolis of Santu Pedru is a pre-Nuragic archaeological site. The necropolis is located on the eastern slope of the trachytic hill of Santu Pedru, in a position of wide visibility over the valley below, in the Nurra, a region in northwestern Sardinia. The complex includes a dozen tombs with a corridor entrance ("dromos") and a planimetric layout composed of multiple cells.
descriptions.NUR6911: Group of seven or more domus de janas located on the pass, near L'azienda Mariani, from which one has a view of the Santa Lucia plain and the underlying necropolis of Sant'Andrea Priu, as well as the valley of the nuraghes of Torralba. The tomb seven, featuring a double spiral in red ochre, has recently been restored.
descriptions.NUR17694: The first chamber has collapsed upon itself, and access to the smaller chamber must be gained by crawling through the ruins.
descriptions.NUR7571: A jewel set among the mountains of Padria, where the Ancient Sardinians carved the rock and sculpted extraordinary bull's-head protomes across an entire wall, enigmatic guardians watching us in silence.
descriptions.NUR7258: Single-cell domus de janas on a rocky outcrop, isolated and rising above the terrain
descriptions.NUR7119: Domus de janas enriched with various bull's-head protomes carved in limestone
descriptions.NUR7118:
It is located within the municipal territory of Orani (NU). It consists of 17 domus de janas and 2 tunnels (probably used as burial sites). In a text by Chiara Chisu, it is stated that there are 15 domus, but I have recorded at least 17 (some may have escaped my notice due to dense vegetation).

Do not confuse them with those of Oniferi, which are known as Sas Concas.
descriptions.NUR9224: Two domus de janas sites located on the slopes of the mountain known as "Sas Monzas". Excavated in Miocene limestone.
descriptions.NUR6980: The complex consists of 13 hypogea situated in a panoramic position on Lake Omodeo.
descriptions.NUR13341: Domus de janas located near the provincial road. Excavated on limestone, featuring particular bull's-head protomes in relief.
descriptions.NUR7236: It consists of five hypogea, one of which is buried and one of which is difficult to identify.
descriptions.NUR19920:
The entrance, about 110 cm x 60 cm, is at floor level. There is a single oval chamber about 150 cm high, 250 cm deep and 130 cm wide, apparently undecorated. At the back of the chamber a pit occupies about two-thirds of the short side and is about 3 m deep; it has not been explored and contains a large niche within the same cavity.

Around the domus de janas cut into the limestone there are rectangular basins that look like quarrying for building material, almost as if the site had been used as a quarry.
descriptions.NUR7711: Serra is Araus is a multilayered site, known for the presence of a rock-cut necropolis (domus de janas) dating to the Neolithic (Ozieri culture), Chalcolithic (Monte Claro culture) and Early Bronze Age (Bunnannaro). The 2013 excavation revealed two new hypogea and brought to light the earliest evidence of a Nuragic village. In particular, traces of a building were found, within which a large-scale model of a nuraghe had been placed.
descriptions.NUR20362: Four domus de janas, adjacent to one another, dug into the arenaria. The first one contains a single chamber, while the others contain multiple chambers. The first domu is not connected to the others, whereas the latter are interconnected.
descriptions.NUR19663: The domus was excavated in a rocky outcrop located halfway down the slope of the hill known as Serra Nuarxis. The tomb has a Greek cross plan and consists of a rectangular vestibule, a square doorway leading to the actual chamber, and a chamber. The semicircular chamber is composed of three niches, slightly raised above the floor level, oriented to the south-west, north-east, and south-east. The niches have arched walls and rectangular bases.
descriptions.NUR9636: It is a two-cell house with a short antechamber cut into a trachytic outcrop. The rooms are arranged along the longitudinal axis and have walls carefully smoothed and ceilings slightly hemispherical; the entrance faces south-east.
descriptions.NUR6963: Among the testimonies of funerary hypogeum in the Usini area, the necropolis of Iscala de Sa Figu, although mentioned in literature for its five domus de janas, has not yet been the subject of specific analysis. Following detailed reports, field investigations and surveys have been carried out at the site using both traditional and innovative methodologies. Such operations have enabled the identification of two additional hypogea and the discovery of previously unknown symbols.
descriptions.NUR7217: The cemetery is located in the municipality of Usini. It consists of three domus, one of which has bull's-head protomes and another repurposed as an underground church.
descriptions.NUR6979: The cemetery is located in the municipality of Usini. It consists of three domus, one of which has bull's-head protomes and another repurposed as an underground church.
descriptions.NUR7224: Interesting from a structural and typological point of view for the domus. It is a true necropolis: the domus are simple in form but also complex. Ranging from those with an antechamber and a single chamber to the most elaborate ones with many well-crafted chambers. The vaults of some have collapsed, but careful visits are still possible. mu
descriptions.NUR11414: Single-chamber domus de janas located underneath an artwork on the S.S.131 heading N.O.
descriptions.NUR7168:
It consists of two single-chambered hypogea dug into a trachytic bed at an elevation of 190 metres.

Surrounded by dense and impenetrable vegetation, it is very difficult to locate.
descriptions.NUR11929: A short distance from the Rio Su Hannavagliu and about a few hundred metres from the nuraghe Luduruju.
descriptions.NUR20145: Noted to the Nurnet editorial office by a resident of Osilo. Single-cellular, situated on a calcareous pedestal from which it takes its name, located near the settlement of Santa Vittoria.
descriptions.NUR7271: It is a large domus de janas necropolis, built on a mass of limestone. Around it, interesting Cart Ruts are visible. Some tombs are decorated with bull's-head protomes.
descriptions.NUR12494: A short distance from the settlement of Gonnesa, in a channel within the shale walls, we find the Domus De Janas. The tomb is very simple, round in plan, consisting of a single burial chamber. Vegetation thrives around the site, suggesting that the channel may conceal other burials.
descriptions.NUR20334: It is probably the domus reported by engineer Melis in the census of archaeological sites in Mamoiada; the site should be Locu Lenardu, although today the entire area is known as Su Dovaru. It is a single-cell domus carved into a granite outcrop.
descriptions.NUR7596: Small tomb with a antechamber and a small chamber.
descriptions.NUR11281: Single-cell tomb that represented the place of entertainment for young people of "an earlier time", known as "su Furreddu".
descriptions.NUR12271: Within 50 metres of the right bank of the "Riu Vacchetta", 250 metres from the railway line, and about 800 metres south of the Proto-nuraghe Gazza, there are two artificial caves, located just a few metres apart.
descriptions.NUR15086: The condition of the domus de janas is unknown.
descriptions.NUR7666: Domus de janas at the edge of the village, next to which a dwelling has been built.
descriptions.NUR7498: Situated near the S'Urri valley (where other domus de janas are found), in the Su Linnarbu gorge, on some outcropping rock faces small rock-cut chambers were excavated, of which only slight traces remain because the large natural inlet was used as a dump for inert materials by Italcementi. However, cut into the upper edges that bound the rocky plateau, a few small cavities are still just visible, attributable to prehistoric tombs of the pre-Nuragic period.
descriptions.NUR15859: The domus has an entrance oriented ESE and features a plan layout similar to the previous one – in the form of a cross, but with a different structure. It has a raised dromos leading to a rectangular vestibule from which access is gained to the main chamber. The chamber is rectangular, and on three of its sides, oriented SSE to NNO and NNE, there are three raised wall niches, originally each equipped with a central pilaster.
descriptions.NUR20413:
The split rock, a narrow and low, dark, dusty space that forces you to kneel, as a reminder that you are in a sacred place.

But when you turn on the light, everything becomes visible—the rock takes form, and the ancient symbols seize you, transporting you through time.
descriptions.NUR18660: In the locality "Su Tiriarzu" we find two domus de janas, about 80 metres apart.
descriptions.NUR19640: Common toponym in Sardinia referring to places where rock-cut tombs existed. Indeed, at the site there are two pre-Nuragic bicellular domus de janas.
descriptions.NUR18504: Small and single domus de janas
descriptions.NUR7147: Complex of 5 domus de janas in the Canyon of the Rio Mannu. Carved into Miocene limestone. Some have suffered collapses.
descriptions.NUR13958: In the chamber, the rock carving of the rectangular hut is very faithful. Indeed, it reproduces the lintel, the lateral beams resting on it and on two horizontal beams parallel to it; two pilasters arranged symmetrically.
descriptions.NUR13344: It faces the road from Alghero to Uri; the tomb is very ruined but still retains within it the typical elements of the false door and the overhanging parts, possibly bull's-head protomes.
descriptions.NUR7311: Group of domus de janas containing petroglyphs "of the overturned" very similar to other analogous ones, and in particular to those of Oniferi Sas Concas.
descriptions.NUR7713: Group of domus de janas containing petroglyphs "of the overturned" very similar to other analogous ones, and in particular to those of Oniferi Sas Concas.
descriptions.NUR6912: Group of domus de janas containing petroglyphs "of the overturned" very similar to other analogous ones, and in particular to those of Oniferi Sas Concas.
descriptions.NUR7195: The complex consists of several hypogean tombs cut into large isolated blocks of limestone, erratic boulders. Among them Tombs I and IV stand out for their decorative ornaments, represented by spiral motifs carved in relief with the direct pecking technique, and architectural elements typical of contemporary dwellings, such as beams and joists (reproducing a double-pitched roof), frames, pilasters, plinths, steps and false doors, carved in bas-relief.
descriptions.NUR6948: Various domus de janas of which no description has been found
descriptions.NUR7437: It includes two complete domus and a third that is just beginning.
descriptions.NUR7176: Domus de janas inside the settlement of Buddusò, excavated in a granite outcrop with a cross-shaped plan.
descriptions.NUR7220:
The site, located at 270 m above sea level, is situated on the shores of Lake Omodeo and consists of a nuraghe, a village, and two giants' tombs; nearby is also the necropolis of Ispiluncas, composed of about thirty domus de janas that have yielded a significant amount of pre-Nuragic material.

The nuraghe, possibly a royal residence, is of mixed type with a three-lobed bastion and dates to the late Bronze Age.
descriptions.NUR3418:
The site, located at 270 m above sea level, is situated on the shores of Lake Omodeo and consists of a nuraghe, a village, and two giants' tombs; nearby is also the necropolis of Ispiluncas, composed of about thirty domus de janas that have yielded a significant amount of pre-Nuragic material.

The nuraghe, possibly a royal residence, is of mixed type with a three-lobed bastion and dates to the late Bronze Age.
