The site, located at 270 m above sea level, is situated on the shores of Lake Omodeo and consists of a nuraghe, a village, and two giants' tombs; nearby is also the necropolis of Ispiluncas, composed of about thirty domus de janas that have yielded a significant amount of pre-Nuragic material.

The nuraghe, possibly a royal residence, is of mixed type with a three-lobed bastion and dates to the late Bronze Age.
descriptions.NUR7369: Group of four single-cell domus de janas with façade.
descriptions.NUR7291: Group of four single-cell domus de janas with façade.
descriptions.NUR7223: Group of four single-cell domus de janas with façade.
descriptions.NUR7256: Group of four single-cell domus de janas with façade.
descriptions.NUR7005: Typical domus de janas with a façade featuring a carved arched stele on the calcare wall.
descriptions.NUR20100: Noted to the Superintendent of Ca’ Or on 17 May 2021 by the Nurnet Foundation
descriptions.NUR11470: The exedra of the Giants' Tomb was cut into pieces and used in the construction of the dry stone wall.
descriptions.NUR10251: It is located a short distance from the beautiful single-tower (single-tower nuraghe) of the same name at s'Enalonga, which is now covered by thickets and thorny bushes. A small spring of water still exists nearby, which in ancient times must have supplied the fountain. No particular walling features are evident.
descriptions.NUR14769: Nuragic spring included in a small municipal park, carved into the rock
descriptions.NUR13595: The temple was built in isodomic masonry, that is, with basalt blocks skillfully squared and shaped as needed with appropriate inclinations. The rocks in the surrounding area are mainly schist or granite, while the volcanic rock used was transported to the site from relatively distant locations, probably from the Dorgali region.
descriptions.NUR16368: Sacred well that shows features of both a well and a Nuragic sacred well. Notable is the presence of a stone with a hollow inside.
descriptions.NUR10759: Large complex nuraghe comprising three defined structures dedicated to water cults. The Supervising Office identifies the third as possibly a nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR10757: Large complex nuraghe comprising three defined structures dedicated to water cults. The Supervising Office identifies the third as possibly a nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR10760: Large complex nuraghe comprising three defined structures dedicated to water cults. The Supervising Office identifies the third as possibly a nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR10259: There are not enough elements to provide a reasoned classification, yet despite the most recent modifications, I consider it to be a Nuragic source.
descriptions.NUR10789: The complex consists of two sacred wells, a large hut, and other rooms. The various structures are surrounded by dry stone walls built in a "spine of the fish" pattern.
descriptions.NUR10792: The complex consists of two sacred wells, a large hut, and other rooms. The various structures are surrounded by dry stone walls built in a "spine of the fish" pattern.
descriptions.NUR10790: The complex consists of two sacred wells, a large hut, and other rooms. The various structures are surrounded by dry stone walls built in a "spine of the fish" pattern.
descriptions.NUR4237: The complex consists of two sacred wells, a large hut, and other rooms. The various structures are surrounded by dry stone walls built in a "spine of the fish" pattern.
descriptions.NUR20314: It has architectural features similar to those of cisterns with a pointed vault. The internal basin is wide and still collects sacred liquid. Its conservation state, as of July 2022, is very poor and the site is not widely known.
descriptions.NUR11751: It has a feature never before described: it is built "ALL-AROUND ROUND". Water collects in a recessed rear body: "The building body, constructed in isodomic masonry using ashlar stones of basalt and trachyte, is preserved in a significant portion of its base (Fig. 1), which reveals its elongated planimetric layout, divided into a straight projecting entrance and a rear recessed body containing the sump for collecting spring water."
descriptions.NUR9871: It appears ruined and covered by thick patches of brambles and thorny bushes.
descriptions.NUR2411: Source very likely of Nuragic origin.
descriptions.NUR19145: The well is in good condition, despite having been repeatedly altered in its basic architectural elements. It is built with trachyte blocks of medium and large size, and features a paved corridor with regular stones, about 5.10 m long, leading to a circular tholos chamber with a dome-shaped roof where the water vein is enclosed. Originally, the corridor was intended to have seating placed along the lateral walls.
descriptions.NUR11034: The territory, today almost entirely devoid of vegetation, was once greener and richer in water during the Nuragic period: the springs, now neglected, were once clean and well-maintained, up to thirty years ago. It is likely that at that time small circular structures were built around many of these springs, constructed from large stones and covered with small domed roofs featuring an opening for water, to keep them clean, as we can observe in the remains of Funtana Gureu.
descriptions.NUR11631: Typical nuragic well with stakes made of ashlar stones and a lintel closure. Interior features a water collection basin.
descriptions.NUR14673: The well has no terraces and is in almost perfect conservation.[1] The entire masonry is granitic and fully preserved; the entrance to the internal chamber is formed by a large vaulted opening. The well is covered by two granitic slabs. The well contains a spring, still active, and features a large threshold stone in front, with a channel carved for water runoff.
descriptions.NUR10717: Small nuragic spring with remains of the original cell built over the spring's source and faint traces of the atrium.
descriptions.NUR15306: In its upper part the corridor appears to have been cut by excavating into the sandstone rock. Below it is covered with soil; the depth is unknown but the distance between the walls is certainly greater further down. Of the conical structure of the well proper, parts made of worked ashlars are visible, especially on our left and in the upper part straight ahead, while the part on the right and the central lower part seem to have been emptied of ashlars, as if they had been taken for other uses or had collapsed. The lower part of the spring is covered with mud.
descriptions.NUR12845: The nuragic spring at Su Musuelu is located about 600 m east of the sacred nuragic spring at Is Molineddus. From the limited information the Spano was able to gather, his temple consisted of a rectangular structure with an entrance on the western side, built with large blocks laid dry and closely joined. Behind the building, water emerged from the rock and collected in a round well, itself constructed of large stones.
descriptions.NUR9811:
The remains of what appears to have been a classical Nuragic well are located adjacent to a dry stone wall and mark the boundary between the territories of Birori and Borore, just a few metres from the underground chambers of Bau Cannas.

Currently, only the circular base profile (diameter 1.40 m) and a wall of two courses of well-cut stones are visible; the bottom, as can be seen through the water that pools there, seems to have a pavement of slabs.
descriptions.NUR20062: The Sos Muros complex occupies an area of over twenty hectares, showing clear signs of circular huts and this sacred well.
descriptions.NUR13426: The S'Ulumu well (Dorgali) features a circular cell with a short external vestibule, built in horizontal courses and covered by a tholos. Precisely because of its simple architectural and structural form, it served essentially as a functional water supply for the nearby village.
descriptions.NUR8419:
The archaeological area is located on the southern slope of Monte Senes, in the Baronia, a coastal region of eastern Sardinia. The source preserves the water collection pit of the natural spring, which is still active, and the western portion of the monumental façade.

Part of the retaining wall, oriented N-S, also extends, built on the granite outcrop.
descriptions.NUR21151: Cyclopean masonry circuit with typical features of Nuragic sources
descriptions.NUR10545: Sacred well nuragica, located a short distance from the complex nuraghe of Ardasai.
descriptions.NUR10749: The spring is located within the archaeological area of S'Orgioloniga, where the remains of a Nuragic settlement also exist.
descriptions.NUR10694: The spring consists of a main body in the form of a horse-shoe and a front enclosure, of which a semicircular sector remains. The spring was already used in pre-Nuragic times, as evidenced by some lanceolate arrowheads in obsidian and especially a ceramic fragment decorated in the Ozieri style.
descriptions.NUR14324:
A monument of exceptional value belonging to the final phase of the Nuragic period, when towers were no longer built and various "federal sacred sites" were established, often incorporating sacred wells constructed with isodomic ashlar and enriched with sculptural architectural elements.

La Fonte is unfortunately not properly maintained and is not kept consistently clean.
descriptions.NUR20053: It is located about 300 metres lower than the corresponding nuraghe. It is built of isodomic ashlar stones. In the vestibule preceding the stone seating and directly in front of it, there is a hole cut into the stone that functions as a overflow for the threshold level. The spring is still active and functioning. Around the spring, a temporary structure made of concrete blocks has been built to protect it from weather, vegetation, and animals.
descriptions.NUR13086: The structure has a constant internal diameter of 4.30 m; the walls currently measure 2.80 m in height from the present floor level, which is covered with debris, and the highest course of stones, located directly opposite the entrance, gradually decreases in height as it approaches the entrance itself. Externally, as one circles the structure, only the highest row of stones is visible; the rest is completely buried in sand deliberately piled there to form a conical mound.
descriptions.NUR10068: It is not certain what it exactly is, perhaps a unique site that encompasses the giants' tomb, the trilithic dolmen, and the Nuragic fortress. Undoubtedly, it was a very important place for the defense of the territory and the clan. It is a sacred place in every sense, and it is no exaggeration to think of the rock where the rite of the Accabadora was performed. mu.
descriptions.NUR1328: It is an excellent example of a fortress with a wall composed of large polygonal stones arranged in a roughly circular, broken-line pattern from north to west, extending to south. To the east it takes advantage of a steep and almost vertical cliff that overlooks the Ozieri plain. To the north there is a large, flat-topped dolmenic trilite. The entrance to the south is smaller. mu
descriptions.NUR5520: Dr. Aste maintains that Su Doladorgiu, in its original form, was a fortress, the reconstruction of which he has proposed, equipped with towers and a nuraghe. For strategic defensive reasons, it was built in the Nuragic period to oversee the entire valley; from the sea, incursions by enemies and invaders were feared.
descriptions.NUR5489:
The complex consists of an extensive settlement defended by a wall (length 120 m; maximum height 5.00 m): the north-eastern end is better preserved, where a tower is incorporated. In the central sector, probably protecting the entrance to the acropolis.

Halfway up the slope are the remains of a second fortification, built of large squared blocks. The village extends over the summit of the plateau and has numerous huts; the complex is datable to 1400–1000 BC.
descriptions.NUR2191:
The fortress was built by adapting an existing Nuragic structure. From the Cartaginian period, traces of buildings—probably pre-Nuragic and later occupied by the Cartaginians—can be seen behind the wall.

The fortress dates to the mid-4th century BCE.
descriptions.NUR8733:
The temple consists of a small vestibule, a narrow descending staircase covered by a stepped lintel roof, and a circular chamber covered by a tholos.

The standing structures are now limited to the keyhole-shaped perimeter wall enclosing the atrium and the well drum. The vestibule, partly paved, has a rectangular plan: the bench-seat is absent. The staircase leading down to the well chamber, with vertical walls, is made up of 12 steps.
descriptions.NUR10071: The area has been furnished for rest and meals, with ample parking, thanks to the local poet Bainzeddu Truddaiu, who recently passed away. Together with family members and other friends, he dedicated himself to organizing this space, where anyone can stop and refuel.
descriptions.NUR9872: It is a bilobate structure of which only a portion remains, although several collapses have affected most of the structure. The trilithic and flat-laid junction is clearly visible and very interesting. mu
descriptions.NUR9873: At the level of ruin, with disconnected circles of large stones fallen in great disorder. Only a very reduced portion remains, indicating the presence of the site. mu
descriptions.NUR6760: The investigations have identified traces of human presence at the site dating from the period between the Late Neolithic (3300–2700 BC) and the Chalcolithic (2700–1700 BC). The most monumental evidence consists of the menhirs present at the site: single, in pairs, in triads, in spectacular alignments formed by as many as 20 menhirs, and in circles. Walking through the site one can see menhirs lying on the ground everywhere, whole or in fragments. The site must originally have been larger than it appears today.
descriptions.NUR6768: The investigations have identified traces of human presence at the site dating from the period between the Late Neolithic (3300–2700 BC) and the Chalcolithic (2700–1700 BC). The most monumental evidence consists of the menhirs present at the site: single, in pairs, in triads, in spectacular alignments formed by as many as 20 menhirs, and in circles. Walking through the site one can see menhirs lying on the ground everywhere, whole or in fragments. The site must originally have been larger than it appears today.

descriptions.NUR19419: Sa Ohe (the mouth), is connected by submerged passages to the nearby grotto of Su Ventu. Incorrectly known as Sa Oche, a misinterpretation of the name meaning "the voice", it has been known and frequented since prehistoric times.
descriptions.NUR19673: A small karst cavity damaged by illegal excavators. Following excavations carried out during the last years of the 1800s, the site yielded a series of metal artefacts, including a bronze boat, two swords and an iron dagger, an iron horse bit, four cups and a bronze cup, a bronze vessel and a ceramic olla containing twenty-two copper fragments. A boat depicting a bovine head found during the 1960s.
descriptions.NUR14424: The cave is about 130 metres long and is mainly composed of three "rooms". Important archaeological finds have been made inside, especially some human remains dated to about 20,000 years ago, which represent the earliest evidence of Homo sapiens in Sardinia. This cave was the refuge of the famous Sardinian bandit Giovanni Corbeddu, after whom it is named.
descriptions.NUR8173: Complex cave with three entrances (two of which are artificial), heavily altered and plundered of its beauty as it was previously used partially as an onyx quarry and as a wartime shelter. It was frequently used during the Early Bronze Age. A small park has been set up at the entrance, managed by an association that periodically organizes guided visits.
descriptions.NUR8188: Natural cave characterized by a large chamber used as a sacred area where various votive offerings (small lamps and miniature cauldrons) were found on a natural stone altar shaped like a countertop. Occupation spans from the Neolithic to the Iron Age and includes the San Ciriaco, Bonannaro, and Nuragic cultures.
descriptions.NUR16542: Linked to the Grotta di sa Ucca de su Tintirriolu. It opens into a tiny niche between stones, then into earth (difficult to identify), followed by a deep and dangerous well of 28 m. Exploration is NOT RECOMMENDED! even for expert speleologists, as the well does not open onto rock.
descriptions.NUR19609: At the base of the nuraghe, beneath a rocky outcrop, there is a cave used as a water reservoir. The entrance to the cave has been narrowed by the construction of masonry structures made by stacking trachyte stones of various shapes and sizes, thus increasing the water-holding capacity of the reservoir. The interior is full of stones and mud.
descriptions.NUR19948: Important natural cavity, known as Grotta de su Mrajani, which has yielded evidence (ceramics) of Neolithic Early humans, predating even the cultures of Bonu Ighinu or San Michele di Ozieri.
descriptions.NUR8244: Natural cave used as a storehouse for large containers for foodstuffs dating to the Middle Bronze Age, with items found on site completely intact.
descriptions.NUR12924: Cave used during the early phases of the Nuragic civilization, known for the discovery of three, older, "Mother Goddess" bone statuettes.
descriptions.NUR8186: Natural cave with a wide entrance leading into a small chamber, followed by a step that leads to an inner chamber. Inside, material dating back to the Neolithic (in particular, Bonannaro) has been found, suggesting that the cave was inhabited.
descriptions.NUR8187: Natural cave with a wide entrance followed by a step and an underlying chamber. Inside, Neolithic and Bronze Age material, belonging to the Bonannaro culture, has been found.
descriptions.NUR19801: The Nuragic structures that closed the two entrances to the Domusnovas cave were already described in 1840 by Angius. He says that at the first entrance, on the left, there are the remains of a cyclopean wall that closed it off. A small doorway by the cave wall is as high as the ordinary stature of a man; to the left of the doorway a staircase 1.30 m wide led up onto the rampart where there were merlons and loopholes. At the exit there is another wall 3.20 m thick.
descriptions.NUR16544: It is the largest and most important cave of Bonu Ighinu. It has recently been connected to the cave above, the Grotta del Pozzaccio. Morphologically the cavity can be divided into two main parts: the fossil branch, which is the initial one, and the active branch, traversed in its entire length by a stream; the fossil branch also includes the large hall in the innermost part. The total length of the cave is 740 m, with a spatial extension of 1500 m.
descriptions.NUR8182: Large cave composed of a single chamber used from the early Middle Bronze Age, where materials belonging to the Bonannaro culture have been found.
descriptions.NUR19675:
A large cave, extending about 40 metres, shows an archaeological layer disturbed by guano diggers and illegal excavators.

From the disturbed layers come ceramic materials dating from the second half of the 5th millennium B.C. to the republican period.
descriptions.NUR10914:
The accessible area consists of numerous rooms adorned with concretions, stalactites, and stalagmites (the highest measuring 11 metres), columns rising up to 15 m, crystals of aragonite, and underground lakes.

Inside, remains of some oil lamps used in votive offerings, of Nuragic origin, as well as Phoenician and Roman artifacts, have been found.
descriptions.NUR19677: The cave contains internal wall remnants and artefacts; it is not ruled out that it was used as a smelting site.
descriptions.NUR8287: Natural cave composed of a single chamber within which prehistoric fragments are visible. The cave has been severely damaged by illegal excavation activities.
descriptions.NUR8285: Natural cave used in prehistoric times as a site for mass burial. It is characterized by a shaft entrance and by some artificial steps. Outside, a fragmentary wall remains visible, severely damaged by quarrying activities. The area is enclosed, and visits are strongly discouraged due to danger.
descriptions.NUR19938: In 1968, about 150 metres from the entrance, the Treasure Chamber was discovered: hundreds of bowls were stacked in three large mounds. A broken stalagmite column used as an altar: here were placed a bronze tripod, a votive vessel, several daggers, bracelets, and rings. Adjacent to the altar was a hearth, where animal bones and signs of ritual sacrifices were found. The C14 dating ranges from 820 to 730 B.C.
descriptions.NUR8032: Series of natural caves used in the Neolithic for collective burials. Remains of the Monte Claro culture.
descriptions.NUR6944: It is an artificial cave cut into tufa and modified over the centuries, very likely by a domus used as a winemaking building or as a storage for agricultural products or as a tool shed. There are many indications pointing to such a use. mu
descriptions.NUR19571: Of particular importance is the cave known as "Su Stampu VI", where pre-Nuragic and Nuragic artifacts have been found.
descriptions.NUR21138: Artificial grotto with access, pseudo-quadrilateral and large.
descriptions.NUR12896: Natural with modifications, it dates to the Bonnanaro culture period (2200–1800 BC). Used as a burial site.
descriptions.NUR12143: A scattered group of menhirs on the ground.
descriptions.NUR19476:
These natural caves are among the largest and most beautiful in Sardinia: their rectangular entrance is immersed in a lush forest of holm oaks.  

The caves, easily accessible, according to ancient legend, were the dwelling place of three janas (fairy beings) who were petrified by God for having killed a friar.  

The cave walls are covered with marble-like flows and drapery. From the ceiling it seems as if a storm of white stalactites descends upon the visitor.
descriptions.NUR14665:
Uncertain location, to be defined. Single petroglyph

Overlapping the upper part of the residential centre of Baunei, it echoes the name of the domus de janas. It is a depiction composed of a total of 18 shallow channels branching out from a main depression a few centimetres deep, which then connect to various terminal cups arranged without apparent pattern.
descriptions.NUR639: From the information I have, it should be a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe of which only a few traces remain.
descriptions.NUR16209: It consists of the remains of a nuraghe of difficult typological classification; collapses and the dense undergrowth that has grown on the emergences prevent a proper survey. Nevertheless, the data collected following repeated inspections carried out at the site—among which the location of the entrance facing north-northeast was identified—lead me to hypothesise that it may belong to the class of corridor nuraghes, with an associated settlement.
descriptions.NUR11746:
The Nuragic village-sacred site of Abini is one of the most famous and important in Sardinian nuragic archaeology.

It consists of numerous huts and a sacred well protected by a enclosure. The huts are mostly circular in plan.
descriptions.NUR18619: The interpretation of these buildings suggests that during festivals the Nuragic (and not only) would trade various goods, taking advantage of the large influx of people. In addition to the "stalls" there are two circular huts used for gatherings and a sheepfold enclosure.
descriptions.NUR12965: Nuragic settlement or sacred site, reused up to the Roman period. Basements of different structures from various historical periods are present.
descriptions.NUR11727: The area, located on the north-western slope of the comune of Giave, includes the remains of a nuraghe, possibly a giants' tomb, and an attached settlement.
descriptions.NUR18908: About 200 m from the rise in terrain indicating the presence of the nuraghe, in a north-north-east direction, an settlement is visible covering an area of 6–700 m² and revealing a series of quadrilateral rooms delimited by large trachyte stones.
descriptions.NUR5611: About 200 m from the rise in terrain indicating the presence of the nuraghe, in a north-north-east direction, an settlement is visible covering an area of 6–700 m² and revealing a series of quadrilateral rooms delimited by large trachyte stones.
descriptions.NUR17821:
Remains of a structured building composed of several rooms (with a vaguely rectangular plan), enclosed by walls constructed with medium-sized stones and clay mortar. In particular, seven steps of a staircase remain, connecting levels set at different heights.

Among surface finds, fragments of Phoenician pottery and early iron-age Nuragic ceramic vessels have been identified.
descriptions.NUR18886:
To the north-west of the Muntone nuraghe, reachable via a path, there is first an settlement and then the megalithic tomb of Tanca Noa.

The settlement, which appears to cover about 400 m², consists of remains of structures with an indistinct plan; the masonry structures, of which only the base course remains, are built using the double-casing technique, in trachyte and dry-stone.
descriptions.NUR18880: About 100 metres west of the nuraghe, a small settlement has been identified, composed of the remains of at least five circular huts and one rectangular structure. South of the nuraghe, about 500 metres away, the base courses of two circular huts are visible, along with short curved wall segments in trachyte; at a distance of about 400 metres, south-west of the nuraghe, the remains of a circular hut are found.
descriptions.NUR10627: Located at about 176 m a.s.l., marked on the topographic map as Nuraghe. This dry-stone complex consists of walls varying in height between 40 and 110 cm. The layout of these wall sections shows a circular form in some areas and a squared form in others.
descriptions.NUR19200: A dozen circular huts and enclosures.
descriptions.NUR16328: Name inspired by which the director Mauro Aragoni drew for his short film "Nuraghes S'Arena"
descriptions.NUR12532:
It is located within the municipal territory of Monastir (CA).

The archaeological area was discovered during excavation works for the 131.
descriptions.NUR11375: It is the "father of all the nuraghes", the proto-nuraghe Madugui (local name) or Maduli (archaeological designation), which projects prominently on the south-eastern edge of the upland. Today its walls are four metres and a half high, though they were once taller. It is one of the most significant examples of proto-nuraghe architecture (or pseudo-nuraghe) – a prototype of the "corridor nuraghes", later evolving into towers or clusters of towers closed in a false dome (tholos).
descriptions.NUR4886: It is the "father of all the nuraghes", the proto-nuraghe Madugui (local name) or Maduli (archaeological designation), which projects prominently on the south-eastern edge of the upland. Today its walls are four metres and a half high, though they were once taller. It is one of the most significant examples of proto-nuraghe architecture (or pseudo-nuraghe) – a prototype of the "corridor nuraghes", later evolving into towers or clusters of towers closed in a false dome (tholos).
descriptions.NUR11027: The archaeological site of Bruncu Suergiu lies in the Giara Park. Hidden by vegetation and hard to reach. Traces of ancient routes, a large settlement with production facilities, and defensive structures characterise the site. Besides the huge quantity of material, a broad terrace looks out over the Campidano, offering a breathtaking view. Only the panorama repays the long and difficult walk. The archaeological area, which is protected, covers about 11 hectares.
descriptions.NUR10882: The settlement consisted of a complex nuraghe surrounded by the village, whose remains are clearly visible amid a dense thicket of mastic and olive trees. The most important part of the ancient settlement developed around a circular depression in the ground that, during winter and spring months, functioned as a small rainwater collection basin.
descriptions.NUR5060: The settlement consisted of a complex nuraghe surrounded by the village, whose remains are clearly visible amid a dense thicket of mastic and olive trees. The most important part of the ancient settlement developed around a circular depression in the ground that, during winter and spring months, functioned as a small rainwater collection basin.
descriptions.NUR12234: The site includes the nuraghe and the remains of an extensive village. It also features two burials: a giants' tomb and a burial known as "the lilies" because there appear to be many of them.
descriptions.NUR18091: Originally it was intended to form, together with that of the nearby N.ghe Ena Ortu, a single extensive settlement.
descriptions.NUR8168: Settlement of which only faint traces remain, located on the hill in front of Monte Cannas in a place not recommended for visits because it was affected in the 1930s–1940s by quarrying activities, with dangerous, unenclosed areas. The settlement dates from the Bronze Age to the Roman period, passing through the Nuragic culture.
descriptions.NUR11621: Remains of a Nuragic village composed of about fifty huts. Communication took place through underground tunnels, many of which remain unexplored to this day. The presence of the "meeting hut" — conspicuously restored — was noted.
descriptions.NUR11620: It includes some tafons, which are thought to have been used both in funerary and domestic contexts.
descriptions.NUR2404: complex nuraghe with a village nearby
descriptions.NUR12443:
It is located within the municipal territory of Orosei (NU).

In the area there should also be a rudimentary sacred well.
descriptions.NUR17387:
It is a village of considerable size; on the ground, dozens of circular structures are visible, especially to the south-west of the named nuraghe.

Given the presence of four other nuraghes within a few kilometres and an exceptional view over the Gulf of Asinara (on clear days, the ships far out at Porto Torres can be clearly seen), it is likely that the village must have played a strategic role.
descriptions.NUR10778: At the site of Sa Brèca two buildings are currently clearly discernible: the Temple with Well and a sub-circular hut with seating along the walls. The entire complex appears to be enclosed by a temenos that would have separated the Sacred Area from the adjacent inhabited zone (not yet subjected to excavation).
descriptions.NUR18726:
The site includes a corridor nuraghe, a circular tower nuraghe with a tholos, two giants' tombs, a sacred well, a Roman necropolis and the ruins of a country church.

The country church preserves only a wall of two square metres. The circular nuraghe and everything else listed above are practically invisible. The corridor nuraghe is entirely covered by dense vegetation, so only a few stones can be seen. Unfortunately, as of April 2013, a visit is not recommended.
descriptions.NUR11047: The building consists of a central tower and a quadrilobate bastion with an internal courtyard. The external face of the main tower, of which only one course attributable to the first-floor chamber is visible, is constructed in isodomic masonry with sandstone blocks. Inside, at S, the projection of the staircase landing is identifiable.
descriptions.NUR10441: The village that developed in the subsequent phase of recent Bronze (1365–1200 BC) is characterized by the presence of numerous dug wells located near residential structures, some of which are set into the ground, while others are built with a masonry base. Currently, after recent excavations, the area has been fully covered.
descriptions.NUR12405:
In the Sas Seddas area, not far from the eponymous megalithic tombs site, some ceramic finds of certain Nuragic attribution have been recovered.

No structural traces are visible at the site. The owner of the pinnetta reports that during excavation work an unspecified “channel” cut into the rock came to light, of unknown length and depth; it has since been reburied. The ceramic material consists mainly of cooking-pot fragments.
descriptions.NUR19551: Remains of the Nuragic village Siseri Alto embedded in the vegetation
descriptions.NUR12412: Within an olive grove, following land clearing, numerous ceramic materials from different periods have come to light; among the prehistoric fragments, there are no doubt typical Nuragic vessels such as storage jars and ovens. No clear structures remain, as the site has undergone constant agricultural transformations.
descriptions.NUR12217:
It is located within the municipal territory of Nuxis (CI).

It was connected to the adjacent Nuragic well, as evidenced in other archaeological sites (Santa Vittoria di Serri, Sant'Anastasia a Sardara, Su Putzu ad Orroli, etc.).
descriptions.NUR11923: It is a Nuragic village located on Monte Tiscali inside a cave, destroyed by Romans and tomb-bearers; the foundations of the huts are visible, with only one hut retaining part of its wall. Access is very difficult, requiring about 45 minutes of walking, as one must climb a narrow track with steep gradient and gravel, and pass through a rock fissure if going from Oliena; in return, one enjoys a panoramic view of the calcareous mountains of the Supramonte.
descriptions.NUR1274: The settlement, which originally was intended to extend to integrate with that of the N.ghe Maiore, consists of numerous architectural remains whose fragments are still awaiting investigation by experts. As also observed in the nearby Maiore, there are remains of rectangular dwellings.
descriptions.NUR11176: Remains of a possible Nuragic settlement currently located at the centre of a road ramp.
descriptions.NUR18102: Settlement belonging to a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe with an outer wall
descriptions.NUR10696:
On the illustrative map of Tharros and at the archaeological site it is marked with number 15.

The tophet was established by the Phoenicians and then the Carthaginians, who had already found the Nuragic structures present.
descriptions.NUR3374: The site consists essentially of two parts: the first, formed by the well temple, a sacred well dating to the Nuragic period, with structures attached to it: a meeting hut, an enclosure, and other smaller huts. The second part of the complex, about two hundred metres to the south-west, consists of a single-tower nuraghe, some elongated stone huts of uncertain date, and a Nuragic village, still to be excavated, of which only a few emerging elements are visible.
descriptions.NUR10718: Remains of some Nuragic huts with curved plans, adjacent to one another, rise within an old courtyard built with dry-stone masonry.
descriptions.NUR12866:
The site is characterized by the presence of a Nuragic-period settlement, documented by the discovery during private construction work of wall structures assignable to the Iron Age.  

It is a section of a structure built of isodomic ashlar made of tuffy marl, dating to the Iron Age, whose exact function has not yet been clarified.
descriptions.NUR14835: It was the earliest settlement in the Villanovaforru area. A short distance from a spring, unfortunately no traces of it remain. A Bonnanaro Culture tomb was found, dated to the Early Bronze Age between 1700 and 1600 BC, together with fragments of a tripod vase and obsidian arrowheads; no osteological remains or tomb structures were recovered. The isolated find is to be interpreted as an open-air site or a funerary deposition.
descriptions.NUR11365: Pre-Nuragic/Nuragic settlement. Remains of two huts were still present up to twenty years ago, but one of the two was dismantled to make room for ploughs.
descriptions.NUR12458: Given all this, in the locality of Serra Neba, an area adjacent to the village of Puisteris had to be established, probably used for livestock rearing and possibly also for agriculture. The archaeological material recovered, unambiguously attributable to the Ozieri culture, confirms the presence of human activity in the area during the late Neolithic period.
descriptions.NUR11173: The discovery of the Monte Idda hoard (Decimoputzu), which took place towards the end of 1914, was described by Taramelli as “perfectly accidental”, and on this subject the famous archaeologist wrote that “two shepherds from Desulo, who were grazing their herds on the mountain known as Sa Idda, found under some loose granite boulders, inside the remains of a terracotta vessel, a mass of bronze weapons and tools, together with ingots and ingot fragments, slag and scrap pieces of the same metal…”.
descriptions.NUR12887: The Tomba di Bau su Matutzu (3rd millennium BC) is located within an olive grove inside the Ecoserdiana dump.
descriptions.NUR12835: In this underground chamber dating to the Middle Neolithic (4600–4000 B.C.) several interesting artefacts were found, including a tetrapod plate made of limestone with a bull's-head protome. This is described as one of the earliest depictions of a bucranium in Sardinia. A bucranium refers to a figure of an animal's head with horns pointing upwards. It is on display at the Archaeological Museum of Cagliari.
descriptions.NUR19516: Subterranean temple in the Pitzu 'e toni area. It has a southern exposure. Along the entrance, a two-metre-long path splits into two branches: the right branch is narrow, while the left is wider. The same name recalls its function. In the early 1960s, during an inspection, Professor Lilliu found a pendant made of smooth animal bones.
descriptions.NUR21155: Externally, two windows are visible, located 1.60 m above the floor level, each measuring about 35 cm in width. The access opening, measuring 1.60 m in height and 1.30 m in width, features a 35 cm descending step to enter the chamber. The room is 4 m wide, 3 m deep, and about 2.5 m high; at its centre there is a circular ditch, 60 cm deep and 10 cm wide, slightly offset to the right of the entrance.
descriptions.NUR10294: Perhaps a Neolithic burial site; Roman and medieval tombs have been identified there over time. Witnesses report that in the 1940s and 1950s, while ploughing with a wooden plough, numerous human bones and fragments of tegulae and imbrices came to light. This was even more evident when the same person (my father Giovanni, almost a centenarian, now deceased) ploughed with an iron Birindelli plough, which turned the soil at a greater depth.
descriptions.NUR12881: Monte Claro culture underground chamber discovered during works at "nuova 554". It consists of two underground chambers with vertical access shafts and various funerary furnishings.
descriptions.NUR19566: The basaltic pillars are majestic basalt formations whose presence indicates a history of submarine eruptions or the existence of ancient volcanoes now extinct. Is Aruttas Santas are a typical example of these basaltic formations, located on Monte Arci in the territory of Villaurbana.
descriptions.NUR10341: When the Rio Murrone meets the Rio Oloitti, further down by several hundred metres, it drops by about twenty metres, forming a roaring, foaming waterfall in a wild and captivating setting of untouched, primordial nature. The river has a winter torrential character and completely ceases during the driest summer months.
descriptions.NUR19831: To the north-west of the nuraghe there is a small pond containing spring water, which is present even in summer, though in small quantities. The pond has an irregular triangular shape entirely natural. The deepest point reaches the overflow level at about 120 cm.
descriptions.NUR19740: In the Is Noccus area there are two ponds, the first at the foot of the nuraghe and the other about 200 m away. The first, at the south-west base of the nuraghe, was created by using a natural lake basin. The pond is circular and shows clear signs of human intervention aimed at catching rainwater and increasing its storage capacity; boulders of various sizes can be seen placed around the edges of the basin for most of its perimeter.
descriptions.NUR16247: Near the nuraghe, scattered over an extensive area (about 12 hectares), the remains of numerous structures with circular plans (generally over 7 m in diameter) and rectilinear plans can be seen, attributable to the ancient settlement and probably also belonging to a sacred area. The wall profiles are double-faced, built with large and medium-sized blocks of basalt or trachyte. To the south-east, at a distance of about 90 metres from the nuraghe, a plateau stands out
descriptions.NUR8473: It is a anthropomorphic rock whose appearance is likened to the face of the Egyptian sphinx.
descriptions.NUR19885: The Tomb of the Three Hundred is the most significant structure and part of a larger necropolis discovered during the construction works of SS131. It is named after the number of skeletons found within the walls surrounding the burial area.
descriptions.NUR13409: Tomb II, particularly imposing, features the entrance, the antechamber, and the burial chamber carved out in two distinct rocky blocks transported on-site and placed upon a carefully prepared mound; in the final stone work, achieved with a hammer, and in the architectural and plan layout, it closely resembles the domus de janas burials.
descriptions.NUR14994: The tomb is considerably disturbed in parts, also due to illegal excavations; it preserves (a rare case for the area) a (likely) large fragment of the central stele of the exedra.
descriptions.NUR10191: In the territory of sa Loca, at the border with that of sa Punta de Bonanotte, the farming family, in addition to cultivating some crops, fruit trees, and olive groves, also maintained a vineyard that required a place for harvesting. On the hard limestone, the vascone (in Sardinian: su lacu) was produced for pressing, and the scolo (in Sardinian: s'ischintorzu) for collecting the juice in a smaller vat.
descriptions.NUR10196: It is an isolated wooded hillock shaped like a cone on a plain, upon which various stones of different shapes are placed, ranging from conical prism to parallelepiped forms. The setting is striking and it is said that events and occurrences take place within sacred or initiation-propitiatory ceremonies. mu
descriptions.NUR19862: Stone forming part of a group of five stone blocks. It is characterized by a flat anterior surface and a convex posterior surface.
descriptions.NUR21120: A powerful curtain wall (16.25 x 10.35 m; 168 m²) with a double wall face (4–2.2 m thick) defines an open internal space, accessed through a covered corridor paved with slabs. The staircase leading to the top of the wall is a particularly notable feature, showing strong similarity to Monte Baranta.
descriptions.NUR2125: This structure is marked as a nuragic well and is located near a livestock water trough.
descriptions.NUR20291: Originally the menhir complex consisted of 12 menhirs arranged in a circle. Today only one remains, about two metres high. The others have disappeared, possibly removed for construction work.
descriptions.NUR6850: It is located near the homonymous nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR6820:
At 150 m from the second group of domus, at the foot of Monte Corru Tundu, there is a colossal monolith of trachytic tuff with its top truncated (remaining height 5.75 m). This menhir, one of the largest in Sardinia, is strongly curved, with one face planed and the other rounded; on the latter, three circular depressions appear to be discernible.

Monolith and cemeteries were functional to the settlement of Monte Padrillonis (San Michele culture, 3200–2800 BC).
descriptions.NUR6809: Site of Cuili Piras behind M. Su Crobu. The surrounding area is ploughed and access to the site is quite difficult. Unfortunately, the land was recently devastated by a widespread fire. The site is located within a private property and it is advisable to inform the landowners of one's presence.
descriptions.NUR6798: The Boeli stele, also known as Sa Perda Pintà, is a large menhir statue of granite (height 2.67 m); it consists of motifs formed by a minimum of two to a maximum of seven concentric circles, obtained through incisions that radiate around a central cup.
descriptions.NUR6766: A short distance from the underground tomb of Putzu, beyond the agricultural road passing through the area of Busola, two menhirs have been identified. One of the menhirs still stands firmly in the ground in its original position. A second menhir, with a sharp lateral profile and an elliptical cross-section on the major side, is embedded within the post of the entrance to the field.
descriptions.NUR20295: The megalithic settlement, now completely destroyed, was located near Casa Manis. Only a menhir remains in the area later occupied by a Roman settlement.
descriptions.NUR6787: More similar to a stele than a menhir, having a parabolic arch shape. A dolmen is present in the vicinity.
descriptions.NUR6844: Isolated menhir, on its back bearing an alignment of cups.
descriptions.NUR6813: In this area, for many years used for cultivation, eight monoliths were discovered during ploughing works; five of them are still present on the ground today; these menhirs, all made from a single local trachyte block, have an average height of 180 cm and feature a flat face and a convex opposite face.
descriptions.NUR12081: It is a sacred area, composed of seven menhirs, six of which are stacked nearby, about ninety metres to the west, and registered during land grading works. While this one is simply laid on the ground, the only one in the area, finely carved, measuring 6.20 m in length.
descriptions.NUR6826: The alignment of closely spaced stones at Serra Pillonadori lies on the south-western slopes of the Su Niu de is Crobus hill and west of Baccu Ungroneddus, in a position from which the valley of S. Barbara and the Rio Solanas can be seen in a single glance. The five granitic stones composing it are arranged along a north-south axis and face east.
descriptions.NUR6781: The three granite menhirs stand on the slope of the saddle: the first, aniconic (length 4.25 m; width 0.98 m; thickness 0.60 m) — pointed and split into two pieces — lies on the ground; the second — re-erected in the 1970s — is of proto-anthropomorphic type with an ogival shape and a plano-convex cross-section; the third, also proto-anthropomorphic, has an ogival shape and a flattened plano-convex cross-section. Two menhirs face each other frontally, almost as if marking a passage.
descriptions.NUR6823: Pre-Nuragic menhir about 5 metres high, still standing upright. This menhir has been named after a giantess, a figure frequently appearing in Sardinian folk legends. The presence of many other menhirs in the area attests to the widespread nature of megalithic religious practices.
descriptions.NUR6840: Located within an area designated for sheep grazing, near the course of the river of the same name.
descriptions.NUR6812: The Pranu Muttedu park represents one of the most striking archaeological sites in internal Sardinia. The park area is divided into two parts, covering a total extent of about 200,000 m². Excavations have revealed numerous artefacts belonging to settled communities of "Ozieri" culture dating to the recent Neolithic (3200–2800 BC). The archaeological complex features the highest known concentration of menhirs in Sardinia.
descriptions.NUR19753: About 250 m from the Nuraghe Noccus, on a rocky outcrop, there are: a very unusual tafone, now partly collapsed; three large monoliths (about 250 cm high), set a short distance apart, which could be menhirs; numerous boulders of various unusual shapes, in some cases next to the monoliths, in others scattered without a clear order but close to them. In the opinion of a (female) archaeologist, the menhirs do indeed seem to mark out the funerary space.
descriptions.NUR6845: The menhir, located within a flat field, is about 1.67 m high, with cup-shaped decorations.
descriptions.NUR6803: A very unusual menhir, pierced at multiple points, possibly artificially.
descriptions.NUR20404: It is located about 500 m east of the Is Perdas Croccadas menhir. In recent times it has been reconstructed and restored from three large fragments.
descriptions.NUR6774: The two menhirs are located about fifty metres apart.
descriptions.NUR6839: The menhir, known as Su Furconi de Luxia Arrabiosa, stands alone on a short rise. The menhir is quadrangular, thinned at the top in a nearly conical shape, and measures 3.60 m in height. On the main face, facing east, 12 small cups are carved.
descriptions.NUR6769: Located near the homonymous nuraghe, some giants' tombs are observed, concealed by dense vegetation that also partially hides the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR6796: At this site, within a short stretch of about two hundred metres, monuments dating to the Abealzu culture, 2700–2400 BC, the early Bronze Age with nuraghic walls, and the Bronze Age up to the Roman period, marked by probable tombs, are present.
descriptions.NUR3214: At this site, within a short stretch of about two hundred metres, monuments dating to the Abealzu culture, 2700–2400 BC, the early Bronze Age with nuraghic walls, and the Bronze Age up to the Roman period, marked by probable tombs, are present.
descriptions.NUR6811: Three or more granite menhirs placed near the homonymous nuraghe
descriptions.NUR6791:
There were two, but now only one is fully visible, while the other lies upside down on the ground and broken into several fragments. They are located within the territory of the comune of Sassari.

Remains of a dolmen should be found nearby.
descriptions.NUR6836:
THE PISCINA'E SALI SITE. To reach the archaeological area, one follows an agricultural penetration track starting from the Cemetery Road, continuing straight to the junction in the area of Gedilis, and then passing the Pranu Corongiu plateau to the adjacent side road.

The area undoubtedly played a significant role in past religious practices; in fact, ten menhirs have been found in the valley and associated with the funerary contexts of Pranu Corongiu.
descriptions.NUR6802: The menhir placed beside the ramp leading to the upper part of the altar was raised prior to the construction of the altar itself. It was the centre of a Neolithic village.
descriptions.NUR6810:
It is located near the campsite of the same name.

It consists of 25 menhirs, 22 of which are standing (but only five in their original position, as the others have been erected by the archaeological site's construction team).
descriptions.NUR6818: These two menhirs can be attributed to the Ozieri Culture (4th millennium BC) and, in the eyes of archaeologists, represent the Mother Goddess and the Bull God, symbols characteristic of other prehistoric Sardinian monuments such as the domus de janas, within which they were depicted, and also recurrent in Nuragic civilization, especially in the bull-shaped forms of the giants' tombs. Over time, they have maintained their original positions and their function as votive monuments.
descriptions.NUR6777: The monolith, finely worked basalt, stands on a flat terrain less than 100 m from a domus de janas known as "Su forru'e su Taleri".
descriptions.NUR6814:
Probable location.

It consists of 4 menhirs.
descriptions.NUR19738: Menhir located about 40 m from the Nuraghe de Chirigu. The menhir has three faces: the two opposite ones are approximately semicircular and have a flat surface, while the third, the rear one, is convex. Natural cuts and grooves are visible, along with smooth areas that appear to be artificially shaped.
descriptions.NUR6776: Small menhir placed along the road facing the junction to Rocca Doria
descriptions.NUR19812: The Menhir Sa Perda de s'Omini, situated on a promontory at an elevation of about 230 m a.s.l., is a monolith whose shape is likely the result of atmospheric agents. It bears the appearance of a human face. Some believe it served a functional role in the ancient cult of the Mother Goddess, and this is also supported by the presence of remains of poorly defined structures adjacent to one of the two monoliths. Anciently, and still today, it is considered the centre of the island.
descriptions.NUR6779: It consists of two menhirs repositioned in the area.
descriptions.NUR6828: Series of menhirs in the area of Brentoni
descriptions.NUR10127: A small alignment of menhirs emerges on the path leading to Mamucada, within the plot of sa Figu at the border with the Padedda land. Upon careful examination, they appear poorly worked and roughly shaped, somewhat reminiscent of a pyramidal prism with a polygonal base that has never been exactly duplicated. According to the elders, most of them come from the steep slope of Badde Saltara, which overlooks the plain of S.M. de Orria Pitzinna. mu
descriptions.NUR12951:
It is located in the territory of the comune of Tortolì (OG).

It consists of three menhirs laid on the ground, two broken into two parts and one small, resembling a baetyl.

They are undoubtedly the remains of a megalithic sanctuary.
descriptions.NUR6807:
The Perda Longa archaeological complex, situated in a hilly area a few kilometres from Tortolì, comprises fifteen menhirs, most of them fallen, two giants' tombs (these are not easy to locate) and three nuraghi on the surrounding hills.

Among the perdas fittas (the Sardinian name for menhirs), several blocks stand over 4 metres high. The archaeological site dates to the fourth millennium BC (pre-Nuragic), but continued to be frequented into the Roman period.
descriptions.NUR5469:
The Perda Longa archaeological complex, situated in a hilly area a few kilometres from Tortolì, comprises fifteen menhirs, most of them fallen, two giants' tombs (these are not easy to locate) and three nuraghi on the surrounding hills.

Among the perdas fittas (the Sardinian name for menhirs), several blocks stand over 4 metres high. The archaeological site dates to the fourth millennium BC (pre-Nuragic), but continued to be frequented into the Roman period.
descriptions.NUR5260:
The Perda Longa archaeological complex, situated in a hilly area a few kilometres from Tortolì, comprises fifteen menhirs, most of them fallen, two giants' tombs (these are not easy to locate) and three nuraghi on the surrounding hills.

Among the perdas fittas (the Sardinian name for menhirs), several blocks stand over 4 metres high. The archaeological site dates to the fourth millennium BC (pre-Nuragic), but continued to be frequented into the Roman period.
descriptions.NUR1321:
The Perda Longa archaeological complex, situated in a hilly area a few kilometres from Tortolì, comprises fifteen menhirs, most of them fallen, two giants' tombs (these are not easy to locate) and three nuraghi on the surrounding hills.

Among the perdas fittas (the Sardinian name for menhirs), several blocks stand over 4 metres high. The archaeological site dates to the fourth millennium BC (pre-Nuragic), but continued to be frequented into the Roman period.
descriptions.NUR6773: The concentration of menhirs in this area is considerable; they are in close continuity with those at Ovau, S'Aspiddarju, and Teularju. The menhir FIRULI in the vicinity and along a stretch of 6 metres and 60 cm.
descriptions.NUR11476:
Originally there were three, but only one remains standing.

Probable location.
descriptions.NUR6817: The Pranu Muttedu park represents one of the most striking archaeological sites in internal Sardinia. The park area is divided into two parts, covering a total extent of about 200,000 m². Excavations have revealed numerous artefacts belonging to settled communities of "Ozieri" culture dating to the recent Neolithic (3200–2800 BC). The archaeological complex features the highest known concentration of menhirs in Sardinia.
descriptions.NUR18506: It consists of several menhirs and fragments recovered during land reclamation.
descriptions.NUR12837: The Menhir Terra Coccoi is located on a hilltop at about 1 km north-east of Nuraxi Figus. It has a remaining height of about 2 metres.
descriptions.NUR11175: It is a monument likely of Nuragic origin, featuring the remains of a cistern, possibly originally vaulted in tholos form, and an adjacent rectangular elongated building constructed with sack masonry.
descriptions.NUR14866: Pre-Nuragic and Nuragic village, of which only very few traces remain, already disappeared by the end of the Bronze Age.
descriptions.NUR7347: It is probably the door closure of a domus de janas.
descriptions.NUR842: Unlikely remains of a nuragic structure.
descriptions.NUR2395: Probable dismantled nuraghe located to the north-east; nearby there is a megalithic wall.
descriptions.NUR3662: Particular site having two different classification types. The first census defined the structure as "Nuraghe Crastu Ruju", the second as "Megalithic rampart of Giusei" in the style of the most famous rampart of Monte Baranta.
descriptions.NUR17375: It is uncertain whether the site dates to the Nuragic period.
descriptions.NUR17231: Nuragic megalithic enclosure of probable defensive use, later repurposed in the Roman period, as evidenced by the presence of pottery fragments on the ground.
descriptions.NUR16396:
A particular structure is present, which appears to be nuragic and may have been used for surveillance.

Probable location.
descriptions.NUR14650: An object classifiable among the pre-Nuragic walls, of which there are various examples throughout the island.
descriptions.NUR20348: The entrance, tall and flat-topped, leads into an interior space that was intended to be a protected area, built at the edge of a cliff. On the left as one enters there is a circular chamber; on the right side of the corridor only the perimeter wall remains.
descriptions.NUR20092: It is located on the southern slope of Monte Lerno. The structure is in a state of severe decay. However, part of the wall is still clearly identifiable due to the presence of one of the entrances, which remains in good condition. At first glance, this might be mistaken for a dolmen because of its particular layout, featuring a large, flat stone resting on the wall. A little further downstream there is another structure, resembling a hut.
descriptions.NUR19956: The megalithic wall is of pre-Nuragic date. It has a covered entrance with a flat lintel on the southern side. It ends at the bend of the stream towards the west and, following an arcuate path, reaches the proto-nuraghe of the same name on the northern side.
descriptions.NUR5579: The Suttaterra rock-cut is located on the limestone summit of "Punta Su Nuraghe", where you can admire not only the natural arch but also a megalithic wall situated at a short distance, giving you a sense of the distance separating you from the Codula di Ilune and from other beauties of the area.
descriptions.NUR11178: The Cala Ostina nuraghe is a low curtain wall with a semicircular layout, having a radius of 7.70 m, protected on three sides by vertical walls; the wall reaches a maximum height of 2 m, built on two to three courses of large stones.
descriptions.NUR7206: Curtain wall of uncertain function, of clearly Nuragic craftsmanship. At the centre of the site there is a singular structure consisting of a kind of silo cut into the rock, with straight walls except at the end (at 2.65 m), where it narrows; the edge, partially worked and squared externally with notches, features some irregular cups.
descriptions.NUR17278: Nuragic wall (200 m long, with double wall face). It enclosed a Nuragic village.
descriptions.NUR10186: A short segment of slightly concave wall composed of stones not particularly large is certainly worth observation because the builders constructed it to meet a family-oriented need, either for residential use or for hunting. Within the context of Sa Mesana di sos Pianos and the adjacent Cudinatos of similar period, contemporaneous with or following the domus, it would assume a different identity. mu
descriptions.NUR10131: Apparently detached from the adjacent tomb, it must certainly have been built in relation to it, or vice versa. The site is also known as Culu de Muru. mu
descriptions.NUR10194: The area is heavily anthropogenically modified and rich in evidence. The presence of this wall, constructed with medium-sized polygonal stones and others only roughly shaped, does not follow a pre-determined direction, but appears entirely random. The surrounding territory is rich in surface features, from which its significance can be inferred. The freely interpreted layout represents an idealized partial view of the sites in that region. mu
descriptions.NUR10187: It consists of about ten metres of megalithic wall made up of large stones placed along the northern slope of Monte Zennaru, facing the Nuraghe Palusedda or Palusedda, at the centre of which the winter torrential stream Rio Murrone flows. The structure appears to have been designed, almost, to watch over that passage in the river. A careful examination reveals no traces of any other construction nearby. mu
descriptions.NUR18930: Tomb I features a elongated, apsidal tombstone, including a burial chamber and a large semicircular exedra facing it. For tomb II, situated to the south-east and overgrown by collapse and earth, only the profile of the apsidal tombstone and the exedra can be identified. Tomb III, possibly a dolmenic burial, is in very poor condition of preservation.
descriptions.NUR13945: Of the monument, legible in the various components that make it up, the large trapezoidal stele is particularly present. It stands in the locality of the same name in the municipality of Aidomaggiore.
descriptions.NUR10258: Composed of several single-cell units, some with antechambers and two or three small internal rooms. It is reasonably believed that other units remain undiscovered yet within the embrace of Mother Earth. Most of them are located along the mountain ridge and on the gentle slope of Sa Pala de s'Ozastru. On the plain, the remains of the homonymous nuraghe are present, with a clear connection between the two sites from different periods, and represent a plausible example of cultural and religious syncretism. mu
descriptions.NUR19991:
In the plain, there are two large rocky outcrops emerging for a length of about 200 metres, 30 m wide and 6 m high.

Site I I saw only from a distance, but the outcrops are clearly visible and confirmed by the landowner, who noted the presence of several domus de janas.

Site II has a dozen domus de janas, all facing perfectly west, mostly very small, except for two which have multiple chambers.

They are situated at various heights within the rock, ranging from 30 cm to 4 metres above ground level.
descriptions.NUR19993:
In the plain, there are two large rocky outcrops emerging for a length of about 200 metres, 30 m wide and 6 m high.

Site I I saw only from a distance, but the outcrops are clearly visible and confirmed by the landowner, who noted the presence of several domus de janas.

Site II has a dozen domus de janas, all facing perfectly west, mostly very small, except for two which have multiple chambers.

They are situated at various heights within the rock, ranging from 30 cm to 4 metres above ground level.
descriptions.NUR1060: It consists of at least three tombs.
descriptions.NUR8211: Cemeteries of domus de janas now integrated into the urban fabric of the city of Carbonia, where 25 tombs of different sizes and types have been identified. Following a major recovery in which the ancient Sardinian medau built in the 18th century was restored, the site is currently managed by the Mediterranean Cooperative, which allows free public access.
descriptions.NUR7762:
It is located within the municipal territory of Bosa (OR), inside an agriturismo.

The name might be incorrect.

It should include two hypogea, partly repurposed.
descriptions.NUR15768: The Preizza necropolis consists of three small domus de janas dug at the base of modest rocky outcrops.
descriptions.NUR16205: It is located within the municipal territory of Giave (SS) and includes 4 domus de janas.
descriptions.NUR11749: There are six domus de janas on site.
descriptions.NUR11750: The cemetery is located in the area of "sa Serra", in a hilly zone overlooking the Tirso river stretch near its confluence with the Taloro. The small cemetery consists of seven hypogea of the domus de janas type, dug into the trachyte that emerges in isolated outcrops or short rocky ridges.
descriptions.NUR19031: It is composed of at least four domus de janas, still under excavation.
descriptions.NUR6971: Complex consisting of 9 domus. Probable location.
descriptions.NUR12165: The find is located in the municipality of Orani and consists of five hypogea.
descriptions.NUR12358:
It is located within the territory of the comune of Buddusò (OT).

It includes at least 10 hypogea.
descriptions.NUR7138:
Domus de janas currently repurposed for other uses.

Should include 9 domus de janas.
descriptions.NUR19558: The necropolis is located about 4 km to the south-west of Alghero, on the northern side of the road leading to Olmedo. The site consists of domus de janas dug at the foot of the trachytic plateau dominated by the Sant'Elmo nuraghe, about 150 metres away.
descriptions.NUR16222: It includes at least eight domus de janas, of which only three are detectable in plan.
descriptions.NUR16220: It includes at least seven hypogea, most of which are damaged by collapses and significant reuse.
descriptions.NUR17309:
The domus of Silattari (Bosa – OR) are dug into the limestone slope, facing south towards the Modolo valley.

They consist of two hypogea with closely spaced entrances: one comprises 12 chambers and the other two cells. Probable location
descriptions.NUR7218: The cemetery of S'Isterridolzu occupies a flat area, crowned to the east by a steep rocky cliff. It includes 10 hypogea dug into low calcareous outcrops, one in an erratic boulder, and a final, unfinished one on a rocky spur: they are distributed across a large area (about 10,000 m²); the distance between each hypogean varies from 10 m to about 0.200 m.
descriptions.NUR17308:
For further details, see the publication "Archaeological Research in Marghine-Planargia" by Moravetti, pages 191–196.

Probable location.
descriptions.NUR15233: The domus of Taulera is located near Alghero's civil hospital. In 1941–42, some soldiers stationed there discovered a skull characterized by a double trepanation. It appears that the individual to whom the skull belonged survived the first trepanation for at least a year, dying probably during the second procedure.
descriptions.NUR16359: Three single-cell domus de janas with rectangular door.
descriptions.NUR7203: It is the premier archaeological site: beautiful, interesting, and easily accessible, thus highly usable by visitors. Unfortunately, the most recent recovery interventions did not achieve the desired results, as not always were the work crews and project directors adequately competent. The area intended to accommodate groups remains poorly equipped. The interiors (when not flooded) and the incisions/drawings on the walls are, however, particularly noteworthy.
descriptions.NUR19243: There are the most important domus de janas in the Pozzomaggiore area. The cemetery consists of at least 20 tombs cut into the rock, some of which are incomplete and not finished, while others are buried or heavily damaged.
descriptions.NUR12831: The cemetery consists of two groups, comprising 7 and 31 units, of hypogean domus de janas; only one is monocellular, while the others have more complex floor plans, and one of them contains up to eleven chambers. They are of the "vertical and horizontal projection" type, meaning accessible either through a vertical shaft or via a descending corridor, the latter usually equipped with steps leading into the vestibule.
descriptions.NUR12942: Subterranean tomb consisting of two rooms. Reweilded in a later period with the addition of a dolmenic corridor; it was reused in the early Bronze Age during the Bonnanaro phase. Looted by clandestine individuals.
descriptions.NUR7008: The cemetery is carved into a granitic outcrop of the Buddusò plateau. It consists of 6 hypogea and dates to 3200–2800 BC. Some domus have single-roomed spaces, while others have a multi-room layout. One of the domus shows traces of red painted murals in parallel bands applied to raised strips.
descriptions.NUR17772: The site includes 17 domus de janas, two of which are incomplete and one almost entirely buried. The numbered positions of the domus are taken from the book Itinerario Archeologico nel territorio Orgolese.
descriptions.NUR6929: The Prunittu necropolis is in the Sorrana area. The complex consists of two clusters about a hundred metres apart and contains 27 domus de janas in total. Most of the hypogea are easily reached, but some, cut into the vertical face of a trachyte bench with their entrances set well above ground level (up to four metres), can only be accessed by lowering oneself from the plateau above.
descriptions.NUR11132: The cemetery consists of four domus de janas, among which the "tomb of painted architecture" is particularly notable, characterized by relief and painted decorations. The underground chamber, with a plan shaped like a "T", is composed of a long "dromos" ending in a rectangular atrium, an antechamber, a central chamber, and two lateral chambers.
descriptions.NUR7332: At the entrance to the Bari Sardo settlement, in the hills of Su Pranu, lies the cemetery of Funtana su Rettore, composed of three domus de janas. The domus, of the double-cell type, date to the recent Neolithic period, 3500–2800 BC. The burials, well preserved, are arranged at nearly the same height along the rocky wall and retain traces of the tools used to dig them.
descriptions.NUR12164:
The domus de janas are located within the territory of the comune of Nuoro, at the border with Orani.

The cemetery consists of at least three tombs dug into granite, but a fourth tomb, hidden among the bushes in the immediate vicinity, cannot be ruled out.
descriptions.NUR7190:
It consists of three small tombs. It is located in the territory of Montresta.

Probable location.
descriptions.NUR13357: The cemetery, dated to the second half of the fourth millennium BC and attributable to the Arzachena culture, consists of five lithic cists, four of which are surrounded by circles of stones driven into the ground that, originally, marked the burial mound composed of earth and rubble erected over the burial.
descriptions.NUR6960: In the middle of the forest, dug into trachyte and decorated on the portal with probable bull's-head protomes.
descriptions.NUR11172:
The tomb has three rooms, rectangular in plan, cut into the rock and interconnected.

It dates to the time of the Bonnanaro culture (1500–1300 BC).
descriptions.NUR6993:
The complex currently comprises 15 domus de janas.

The underground chambers, located at a considerable elevation above the plain (ranging from a minimum of 0.60 m to a maximum of 4.00 m), were originally accessible via stone steps; today, collapses and fractures in the rock wall make access particularly difficult.
descriptions.NUR14186: The site includes the remains of a Carthaginian necropolis (about 120 tombs) built by the inhabitants of the Phoenician settlement located near the altitude of Santu Teru, which emerged at the end of the 6th century BCE.
descriptions.NUR12142: Subterranean complex consisting of six domus de janas.
descriptions.NUR12880: Monte Claro culture underground. The site was used during the Nuragic, Roman, and medieval periods.
descriptions.NUR12072: It is located in the municipality of Orani and consists of 8 domus de janas.
descriptions.NUR1329: There are numerous sarcophagi, each made from large trachyte and basalt blocks shaped into large rectangular prisms of considerable dimensions (2.50 x 0.90 x 0.90 m). Since the blocks are placed here and there without any defined or logical order, it is inferred that the site was a place where these sarcophagi were constructed.
descriptions.NUR8149: The nuraghe is composed of a seven-sided curtain wall, with a tower at each corner (partially visible), and a multi-lobed bastion of difficult interpretation, with an opening facing towards N.ghe Melas, or Fumiu.
descriptions.NUR574: Completely collapsed and overgrown with bushes. Like the nearby Zianeddu (B), it is classified as a "tancato" nuraghe: on the front face of the main tower there is a wall structure enclosing a smaller tower and a courtyard situated between the two towers.
descriptions.NUR1884: Single-tower nuraghe built of chalky sandstone. Nuragic settlement with finds of ceramics from the middle Bronze Age. The site is neither accessible nor easily readable at present, and a study for a philological reconstruction of the site would be advisable.
descriptions.NUR18117: A few metres from the S.Giagu Nuraghe, the remains of a nuraghe completely covered by Mediterranean vegetation and brambles can be seen.
descriptions.NUR925: The nuraghe is in a state of complete abandonment. Partly buried and completely overgrown by vegetation.
descriptions.NUR1615: Destroyed nuraghe. The interior of the nuraghe can be seen only from the top of the tholos. An architrave of access is visible.
descriptions.NUR15264: Nuraghe reported on Wikimapia, no name in the locality Punta Sa Cresia
descriptions.NUR15945: Lapidary circle. It could be a nuraghe left incomplete.
descriptions.NUR3346:
Nuraghe immersed in vegetation. Nearby lies the homonymous Nuragic burial.

Of the monument, on the west side, a short stretch of wall tangent to the main tower remains partially visible, while in plan the outline of the external perimeter can be observed.

The entrance to the tower is linted, with a trapezoidal cross-section, and leads into a passage with a flat floor.
descriptions.NUR6202: Nuraghe Abbaia (Acquaviva); it is situated halfway up the slope of this mountain, near two abundant springs; this nuraghe, which remains with only a few traces, served as a coastal watchtower in relation to the nuraghe Ottiolo.
descriptions.NUR6036: An area rich in archaeology is located where the nuraghe stands, situated in the highest part of the Sèa plateau, dominating the Torralba Nuragic Valley and visible (even at a distance) from S. Antine. About 50 metres to the north lies a strange structure: a fenced area surrounded by a wall about two metres high, with an elongated shape of about 10 x 30 metres.
descriptions.NUR5932:
The Accas nuraghe is in a fair state of preservation. The monument has not been excavated, and both the entrance and the interior are partly buried, probably to a depth of about 2 m relative to the nuraghe's original floor level.

The chamber is nevertheless accessible. Inside, on the left, the stairwell is completely buried and inaccessible.

Inside the chamber, along the walls, the three niches are only just distinguishable because they too are filled with earth.
descriptions.NUR5613: Nuraghe in good condition. The interior is almost complete. The tholos is open because the closure ashlar is missing.
descriptions.NUR3950: The Acchettas nuraghe at first glance appears completely destroyed; only part of the polygonal walls remains visible on the western side. During ground-breaking works, large amounts of debris have accumulated on the monument.
descriptions.NUR3035: It now appears as a single-tower nuraghe, surrounded by well-cultivated fields; it is imposing, with free-standing walls about seven metres high. To the right a steep helical staircase leads up to the top of the nuraghe; to the left a niche overlooks the entrance area. Inside the circular chamber three further niches can be seen, clearly defined. The view from the terrace takes in the woods and the well-tended lands of the industrious people of Samugheo. It deserves to be visited and enhanced.
descriptions.NUR2161: Single-tower tholos nuraghe. Despite poor conservation conditions, the circular plan characteristic of such a nuraghe, of relatively small dimensions, can still be discerned; it was built from locally sourced polygonal basalt blocks, with the external wall face retaining a maximum height of about 2 m.
descriptions.NUR2271: Circle of large stones but without a foundation, thus its attribution is questionable. This structure has so far been classified as a "nuraghe", assigned the function of "meda" as an entrance to the cove.
descriptions.NUR4828:
Complex nuraghe consisting of a central body with a bastion and four lateral towers. Bronze Age II, 2nd millennium B.C.

A large nuraghe at the top of the hill dominating the Colostrai pond, in an area that during the Nuragic period was densely inhabited. A harbour and two inlets, partly navigable, completely controlled.
descriptions.NUR5417: The Adoni nuraghe is a complex nuraghe dating to the Bronze Age, located in the municipality of Villanovatulo in the province of Cagliari. The site stands on a rise about 800 m high in the centre of the historic Sarcidano region. The first excavations date back to the mid-nineteenth century. The whole complex consists of a central tower and a four-lobed bastion, surrounded by a village. Various finds have been recovered at the site, including pottery and a fragment of a bronze handle.
descriptions.NUR3395: It is a completely collapsed nuraghe that retains a maximum height of 1.90 m.
descriptions.NUR5539: The Aeddos nuraghe stands at 368 metres above sea level in the "sa serra" plateau of Orotelli. The first construction dates to the Bronze Age (1300–900 BC). The nuraghe has a three-lobed structure, composed of a central tower and three concentric towers. It is built with large polycarved granite blocks from the local area arranged in irregular courses. The height of the visible wall from the central tower reaches 8.30 metres.
descriptions.NUR965: It is a complex nuraghe of unclear reading, consisting of a main tower and remains of two other possible towers. The nuraghe is built with roughly hewn blocks of sandstone and shale, set in polygonal masonry. In the west/south-west area, the wall structure encloses a rocky spur.
descriptions.NUR3848: The Agnu nuraghe is built of granite and has a horse-shoe shape, as part of it is set against a rocky cliff. It features a monumental entrance oriented to the east, equipped with a lintel, from which one enters a corridor that originally had a wooden sliding door, which descended from the upper level. On either side, two corridors open out; one leads to a domed chamber, the other passes through the wall and extends outward through the natural rock.
descriptions.NUR2612:
It is one of many prehistoric monuments that make Seneghe one of the Sardinian comuni with the highest density of material evidence from that remote civilization.

Single-tower partially collapsed and overgrown with vegetation
descriptions.NUR5857:
It is one of many prehistoric monuments that make Seneghe one of the Sardinian comuni with the highest density of material evidence from that remote civilization.

Single-tower partially collapsed and overgrown with vegetation
descriptions.NUR5680: With the presence of two nuraghes, the remains of a village and a giants' tomb, a significant assemblage is formed for reconstructing the historical events of the area. The single-tower nuraghe Corru 'e Oe rises on a small plateau visually connected to the four-lobed Aidu and to three others, which appear to have belonged to a single defensive and surveillance system covering the territory. Nearby the nuraghe, remains of a village have been found, consisting of circular huts;
