descriptions.NUR2808: With the presence of two nuraghes, the remains of a village and a giants' tomb, a significant assemblage is formed for reconstructing the historical events of the area. The single-tower nuraghe Corru 'e Oe rises on a small plateau visually connected to the four-lobed Aidu and to three others, which appear to have belonged to a single defensive and surveillance system covering the territory. Nearby the nuraghe, remains of a village have been found, consisting of circular huts;
descriptions.NUR6149: With the presence of two nuraghes, the remains of a village and a giants' tomb, a significant assemblage is formed for reconstructing the historical events of the area. The single-tower nuraghe Corru 'e Oe rises on a small plateau visually connected to the four-lobed Aidu and to three others, which appear to have belonged to a single defensive and surveillance system covering the territory. Nearby the nuraghe, remains of a village have been found, consisting of circular huts;
descriptions.NUR2544: With the presence of two nuraghes, the remains of a village and a giants' tomb, a significant assemblage is formed for reconstructing the historical events of the area. The single-tower nuraghe Corru 'e Oe rises on a small plateau visually connected to the four-lobed Aidu and to three others, which appear to have belonged to a single defensive and surveillance system covering the territory. Nearby the nuraghe, remains of a village have been found, consisting of circular huts;
descriptions.NUR3462:
Nuraghe that features an inscription carved on a stone slab, attesting the boundary line between the territory of the Iliensi people and the Balari.

The inscription reads "ILI IVR IN NVRAC SESSAR M C", meaning the rights of the Iliensi of Nurac Sessar. Its significance also lies in being one of the earliest testimonies of the name given to Sardinian towers.
descriptions.NUR6474: It consists of a central tower and three auxiliary towers connected together by stairs and corridors, some of which are no longer accessible today. Access to the ground floor and the upper level—currently without a roof—is provided via a staircase on the right. The ground floor chamber, of considerable size, is characterized by the presence of three large niches reaching up to 4 metres in height.
descriptions.NUR5538: Here also a mezzanino and a subsidiary staircase, elevated within the right niche of the chamber. A nuraghe that reminded me, in layout, of the Crabia at Bauladu.
descriptions.NUR2936:
It is a corridor nuraghe with a roughly quadrangular plan (18 m x 15 m) featuring a singular projecting wall section (length 7 m – width 3 m) at the south-west corner.

The wall face is composed of polygonal masonry with large, roughly shaped blocks.

The monument is reduced to a heap of stones, making it impossible to clearly define the internal spaces.
descriptions.NUR3020: Single-tower with its top missing and a tholos partially collapsed, accessible from the inside
descriptions.NUR3222: Single-tower with its top missing and a tholos partially collapsed, accessible from the inside
descriptions.NUR13362:
Located just outside the town of Arzachena, it appears as an imposing structure, although the upper level has partially collapsed.

It is built with large granite blocks and dates back to the Middle Bronze Age (about 1600 BC), based on the numerous materials recovered during excavations.

The nuraghe's walls are built against a large granite outcrop; for this reason, the structure has an irregular plan, giving it a "pseudo-nuraghe" appearance. (MIBACT)
descriptions.NUR4172: The nuraghe, in good state of preservation, consists of a main tholos to which additional masonry sections were later added. From the entrance of the nuraghe extends a long corridor and a staircase. In the main chamber, where the roof has collapsed, there are several niches. Dating to 1500–1200 BC, the nuraghe stands on a hill, whose slopes contain circular and oval wall remains, likely belonging to a village.
descriptions.NUR869: The single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe, in medium-to-low state of conservation (six courses above ground), is located at the top of a promontory jutting over a rocky cliff, directly against the virgin rock.
descriptions.NUR5640: Wikipedia identifies this nuraghe as one of the last to be built, with progressively less pronounced external wall slopes. It retains the tholos almost intact, except for some courses.
descriptions.NUR5698: Quadrilobate nuraghe Alvu, built with squared white stones, with numerous hut foundations surrounding it. It exhibits particular architectural features in the way the corner walls are interlocked, a detail not found in other nuraghes.
descriptions.NUR2993: The central tower remains externally to a height of 6.40 m; on the left side of the corridor opens the staircase niche, trapezoidal in shape, completely collapsed; the entrance to the chamber is also trapezoidal; the internal chamber, essentially circular in plan, has a maximum diameter of 4.76 m and a maximum height of 5.60 m; the tholos is preserved almost entirely, except for the last two courses.
descriptions.NUR6238: Nuraghe Alvu di Nulvi: "alvu" = white. A four-lobed nuraghe, very beautiful, although in a fairly degraded state of preservation. Human and institutional neglect, together with the harshness of the elements, contribute to its deterioration. Let us remember that present-day municipal boundaries make no sense when referred to the Nuragic period, and future generations will have one piece fewer with which to reconstruct the historical and cultural period of our forebears.
descriptions.NUR3357: The structure still preserves 12 benches. Complex nuraghe with an outer wall and a surrounding village built of basalt blocks. Notable for the presence of benches still in situ. Entrance to the west (rare). Unfortunately, it is covered by dense vegetation.
descriptions.NUR6242: A circular single-tower nuraghe with three niches. It stands on an island in the middle of Lake Cuga, which was spared when the dam of the same name was built. It cannot be reached by land; the only access is by boat or canoe after a journey of 20–25 minutes. Each time one lands there after the winter season, the rebirth of the flora and fauna is revealed anew, forming a natural frame for the archaic shapes of the nuraghe. The quantity of incisions and cupmarks is striking.
descriptions.NUR3339: Complex nuraghe: due to the state of degradation and the significant burial of the structures, it cannot be securely assigned to any defined type.
descriptions.NUR4727:
Complex consisting of five towers connected by thick curtain walls resting on natural rock.

The site is internationally known because, for the first time in Sardinia, Minoan ceramics have been discovered.
descriptions.NUR14967: Disappeared nuraghe but of which traces remain in local memory and the basal circle
descriptions.NUR2494: Practically the nuraghe no longer exists; only some piles of large stones remain, which still allow one to perceive its original location.
descriptions.NUR2075: Nuraghe completely collapsed, only some courses remain among the dense Mediterranean scrub.
descriptions.NUR2118: Complex nuraghe consisting of a central tower and a bastion with three towers. The original tower survives, filled with earth and collapse. To the south-east stands a tower of which part of the wall structures can be seen; the inner wall face is barely visible because of collapse and vegetation. A curtain wall links this tower with another oriented to the north-east, of which almost the entire wall outline survives. A third tower oriented to the south-west preserves its external perimeter almost intact.
descriptions.NUR19653: Complex nuraghe consisting of a central tower and four towers. The outline of the walls of the original tower survives almost entirely; its interior is filled with earth, collapse debris and vegetation. Three towers added laterally stand to the south-east, north-west and north-east, all overgrown with vegetation that makes their structure hard to see. The fourth tower lies to the south-west, detached from the main body. Traces left by illegal excavators are clearly visible.
descriptions.NUR4465: Complex nuraghe completely collapsed. It projects towards the "Seven Brothers" and towards the Geremeas Sea.
descriptions.NUR1817: Location of the remains of the Antoi Letze nuraghe
descriptions.NUR3022: Basically a pile of stones; at the top a circular opening is visible, forming a 2 m deep shaft, which I assume was the flat lintel of the staircase that ran along the inner wall.
descriptions.NUR4327: The Anulù nuraghe belongs to the homonymous settlement, a large village dating to the late Nuragic period, and is composed of about thirty circular huts of medium and small size, separated by several walls.
descriptions.NUR21014: Located on a hilltop. It appears to be a single-tower nuraghe with evidence of huts in the surrounding areas.
descriptions.NUR8526: The archaeological area includes a complex nuraghe, the Appiu nuraghe, located at the foot of Monte Cuccu, facing the sea, three-lobed, externally collapsed, but with three large interior rooms remaining intact; an associated village of about 200 huts; another nuraghe, a single-tower (single-tower nuraghe); a giants' tomb and two small dolmen. Nearby are also a megalithic circle and a temple "a megaron".
descriptions.NUR5553:
The four-lobed bastion has a rather disordered structure of large polyhedral blocks; all the chambers have collapsed vaults, while the courtyard is partly filled with rubble; the main entrance is visible on the eastern side.

A stretch of enclosure wall can be seen to the west of the bastion, but it is not clear whether it extends around the other sides as well. All the ground around the bastion has been completely cleared of stones and is cultivated, with abundant Roman pottery on the surface.
descriptions.NUR4561: The monument, although very well preserved, is hard to read in plan because of the dense vegetation that also makes it difficult to locate. Two towers, an internal courtyard and parts of the connecting walls between the structures can be recognised. The central body, which survives to a height of 10 courses of medium and large blocks of volcanic stone in polygonal masonry. It is characterised by steeply sloping walls and an elliptical plan.
descriptions.NUR5979: Structures belonging to a single-tower tholos nuraghe. The nuraghe, built of local polygonal basalt blocks, survives in its outer wall face to a maximum height of just over 4 m. The inner chamber has collapsed and the remaining part is filled with the same collapse material. The entrance, identifiable to the south, is lintelled with a height of 1.20 m. The workmanship of the lintel and jambs is fairly rough, with barely dressed blocks.
descriptions.NUR6274: The nuraghe structures, of the simple tholos type, are buried and covered by dense vegetation. Partially emerging at the top of the small ridge formed by the structures and the soil covering them are some courses composed of local basalt blocks.
descriptions.NUR4652: No official documents have been found, yet in the village it is said that beneath the hill there lies a complex nuraghe and a very large village, as would emerge from the traces left by tomb raiders.
descriptions.NUR5385: Complex nuraghe with a village and sacred well in the vicinity
descriptions.NUR2609:
Complex nuraghe, in which various structural elements, visible only in part, project against the central body, a tower made of trachyte blocks, with a circular plan. In the surrounding area, especially to the south-east, there are numerous Roman ceramic fragments.

The urban plan of Sassari (11 Dec. 2014) designates it as "Nuraghe Arcone II".
descriptions.NUR6326: It seems to belong to the category of "uncompleted" nuraghes, yet the dense vegetation cover prevents a precise definition.
descriptions.NUR5464: From a period subsequent to the adjacent Monti Pintau II, about seven courses of ashlars strongly densified remain.
descriptions.NUR4892: Five courses remain, their irregularity suggesting a proto-nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR5146: The nuraghe consists of a central tower surrounded by a curtain wall, to which several secondary towers are attached. The central tower, which originally comprised multiple superimposed levels, currently retains only the lower level and the staircase leading to the upper levels, partially blocked by collapses.
descriptions.NUR966: In the archaeological park there is an underground cemetery, composed of about fifteen domus de janas (the houses of the fairies), the prehistoric tombs dug into the rocky walls of Sa Carona Arrubia (the red rocky wall) and into the large basalt erratic boulders, and a few single-tower (single-tower) nuraghes.
descriptions.NUR2180: In the archaeological park there is an underground cemetery, composed of about fifteen domus de janas (the houses of the fairies), the prehistoric tombs dug into the rocky walls of Sa Carona Arrubia (the red rocky wall) and into the large basalt erratic boulders, and a few single-tower (single-tower) nuraghes.
descriptions.NUR5113: In the archaeological park there is an underground cemetery, composed of about fifteen domus de janas (the houses of the fairies), the prehistoric tombs dug into the rocky walls of Sa Carona Arrubia (the red rocky wall) and into the large basalt erratic boulders, and a few single-tower (single-tower) nuraghes.
descriptions.NUR7014: In the archaeological park there is an underground cemetery, composed of about fifteen domus de janas (the houses of the fairies), the prehistoric tombs dug into the rocky walls of Sa Carona Arrubia (the red rocky wall) and into the large basalt erratic boulders, and a few single-tower (single-tower) nuraghes.
descriptions.NUR7028: In the archaeological park there is an underground cemetery, composed of about fifteen domus de janas (the houses of the fairies), the prehistoric tombs dug into the rocky walls of Sa Carona Arrubia (the red rocky wall) and into the large basalt erratic boulders, and a few single-tower (single-tower) nuraghes.
descriptions.NUR7011: In the archaeological park there is an underground cemetery, composed of about fifteen domus de janas (the houses of the fairies), the prehistoric tombs dug into the rocky walls of Sa Carona Arrubia (the red rocky wall) and into the large basalt erratic boulders, and a few single-tower (single-tower) nuraghes.
descriptions.NUR5090:
It is located to the south, near the border with the territory of Usellus.

It is a simple type and is very damaged.
descriptions.NUR5752: The Aresti Nuraghe lies on the border between the municipalities of Narbolia and Seneghe and is located about 1 km northeast of Narbolia, near the SP 11. It is a complex nuraghe in good state of preservation. The main tower is accessible and features a fine entrance with a covered corridor and an intact tholos in the internal chamber.
descriptions.NUR3236: It is a corridor proto-nuraghe built of basalt.
descriptions.NUR4005:
Hidden beneath thick vegetation, we find the nuraghe Arigau. Completely covered by soil and vegetation, with only some of the base courses visible.

The nuraghe is located at Santa Maria Acquas, on a hill behind the amphitheatre. Apparently a single-tower (single-tower nuraghe). Never studied and completely covered by soil and vegetation.
descriptions.NUR2741:
It is located within the municipal territory of Nule (SS).

The nuraghe is a single-tower with a staircase, a passage niche, and a chamber surrounded by three niches arranged in a cross.

The tower is circular in plan, while the roof has collapsed.
descriptions.NUR4499: The nuraghe, datable to the Middle Bronze Age (15th–14th century BC), has a single-tower structure and a truncated-conical shape with a diameter of twelve metres and a surviving height of ten metres. It is built of well-worked limestone-schist blocks laid to form the tholos, which has lost its top courses. The entrance leads into a corridor four metres long, equal to the wall thickness, which opens into the main chamber, circular and over five metres in diameter.
descriptions.NUR2667:
The building, situated in a dominant position at the eastern end of the named hill, appears as a three-lobed complex nuraghe with a village surrounding it.

Here too there must have been a king who dominated the entire plain.

From the remains it seems that Romans also arrived later.
descriptions.NUR4986: (da Mitz'arramini, site where it is located), it is a complex nuraghe with multiple towers, near which a village also exists. The building is situated in an area with a toponym indicating a copper-related reference, where the central tower and a secondary tower can clearly be identified, although both are currently sealed by eolian and agricultural deposits due to the lack of thorough investigations.
descriptions.NUR5178: Up to five courses emerge, composed of cyclopean blocks of varying shapes, massive, reaching a height of up to 2.5 metres, in basalt. The central tower is incomplete, forming an angle of 270 degrees. From it extend a wall to the east and another to the north. The structure enclosed by these walls is entirely unclear due to brush and various restorations.
descriptions.NUR2823: It is located within the territory of the comune of Seneghe (OR). Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe with a tholos, built from locally sourced polygonal basalt blocks. The vault has collapsed and the chamber is filled with debris from the collapse. The remaining height of the structure is about 3.50 m. The entrance, trapezoidal in shape, is clearly visible, featuring a monolithic lintel and oriented to the east (1.70 m in height x 0.80 m in base width).
descriptions.NUR5472: Nuraghe of the tancato type with a main tower and an additional structural body (second tower and courtyard). The monument is located adjacent to the parish church.
descriptions.NUR3843: The nuraghe structures, of the simple tholos type, show considerable erosion and are covered by dense vegetation. Partially emerging at the summit of the small ridge formed by the structures and the soil covering them are some courses composed of local basalt blocks.
descriptions.NUR4277: Four-lobed nuraghe. A nuraghe with the addition of two lateral towers connected to the original tower by a semi-circular corridor.
descriptions.NUR5308: It dates to about 1500 BC; the collapse is dated to the 9th century BC, and it remained uninhabited until 100 BC when the Romans arrived. It consists of a central tower surrounded by five other towers and an outer wall (outer enclosure), with a further seven towers forming another defensive curtain wall enclosing several courtyards. A second outer curtain wall and a third with three more towers are also present. The total number of towers is twenty-one. The area exceeds 5000 m².
descriptions.NUR5304: The nuraghe is of single-tower type, with a curtain wall reinforced to a thickness of about 80 cm; it rises above the surrounding vegetation, reaching a height of up to 4 metres. Its location is strategic, as it lies halfway between the Fenu nuraghe and the nearby thermal area, where three other nuraghes are located, one of which belongs to the same thermal complex. It is the best-preserved nuraghe in the territory of the comune of Sardara. The size of the lintel is particularly striking.
descriptions.NUR15038: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe with a dismantled and buried village
descriptions.NUR10755: Nuraghe Artòra dominates the Capo Comino promontory at a height of 120 m above sea level and once fulfilled the role of a watchtower, equivalent to the current traffic light. Located at a short distance from the lighthouse that overlooks Capo Comino, it is described by Relli as a complex nuraghe situated on the summit of the same name; however, it is very difficult to distinguish due to being covered by a concrete platform built for military purposes during the Second World War.
descriptions.NUR2755:
It is a single-tower nuraghe roofed with a tholos, still in good condition: it survives on the N-NE and N-W sides to a height of 10.50 metres, while the SE side, corresponding to the entrance, has collapsed.

The external wall face, of 26 courses of stone, is formed by large polygonal blocks in the base, which has a diameter of 14 metres, while in the upper part the blocks are sub-square and of modest size, becoming more regular as the height increases.
descriptions.NUR6337: In this case one is faced with a critical situation because the remains of the nuraghe form an irregular heap of stones, although certain constructive features of the structure are still discernible. Ritualistically, as in most of the Chiaramontes nuraghes, the entrance is still clearly visible, with both pilasters and the lintel still present, both oriented towards east-southeast.
descriptions.NUR2776: Complex nuraghe with the tholos intact. Part of the external wall face has collapsed.
descriptions.NUR1805:
It is a single-tower nuraghe with a staircase, a corridor niche, and a chamber flanked by two opposing niches.

The tower cannot be fully defined in its outer perimeter because of collapses and dense shrub vegetation, but a circular ground plan about 10 metres in diameter at the base is to be assumed. The surviving height is 6.50 m on the south-east side and 4.80 m on the north-west side. The masonry consists of medium and large basalt blocks laid in horizontal courses that are not always regular.
descriptions.NUR2756: It is a single-tower (single-tower nuraghe) and is in an advanced state of degradation. However, some elements of the structural apparatus are still visible. At present, it provides shelter for domestic animals right at the main entrance. I wish to exorcise the situation by thinking of the great people of the nuraghi: "from the stars… to the stables". If institutions and civil awareness delay and harden in abandoning our monuments. mu
descriptions.NUR3393: Single-tower (single-tower nuraghe): this is a new emergence because the central chamber has collapsed and the wall face has collapsed to the west. Some features of the Nuragic apparatus are visible. San Pietro nuraghe. Local tradition does not recall a church dedicated to San Pietro existing at this site. It is likely that this structure belonged to a property linked to the church of San Pietro, which stood in the village located in the area of Elva nàna, of which the name has been lost.
descriptions.NUR11143: Submerged single-tower nuraghe in the waters of Lake Cuga. It was detected by archaeologist Ercole Contu during the period preceding the construction of the dam on Cuga. It belongs to the complex of nuraghes in the Chessedu–Cuga valley.
descriptions.NUR5024: The Asusa nuraghe, built around 1300 BC, consists of two towers projecting over a courtyard and features its main entrance to the east. Inside one of the internal rooms, archaeologists have uncovered a circular arrangement possibly related to a well or a cistern, still to be explored.
descriptions.NUR3625: The name derives from the toponym of Atarzu mountain. In the Chiaramontese dialect we call it de sa pedra atarzina, a name that aptly describes the mountain's abundance of such stones. Never has the name been more fitting, as several sites of flint working have been identified, where tools for daily use or for hunting—such as blades and arrowheads—were produced. Only a few large megaliths exist, hidden beneath a massive mass of mastic.
descriptions.NUR6438: A "antenna" bronze sword found at Ploaghe near the nuraghe "Attentu" (in 1874 the nuraghe was studied by the archaeologist Giovanni Spano, native of Ploaghe, who carried out the first stratigraphic excavation in Sardinia there).
descriptions.NUR6100: Quadrilobate nuraghe, consisting of a central tower and three additional smaller towers. The diameter is about 11 metres. The central tower is composed of large stones, while the front addition is made of smaller stones.
descriptions.NUR5622: Preserves the tholos intact. There is a Nuragic settlement around the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR5609: The Atzara nuraghe is a complex, three-lobed type featuring a slender main tower characterized by a wide base. The walls connecting the three external towers are still in good condition, while the reinforcement structures were built during Punic and Roman times. Recently it has been cleaned, but it awaits a more detailed excavation to better understand its structure.
descriptions.NUR6333: The remaining buried structure extends at least two metres below the current campagna level, due to the outward escape of the “sacco” from within the wall face, making it impossible to access the internal rooms of the corridor nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR3077: Proto-nuraghe of corridor type. The nuraghe stands on a hillside slope and is organized on two distinct levels, adapting to the terrain's shape and slope. The structures are largely covered by vegetation, but the northern and eastern and eastern parts can be observed. The northern and eastern section has a semicircular layout, while the eastern section is formed by a solid wall that extends in a straight line towards the south.
descriptions.NUR1994: Single-tower tholos nuraghe built from polygonal basaltic blocks. Of the nuraghe, only 4–5 courses of large blocks remain arranged in a circular pattern to form a structure of considerable size, very similar to other nuraghes in the area. The maximum remaining height is about 3 m. The internal chamber has collapsed and is filled with collapse debris. The entrance cannot be identified.
descriptions.NUR5948: It is a single-tower nuraghe equipped with a large circular chamber whose walls are particularly corbelled. A distinctive feature of the nuraghe is the absence of the passage niche and the staircase. Outside, around the tower, several worked stone blocks of varying sizes are visible.
descriptions.NUR4669: It is a complex nuraghe, whose plan is impossible to determine because it is largely buried. A tower to the west is visible, with about five courses visible. From the other areas, scattered circular courses emerge.
descriptions.NUR570: Complex nuraghe of difficult definition due to its state of degradation and the significant burial of its structures. Located on the summit of Capo San Marco, with panoramic views in all directions.
descriptions.NUR5831: Damaged nuraghe of which no description is available
descriptions.NUR6370: Damaged nuraghe of which no description is available
descriptions.NUR6410:
It is completely covered with soil and vegetation; one would not notice it was a nuraghe unless one saw some calcareous stones stacked one upon the other at the top of the hill.

On the side opposite the sea, a few metres from the summit where the central tower stands and inside a hole, one can see one of the towers of the nuraghe, in which the tholos is visible, cut in half, composed of sandstone and limestone blocks.
descriptions.NUR8248: Single-tower nuraghe built on a rocky outcrop. Only a few courses remain visible, intersected by the rock, together with some lower wall structures, though still connected to the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR20071: Complex nuraghe, severely collapsed and never studied. Completely enveloped by vegetation, it is difficult to interpret. It shows a possible internal staircase and remnants of external walling of secondary rooms.
descriptions.NUR4223: The site is very difficult to identify. To the visitor it appears as a heap of buried ashlar stones, only partially exposed. Accessible via the half-coast path behind the Capoterra settlement.
descriptions.NUR6157: From its position on the ridge of Badde, it dominates the right bank of the Rio Giunturas and is exceptionally aligned along the edge of the cliff, almost as if to assert its position of dominance. The internal chamber can be identified by its orthogonal cells, and the chamber is covered on its sides by organic debris.
descriptions.NUR5933: From the top of a hilltop, the surrounding landscape is visible, where, at a small drop of the river Iscanneddu, there were two water mills. It is a single-tower nuraghe with only a few basal circles of medium-sized stones, partly roughly shaped. Its name undoubtedly derives from the medieval period, when monastic orders established themselves in the area (X–XI centuries).
descriptions.NUR1059: Remains of a nuraghe tower built from basalt blocks.
descriptions.NUR1815: in poor condition, the external megalithic circle was destroyed to make way for sheep grazing; in this nuraghe a bronze boat was found and stolen, the largest ever discovered in Sardinia, measuring about 38 cm in length, known as the boat of the sun king, now preserved at the archaeological museum of Sanna in Sassari.
descriptions.NUR2920: The monument, made of trachyte, has a rectangular plan (12 m x 7 m) and includes an 'elbow'-shaped corridor inside. It shows significant collapse along both the western wall and the southern side.
descriptions.NUR1583: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe in good condition, partially covered by vegetation. In the field, dispersion of Roman-era tiles.
descriptions.NUR3354: This emergency loudly signals the worsening state of decay. Abandonment and neglect contribute to making an urgent intervention for recovery and structural consolidation all the more pressing. The less systematic efforts are initiated to conduct surveying and verification of the vast archaeological heritage within the territory of Chiaramonti.
descriptions.NUR3874: Reduced to a state of ruin, like most of the other sites in the commune of Chiaramonti. It nevertheless shows a few basal circles of cyclopean stones, with the main opening particularly well highlighted by a massive lintel oriented towards south-south-east.
descriptions.NUR6377: It is a circle of cyclopean polygonal stones that is improperly known as a nuraghe. Lacking a specific designation for its form, I continue to classify it as such, but I tend to consider it rather as a ceremonial circle. Nuraghe of the Guado della Moglie. See Badu muzère. mu
descriptions.NUR1656: Single-tower nuraghe composed of trachyte and andesite blocks. It remains about 3 metres high above the current campagna level.
descriptions.NUR2874:
Today, unfortunately, it appears to be considerably damaged.

It also had a bilobate bastion added at a later date.
descriptions.NUR14359: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe located near a small hotel. Diroccato
descriptions.NUR1992: Single-tower tholos nuraghe. Located on a rocky spur dominating the entire western slope of Montiferru down to the sea, it is almost completely hidden by forest vegetation. It is constructed from locally sourced polygonal basalt blocks and stands about 2.60 m high. The internal chamber has collapsed, and the remaining portion is filled with debris from the collapse itself.
descriptions.NUR3873: Single-tower tholos nuraghe. The nuraghe is almost completely dismantled, and the remaining structures consist of the first two courses of the base, built from locally quarried basalt blocks. The maximum remaining height is about 1 m, while the diameter of the nuraghe is about 12 m. The entrance must have been located to the south-east, where a hut was constructed.
descriptions.NUR5707: It belongs to the group of nuraghes with a flat base; I state this with a note of inventory, as the survey is obstructed by robust thorny plants that have colonized the structure. The basal circle is composed of roughly squared stones that intersect well, forming a regular wall arrangement with some natural rocks. It has a raised entrance above the camp level, highlighting the sacred character of the construction.
descriptions.NUR6243: In a precarious state of conservation, it is surrounded by patches of rowan and shrubs that may compromise its stability.
descriptions.NUR3869: Single-tower nuraghe with a cylindrical shape, neither niches nor stairs are present.
descriptions.NUR3788: Nuraghe covered with ficus indica plants and disturbed by a structure that has developed beside it.
descriptions.NUR1535: In the area of Baratè, on a modest elevation in a zone partly used for olive groves and partly for vineyards. On the north side, 4 courses (h m 1.80) of trachytic blocks remain; on the south side, the remains of the raised portion are covered by vegetation. Boundary walls attached to the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR8233: Nuraghe probably a single-tower, covered by collapse and vegetation. Only a single course emerges.
descriptions.NUR913:
The monument, of simple type, is located in an area currently used for sheep grazing; the entrance features a lintel topped by a drainage window, while the pilasters are composed of finely shaped granite blocks arranged in decreasing order towards the top.

The entrance leads into a passage leading to the chamber, composed of finely worked granite ashlar and a vaulted roof section.
descriptions.NUR5721: The proto-nuraghe Bardalatzu is located at the western end of a basaltic tableland, in a remote and difficult-to-access area, dominating a narrow and deep valley where the Riu Murtazzolu and the Riu Cuguttu meet. The monument appears to be of considerable size, with an irregular planimetric form that fits the triangular profile of the hill on which it was built.
descriptions.NUR4273: Well-preserved nuraghe, part of a larger settlement. The central tower still has its roof and a lower level below which entry has not yet been achieved.
descriptions.NUR2926: Complex nuraghe, cannot be definitively classified by its state of degradation or by the significant burial of its structures; in the vicinity, traces of an inhabited settlement, village.
descriptions.NUR10449: The central tower is elliptical, typical of a proto-nuraghe. The towers are more regular in shape, suggesting they were built in later phases, as was the curtain wall of the courtyard, which encloses a system of stairs and silos (presumably for storing agricultural produce). Some parts of the towers show a smaller-scale fabric in the curtain wall, with flatter, more regular stones.
descriptions.NUR4338: It stands on a rocky spur along the Pardu River. It is a nuraghe with at least four towers surrounded by a defensive curtain wall. Of the four towers, three remain in good condition, while the fourth is known only by its base. The site appears today as divided in two. The eastern side, which does not face the river and rises on the rock, is still intact. The western side, which faces the river, is almost completely collapsed and features a large number of scattered stones along the slope.
descriptions.NUR1448: It consists of only a few meagre remains and some stones of the nuraghe, which is completely overgrown by vegetation.
descriptions.NUR5340: Single-tower nuraghe completely collapsed, with only a few courses emerging from the low scrub.
descriptions.NUR5623: It is a single-tower (single-tower nuraghe) built of large basaltic blocks finely shaped. The entrance, oriented south-southwest, is topped by a rectangular window for drainage and leads into a corridor with an ogival roof on the left side, where a niche is located. The chamber, completely filled by collapse, is preserved for almost 5 metres (9 courses). On the right side of the chamber, a niche cut into the wall thickness is visible.
descriptions.NUR4101:
Just before Muravera, at km 51, adjacent to SS 125, the site is well marked and easily accessible. The structure consists of a central tower to which, in later times, a three-lobed bastion with a concave-convex profile was added, enclosing a small courtyard. The entire complex measures 24 m along the N-S axis and 16 m along the O-E axis.

The tower, circular in plan (9 m in external diameter), survives to a maximum residual height of about 10 m.
descriptions.NUR811: The nuraghe stands near the coast of Trinità d'Agultu, south of Isola Rossa. It has an almost elliptical plan and is accessible from the hamlet of Paduledda by taking the road to “La Scalitta”.
descriptions.NUR4010: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe that reappears from the lake only during dry periods.
descriptions.NUR5595: The Battizzone nuraghe is a three-lobed type, with towers joined by an outer wall that forms an internal courtyard at the front. At present the courtyard and the lateral towers are completely filled with collapse debris, making access to the central tower impossible; the entrance lintel is partly visible. A corridor is also visible in the courtyard area, which probably served as the entrance to one of the lateral towers and is notable for its considerable height.
descriptions.NUR2304:
Traces of a nuraghe built of basalt. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.

PUC Arbus Historical and Cultural Report p. 13 Table 12C No. 3360
descriptions.NUR12990: The Bau ' Tanca talana nuraghe rises at an elevation of 1,122 m a.s.l. and is surrounded by a village, where traces of some huts' filaments and stone accumulations used in their construction are still visible. Notable for the unusual symmetry of the village nuclei.
descriptions.NUR502: Completely embedded in the scrub, it is difficult to identify.
descriptions.NUR3228:
The complex consists of a nuraghe, an outer wall, and a village.

The nuraghe includes a central tower to which at least two lateral towers have been added, now only partially visible.

A large outer wall, enclosing at least four towers and having an irregular, curvilinear layout, surrounds the complex.

In the area directly in front, the remains of numerous huts and rectangular, raised-above structures, attached to the inner profile of the outer wall, are present.
descriptions.NUR14990: Damaged and buried nuraghe, whose structure is difficult to define
descriptions.NUR8833:
It lies to the north-east of the village, a short distance from the nuraghe Luas and the proto-nuraghe Friarosu, and is visible from the provincial road that leads to Ruinas after the turn-off for Villa Sant'Antonio.

The plan of the nuraghe is decidedly unusual in that it has two circular structures joined by a corridor.

What makes the site even more interesting is the presence of a large granite boulder, oriented to the east, placed there presumably in the pre-Nuragic period.
descriptions.NUR5664: The monument, although classified as a proto-nuraghe, is in fact a structure resulting from the union of a corridor nuraghe and a tholos nuraghe. The complex consists of a central tower with a terrace, a bastion, and various huts located both inside and outside an outer wall. Currently, it is overlaid by a viaduct; in fact, only a few centimetres separate the last remaining stone rings of the monument from the concrete beams supporting the road.
descriptions.NUR5555: The Benas nuraghe is located on a hillock in the area of 'Tanca sa cresia', northwest of the Jana nuraghe, in the territory of Solarussa, about 200 m from the border with Zerfaliu. It is a complex nuraghe, with a courtyard and three secondary towers. Particularly interesting is the main tower, which retains intact the tholos roof of the ground level. Inside there are three niches, and a curious staircase on the right side of the entrance corridor.
descriptions.NUR9878: The nuraghe is completely collapsed, probably known also by the name Tostoinus.
descriptions.NUR4182: Complex nuraghe partially dismantled, with only the low courses remaining
descriptions.NUR2273:
Remains of a nuraghe and traces of a Nuragic village.

Built on a granitic rise, this nuraghe is not currently discernible among the remains of an extensive village that persisted into the Roman and late medieval periods, as evidenced by fragments of pottery, bricks, and jars.
descriptions.NUR3977: The Bia nuraghe currently appears as a ruin. It is not a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe (although the most visible structure is likely the main tower), as other wall sections can be identified to the south.
descriptions.NUR1004: The nuraghe lies inside the Fertilia Military Airport, in an area skirted by one of the internal connecting roads. The construction of the military structures and the subsequent underground services installed nearby must have erased every possible surface trace of the site's occupation in historical times, to the extent that no scatter of ceramic material relating to the nuraghe's phases of use could be identified.
descriptions.NUR5128: The nuraghe is named after the light colour of the lithic material used in its construction.
descriptions.NUR5373: Some wall courses remain, probably belonging to the outer wall.
descriptions.NUR3498: The nuraghe is not marked on IGM maps and its type is undetermined.
descriptions.NUR10885: Towards the road that leads from Samatzai onto the SS 128. On the right you reach the locality of Bidda Mendula. On a low sandstone promontory (altitude 150 m) the ruins of a nuraghe built of large sandstone marl blocks can be seen, belonging to a Nuragic settlement. On the surface a circular building is visible, probably a single-tower nuraghe, 14 m in diameter, which on the west side shows the remains of a facing wall 2.30 m thick, visible for several metres.
descriptions.NUR5283: The nuraghe is very badly degraded, certainly repurposed over time for various uses.
descriptions.NUR1180: Damaged nuraghe, of which only a few courses remain standing, embedded in natural rock masses.
descriptions.NUR4689: Complex nuraghe, eroded and enveloped by vegetation, of difficult definition
descriptions.NUR3325: The single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe Bidighinzu or Su Idighinzu, translated in Sardinian as "tralcio secco", is a monument located in the territory of Ploaghe, preserving an intact tholos.
descriptions.NUR5321: It is located in the territory of the comune of Mandas (CA). What remains of the nuraghe is visible on the north and north-west sides, where three rows of calcare ashlar emerge; the rest of the stones are scattered around the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR5801: Very complex nuraghe. It has a trilobate outer wall and an internal central tower. Traces of a village outside. The state of conservation is very poor.
descriptions.NUR3541:
The nuraghe has an almost elliptical plan, with the longer sides aligned east-west. The masonry work is roughly polygonal.

The entrance, facing north, has a lintel resting on a few large and small blocks forming the footings; this lintel is topped by a smaller ashlar, itself contained within a ring of blocks arranged in a semicircle, thus deflecting the weight of the superimposed structures onto the piers.
descriptions.NUR1803:
The nuraghe is a complex type, consisting of a central tower enclosed by a quadrilobate bastion with four corner towers connected by curtain walls with a concave-convex profile.

The bastion (NS axis m. 17) is well preserved on the western side and only partially on the northwest side, while it appears completely collapsed and covered in debris along the remaining perimeter.
descriptions.NUR6069:
The site is now known as Nuraghe Urpes, but in fact it is Nuraghe Bighinzone; the Nuraghe Urpes, which stood nearby, has completely disappeared.

At first glance, the nuraghe appears to be a single-tower structure, but a closer examination of its features reveals it to be four-lobed, with concave-convex curtain walls, surrounded in turn by an outer wall featuring towers, of which only a few but significant traces remain.
descriptions.NUR3185:
The nuraghe, almost completely demolished, can still be identified in its entire planimetric profile (diameter about 11 m, residual height about 2 m).

In the vicinity of the nuraghe and scattered over an extensive area (about 12 hectares), the remains of numerous circular (diameter generally exceeding 7 m) and straight structures can be observed, attributable to the ancient settlement and possibly also related to a sacred area.
descriptions.NUR6303: The monument, built of granite stones and preserved to a maximum height of 3 m, features an architraved entrance leading to a corridor with a flat-laid roof, accessible only for a short stretch due to a collapse.
descriptions.NUR5567: Complex nuraghe forming part of the nuraghes of the Cuga valley. The associated village and its external structures have been extensively modified. It allows access to the interior, where the tholos remains perfectly intact.
descriptions.NUR18916: Proto-nuraghe with a central corridor leading to two rooms.
descriptions.NUR4462: The nuraghe is located not far from an indistinct and now completely ruined domus de janas, situated on top of a hill that overlooks the Collinas valley. The structure is almost entirely neglected, abandoned to itself, yet its former extent is evident as the surrounding terrain is surrounded by stones.
descriptions.NUR5510: From the aerial photograph it appears to be a complex nuraghe with a village.
descriptions.NUR3001:
The nuraghe is heavily eroded.

In the vicinity lies a pre-Nuragic settlement dating to the Neolithic period.
descriptions.NUR5511:
The Nuraghe Biriola is located at Dualchi, about four hundred metres from the Nuraghe Piddio. It is a complex nuraghe that appears to be a true fortress with considerable dimensions (about 38 by 22 metres). The central tower features a large circular chamber with a false vaulted roof; in the central part of the structure there are niches, some of which are partially accessible.

Around the nuraghe there once stood a village, traces of which are still visible.
descriptions.NUR4947: The Dom'e Biriu nuraghe is located about 1.5 km north of Genoni. In large part eroded, a tower in masonry with a nearly square plan can still be seen, with horizontal courses and nearly squared blocks.
descriptions.NUR21006: Granite nuraghe, composed of large and medium-sized blocks. It appears to be a corridor nuraghe with two towers, with documented remains: a section of the central tower's wall on the northern side, consisting of three courses, and the interior of the upper part of the secondary tower.
descriptions.NUR6335:
The monument, of tholos type, is not accessible internally due to collapses, but features a circular plan with a diameter of about 9 m and retains, externally, a section of wall up to 2.20 m high, composed of 5 courses of large trachyte stones.

A short distance from the nuraghe, the remains of a wall are found, likely a surviving fragment of an outer wall.
descriptions.NUR18893: The corridor nuraghe, with a rectangular plan and constructed of large granite blocks, survives to a maximum height of 4 m; it features an entrance topped by a lintel leading to a flat-topped corridor, from which a semicircular niche and a long, elongated chamber open.
descriptions.NUR14322:
Should preserve the intact tholos.

Complex nuraghe, today appears as a wooded hill.

On top, a staircase provides access to the internal areas, probably the central tower.

I do not recommend an internal visit, as the nuraghe is very unstable due to the large roots of the vegetation that inhabits it!
descriptions.NUR17914: The site is located in the area of Boe and is completely destroyed; only some courses of the foundation remain visible.
descriptions.NUR6049: Complex nuraghe with only a few courses remaining, partially collapsed and overgrown by vegetation.
descriptions.NUR18264: It is located within the territory of the comune of Furtei. It is mentioned by Vittorio Angiu in the Geographical-Historical-Statistical-Commercial Dictionary of the States of S.M. under the entry Furtei as Nuragi-Ais.
descriptions.NUR5860: Corridor nuraghe in good state of conservation
descriptions.NUR2862: Partially eroded, invaded by vegetation, and difficult to explore. The central chamber, the entrance, and the circular corridor remain clearly visible.
descriptions.NUR2425: The monument is situated in a dominant position; the external curtain wall's extensive collapse prevents a precise assessment, and it appears to be a single-tower (single-tower nuraghe) with a circular plan in two levels and a detached outer wall.
descriptions.NUR5031: Damaged and collapsed nuraghe, of which only the entrance portal and the interior remain.
descriptions.NUR863: Single-tower nuraghe hardly accessible due to vegetation.
descriptions.NUR4106:
A. Sanguinetti, who in 1970 noted that, among other things, part of the structure was buried beneath stone accumulations caused by land reclamation in the surrounding agricultural areas.

The author described nonetheless a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe with an elliptical plan, with an entrance oriented to the northeast, and hypothesized the presence of a straight-line access corridor.
descriptions.NUR4624: Nuraghe located in the mountain known as Punta Breigara. The locals call the site "nuraghe de s'omu e is abisi". A tholos base of about 1.50 m height is present. Vegetation has completely covered the site, making further identification impossible. Difficult access; the roads are on private land.
descriptions.NUR6130: Small single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe; around it is a small domus de janas cemetery, in which there are decorations carved in bull's-head protomes.
descriptions.NUR2893: Complex tholos nuraghe. Completely enveloped by vegetation, it is a large nuraghe whose features can only be roughly inferred. It appears to consist of a central tower and two additional towers, with an internal courtyard today filled with rubble from collapses. Built from large basalt blocks locally quarried, it is well preserved, despite being scarcely visible due to the thickets that surround it.
descriptions.NUR4146: Complex nuraghe completely collapsed and buried.
descriptions.NUR14923:
Nuraghe. Located on top of a hill, with views over the area of Sa Gruttixedda (Pozzo/Village Nuragic)

Covered with large stones and vegetation.
descriptions.NUR4584: Located at the border with the territory of Guasila, at the foot of the basaltic plateau of Lasìna, on the western side which slopes down towards the Samatzese territory. The structure consists of a single tower with an external diameter of 12 m and retains intact along its entire circumference the base course. The materials used are sandstone.
descriptions.NUR4290: The complex includes a nuraghe consisting of a central tower located on the summit of a basaltic hill and several additional structures positioned along the slopes of the same hill, the subject of archaeological investigations in 2003, and an important hut village situated on the south-eastern slopes of the hill.
descriptions.NUR4616: Complex nuraghe, collapsed and with only a few buried courses remaining, where a frontal addition followed the original tower.
descriptions.NUR4309: Complex nuraghe, collapsed and with only a few buried courses remaining, where a frontal addition followed the original tower.
descriptions.NUR4311:
A. Sanguinetti, who in the 1970s described a tower with an elliptical plan and an outer circumference somewhat irregular, with large gaps especially to the south-southwest, where he hypothesized the opening of an access chamber.

The maximum diameter of the monument has been calculated at about 11.10 m, while no observation can be made regarding the construction technique used, as no wall faces are still visible.
descriptions.NUR15059: Complex nuraghe, quadrilobate, of which only a small amount remains
descriptions.NUR5454:
It stands on the summit of a conical hill at 275 m above sea level.

Ruins of a very important settlement. Complex nuraghe with a probable surrounding village. The ground plan consists of a central tower surrounded by four lateral towers joined by curtain walls. The materials used are large roughly hewn blocks of calcareous marl. A large circular livestock enclosure, still visible, was built on the north-west side with the collapsed material from the settlement.
descriptions.NUR4869: Multi-lobed, with a central tower of which only the basal course survives; this breaks off to the south and south-west for a length of 8 m, where the foundations of four peripheral towers appear, originally joined by straight curtain walls, forming a basal platform supporting the main tower, which has a diameter of 9.60 m. About 11 m from the central tower the basal walling of a circular hut 8.40 m in diameter is almost entirely visible. The structures of the complex are composed of sandstone blocks.
descriptions.NUR15062: Complex nuraghe with a dismantled and buried village
descriptions.NUR4511: Settlement in considerable disrepair. Located at 256 m a.s.l. On the summit a calcareous rock cap is visible, surrounded by scrub vegetation including arrùda (Ruta d'Aleppo). The remains of the nuragic structure have an internal diameter of 4.05 m. It appears to be a single-tower (single-tower nuraghe), but the dense scrub cover could conceal other structures. The site is strategically elevated, with a very wide visual basin.
descriptions.NUR14998: Complex nuraghe with a dismantled and buried village, the structure of which cannot be defined.
descriptions.NUR5362: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe located on the so-called basaltic crown of the Giara di Gonnosnò/Genoni. Covered by vegetation, it is difficult to access.
descriptions.NUR18225: Nuraghe known from ancient writings (Taramelli) and in the toponym recognized by the elders of the village. Noted by Costantino Corongiu.
descriptions.NUR11568: It is a proto-nuraghe or early nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR12748: Near the settlement, never subjected to excavations or studies. Particularly eroded, it shows traces of huts in the vicinity.
descriptions.NUR4658: On the summit of the nuraghe ruins, during the post-war period a watchroom was built for the sentinels of the powder magazine. Single-tower, rock-cut, collapsed and buried.
descriptions.NUR5673:
Complex nuraghe.

Although listed as Brundette Nuraghe, it is instead known (even by the local elders) as Chentucheddas Nuraghe, and it is situated on the edge of the named rock.
descriptions.NUR1218: This nuraghe, located at the border between the municipalities of Olmedo (SS) and Sassari, is listed in Filippo Nissardi's Nuragographic Map of the Nurra (published by G. Pinza in 1901) as "Nuraghe Grascioleddu" and assigned to Olmedo.
descriptions.NUR6402: In a dominant position relative to the Riu Liscoi, on a granite outcrop, a corridor nuraghe of elliptical plan, built of granite and pinkish trachyte, is visible; it is not accessible inside due to collapses, and is accompanied by the remains of some circular huts.
descriptions.NUR3016: Bocca d'Irghiriai is a narrow and difficult rocky saddle that separates the wall of Monte Bàrdia from the massif of Monte Irveri. It must have been a pass used also in antiquity: near the spur overlooking the east side of the saddle, only the remains of a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe in limestone are found.
descriptions.NUR3174: It is located on the shores of Lago del Cuga and spends most of the year submerged under water. It also belongs to the nuraghes of the Cuga valley.
descriptions.NUR6393: Single-tower tholos nuraghe built from locally sourced polygonal basalt blocks. The structure is in fairly good condition despite significant later modifications. It has a residual height of about 5 m. The external wall face is clearly visible and better preserved in the northeast section, while in the southern part it has been heavily altered and is heavily overgrown with vegetation. (Pruna on I.G.M. map)
descriptions.NUR3180:
It has a vaguely trapezoidal plan (m. 0.10.50 x 10.20 x 11.10 x 4.50) with rounded corners and an elevated entrance (0.75 above the camp level), featuring a rectangular opening (width m. 1.47 – height 1.98), linteled and oriented to the northeast.

The interior of the monument is not discernible due to collapse

The masonry work is composed of polygonal blocks of medium and large size, roughly hewn and arranged in irregular horizontal courses
descriptions.NUR814: Three-lobed nuraghe, reused in the Roman and medieval periods. The village surrounding the tower, now almost entirely vanished due to agricultural mechanization, is one of the largest in the Uri region.
descriptions.NUR6354: The monument, a complex (four-lobed) structure, includes a central tower to which four secondary towers have been added, connected to the north and east by straight curtain walls, while the connecting wall to the west follows a curved outline.
descriptions.NUR2106: The monument, located near the Borore cemetery and at a short distance from the Pischedda nuraghe, remains reduced to a few prominent courses, yet these allow us to identify it as a complex nuraghe of the "tancato" type, composed of a central tower located to the north-west, which connects to a smaller tower opposite, to the south-east, with two straight wall sections enclosing a trapezoidal space; the entire structure is bounded by an outer wall. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR6010: The Nuraghe Busoro is located in the Sedilo municipal territory, about 1.5 km north of the village. It is a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe, built of basalt; the internal tholos lacks its last courses.
descriptions.NUR3202: The Busurtei nuraghe is located on the summit of the Omomima hill from which a breathtaking panorama can be enjoyed. In the vicinity of the nuraghe, in the medieval period, there was a small village known as Busurtei, Busateri, or Buzarcheri, which belonged to the diocese of Santa Giusta in 1224. About one hundred metres from the nuraghe in a northward direction, there is a spring whose water is said to be the best among the springs of the Sedilo territory.
descriptions.NUR5101: Complex nuraghe or nuragic fortress, apparently earthen and completely levelled to the ground, with only the low courses partially buried remaining. From it, a large part of the Marmilla could be seen.
descriptions.NUR3591: It is located just a few tens of metres from the pavilion. It is a good example of a single-tower (single-tower nuraghe) in a fairly advanced state of degradation. Some signs, however, appear to be later additions, dating from a relatively recent period, and thus not attributable to the Nuragic construction. It seems to have served as a sacrificial altar. Nuraghe of the site in early development. See Càcchile. mu
descriptions.NUR10095: Complex nuraghe with frontal addition and lateral extension, featuring a central tower and two additional towers with bastions, and in the middle lies the courtyard as an integration space.
descriptions.NUR6002: It is a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe with a niche, a ramp, and a chamber surrounded by three niches arranged in a cross. The monument was surrounded by an outer wall extending about 10 metres from the tower, possibly for 380°; it is located on the boundary line between the territorial areas of Dualchi and Sedilo.
descriptions.NUR5554: The Cae Nuraghe is a complex type, featuring a central mastio and at least two towers connected by a bastion, with probable evidence of two additional towers on the south-eastern side, and references to a subterranean gallery. A small village is also present, along with signs of area reuse during the Roman period.
descriptions.NUR6467: It is located to the south-east of the village, not far from the Tirso river. Its state of preservation is very poor, being almost entirely destroyed, just like the nuraghe Jana. However, the extent of the ruins, about 25 x 18 metres, suggests a complex of considerable size. It must also be noted that the long field boundary in which it is situated is entirely constructed from stones taken from the nuraghe itself.
descriptions.NUR6321: It is a single-tower nuraghe, with a stair and a corridor niche, a ground-floor chamber flanked by two subsidiary rooms, and a further room above the corridor. It probably had an added structure (a courtyard?) and an outer wall enclosing various related structures of the adjoining settlement. The nuraghe is easily reached from the road called Valle dei Nuraghi, following an unsurfaced track that lies on private property, so access is not guaranteed.
descriptions.NUR4047: The Caìu nuraghe is undoubtedly the remnant of a corridor nuraghe, that is, two towers enclosing an internal courtyard, which may have been built at the end of the Recent Bronze period. It is located near the Genna Salixi necropolis.
descriptions.NUR15254: Single-tower nuraghe, eroded and enveloped by undergrowth. Likely a complex. Of the monument, several courses of the wall are clearly visible. The perimeter of the central tower and some secondary rooms connected to it can be seen.
descriptions.NUR3447: The monument is located on a natural terraced area, in a hillside region used for grazing. About 300 m to the north-west lies the giants' tomb of Funtana Morta. The nuraghe is almost completely destroyed, and only the external plan can be observed, faintly circular.
descriptions.NUR3074: On a plateau used for cultivation and grazing, only the base row has been located, consisting of large, roughly shaped blocks, possibly belonging to a nuraghe that once existed. Only the plan of a sub-circular form remains visible, which includes a large natural granite block. Due to land clearing works and the use of the ashlar blocks for constructing dry walls, even traces of the collapse are absent.
descriptions.NUR5744: Possible remains of a proto-nuraghe on which later Roman activity also took place, constructing part of a military outpost.
descriptions.NUR6289: Very eroded, so its structure is difficult to identify. To the north of the chamber a flat-laid corridor is visible. To the south an ovoid chamber. Around the remains of the village huts are discernible.
descriptions.NUR4194: The central tower, which has a diameter of about 8 m at its top, is clearly visible. It retains nine courses in height, built in regular sub-square masonry with medium-sized blocks set with rubble in scalloped patterns. The internal upper portion is completely blocked by collapse. Some added structures, hidden by vegetation, are discernible, though only with difficulty.
descriptions.NUR2694:
Located on an acrocoro from which the valley where the Nurritani people lived could be monitored. Bounded by the Roman cippus found in that area by Professor Mastino.

The region south of Tirso extended between Orotelli and the sources of the Tirso to the east of Benetutti, bordering the Goceano to the north and the Barbaria to the south.
descriptions.NUR1923:
It is a complex nuraghe, of which the central tower and three other perimetral towers (although a fourth may also be present on the south-southwest slope) are visible, joined together by a curtain wall with a straight-curvilinear profile.

The latest excavation campaign ended in 2009.

The masonry work is composed of cyclopean basaltic andesite stones, each averaging 3 quintals in weight, with small stones and mud mortar also used in the joints.
descriptions.NUR2787:
The nuraghe still has an accessible tholos, although its top is missing. The entrance lacks its original material all the way up to the top of the tower, perhaps because of a collapse that affected the load-bearing structures of the wall in the past. The masonry has been rebuilt.

The nuraghe was almost certainly used both as a shelter and as an animal pen, and this has allowed it to be preserved in good condition.

The monument has the stairway on the left, with 13 steps still in place.
descriptions.NUR3605: Single-tower tholos nuraghe. In very poor condition, only some stones of the entrance pillar and part of a base course are visible. The entrance is oriented to the west. The nuraghe has undergone numerous plunderings, as can be inferred from the presence of several basaltic stone piles located nearby. Despite this, it is not ruled out that the nuraghe was never fully completed, as in other cases documented in the region.
descriptions.NUR2296:
Small single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe completely destroyed.

The nuraghe was known as Pirastu Fattu, but the owner, Sig. G. Raspa, who was born and lived in those areas, claims the true name is Campo Maggiore.
descriptions.NUR2687: Single-tower built on the summit of a cliff, almost completely collapsed, walls about two metres thick, previously used as a shelter for animals.
descriptions.NUR2717: Complex nuraghe of the type with lateral addition. Built of local basalt. It has a partially collapsed and recently restored vault, in relation to the last use as a sheepfold.
descriptions.NUR10798: It is a proto-nuraghe or early nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR3710: It appears to be a corridor nuraghe, partially collapsed and immersed in vegetation.
descriptions.NUR2140: Single-tower tholos nuraghe, built with large polygonal blocks of local basalt. It retains about 4 to 5 courses, and the internal chamber has collapsed upon itself, being filled with collapse debris. The diameter is about 12 m. The entrance is oriented to the south-east, although it is obscured by the structures of a more recent hut attached to it.
descriptions.NUR3921: Structures related to simple single-tower tholos nuraghe, built from locally sourced polygonal basalt blocks. The remains of the nuraghe, very scarce, are scattered among various contemporaneous structures. It appears to have been a small nuraghe, with only some base courses visible, overlain by a series of detached blocks, reaching a maximum residual height of 1.50 m. The chamber has completely collapsed. The entrance cannot be identified.
descriptions.NUR5858: Single-tower with a circular plan and a chamber completely missing its top; three niches arranged in a cross can be seen. The external wall face remains with five courses. The entrance, located in the south-east, has collapsed.
descriptions.NUR2138: Nuraghe probably of a single-tower tholos type. Almost completely hidden by dense vegetation, it appears as a heap of polygonal basaltic blocks arranged in a disordered manner. Some courses can be read inside a lentisco thicket, on the west side.
descriptions.NUR6363: Near one of the 5 corridor nuraghe present in the territory of the comune of Ghilarza
descriptions.NUR5010: It is a powerful nuraghe made of andesite with a three-lobed plan, resulting from the addition of two secondary towers in front of the central tower, connected by walls enclosing a central courtyard. Nearby stands a large hut; adjacent to it is also a well carefully lined internally, which is also likely dated to the Nuragic period.
descriptions.NUR5391: In the territory of Sanluri there are remains of as many as 15 nuraghe, three of which are complex nuraghe with multiple towers: Corti Sa Perda, Geni, Nuraxi Candelas.
descriptions.NUR1905: Nuraghe no longer existing. The nuraghe is mentioned in documents, in Spanish, by the Bishop's Chapter (12 October 1720), as a reference point, under the name "Nuraxy de Condiazzus/Candiazus". It is also found referenced by Angius as "Nuargi de Candiazzus" (1840), in the IGM maps (1897), by Taramelli (1910?), and by my native Pinuccio Orlando, "Nuarxi de su candiacciu" (Toponyms of the Island).
descriptions.NUR2794: It is also known as Su Canarzu and is recognised as Su Aijanu, which is the name of the plot of land on which it is built. Only the large closure stone and the two jambs are visible. In the surrounding area there are stones worked by man that were used to mark boundaries, and also wild olive or mastic trees.
descriptions.NUR12967: Remains of a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe and village.
descriptions.NUR3152: Unusual rectangular plan with a probable entrance on the southern side, completely collapsed. The northern, western, and eastern sides remain visible. Erected along the edge of a steep slope, likely a temple dedicated to the cult of water, as suggested by two sources (now dry) located at the base of the structure on the southern side. One of the sources is covered by a tholos almost intact, with partial obstruction of the entrance due to a collapse; the other, triangular in plan, shows clear traces of a spring at its apex.
descriptions.NUR4040: Complex nuraghe, collapsed and with only a few buried courses remaining, where a transverse addition followed the original tower.
descriptions.NUR6094: Nuraghe “a tancato” has on the front face of the main tower a wall of irregular shape that encloses a smaller tower and a courtyard situated between the two towers.
descriptions.NUR4787: Complex nuraghe still entirely to be discovered and described
descriptions.NUR1424: Provided with a corresponding Nuragic settlement.
descriptions.NUR3465: Nuraghe surrounded by vegetation. at the edge of the village, single-tower nuraghe with an elliptical plan, still in good conservation.
descriptions.NUR576: Complex nuraghe, it cannot be confidently assigned to any defined type due to the state of degradation or the significant burial of the structures.
descriptions.NUR16406: Of the nuraghe (later converted into an anti-aircraft post during World War II) no traces remain as it was erased by the construction of the restaurant, which was subsequently abandoned.
descriptions.NUR19410: The nuraghe, of which no trace remains, was located at the cape now known as Torre Canai – Turri. The map of Sant'Antioco, drawn by the geographer Maggiore Besson in 1744, suggests that the tower, built at the order of the King of Sardinia, Carlo Emanuele III, in 1757, on the cape “su moru”, was constructed using nuragic structures.
descriptions.NUR5923: Nuraghe in very poor condition of conservation
descriptions.NUR6031: Single-tower with a tholos in polygonal basalt ashlar. Broken lintel. Stairwell on the left side from the entrance corridor. Two niches visible inside the chamber. Traces of huts in the vicinity.
descriptions.NUR4888: Nuraghe Carcina stands in the countryside of Orroli, about 1.5 km south-east of the village. It is abandoned but in fair condition. It appears as a complex nuraghe with two towers clearly visible. The main tower has a surviving height of over 3 metres and is entered through a doorway topped by a fine sloping lintel. This doorway is largely buried and gives access to a chamber with a tholos that is missing its top courses.
descriptions.NUR5212: On an isolated hilltop located about 40 metres south-southwest of the Su Sonadori nuraghe, the remains of a complex nuraghe were observed; currently it is concealed by heaps of rubble stones.
descriptions.NUR5256: At the western end of the elongated Carronca Simoi ridge, beneath the ruins of a small rectangular building, only scant remains of a probable nuraghe are visible; about 20 metres to the east of it, some stone blocks appear to belong to a circular nuragic hut.
descriptions.NUR674: Nuraghe with extensive collapse on the eastern side, difficult to read in plan. Adjacent huts belonging to a probable village.
descriptions.NUR4908: Probably four-lobed, and one of the most imposing in the region. It is indeed composed of a central tower enclosed within a bastion featuring three transverse towers at the front. Currently, the lintel is visible at the level of the collapse that fills the courtyard. Inside the chamber, the entrance passage is visible. From this passage a staircase must have led up to the upper part of the tower, likely to two floors, given the extent of the collapse on the northern slope.
descriptions.NUR4397: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe with a circular plan, of which only the base remains, controlling the valley of the Rio Gutturu Mannu to the east. Extract from the archaeological map of Sant'Andrea Frius drawn by Roberta Relli and Antonio Forci.
descriptions.NUR995: In very poor condition of conservation, only scant elements of the structure remain embedded within the vegetation. Location uncertain, on the left bank of the Orune Channel, adjacent to a water reservoir built during the Second World War.
descriptions.NUR11483: Complex nuraghe with settlement. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR11531: Complex nuraghe, a main tower with a frontal addition of a second tower. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR994: Single-tower built of large white limestone blocks, situated in a cleared area within an olive grove, with a direct drop to the Orune Channel to the north-northeast. Only three courses remain, with a maximum height of about 3 m.
descriptions.NUR3531: On the map provided by the Forests Agency, it appears as such, and shares the same toponym as the nuraghe located a few km to the north-east.
descriptions.NUR1086:
Nuraghe "CASTEDDU" located in the hamlet of Pozzo S. Nicola (municipality of Stintino).

It could be a three-lobed or four-lobed nuraghe, currently buried.

L.L.
descriptions.NUR17933: The eastern section, which enjoys an excellent view over the entire internal gulf of Olbia, is the best preserved. From the ground it rises by about four metres. The lintel is barely visible (see photo), while the entrance is almost completely buried. Traces of the megalithic enclosure are barely discernible, but the abundance of remains and fallen blocks suggests the monument's significance.
descriptions.NUR15002: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe eroded and buried, for which it is not possible to define the structure
descriptions.NUR5132: It is a complex nuraghe consisting of two towers. The original second floor has collapsed, blocking part of the first level.
descriptions.NUR6017: Only a few courses of porphyritic material are visible.
descriptions.NUR5900: Single-tower with its top missing and a collapsed vault inside. The best-preserved section is four metres high and has eight courses. To the south-east the entrance is preserved with an architrave and a window for drainage.
descriptions.NUR3347: Nuraghe with a large village and giants' tomb of attachment. Damaged and overgrown with vegetation. The shape is difficult to identify.
descriptions.NUR2814:
The Cherbos Nuraghe is an extensive heap of rubble that does not allow any definition of the building's plan, though given the dimensions of the collapse it might prove to be a multi-lobed nuraghe.

Around it, over a wide area, the remains of a large circular settlement of huts are clearly visible.

Already in the time of the Taramelli, the monument appeared in very poor condition: “ruined: a pile of ruins about 2 m high is visible;”
descriptions.NUR1579: It is located within the territory of the comune of Sassari. It is heavily eroded and surrounded by dense vegetation.
descriptions.NUR3473: Diroccato, only the first courses are visible. It must have been of considerable size, having a base diameter of about 15 metres.
descriptions.NUR2736:
The nuraghe is located near the settlement of Birori and is composed of a modest hill that has formed over time on top of the ruins of the monument.

From the available evidence, it is a four-lobed nuraghe with a central tower enclosed by a bastion with four corner towers. Around the fortress, clear traces of an outer wall are visible, as well as the circular profile of numerous huts.
descriptions.NUR2803: The nuraghe, as shown on the maps of the former cadastral survey, is listed under the name "Chessalzu". Only a few buried courses remain.
descriptions.NUR11141: Nuraghe with frontal bilobate addition. Today completely submerged by the waters of the Cuga basin. It belongs to the complex of nuraghes surrounding the Chessedu Cuga valley.
descriptions.NUR4867: Impressive nuragic site. Various hypotheses and recent analyses suggest the remains of a quadrilobate (or pentalobate) complex nuraghe. Currently open to the public, the northern tower is accessible. A central well leads to internal chambers and extends through narrow, precarious tunnels, suggesting a complex and intricately structured layout.
descriptions.NUR2715: Single-tower tholos nuraghe built from locally sourced polygonal basalt blocks. It is almost entirely covered by climbing vegetation, especially on the N–NE exposed face. The west face is the most visible, with structural remains exceeding 4 m in height, while the tower as a whole reaches a total height of about 7 m.
descriptions.NUR737: Always within a private plot of land lies the base of this nuraghe. A probable presence of a village in the immediate vicinity.
descriptions.NUR3423: Reduced to the extreme act of ruin. Only some basally arranged stones, variously shaped, remain, all set within a large mass of mastic wood.
descriptions.NUR5369: Nuraghe and structure of uncertain definition
descriptions.NUR2269: Under current conditions, there is no evidence of lithic or ceramic material scattered on the ground; however, the presence of possible village structures cannot be ruled out, whose remains might have been obscured on the surface by land transformations and land use.
descriptions.NUR3897: The structure remains only with traces; the site is neither accessible nor easily legible at present. Following the incursion of the Greek Church, Greek-Orthodox monks and hermits taught the inhabitants the production of crude bricks in the Eastern style, made from mud and straw (ladrini), which were used for building houses, with the rubble from the Nuraghe Zira serving as the foundation.
descriptions.NUR19888: It is located on Cuccuru Cireddu at 130 m above sea level. It is in poor condition and is almost completely surrounded by lentisco. It is visually connected to the Nuraghe Monte Eghedda, about 1 km away, and to the Nuraghe S'Omu and S'Orku, about 2 km away by air. According to documents from the Municipality of Maracalagonis, there is also a necropolis, possibly "Roman", as numerous artefacts are found around the nuraghe over a wide radius.
descriptions.NUR5769:
More precisely, it is a proto-nuraghe or corridor nuraghe.

It appears in the maps of the former cadastral survey and is listed as Nuraghe Piraruja.
descriptions.NUR5228:
The nuraghe was raised directly on the rock, and it appears that its plan was adapted to the irregularities of the surface, since on multiple levels along the slopes of the hill, wall constructions are visible.

At the summit, the monument, now almost completely destroyed, seems to have an elongated plan, but its poor state of preservation and clandestine excavations undermine the overall legibility of the structure.
descriptions.NUR4387:
In its current state of preservation, it is possible to speculate—based on only a few identifiable wall segments— that the monument extended over multiple levels, following the different elevations of the rocky peak on which it was built.

Its main axis may have been oriented north-south, but the position of the entrance or the planimetric layout of the chamber remains undefined.
descriptions.NUR5576: It consists of a central nucleus belonging to the type known as "corridor nuraghe", older and structurally distinct from the "tholos" type (as the roof is not a false dome but a flat-laid structure). Within this nucleus two rooms are identified: one is circular, with a diameter of about 7 metres, the other oval, with a diameter of about  8 metres, connected by a covered corridor with a flat-laid roof.
descriptions.NUR3114:
It is in very poor conservation condition.

It is a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe, circular (diameter 11.50 m), built using large blocks of limestone. At present, the wall face is preserved to a maximum height of 1.80 m on three stone courses to the south and 0.80 m on a single course to the north.
descriptions.NUR6268: Name and/or location might not be accurate.
descriptions.NUR658: Name and/or location might not be accurate.
descriptions.NUR4670: Proto-nuraghe of elliptical or sub-elliptical profile
descriptions.NUR6294: DIRROCCATO NURAGHE WITH ABOUT SIX COURSES EXTERIOR TO GROUND LEVEL
descriptions.NUR6188:
