The monument stands on the edge of a steep rock face that drops sheer to the south, in an area of particular interest for the presence of numerous archaeological monuments, both prehistoric and Nuragic.

The building has a roughly quadrangular plan and is crossed by a through corridor flanked by opposing pairs of large niches; the corners are rounded, the walls where the entrances open are straight in profile to the ESE and slightly concave to the ENE.
descriptions.NUR20354: It is a quadrilobate rectangular structure very similar to Santa Barbara in Macomer. It has a ground area of about 400 m².
descriptions.NUR5924: The nuragic site is located in the area "Su cuccuru de i Zannas", in the outskirts of the village. It is a five-lobed nuraghe equipped with an internal courtyard, whose initial construction dates to the Late Bronze Age, with subsequent phases of reuse extending from the late Punica period to the Roman Republican period. Adjacent to the monument stands an ancient–late medieval settlement that was inhabited at least as late as the 7th century BCE.
descriptions.NUR3390: The Nuraghe Codas is a single-tower (single-tower nuraghe) built from basalt blocks, located about 7 km south of Paulilatino. Together with the nuraghes Forreddos, De Mesu, and Su Guzzu, it forms a quadrilateral across the territories of Zerfaliu and Paulilatino. Despite having suffered several collapses, it has retained the integrity of its grandeur.
descriptions.NUR5507:
Very deeply buried four-lobed nuraghe, probably still preserving intact environments.

Access to it is currently impossible.
descriptions.NUR6352:
Single-tower tholos nuraghe located in the midst of a dense thicket of cork and holm oaks in the Sos Paris region, at the site of Codinazza. Four base courses are visible, constructed from large polygonal basalt blocks locally sourced, reaching a maximum height of about 2.50 m. The base diameter of the nuraghe is about 13 m.

The internal chamber has collapsed at its upper portion, and the remaining structure is subjected to a significant debris accumulation resulting from the collapse.
descriptions.NUR777: It is a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe; currently two courses of the base remain standing; stones both inside and outside the structure are still present. The entrance is clearly visible, while the lintel cannot be identified with certainty. Built of basaltic stone, it dominates the entire Gulf of Gonone to the south. From its summit, the nuraghe Buca d'Irghiriai can be seen, located on the same-named pass.
descriptions.NUR2693:
The nuraghe, collapsed internally, shows a fairly irregular plan, typical more of proto-nuraghe than of true tholos nuraghe.

For further details:

eprints.uniss.it/9371/1/Merella_S_Indagini_territoriali... pages 339-340
descriptions.NUR3686:
This nuraghe rises on a hillock facing the village of Mara.

It is well marked but also completely overlooked. To reach this monument one must wend through tall, thorny scrubland that makes it almost invisible. For this reason it is difficult to describe, especially by a non-specialist.

It appears to be of corridor type.
descriptions.NUR2753: Nuraghe built of calcare ashlar. On top of it a shelter was constructed with the erection of new walls made of small calcare ashlar. To the north, at the entrance, there is a concio with a carved recess.
descriptions.NUR6318: It is one of many nuraghes in the Thiesino area, of which today only a few remains can be identified.
descriptions.NUR3119: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe in excellent state of conservation. Corridor entrance with a pointed end and an internal staircase on the left.
descriptions.NUR6230: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe, in basalt, with its tholos collapsed.
descriptions.NUR5781: Complex nuraghe with remains of a village; in 2016 it was surrounded by dense vegetation, making it impossible to visit.
descriptions.NUR6439: It is a good example of a nuraghe with a subsidiary staircase and a sub-floor chamber. Access is possible to examine its structure, which projects above with white, friable limestone blocks, set within a group of oaks, ashes, and tassels that create a pleasant and evocative atmosphere. The nuraghe is almost completely covered by soil eroded from the slope, so much so that it is almost fully buried. Nuraghe of the valley of the Judge, of the king of Torres.
descriptions.NUR3764: Eroded by the force of water
descriptions.NUR6050: Conca e Bentu (Porta del vento). Single-tower nuraghe built with cyclopean technique; it features a central chamber with three niches arranged in a cross, only the ones on the right and left sides are visible, the central one has collapsed. Access to the chamber is via a corridor with a lintel, which on the right has a storage niche and on the left the beginning of the staircase leading to the upper floor or to the terrace.
descriptions.NUR2799: Simple single-tower nuraghe, in very poor condition, with traces of a possible settlement.
descriptions.NUR552: On the north-eastern tip, some alignments of small stones suggest the remains of a nuraghe tower; on the south-eastern tip, a short curved wall segment is present, and in the depression to the north, a closure wall runs between the two tips.
descriptions.NUR944: Single-tower nuraghe stands on a cliff face with a sheer drop, along which the structure has collapsed, rendering it inaccessible but with a base at least 12 m in diameter. Around it, the remains of a megalithic wall, intended for site defence, are present.
descriptions.NUR4241: The tower at Conca Santinta must have had a function extending beyond a purely strategic one, since many stone-working debris have been found on the site, and this is further supported by the fact that the minerals composing the outcrop have particularly favourable characteristics for use in stone-working and ceramic production.
descriptions.NUR3919: Located at the base of a cairn on the southern side of Berchida valley, there stands a small village composed of several huts built with dry stone masonry. Initially identified as a nuraghe, it actually lacks the defining characteristics of one.
descriptions.NUR2587: Nuraghe completely immersed in vegetation and partially eroded due to this. Structure not easily legible
descriptions.NUR1026: The poor state of preservation does not allow a clear reading of the structure, which nevertheless appears to be a single-tower nuraghe with an elliptical shape.
descriptions.NUR6465: Only faint traces of the nuraghe remain.
descriptions.NUR5967: Corridor nuraghe with a tholos and relatively intact. It has the peculiarity of a double symmetric entrance, as seen in corridor nuraghe, although it features a tholos. In excellent condition and carefully maintained by the community of S'Aspru.
descriptions.NUR6257: Nuraghe with buried entrance. Access to the interior is possible through a passage leading to a staircase chamber. The chamber features three niches, with the tholos intact. In the area, several baetyls and cremation urns are also present.
descriptions.NUR4930: The nuraghe is in a state of considerable degradation, and there are artificial structures also inside the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR4492: The nuraghe is in very poor condition, reduced merely to some courses.
descriptions.NUR15939: In the current census this monument is listed as "Nuraghe su Nidu su Cojvu".
descriptions.NUR4716:
Corridor nuraghe, affected by a conspicuous collapse, built with locally sourced polygonal stone blocks. Among the remains of the collapse of the imposing curtain wall, the perimeters of the upper portions of some oval chambers are discernible.

To the north-west, traces of pre- and historical occupation are observed, consisting of short and partially concealed wall segments.

Santoni refers to it as nuraghe Moru Nieddu B.
descriptions.NUR8274: Complex nuraghe almost completely devastated by the construction of a aqueduct with a cistern directly situated upon the nuraghe itself.
descriptions.NUR3149: The nuraghe is of a complex type, probably with a frontal addition, although the poor state of conservation and the abundant presence of spontaneous vegetation on the ruins do not allow for a clear interpretation. The structure is built from local basalt blocks arranged in polygonal masonry. The central tower, with its chamber collapsed, and a bastion enclosing the structure, with two possible towers on the front face, remain.
descriptions.NUR15047: Complex nuraghe, partially eroded and buried, for which it is not possible to define the structure.
descriptions.NUR704: The remains of the nuraghe Corongiu are located in the territory of Ollastra, in the area of Serra Laccus. Unfortunately, the monument has been almost completely dismantled. It was presumably a tholos nuraghe, although its planimetric layout is not clear.
descriptions.NUR4764:
It is a proto-nuraghe situated in a dominant position at the edge of Pranu and Muru, within the basaltic lava flow area in the territory of Nurri, east of the Flumendosa river course. From its red crown, the mountains of Santa Vittoria extend to the Gennargentu, and below, the canyon where the approximately 17 kilometres of the Medio Flumendosa lake were excavated.

The corridor nuraghe combines its austere simplicity with the grandeur of the landscape, which can be admired in all directions from the site.
descriptions.NUR2116: Complex nuraghe of which a circular area remains in the central position. It could be the central tower, for which the full perimeter outline is preserved, although only for one course. The inner wall face of the tower is visible on the sides oriented from north to south-east. The tower is attached to the edge of a rocky cliff, projecting sharply to the north. Attached to the original tower is a building body, of which the points of contact are preserved, oriented to the west and north-west.
descriptions.NUR3720: What remains of the probable nuraghe rests on a granitic rock outcrop, from which, very likely, some portion was incorporated into the wall face. Currently, only a half-circle of roughly shaped granitic blocks, of medium and large size, is preserved in plan. At the base of the rock outcrop, at a slightly lower elevation, two short stretches of wall remain, whose function cannot be precisely determined due to the state of preservation of the monument.
descriptions.NUR3834: It is in a severe state of ruin and the external wall face is "bulging" towards the north-east. Unfortunately, even for it, time is running out. Too old and forgotten, and subjected to the plundering of treasure hunters, it is exposed to every illegal act. Despite itself, it once appeared in the national broadcast of Rai Tre, "in the final minute". It belongs to that group of nuraghes with a subterranean chamber. Its visit is strongly discouraged.
descriptions.NUR4395: More likely it is an ancient nuragic hut.
descriptions.NUR15043:
Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe, buried, with an indeterminate structure.

Traditionally the local people place it near the river. Visually it appears only as a circle of stones at ground level.
descriptions.NUR4001: The Corrulia or Currulia nuraghe is located in the valley of Flumendosa, within the territory of Villasalto. To reach it, one must cross a bridge leading to a farmstead, near which the nuraghe stands. It is a single-tower nuraghe now missing its top, in a state of abandonment.
descriptions.NUR21100: Nuraghe heavily collapsed, located in the heart of the city
descriptions.NUR5568:
Almost in the city, on a hilltop from which Tossilo is seen, this single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe stands out, completely ruined. Its configuration is the classic one, with a niche on the left side of the southern access, south-east, and a staircase leading to the upper level on the left. Inside the tholos, despite being completely overgrown with brambles, three typical niches can still be distinguished.

A splendid place for meditative sunsets of nostalgic contemplation.
descriptions.NUR4980: Nuraghe in very poor condition, only a few external points are visible, many stones are scattered in the adjacent ground, and almost the entire structure is enveloped by vegetation.
descriptions.NUR5685: Single-tower nuraghe in good state of conservation, missing the lintel and access to the staircase leading to the upper floor. Maximum height five metres.
descriptions.NUR12149: It is a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe with a settlement now completely destroyed.
descriptions.NUR976: Remains of a small single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe built of limestone.
descriptions.NUR5077: Complex nuraghe with a main tower and an additional tower on the eastern side.
descriptions.NUR5318: Remains of a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe built in basalt.
descriptions.NUR3355:
Corvos, apparently a single-tower nuraghe, is in fact a complex nuraghe, whose central tower—bicoloured—is still preserved in excellent condition, the lower level in limestone and the upper in trachyte.

Once past the entrance threshold, an unusual antioral staircase immediately comes into view, starting on the left side of the corridor; the chamber, featuring three niches and significantly buried, retains an intact tholos about 5 metres high. The first floor, however, has collapsed.
descriptions.NUR3305: Single-tower nuraghe probably. Completely covered by vegetation, making its structure difficult to interpret.
descriptions.NUR3850: The nuraghe located at the summit of a rugged hilltop, characterized by dense undergrowth, is built on a granitic rocky outcrop that provides an excellent view of the areas below. The monument, in a severe state of degradation, is a simple single-tower nuraghe with a sub-circular plan, barely discernible due to the extent of the collapse.
descriptions.NUR16859: Sparingly visible and identifiable, completely engulfed by mastic and cisto. Presence of numerous large trachyte boulders.
descriptions.NUR5019: Single-tower nuraghe now completely destroyed, nearby remains dense material deposits extending from the Abealzu face up to the imperial Roman period. The site is located in a locality accessible only by hiking near one of the forest watchtower structures on the slopes of Monte Arci. The nuraghe, hidden beneath thick vegetation, is in very poor condition.
descriptions.NUR3830: Single-tower nuraghe with its top missing; the position of the nuraghe is uncertain, and it does not appear marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR1055:
This is an archaeological area that cannot be defined because of the collapses and the vegetation. However, the data collected lead me to determine that it is a complex nuraghe, consisting of an ancient tower surrounded by a massive wall (bastion) with a continuous, concave-convex profile that probably encloses a courtyard, and some minor towers.

All around, the remains of walls (outer wall?) built with blocks of considerable size are visible.
descriptions.NUR2565:
It is a single-tower with a niche, a ramp, and a chamber bordered by two niches.

The tower, circular in plan (diameter 11.60 m), survives to a maximum height of 6.00 m with 14 courses on the north-west side, while at the entrance the height is 5.20 m on 11 courses; the south-east wall, however, is largely collapsed.
descriptions.NUR2063: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe with the tower collapsed inward, leaving only the entrance portal and about five courses of the tower.
descriptions.NUR2747: Complex-type nuraghe with lateral additions, featuring two secondary towers added to the main tower. Built with local basalt blocks arranged in fairly regular courses. The entrance to the main tower is located to the east and appears trapezoidal, with an architrave formed by three irregular blocks, topped by an irregular-shaped window for drainage.
descriptions.NUR3369: The Crabia nuraghe is a single-tower type, built on two superimposed storeys that are still intact, each with a circular central chamber roofed with a tholos. Its distinctive feature is the presence of two staircases: one to the left of the entrance corridor, leading to the first floor and perfectly preserved, while the other, running in the opposite direction to the first, is concealed in a niche inside the tower on the right and leads to a hidden niche on the first floor.
descriptions.NUR1434: The nuraghe has about eight courses of remaining wall. The external lintel at the entrance is missing. On the left side the staircase is visible, and on the opposite side a passage niche. The tholos chamber is missing its top and is almost entirely filled with vegetation, debris from collapse, and sediments, reaching a height at the back of the walls that exceeds the arches of the niches, except for one—on the left—where only the terminal portion is visible.
descriptions.NUR4725: This nuraghe is just one of the countless ones found throughout the territory. Its condition is commendable, but maintenance work was required by the municipality due to several landslides.
descriptions.NUR5066: It is built of cyclopean andesite blocks and consists of a large central tower joined to three towers. Of these, two show their entire interior structure: precisely the east and the west towers. It would be possible to enter the west one to explore the inside of the nuraghe, but I had neither the time nor the wish to risk it. Up to seven courses of the central tower are visible, reaching a height of almost three metres, while up to six courses of the west tower are visible, reaching a height of two and a half metres.
descriptions.NUR5584:
The previously unrecorded proto-nuraghe Crapianu appears to represent a decidedly original example among the early nuragic buildings known as proto-nuraghe.

The most significant feature lies in the fact that it preserves, within a large rectangular chamber, unmistakable traces of a floor support (risega) that once supported the first-floor chamber, at a height of about two metres and fifty centimetres.
descriptions.NUR6252: It is almost certainly a single-tower (single-tower nuraghe) emerging from a cliff, highlighting its likely invulnerability to a probable hostile attack. About twenty courses of stones are arranged in circular patterns. The tholos, which is inaccessible, is probably intact.
descriptions.NUR4653: A few surviving courses of the Crastu nuraghe, located within the village of the same name
descriptions.NUR6284: Of the corridor nuraghe, possibly with a sub-elliptical plan, only some fragments of granite walling from the first course of the base remain.
descriptions.NUR6156: Probable proto-nuraghe, of semicircular plan attached to a rocky mass. Presence of two menhirs
descriptions.NUR5946: It has an elliptical plan and is built on a granite bedrock outcrop. The interior, completely collapsed, suggests the presence of a chamber located to the north, which has a curved layout. Currently, the entrance is not visible, but it is likely to have been situated on the northern side, as that side was most accessible. During the clearing works, various Late Medieval decorative items were found, decorated with "stamped" patterns.
descriptions.NUR918: The nuraghe, of simple type, retains three-quarters of the external perimeter, while on the south side—where, presumably, the entrance should have been located—it has suffered collapse. It has an externally sub-circular plan and is built with roughly shaped granite blocks laid in irregular courses. The interior is not discernible due to the debris of the collapse. Nevertheless, from the top of the surviving section, the circular outline of the chamber can be observed.
descriptions.NUR5716: Four-lobed nuraghe, with four towers at the corners of the quadrangular bastion and an internal courtyard facing the central tower's entrance.
descriptions.NUR15177: The entire oval perimeter outline is preserved. The external wall face reaches its maximum height on the western side, where eight courses of polycyclic stones are counted. Unfortunately, the internal space is covered by vegetation and collapse, preventing any view of its contents.
descriptions.NUR19543: The nuraghe, probably of complex structure, was built on the same rocky ridge as the corridor nuraghe, to the north of it. It shows a very extensive collapse. The central tower can be identified thanks to the presence of two courses of boulders that survive in their original position. On the rocky ridge there is a curvilinear wall running from the west side round to the south-south-east side. On the south side stretches of walling, not well defined because of the collapses, appear to link the two nuraghi.
descriptions.NUR4418: The central tower is visible for 4 courses in cyclopean blocks. It is probable that at least 4 courses lie beneath the surface. To the east and north, the remains of two secondary towers are visible, only partially discernible. Superficially, some wall connections can be seen.
descriptions.NUR11023: On the remains of the nuraghe Crixionis, during the Second World War, a concrete fortification was built, protected against small arms fire, serving as an observatory for the Coastal Battery positions in the area.
descriptions.NUR18441: Likely three-lobed, with only the base courses remaining.
descriptions.NUR3570: Complex nuraghe of mixed type, consisting of a main tower with an internally partially collapsed chamber, a second tower on the south-western side, and an imposing body traversed by a corridor that appears to terminate in a courtyard containing an additional tower. The interpretation of the monument is greatly hampered by dense vegetation, significant erosion, and the unusual nature of its construction.
descriptions.NUR17081: Single-tower nuraghe built of basalt. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR2166: Single-tower nuraghe built of basalt. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR14798: It is located in the area of the great Nurra land reclamation and is one of the nuraghes in the region equipped with a mezzanine or mezzanine floor. Complex nuraghe constructed from recently shaped sandstone blocks, well preserved, situated within a private agricultural property used for horticultural and fruit cultivation. It was repurposed during World War II for the construction of bunkers. From 1940 to 1943, Nuraghe Cubalciada was incorporated into the defensive system of the 204th Coastal Division.
descriptions.NUR5993:
It is a proto-nuraghe; the tower survives to a maximum height of 5.50 m.

Within a radius of 400 m there are 3 giants' tombs, one nuragic spring, and 5 baetyls.
descriptions.NUR4700: The Cuccurada archaeological complex stands on the southern tip of the Mogoro basalt plateau of “Sa Struvina”, in a position commanding a wide view over the Campidano plain and the Rio Mogoro valley. Excavations carried out from 1994 to the present have revealed the presence of monumental structures attributable to different periods: a megalithic wall and a cyclopean structure with an elliptical plan (Cuccurada A), attributable to the developed Eneolithic (Monte Claro Culture, 2700–2200 BC).
descriptions.NUR4083: The actual nuraghe no longer exists, though a section of the perimeter walls is still visible at the summit of the hill. The hill's shape suggests it may conceal more than what is presently apparent.
descriptions.NUR3879: Single-tower tholos nuraghe. The structures are completely enveloped by vegetation, appearing as a small natural rise covered with moss, bushes, and debris. Although the type of monument can only be barely discerned from observation, it is plausible that, once freed from the vegetation, it might reveal itself in good state of preservation.
descriptions.NUR10527:
Nuragic settlement with ceramics from the middle and late Bronze Age, following deep industrial excavations, the site has recently undergone significant changes.

The single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe has been demolished and the construction stones have been removed, though the materials are still visible.
descriptions.NUR14959: Damaged nuraghe of which it is not possible to define shape and dimensions
descriptions.NUR4579: The structure's upper portion is visible because it is buried. It consists of a larger tower joined by walls to a smaller tower. The features best visible and documented are in the north, where 2–3 courses of the towers and the wall connecting them emerge. The stone used is limestone.
descriptions.NUR4257:
The monument has a complex plan in which at least two bodies can be distinguished, one leaning against the other, developing along a north-east–south-west axis 16.50 m long.

The perimeter of the north-eastern body, which has almost completely collapsed and is partly buried, can be traced only at the point where it joins the other tower and in part on the western side.

It may have been an elliptical element whose major diameter measures about 7 m.
descriptions.NUR4806: The nuraghe is completely hidden by the earth and vegetation, which give it the appearance of a humble hillock (in Sardinian "cuccuru") several metres high rising above the waters of the State salines; the material conceals the millennial structure.
descriptions.NUR3163: Nuraghe belonging to the category of "uncompleted"
descriptions.NUR2678: Nuraghe belonging to the category of "uncompleted"
descriptions.NUR15639: Nuraghe belonging to the category of "uncompleted"
descriptions.NUR15011: Damaged and buried nuraghe, whose structure cannot be defined.
descriptions.NUR15013: Damaged and buried nuraghe, whose structure cannot be defined.
descriptions.NUR15016: Damaged and buried nuraghe, whose structure cannot be defined.
descriptions.NUR14996: Damaged and buried nuraghe, whose structure cannot be defined.
descriptions.NUR15045: Damaged and buried nuraghe, whose structure cannot be defined.
descriptions.NUR15049: Damaged and buried nuraghe, whose structure cannot be defined.
descriptions.NUR15034: Damaged and buried nuraghe, whose structure cannot be defined.
descriptions.NUR4666: The basal courses of the single-tower nuraghe are visible among the bushes.
descriptions.NUR4502: The structure identified here has an unclear form; it may represent a small complex nuraghe built upon a previous proto-nuraghe. Fragments of ceramics from the Nur I-IIA/B periods are observed nearby. It could also be a small mixed nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR11039:
It is located in the territory of the comune of Marrubiu (OR).

More precisely, it is a proto-nuraghe or corridor nuraghe with an elliptical plan, accompanied by a large settlement of circular huts.
descriptions.NUR4594: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe, of which only a few ashlar pieces remain, not easily distinguishable. Occupied until the Iron Age.
descriptions.NUR3140: It appears to be a single-tower, though unfortunately this has been reduced to ruin. Only a few features remain, as the site is covered by a soil fill and an unstructured heap of stones resulting from land reclamation, but due to historical and cultural degradation, its essence has been destroyed. mu
descriptions.NUR19453: It is very ruined and overgrown with dense vegetation.
descriptions.NUR1577: It is very ruined and overgrown with dense vegetation.
descriptions.NUR11019: It is buried in a cucuzzolo, a sardo cucuru. The upper part, certainly the top of the main tower, is accessible. We observe concentric courses of large stones. At the summit, small openings are visible; if dug, they would lead into the structure.
descriptions.NUR5815: Single-tower nuraghe belonging to the complex of nuraghes in the Cuga valley. Currently almost invisible and impenetrable due to the thick vegetation.
descriptions.NUR4425: One of the most important and nearby historical testimonies to the commune of Arbus is the nuraghe of Cugui, one of the most original in Sardinia. Located on the summit of a hill facing Fluminimaggiore, the nuraghe of Cugui is easily accessible from the Canau area, known for its spring. The nuraghe has three towers, one of which is accessible, although the taller ones may present considerable difficulties for visitors to enter.
descriptions.NUR3904: The structures, very likely to be interpreted as remnants of a single-tower tholos nuraghe, are literally concealed by a mass of mastic. Some base courses can be seen, composed of locally quarried polygonal basalt blocks, on the south side. The nuraghe is practically destroyed.
descriptions.NUR19636: It is a small single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe. The ruin reaches a maximum height of about 2 metres and consists of a few overlapping courses of medium-sized roughly worked stones. The external diameter of the nuraghe is about 11 metres. It is built with a mixture of basalt, limestone, and schist stones. The state of conservation of the monument is precarious.
descriptions.NUR1085: Likely single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe, built of calcareous stone.
descriptions.NUR5436: The remains of the Lepuri nuraghe are not easily identifiable. Of the nuraghe, located possibly to guard a stream flowing a little distance to the south, only a few discontinuous wall segments remain, suggesting a structure of elongated plan built using large, unworked or very roughly shaped stones.
descriptions.NUR5424: Complex nuraghe with a central tower, with a facade featuring two additional towers. Surrounding it are the remains of what must have been the village.
descriptions.NUR3847: Extensive ruin remains only a small portion of masonry, composed of medium-sized stones arranged on two or three circles.
descriptions.NUR3294: The remains of the nuraghe "CULZU" are located in the municipal territory of Torralba (SS), in the area of Segadu, just tens of metres from the Longu nuraghe, in the so-called Valley of the Nuraghes; it is a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe built of basalt with a chamber surrounded by three niches. It has an entrance and a passage leading to the chamber; the dome is missing its top and various trees have grown inside the central chamber;
descriptions.NUR4560: Four-lobed nuraghe in which a bronze figurine and the hull of a boat, also bronze, shaped like a four-tower nuraghe, were found.
descriptions.NUR6215: The building has collapsed on the south side and dense vegetation conceals its full extent. The central tower measures about 12 m in diameter and its present height is 7.30 m. At present a short stretch of the stairwell is visible on the north side, where the facing survives and may be the remains of the bastion of a complex building. The nuraghe stands on natural outcrops of trachyte. Around the nuraghe lies an extensive settlement that was also occupied in Roman times.
descriptions.NUR3819: Remains of a nuraghe, of which only the bases remain.
descriptions.NUR5328: Complex nuraghe with a main tower and bastions featuring two additional towers. On the north side there are two further towers with a wall, located at the narrowest point of the Taccu Ara plateau. Built in basalt.
descriptions.NUR8045: THE NURAGHE THAT THE FOREST HIDES – Nuragic base, probably still under construction and never completed, as there is no evidence of collapse; the built structure rises about 1.8 m above the campagna level.
descriptions.NUR3511: It is located within the territory of the comune of Nuoro. Only a small remains, but nearby there is a giants' tomb.
descriptions.NUR4733: Between Tratalias and S. Giovanni Suergiu, near Is Loccis. In very poor condition.
descriptions.NUR5819: Interesting is the nuragic structure at Donna Ciccia, a name derived from the toponym of one of the fields on which it stands; locally it is better known as "sa traversa" because it lies at the intersection of roads leading to Sassari and to Ozieri. It immediately stands out for the colouring of the stones used in its construction. Part of it is still accessible, despite being in an advanced state of degradation. I would urge any reporters to visit it with reasoned justification "and not merely on hearsay".
descriptions.NUR3525: The nuraghe, near an agricultural farm, features a small tower added.
descriptions.NUR4396: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe. The central tower is clearly visible for 10 courses. There is a possible trace of an outer wall preceding the northern tholos. The southern-eastern tower is completely collapsed. The nuraghe appears to have collapsed upon itself at some point in the past, not recently. At a short distance, a structure is identified that suggests it may be a dolmen.
descriptions.NUR5461: It is located within the territory of the comune of Guasila, inside a private plot planted with Mediterranean scrub.
descriptions.NUR4399:
nuraghe, probably a complex, with a village.

In the area, successive occupations after the Nuragic period are evident, evidenced by the dispersion of historical-era fragments in the soil.

The complex, difficult to access, is currently covered by dense vegetation that conceals the huts, making a correct planimetric reading and the full understanding of its layout extremely difficult.
descriptions.NUR4589: Only a few traces of the completely collapsed settlement remain to the south. Excavated by illegal diggers. Remains of the wall faces are visible.
descriptions.NUR2584:
The nuraghe is located on the outskirts of Sassari, on SS 127 towards Osilo, behind a sheepfold, and sits on the edge of a cliff in a dominant position overlooking the valley below. In addition to being on the edge of the cliff, it is built upon a natural bastion, as it stands atop a block of limestone detached from the cliff face itself.

Various structures of uncertain chronology are attached to the main tower.
descriptions.NUR5544: It is a complex nuraghe, partially eroded, located at the centre (mesu) of a wide valley bordering the Alto Oristanese plateau.
descriptions.NUR3795: Among the Florinas nuraghes of simple tholos type, the De Mesu nuraghe (a single-tower, circular structure fairly well preserved) is particularly significant, featuring three deep niches arranged in a cross pattern within the chamber.
descriptions.NUR10185: At the level of the great ruin, only a few polygonal stones from the basal circles remain, often roughly shaped. The main entrance is evident in the south-east direction. The surrounding area is rich in ancient traces and artifacts. Of interest is a structure on bachile that may date back only a few centuries.
descriptions.NUR1892: Nuraghe of which only a small amount remains due to construction in immediately adjacent areas
descriptions.NUR11529: Small nuraghe facing the Giants' Tomb of Coddu Vecchju. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR3666: The Orizanne nuraghe is located alongside the road from Nuoro to Bitti. Like other nuraghes, it has a large oak tree inside the collapsed tholos.
descriptions.NUR10070: In total ruin, only a few large subsquared stones remain. The older inhabitants of the area recall its existence, though only a few basal circles are known. When the Sassari Tempio fast-moving road was constructed, excavation work affected more than one site, in total disregarding their immense historical value, in order to serve as a foundation for the road network.
descriptions.NUR4011: It consists of the ruins of a site and a settlement that originally must have had medium to large dimensions. Indeed, the central tower, which was likely imposing, remains only with its base, lateral walls, and lintel at the entrance; at least three other towers and extensive fortifications along the entire perimeter of the small hill on which the site is situated.
descriptions.NUR4117: Tholos nuraghe. There were two towers; one has been completely dismantled to build the drystone wall that runs along the mountain. On the south-east side the tower stands over 4 m high, while the interior is blocked by a layer of earth and debris that makes it inaccessible. Beside it is a cave recently explored by the Uras caving group.
descriptions.NUR1861: Complex nuraghe, of which remain the central tower with its facing and fragments of walling from three possible lateral towers. Of the central tower, three courses of slabs are preserved; unfortunately, vegetation and rubble accumulated from collapses conceal its inner wall face. The central tower is surrounded by remnants of a bastion wall, with fragments of curtain walls aligning the remains of three possible lateral towers.
descriptions.NUR2641: It is a single-tower nuraghe with the tholos collapsed. Only a few courses of masonry and part of the internal niches remain, although these have been used locally by herders as a place to store goods and also as a site for various plastic waste.
descriptions.NUR10489: Another nuraghe completely destroyed, but partially visible on the maps of Sardinia from 1954 and 1977.
descriptions.NUR3135: The name is the one given in: Archaeological Maps of Sardinia by Antonio Taramelli.
descriptions.NUR4814: Nuraghe of the final phase of the Nuragic period, built on the cliff that dominates the valley of the San Pietro Paradiso waterfall, also known locally as "Cascata de s'ascedu".
descriptions.NUR10126:
From a distance, it appears as a rubble hill that scarcely suggests any prehistoric monument. We are facing a colossal structure that offers multiple interpretations, which I personally classify among those located at low elevation.

Nuraghe of the (land) closed to the re. The presence of the term "re" almost certainly indicates that the site belonged in the time of the giudicale to the personal or familial estate of one of the judges or kings of Torres or of Logudoro. See Tanca de su re. mu
descriptions.NUR5386: Up to six courses survive for over two metres in height, in large worked sandstone blocks laid and fitted to give the tower perfect circularity. The perfection of the shape is not only horizontal but also vertical. What is visible is the central tower, and it was probably a single-tower nuraghe, but since there is a high mound to the south-east of the visible tower, the presence of something else there cannot be ruled out. The visible tower must have at least four or five courses below ground, judging by the height of the mound of ashlars and earth surrounding the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR12244: Single-tower nuraghe in the territory of Oniferi, located just tens of metres from the necropolis of Sas Concas, is situated in the valley below near the river. Only some blocks remain visible.
descriptions.NUR3271: In total ruin, the few remaining fragments are incorporated into a section of the perimeter curtain wall. Its existence is remembered only through the historical accounts of the adjacent landowners. A few stones of medium and large size are barely visible.
descriptions.NUR1903: The present structures suggest the remains of a possible proto-nuraghe. From a high vantage point, at least two rectangular rooms can be distinguished, while the rest of the structure is hidden by vegetation. Unfortunately, the various field clearing operations, followed by the accumulation of stones above the ancient structures, create doubts about the true nature of any other possible buildings.
descriptions.NUR4660: Corridor nuraghe, hypothesis supported by the shape of the entrance (lintelled). Site easily accessible and usable. Traces of ceramics found outside suggest non-regular excavations. About 200 metres away there is a giants' tomb in the style of an allée couverte, of which some scholars speak as an incomplete work.
descriptions.NUR5794: It had a very complex plan.
descriptions.NUR4168: A double curtain wall of large stones appears along the edge of the hilltop, enclosing a previous Nuragic structure, the nuraghe Diana.
descriptions.NUR4914: The Diana Nuraghe, of complex type, consists of a tholos and two smaller towers connected by a curtain wall, forming a general triangular shape. At the centre there is an open courtyard in a quadrangular form, providing access to the various rooms.
descriptions.NUR10236: If one considers the defensive function of the nuraghes, this one at Elighia I° is the most evident example. It stands at an elevation above 600 m.a.s.l., dominating the surrounding countryside at 360 degrees and acting as a sentinel, keeping watch over anyone who might unwise enough venture into these territories. Unfortunately, it is also in a state of ruin. mu
descriptions.NUR5594: Site of difficult interpretation. Certainly there is a nuraghe, and it seems certain that a giants' tomb also existed, which disappeared after the land reclamation works. The term cantòne refers to squared stone blocks, often of calcareous tuff or trachyte (pèdra contonina). This name, now obsolete, probably originated from the occupation of stone diggers, who were the unknown brothers from whom the toponym is derived.
descriptions.NUR9817: Due to the almost complete absence of construction stones, only the essentials remain to understand the original foundation of the nuraghe. Essentially, a kind of radiograph of the plan survives: it is as if someone had levelled the structure to the ground, revealing a massive entrance with an architrave in situ and another, megalithic slab laid on the ground. The basal circle is composed of stones arranged with a corridor and orthogonal cells. Remarkable for specialists to study.
descriptions.NUR12917: Nuragic hut or nuraghe base, not marked on IGM map, currently reduced to a rubble heap
descriptions.NUR20260: Probable nuraghe (Ugas 2022), located beneath the remains of a 18th-century fort, later used as a signal point. For some archaeologists it would have been a quadrilobate, Nuragic royal residence. Others consider it unlikely. Further studies are pending.
descriptions.NUR9870: The grave is the state of abandonment and decay we currently face. Unfortunately, the lack of institutional interest—despite numerous requests for intervention—leaves us indignant. The structure is interesting and some parts are accessible despite the collapses. The corridor emerges with a dolmenic door onto the cliff face a short distance away. mu
descriptions.NUR11453:
Proto-nuraghe Mura Barbaros: the monument consists of an outer wall enclosing, for at least three-fifths, a building of rather irregular form. On the surface of the top, a short corridor to the south-east is visible, partially closed by four flat slabs, while to the south there is a glimpse of an entrance with a lintel belonging to a second corridor.

Almost a continuation of the previous.
descriptions.NUR10198: The name of the nuraghe derives almost certainly from the toponym of the location. It is a particularly unusual nuraghe in terms of its construction. Unfortunately, it has suffered a conspicuous collapse to the west, limiting its survey. Nuraghe of the elongated height of Pantaleo or "Pantaleo Serra", proper name. It is the first of three nuraghi situated along the edge of an elongated height. See Sèrra Pantalèo. mu
descriptions.NUR14918: Located at 140 m above sea level, this Nuragic complex is partially damaged by works carried out for the construction of the Provincial Road Ussana, Donori Barrali. The plants of the structures related to the Nuragic complex were to be uncovered in order to define their structural features and assign a precise chronological age; despite the owners having granted authorization, the excavation campaign was not carried out.
descriptions.NUR11966:
The monument is situated on the summit of a granitic rock outcrop and dominates the surrounding area, bordered on one side by an outer wall and on the other by natural rock.

It is not clearly legible, as only some stones from the first course remain, suggesting a small nuraghe or a nuragic observation point.
descriptions.NUR10488: The nuraghe has been completely destroyed. It is mentioned in a zone characterized by a Nuragic settlement encompassing an extremely large area.
descriptions.NUR3248: It is a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe built from basalt blocks, located in an area with a large number of nuraghe, possibly functionally connected, all situated along the course of the Rio sa Mela, a right tributary of the Tirso.
descriptions.NUR5954: Both the nuraghe and the giants' tomb are in very poor condition of conservation and are surrounded by vegetation.
descriptions.NUR4918: Damaged nuraghe of which only 5 or 6 courses remain.
descriptions.NUR4970:
Nuraghe of corridor type, composed of two towers connected by an internal courtyard, accessed through the entrance.

The oldest part of the nuraghe is the tower on the right when entering, while the left tower and the connecting walls were added later.
descriptions.NUR4478: Remains of the nuraghe and the Nuragic and Neolithic village.
descriptions.NUR3407: The De Planu or Don Micheli nuraghe has a diameter of 12.50 m and a wall width of four metres. Access is provided through a corridor 4.50 m long, which is blocked for two metres. At a depth of two metres, fragments of vessels with handles of different shapes and a central excavation were found; at a depth of one metre, fragments of tableware, human bones, and a cremation tomb were discovered.
descriptions.NUR861: Single-tower nuraghe built from roughly hewn limestone blocks. It is hidden beneath an impenetrable layer of vegetation.
descriptions.NUR2843:
It is a mixed type, built with large granite blocks, featuring a central tower reaching 12 metres in height, surrounded by three secondary towers. The entrance, with a lintel, provides access to the corridor, which has a lateral chamber containing a deep well just under 2 metres in depth. In the central chamber there is another corridor housing a spiral staircase leading to the upper level.

The other three towers are partially collapsed and only sparsely accessible;
descriptions.NUR6123: Composed of a central tower about 7 metres high and two lateral towers connected by a bastion that encloses and protects the entire structure. The central tower features an intact false-dome (tholos) roof, while the lateral towers have collapsed. Access is from the south-east, via a small triangular courtyard that directly opens into the entrance. To the left, after a short corridor, a staircase leads to the summit.
descriptions.NUR7162: Multicellular and with an unusual plan.
descriptions.NUR492: Single-cell domus de janas with a carved stele above the door.
descriptions.NUR3419: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe with collapsed sections and restored, even with concrete block masonry.
descriptions.NUR5715: Around the area there are numerous traces of extremely ancient presence, such as votive menhirs and stones of various shapes. Other constructions enrich the landscape, such as the homonymous spring nuraghe. Quadrilobate, situated on the summit of the mountain of the same name, and a little further on, one of the most important nuragic sacred wells: Su Tempiesu.
descriptions.NUR4401: South-east of Siurgus-Donigala, near the border with the territory of Goni. Built on a hill at an elevation of 494 m a.s.l., blocks of finely worked limestone were used, which today remain to a height of about 5 m. The internal chamber is missing its top, filled with debris from collapse and reveals an entrance in the form of a vault. Around the nuraghe, the base courses of huts from a village and stones driven into the ground are visible, which may indicate burial sites.
descriptions.NUR6084:
His Majesty the ERGULIS, the largest of the nuraghi in the Cuglieritano area, is a single-tower nuraghe standing 106 m tall and is intact both in its walling and in its vault.

It features two niches directly opposite each other just beyond the entrance lintel, and two more inside the chamber, while a niche at the front of the entrance is notably absent.

The lintel is equipped with a drainage opening directed to the south.
descriptions.NUR5545: Proto-nuraghe partially collapsed and covered by a dense vegetation layer
descriptions.NUR3261: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe situated beside an agriturismo, of which only three courses remain.
descriptions.NUR2677: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe situated beside an agriturismo, of which only three courses remain.
descriptions.NUR5913:
It is located in the territory of the comune of Santu Lussurgiu (OR), a few kilometres from the hamlet of San Leonardo de Siete Fuentes.

It is a three-lobed nuraghe with a main tower and two smaller towers, one to the south-west and the other to the north-east. Traces of a curtain wall remain a few metres from the entrance to the first tower, enclosing the complex.
descriptions.NUR5812: It is in a severe state of degradation. Nevertheless, enough remains are still present to allow for a basic assessment. From its height of about 600 m a.s.l., it overlooks the underlying basaltic plateau, performing effectively as a watchtower. A short distance away, near the nuraghe, some stones can be seen that may be baetyls or part of a giants' tomb. mu
descriptions.NUR3023: Single-tower nuraghe partially buried in vegetation, with only the large lintel remaining, resting on the lateral walls and free above.
descriptions.NUR5551: Complex nuraghe with a village, located very close to the better known Nuraghe Majore. At the central tower, which still retains an intact tholos chamber, a transverse-frontal bastion with two towers and an intermediate courtyard has been built. Moreover, a third tower, set back from the two front ones, is clearly identifiable, featuring a corridor of access and an intact tholos.
descriptions.NUR4989:
Complex nuraghe hidden beneath a conspicuous collapse. A large village of huts in the south-southwest is entirely covered by bushes. Near the southern periphery of the village, a building with straight walls made of squared blocks might date back to the Nuragic period.

On the hill to the west of the main ridge, a Nuragic structure—already considered a giants' tomb—appears to be actually a circular building ("tower-hut?").
descriptions.NUR5995:
The monument, four-lobed and sub-rectangular in plan, features a central tower made of trachyte in circular plan, with a diameter of about 10 m, and lateral towers connected by a curtain wall constructed using polygonal masonry with roughly shaped stones.

Remains of some structures with circular rooms are visible at the south-east and north-west corners.
descriptions.NUR2965: Near the nuraghe there is a Nuragic spring. It is located in the Pedruitta plain. It is immediately evident that it represents an extremely ancient Nuragic feature.
descriptions.NUR2975: (16th–13th century BC), it is built of trachyte. It has a corridor with a spiral staircase on the left and a guard niche on the right, and a vaulted chamber, perfectly preserved, with three niches arranged in a cross. The entrance jambs of the nuraghe are 1.52 m and 1.24 m high respectively. The tower reaches a maximum height of 8 m and consists of seventeen courses of stone. The entrance faces east; its perfectly worked lintel is 1.60 m long, 0.70 m high and 0.80 m wide.
descriptions.NUR6211: Complex three-lobed nuraghe. The central tower has a chamber with three niches set around it. Built of granite.
descriptions.NUR1576: The Ertas nuraghe is the largest Nuragic monument in the Sassari region. Fully subterranean and quadrilobed, completely enveloped by impenetrable vegetation. From the access point located to the south-east, it is possible, by crawling, to reach the main tholos still intact.
descriptions.NUR8683: Single-tower with a large diameter, of which only the courses remain up to about 2.50 m in height, with the entrance and lintel.
descriptions.NUR881:
Small observation tower.

Nearby is a hut with a "rotonda" equipped with a bacile.
descriptions.NUR4473: The ceramic artifacts found date to the Monte Claro phase and correspond to those from the nearby nuraghe Trobas. This site is located on a rise flanking the prehistoric route to Villanovaforru and has an atypical plan with a large subterranean chamber and four adjacent rooms.
descriptions.NUR865: The nuraghe is located in the middle of a field cultivated with grain, with very poor visibility. The nuraghe's structure is visible in the field, but not the extent of the village area.
descriptions.NUR2646:
It is a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe with a facing and outer wall that resembles, in some respects, the Nuraghe Aidu Olostru at Bortigali. Along a stretch of about thirty metres, the remains of a powerful outer wall (thickness 2.30 m; height 3.00 m) are visible, which may have originally delimited the nuraghe tower but now survives only partially, with three-quarters of the courses spaced about 12 to 20 metres from the nuraghe.

An extensive settlement, with its remains extending around within the outer wall, is visible.
descriptions.NUR8570: This site is located in an olive grove and was previously studied. Today it is completely destroyed, and it is unclear whether there are still remains of a village underground. Some forms of hut or nuraghe are recognizable. The agricultural land is covered with squared stones and fragments of stone. Most of the stones of various sizes have been incorporated into the numerous dry stone walls surrounding the site.
descriptions.NUR5488: The nuragic village is located at 1,200 m a.s.l. and is one of the highest in Sardinia. Part of the village is enclosed, but the gate is open. The three-lobed nuraghe is surrounded by springs and mountains and is set within an environment free from human modification. Inside the nuraghe, a staircase leads to the upper level and to the central mastio, whose tholos is intact. The remains of the circular huts that formed the village and the nuraghe are made of granite.
descriptions.NUR5783: At the site, especially on the steeper side facing the Aldo Moro road, remains of numerous huts are visible, along with worked stone and ceramic material of various types. Ceramic material is also present in large quantities on the opposite, flat side, to the south of the nuraghe. In appearance, some fragments with smoothed surfaces and fewer intrusive elements suggest later occupations following the Nuragic period.
descriptions.NUR1264: Area where ancient maps indicated the location of the nuraghe Evrassu, in the countryside of the commune of Pozzomaggiore (SS); what remains of the nuraghe Frassu (in the countryside of Pozzomaggiore)
descriptions.NUR4064: Four-tower nuraghe, with towers arranged in a cross around a large courtyard. It consists of a central tower, about 3 m high, connected to two secondary towers via a curtain wall. Some studies define the complex as quadrilobate with concentric addition.
descriptions.NUR4470: Nuragic village, never the subject of studies or excavations, located within the Gutturu Mannu park, in the Assemini administrative enclave, on the left bank of the river, facing the homonymous springs. Completely surrounded by the cork oak forest, it is almost invisible from the outside.
descriptions.NUR4844: Nuraxi Fenu, within which during excavations remains of a hearth and animal bones, fragments of Roman pottery, and a coin datable to the 3rd century AD were found, suggesting occasional occupation of the site between the 2nd and 3rd centuries AD. A violent fire marked the end of Nuragic occupation, although the site was occasionally used during the Punic and Roman periods.
descriptions.NUR5877: It is impossible to enter due to the conspicuous collapse affecting the entrance area.
descriptions.NUR4685: It is located to the south, near the border with the territory of Usellus. It was presumably of a simple type with a single tower. It is in very poor state of conservation, although it is not ruled out that its portion may have been buried over the centuries due to the action of atmospheric and human agents.
descriptions.NUR1246: At present it is completely buried and covered by shrub vegetation. Because of this its ground plan cannot be read, except for a single course of blocks emerging from the hillock; judging by the extent of the remains it is likely to be a complex type. In the surrounding ground outcrops of roughly dressed limestone ashlars can be seen, suggesting the existence of a village, traces of which are also detectable through photogrammetric analysis.
descriptions.NUR8207: The nuraghe is not visible on the ground due to the presence of a dense thicket covering what may have been the site of destruction. However, the abundance of ceramic material still indicates Nuragic origin for the site's occupation.
descriptions.NUR14937: The monument lies at 191 metres above sea level in the locality of Fidrigu. The nuraghe is completely destroyed; the few remaining boulders are scattered and it is impossible to reconstruct the original structure. The situation was made worse by the work carried out to install an Enel pylon. As stated above, the nuraghe was abandoned and consequently completely destroyed, and now not even all the boulders that made up the nuraghe remain. The site is on private property.
descriptions.NUR2813: Damaged nuraghe but with the interior accessible. The portal and about five courses of the wall masonry remain.
descriptions.NUR3642: Damaged nuraghe, whose classification as either a non-completed nuraghe or a single-tower (single-tower nuraghe) is difficult to determine.
descriptions.NUR3391: Single-tower nuraghe with its top missing but free from the ashlar fragments of the collapsed tholos. Used as a sheepfold.
descriptions.NUR17371: It is heavily eroded and surrounded by dense vegetation.
descriptions.NUR992: Now fully incorporated into a mass of rubble, it is in very poor condition with stones scattered throughout.
descriptions.NUR5904: The complex includes a corridor-type nuraghe with an attached dwelling and giants' tomb. Access to the proto-nuraghe was provided through an entrance located at the northwest corner. At a short distance from the nuraghe, the remains of some huts from the ancient village can be identified.
descriptions.NUR10518: Nuragic settlement with a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe built of chalky sandstone blocks. Bronze Age ceramics. The landscape context relating to the presence of the nuraghe has been radically altered since the time of the monument's initial survey; nevertheless, traces of it remain worthy of preservation.
descriptions.NUR3863: The nuraghe, located in a pastureland area, is completely covered by vegetation. Due to the conditions in which the nuraghe lies, we have been unable to identify its type, and the possible presence of an entrance or lintel.
descriptions.NUR3716: The site, located in a currently pastureland area situated mainly on hills, is irreparably ruined. The external perimeter base can still be observed, as granite outcrops rise from the ground forming a circle.
descriptions.NUR529: Single-tower nuraghe with probably a settlement.
descriptions.NUR795: Masonry made of roughly hewn stones, some of which are more finely shaped and of varying sizes. The lateral towers: the one on the left is better preserved than the others, rising from the ground for four courses of large blocks; the tower on the right is barely visible at the surface, indicated by two courses partially buried; the third tower, whose footprint is covered by debris from collapses, is located directly in front of the entrance.
descriptions.NUR5678: Situated on the boundary between Sindia and Macomer, this nuraghe lies about 1000 m from the important and well-known archaeological area of Tamuli (Macomer). It is a complex nuraghe with a central tower and two partially preserved secondary towers. The main chamber is circular and has three niches arranged in a cross; the tholos survives intact. At present it appears to the visitor 'protected' by dense vegetation that almost completely covers it.
descriptions.NUR21004: Nuraghe reported whose category cannot be defined
descriptions.NUR15238: The Flumenlongu nuraghe is a single-tower structure with at least two superimposed levels, and beyond these, in addition to an open courtyard, there is a secondary tower and several accessory chambers. Along its margins extends a village of circular huts, the extent of which has not been defined; from one of them comes an important storage site that has yielded panels, axes, a few scapulae and some bracelets.
descriptions.NUR2729: It is a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe with a circular plan, diameter 11 m, preserved to a height of about 2.5 m on three courses. Cyclopean wall with roughly hewn stones. Entrance on the south-east, without lintel, leads into a corridor about 2 m wide.
descriptions.NUR15020: Single-tower nuraghe, it faces the Nuraghe Su Nuraxi on the other side of the Rio su Gaffu.
descriptions.NUR3380:
Located in the territory of the comune of Florinas (SS).

A very ruined nuraghe, only some courses of calcareous ashlar remain at the base.

A old cart track once passed nearby, branching off from the Florinas–S. Maria di Sea municipal road, whose route has almost entirely been erased by pastureland.
descriptions.NUR15951: The nuraghe shows some remaining wall courses; those on one side are more evident. The original position of the entrance can be identified, while although the base of the chamber is detectable inside, no interesting details can be observed as the chamber is filled with rubble of varying stone sizes.
descriptions.NUR3995: another nuraghe in the Segariu area, though neglected and eroded
descriptions.NUR17650:
Completely buried externally, it retains internally a small tholos that extends into a dead-end corridor.

More precisely, it is a proto-nuraghe or corridor nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR5835: It has a vaguely circular, oval shape, with two entrances and a central chamber featuring a niche. Maximum height: 4.50 m. The corridor's cross-section is trapezoidal-ogival, and the roof is formed by four large slabs laid flat. On the exposed surface, between the two corridors and the chamber, a section of corridor (length 4 m; width 1.25–1.50 m) is visible, though at present it is difficult to define its exact path and function.
descriptions.NUR3209: The Franzesu nuraghe is situated in a dominant position on the plateau of Spiritu Santu, offering a wide view from the Asinara Gulf to Corsica, controlling important access routes. The nuraghe consists of a central tower and a front bastion with a bilobate shape and no facing. The bastion is built with large trachyte blocks; it is suspected that some of these blocks were reused menhirs, and at least one certainly was.
descriptions.NUR4563:
The nuraghe is situated practically at ground level.

The poor quality of the rock has likely contributed to the poor condition in which the monument now exists.
descriptions.NUR3572: The nuraghe was almost completely destroyed in the 1960s to extract stone for use in house construction. Nearby, a well of the same period and likely belonging to the structure is present.
descriptions.NUR5758: easily visible, adjacent to the municipal road, almost destroyed at the top of the tower, there is a covered entrance surrounded by bushes.
descriptions.NUR5929:
It is located at the border between the municipal territories of Bortigali (NU) and Dualchi (NU), but belongs to the municipality of Dualchi.

More precisely, it is a proto-nuraghe. Around it are several cinerary urns. It consists of two megalithic walls still partially intact.
descriptions.NUR5164: The proto-nuraghe Friarosu di Mogorella has a sub-rectangular plan with short sides convex, as it includes, at the base of the masonry, three rooms: two oval and one ellipsoidal, each covered by a truncated arch.
descriptions.NUR5607:
The Fronte Mola is an interesting corridor nuraghe, the only one so far known to have a rectangular plan (length 16.20 m; width 12.00 m; remaining height 8.00 m).

It aligns its longer side along the N-S axis and shows the entrance to the south.

It is built at the base with large calcare blocks roughly shaped and in the upper parts with smaller stones stacked and buttressed with pegs.
descriptions.NUR15847: Stunning single-tower nuraghe, partially collapsed. It features an intact tholos and an anti-clockwise staircase.
descriptions.NUR6186: Single-tower (single-tower nuraghe) buried and enveloped by vegetation. It appears to be a single-tower.
descriptions.NUR3269:
The single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe is located very close to SS131, adjacent to a sheepfold. It is used as a shelter for sheep. The tholos is almost intact except for the last courses.

Very little or nothing remains of the huts that likely existed beside the tower.
descriptions.NUR6046: Single-tower tholos nuraghe, visible under a dense canopy of olive and mastic trees. In addition to a scattered concentration of stones, some base courses of the structure remain, built from locally sourced polygonal basalt blocks. The remaining portions of the structure are filled with rubble from collapse.
descriptions.NUR3701:
Single-tower tholos nuraghe built from locally sourced polygonal basalt blocks. Several courses are visible and the entrance, facing south, can be observed with the monolithic lintel still in situ.

The interior of the chamber is filled with debris from the collapse of the structure. Blocks from the collapse are found around the raised remains, especially in the north, east and south directions.
descriptions.NUR2839:
This nuraghe has a three-lobed plan consisting of three towers: one central and two lateral, the latter partially destroyed.

In the central tower we find the main chamber, a circular space in which the wall tapers upward to form a true vault, ending with an opening that may have been previously sealed by two smaller stones. Near the entrance, on the left side, a spiral staircase with crude steps rises to the upper level.
descriptions.NUR5982: A tholos nuraghe, presumably of the single-tower type. Vegetation currently covers almost the entire nuraghe, except for a short stretch of the west side where a few courses of the outer wall face, made of polygonal basalt blocks, can be glimpsed.
descriptions.NUR916: Remains of a small granite nuraghe
descriptions.NUR4556: The single-tower nuraghe was located at a height near a spring where it had been built, and today a protected spring with masonry still exists. Comparison with the 2017 and 2019 aerial photographs shows that buildings have been constructed in place of the little that remained of the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR18842: Unfortunately, almost entirely destroyed by erosion. Only a few blocks remain in their original position.
descriptions.NUR3337: It stands on a basaltic spur accessible only from one side, west of the village of Sagama. It has a polygonal plan with a straight, slightly convex façade to the north-west where the entrance opens. At the centre of the main wall is the main entrance, featuring a rectangular opening and a lintel. Entering, we find a straight corridor; at the right end of the first section, two adjacent niches open.
descriptions.NUR2653: It is a well-proportioned and harmonious three-lobed nuraghe. Only part of it is accessible due to obvious and widespread collapses. The construction techniques and features of first order are particularly noteworthy. Although the name derives from the local topographic term, it nonetheless indicates intense copper-smelting activity. Numerous semi-finished bronze artefacts with a bull's hide form are present.
descriptions.NUR3103:
In a dominant and strategically privileged position.

It is a single-tower with an added body, featuring a circular chamber with three niches arranged in a cross pattern.

Due to the collapse, the entrance to the south-east and the passage, as well as any associated auxiliary spaces (niches and/or stairs), are currently not visible; however, their presence is likely certain given the evolved typology of the chamber.
descriptions.NUR2714:
Despite the very dense vegetation and the collapses suffered by the monument, the ruins of a central body flanked by two towers can be identified, built with trachyte blocks of rose colour.

At a short distance, in the south-west direction, traces of some circular stone constructions are visible.
descriptions.NUR6128: The collapses and dense vegetation prevent a clear outline of the structure, which nevertheless appears to be elliptical and of mixed type: a corridor nuraghe, probably adjacent to a tower built at a later date, to which may have corresponded an additional circular tholos structure.
descriptions.NUR4264: The nuraghe, the side most visible of which faces the pigpen from the adjacent field, appears nonetheless to have been a single-tower (single-tower nuraghe), built with roughly shaped blocks in roughly parallelipipedal form and fairly regular in shape, of medium to large dimensions.
descriptions.NUR19954: Four-lobed nuraghe, fairly well preserved. Tower A appears to be older and more imposing. Around the nuraghe remain the ruins of the village of the same name. Some believe the five windows were related to astronomical events.
descriptions.NUR4810: A hill covered with vegetation hiding a nuraghe among the largest in the area. It extends over at least two hectares of land to the lacaras.
descriptions.NUR4798:
The Nuragic people decided to wall up the tafoni and erect a single, distinctive tower that probably had an additional room above the surface of the rocky outcrop.

Inside these walls fitted into the granites there are very steep stairways.

Not much remains of the large central communal building, perhaps also because of the choices made by La Marmora and Spano who, in their search for the "floor level", had part of the original superstructure moved and pushed down below.
descriptions.NUR5254: The nuraghe is a complex type, consisting of a five-lobed bastion enclosing the original tower and a courtyard. The mastio, circular in plan (13 m in external diameter), survives with a maximum residual height of over 12 metres. The wall face is composed of blocks arranged in horizontal courses. A stone mass in the lower chamber, laid transversely with respect to the spiral staircase—already blocked off—originally extended from the ground level.
descriptions.NUR4048:
It stands on the summit of a hill in the Marmilla. The structure is a complex type, formed by an original central tower built in the Middle Bronze Age, to which four more towers and a bastion were later added. One of the four towers was subsequently sacrificed during a further building phase that presumably also saw the construction of the massive hexagonal outer wall.

In the Early Iron Age a new village developed on the site.
descriptions.NUR11567: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe, marks the boundary between the municipal territories of Villamar and Pauli Arbarei.
descriptions.NUR20319: Single-tower nuraghe with only the two base courses apparently remaining. It is very likely that there was an entire village nearby, given its strategic location and the traces that are still visible.
descriptions.NUR4852: One of the nuraghes located within the territory of the comune of Villa Sant'Antonio is the 'Genna sa Pira' nuraghe, fully encompassed within the Middle Bronze Age (1500–1200 BC), although its construction has seen numerous later additions over the centuries.
descriptions.NUR4626: Single-tower nuraghe of which only a very small, or no, remains. Inhabited until the Recent Bronze Age. Afterward, life ceases at many nuraghes, which have lost their original function.
descriptions.NUR4601: A proto-nuraghe later transformed into a single-tower (single-tower nuraghe).
descriptions.NUR3969:
It is a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe with a circular plan reaching 29 m in length, including the closest collapses.

Its state of preservation allows the general structure to be traced along its entire outer perimeter, which was never covered by any additional masonry. It is difficult to identify the location of the entrance opening, which probably lies in the southern quadrant.
descriptions.NUR15133:
Complex of pre-protohistoric date that includes a modest Neolithic village, a complex nuraghe enclosed by an outer wall, and its associated village of huts. Within the village a water well has been dug, of uncertain chronology.  

The buildings are constructed with local andesite blocks.  

Above the nuragic huts village a fine sheepfold has been built, enclosed by dry stone walls.
descriptions.NUR1916:
four-lobed (?) nuraghe on the top of the Ghilotta hill, built with polygonal blocks of the local volcanic rock.

The towered structure is surrounded by a settlement of circular huts, with the perimeter walls preserved to a considerable height. Collapses and vegetation make the interpretation of the complex extremely difficult.

At the south-eastern edge of the complex, the Lenzu Houses, an agricultural-pastoral enterprise of the medau type, have been extensively modified in recent times.
descriptions.NUR19705: Nuraghe partially destroyed by quarry work. The site is of particular interest because of the discovery in the area of three swords, with pistil-shaped blades and a central rib, and a tang to which two wings with holes for fixing the handle are attached, recovered during the 1950s. This typically Iberian type finds comparisons with specimens from the territory of Baunei, and with the sword resting on the shoulder of the “Warrior” of Uta.
descriptions.NUR18177: The nuraghe has suffered significant collapses and is surrounded by dense vegetation.
descriptions.NUR3820: At the level of ruin but very interesting in its star-shaped structure. It features a Megaron-type temple. Just to clarify, I will use number I° to indicate the first of the three present in a very restricted area known as Giaganu Dominigu. I do not possess the systematic work carried out by the Sassari supervisor; on my part, I propose a reconstruction that comes as close as possible to the actual one, considering that we "are playing at home".
descriptions.NUR5029: Nuraghe almost entirely destroyed, with only a semicircular stretch of masonry remaining.
descriptions.NUR2115: Nuargi Ega de is gruttas (V. Angius 1840). Complex nuraghe devastated by illegal diggers. The curtain wall outlining the central tower is still visible, with clear signs of illegal interventions inside. The outer wall, though largely covered by vegetation, is preserved along almost its entire perimeter. To the south-east there is a small break in the wall face, where the entrance was likely located.
descriptions.NUR5231: Mainly composed of stones similar to those of the Arresi nuraghe, four towers are visible, plus one almost completely destroyed. Some elderly people still remember that the tower exposed to the north-west was intact. They say there was a well so deep that the sound of stones being dropped into it could not be heard.
descriptions.NUR20106: Located in the area of Tidula, it features a corridor niche and one in the tholos, still intact.
descriptions.NUR3561: Built with granite blocks quarried on site, the nuraghe consists of a circular tower with a diameter of about 4.5 m and an additional body with a pseudo-elliptical plan (with a principal axis of about 12 m and a secondary axis of about 8 m). No traces of huts are currently evident, but it is likely that some structures were built along the perimeter of the site and that natural caves were used for various purposes.
descriptions.NUR5957:
It is built with medium and large stones arranged in poorly precise courses; it has an oval plan and two entrances and two staircases leading to the upper level.

The roof is formed by large slabs placed side by side.

The southern entrance is partially collapsed and may have been connected to the staircases, while the western access leads to the central corridor, from which a deep niche and a staircase almost entirely collapsed open. Probable proto-nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR3130: Traces of the Nuragic village are also present.
descriptions.NUR3132:
It is located at the highest point of Florinas. (517 m a.s.l.)  

Today, unfortunately, it has collapsed inward.  

It features a main tower and two additional towers.
descriptions.NUR3329: The nuraghe, situated within the Girgini-protected area, is irrevocably ruined; what remains visible is only the base course, while various parts of the nuraghe have been reused in the construction of a wall in the immediate vicinity.
descriptions.NUR3069: Bitorre nuraghe, collapsed and inaccessible, faces north and dominates the entire northern coast from Stintino to Isola Rossa.
descriptions.NUR14927: Complex nuraghe with village. It is located at the border with the municipality of Sinnai in the Campidano State Forest. It is situated on a mountain side completely covered in stones and it is very difficult to see the structures. In some areas walls can be observed.
descriptions.NUR2492: Complex nuraghe with a central tower and three additional towers with bastions (four-lobed). Around the nuraghe, traces of a settlement.
descriptions.NUR3467: The Golunie nuraghe is located on land owned by the Guiso family (ancient barons), precisely at the border between the territories of Orosei and Dorgali, in the Cala Osalla area, and it overlooks both the Marina beach near the second Osalla mole (Orosei) and the adjacent beach of the same name (Dorgali).
descriptions.NUR4925: The building, a circular single-tower nuraghe about 10 metres in diameter, adapts to the plateau, incorporating rock outcrops into its basal structures. The external wall face, made of roughly dressed limestone blocks laid in regular courses, survives to a maximum height of 8.10 metres. On the west and south-east sides, at a height of 3 to 3.5 metres from the ground, a restoration carried out in antiquity is clearly visible, made necessary by the subsidence of the masonry.
descriptions.NUR3792: It is in a state of complete abandonment. The structure, built with limestone and shale, shows part of the tholos wall face, as well as some additional features suggesting a complex monument. Around the structure, there is a noticeable dispersion of materials emerging at the surface, almost certainly related to the presence of a settlement attached to the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR8972: The Gorroppu or 'Presethu Tortu' nuraghe stands on a rocky spur located southwest of the gully of the same name. The settlement is naturally fortified on the south side, while on the opposite side it is protected by a substantial curtain wall built of megalithic stone, very well preserved, reaching a height of over 3 metres. Inside the settlement there are numerous quadrangular buildings, some of which are in fairly good condition.
descriptions.NUR544: It is a quadrilobate nuraghe destroyed due to the construction of the Marine Military base on the same site. Lamarmora and Cugia mentioned it in the 1800s. Lamarmora surveyed the nuraghe and produced monographs in which the Roman aqueduct's tunnels are clearly visible, passing directly through the nuraghe. Around it, at least two nuragic wells were present.
descriptions.NUR5477: Illegal diggers have exposed some courses of the wall of a small elliptical structure.
descriptions.NUR4797: Single-tower nuraghe located in the plain, enclosed with a metal mesh. Currently visible are four courses of the external wall face on the north-east side, composed of medium-sized stones. The presence of other archaeological remains in the surrounding area cannot be ruled out.
descriptions.NUR2047: Only the lower part of the nuraghe remains, used also as a sheepfold. Likely elliptical in shape or at least non-circular. Diameter at the top is about 10 m.
descriptions.NUR19553: Few remains of a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe built of limestone. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR10636: What remains of a small nuraghe near Santu Sciori. A church has been built upon it. Mentioned in the writings of Vittorio Angius for the discovery of some giant bones.
