descriptions.NUR4464: The nuraghe is currently in poor state of conservation, with several collapses that prevent a precise assessment. Only two towers are clearly distinguishable, between which a small courtyard—typical of complex nuraghe—may have once existed. In the main tower (mastio), niches and a staircase are present, which led to the upper levels, now collapsed.
descriptions.NUR4440: The tower remains as a mound of earth on which the filars of the nuraghe emerge, probably part of a complex.
descriptions.NUR4070:
The nuraghe is inaccessible due to the presence of a high metal mesh.

Nearby is a menhir, always within the fenced area.
descriptions.NUR3158: Located about a hundred metres east of the well-known giants' tomb of Imbertighe, with which it shows clear cultural connections, the nuraghe is now situated within an agricultural farm; it is a single-tower (single-tower nuraghe) with a slightly elliptical plan (14.10 x 15.25 m), featuring an entrance to the south-east and a remaining height of 2.75 m to the north-west and 1.70 m to the south-west, respectively with 5 and 4 courses.
descriptions.NUR2268: Located near the quarry of Monte Ladu, on the banks of an artificial pond. Part of the base is still visible.
descriptions.NUR6299: Among the heaps of stones the main tower emerges at the highest point, where the entrance is topped by a bare lintel. The open-air entrance has the niche on the right intact and on the left the collapsed stairwell, passable up to the upper floor from which the interior of the tholos with its two side niches can be seen. On the north-west side a double chamber, partly underground, is entered; it probably connected with the central tower in the lower part, which is now below ground.
descriptions.NUR4741: The monument, also known in the literature as "Pranu Nuracci", is a complex nuraghe of quadrilobate type. Two lateral towers, the perimeter walls, and the central mastio remain. The southern-western and northern lateral towers are preserved for about 4 to 5 courses. The central mastio, in good state of preservation, has 12 courses in polygonal masonry with large blocks only roughly shaped, with an entrance to the south-east, featuring a monolithic lintel.
descriptions.NUR3805: Perhaps it is the same nuraghe referred to as Thorcodossile in some books, located about 500 metres further west. Only a few ruins remain at the top of the hill.
descriptions.NUR1163: Visitable, collapsed upon itself, central tower with a tree inside, large walls of calcareous tufa. Used in Roman times, evidenced by the presence of broken amphorae. In the nearby rocky outcrops, laccus are present. Traces of a village nearby.
descriptions.NUR5491: Complex nuraghe, known to many elders by the name "Sa Reggia", was probably a three-lobed structure with a village. Today it is a heap of ruins and undergrowth more than 10 metres high.
descriptions.NUR10184:
Proto-nuraghe of sub-circular shape (D. Carta 2010)

The single-tower nuraghe dates to the Middle Nuragic period. The building is unusual; its chamber is partly cut into the rock.

Investigations by G. Ugas led to the identification in 1981 of a Punic settlement at Is Argiddas, on the border with the municipality of Sanluri.

The Punic centre, of which stretches of walling in small stones bonded with mud have been identified, overlies a prehistoric and protohistoric settlement.
descriptions.NUR4336: The monument is partially collapsed and its interpretation is not entirely clear: apparently it appears to have been a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe, yet other curved curtain walls are observed around the main structure, for which the explanation could be either that they represent residential units (huts?) or additional structures attached to the main body, in which case it would be a complex nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR1880: “massive and irregular in plan, in which the dimensions of the walls predominate over the internal spaces, indicating an imperfect mastery of the constructive techniques typical of later tholos nuraghes”. Following the traditional classification, the megalithic structure at Is Bangius can be assigned to the type of monuments of the archaic phase, such as corridor nuraghes.
descriptions.NUR4946: Complex nuraghe consisting of two towers joined by a corridor, built in basalt.
descriptions.NUR5722: It is a simple nuraghe, evidenced by only a few stones scattered here and there inside and outside a centuries-old lentisco thicket. The stones are of medium size, and some appear slightly rough-hewn. Only a few circles remain, which do not provide sufficient clarity for proper assessment.
descriptions.NUR812: Nuraghe destroyed by agricultural mechanization, now no longer visible
descriptions.NUR6131: In a state of ruin, only a few medium-sized stones from the basal circle remain, within which the entrance facing south-east is visible. Due to the absence of the main nuraghe structures, the site is likely classified as a burial tomb.
descriptions.NUR5163: From the nuraghe one enjoys a breathtaking view of the underlying Lake Flumendosa.
descriptions.NUR18385: Complex nuraghe of an evolved type, definable in plan as consisting of only the central tower.
descriptions.NUR19125: It is located in the middle of a large cultivated area; no road or path passes near it.
descriptions.NUR3083:
The Iscobalzu nuraghe features a nuraghe tower about 5 metres high. The door is subterranean and does not allow access to the interior due to the collapse of the dome's stones.

Its size and state of preservation are the best among the nuraghes in the area.
descriptions.NUR3622: It is a good example of a single-tower (single-tower nuraghe) with a tholos chamber that has collapsed but is still accessible. It is a nuraghe that exhibits a variety of constructive and architectural features. Facing north, it has a poorly constructed, recently added stone entrance that is situated at a height of about 2.00 metres above the campsite level.
descriptions.NUR3714:
Not easily accessible, one reaches it after a rugged climb, through arid and rocky pastures, among emergent stones that reveal the ancient presence of a large village.

Nothing has been excavated from this monument, and only the tholos of the second level is accessible.

Completely overgrown with stones and brambles lies the courtyard opposite the main tower.
descriptions.NUR14202:
There are nuraghi that are not only grandiose in themselves but also for the landscape in which they stand.

The nuraghe Iscolca is one of these: it dominates the Semestene valley and those of the surrounding villages. Not easily reached, it is accessed after a steep climb through dry, rocky pastures, among protruding stones that hint at the ancient existence of a large village.

Nothing of this monument appears to have been excavated, and only the tholos of the second level is accessible.
descriptions.NUR20230: Nuraghe of which only a small portion remains at the centre of the settlement of Is Collus. Following a report to the supervisor, archaeological investigations were carried out, but the results are unknown.
descriptions.NUR21162: Nuraghe that was demolished to build a radar base at the tip of Is Ebbas in the 1960s, known as Nuraghe Is Ebbas or Nuraghe Su Brecconi. Information provided by local elders
descriptions.NUR4271: It is a complex nuraghe, with at least the upper courses of the walls skillfully dressed in arenaria. Unfortunately, it is difficult to visit and document due to the vegetation.
descriptions.NUR12905: Nuraghe almost completely dismantled, only a few courses of stones remain.
descriptions.NUR3966: Military outpost of the war 1940/45 built on the remains of the Nuraghe Is Meris.
descriptions.NUR4717: It consists of a nuraghe of an unusual type, built of roughly squared megalithic blocks laid in fairly regular courses. To the north-east an extensive village spreads out, mostly reduced to a scatter of stones; from the general collapse a few megalithic structures and some huts uncovered by unauthorised diggers emerge. The nuraghe, on the other hand, retains its original elevation to a certain height, but its ground plan is not immediately legible.
descriptions.NUR10096: Complex nuraghe with a single tower and a secondary tower connected by walls, with a courtyard situated between the two towers. There are also remains of walls, bunds, and wells that were used for water collection.
descriptions.NUR4065: Among the few remaining elements of the nuraghe, the lintel deserves special mention, appearing almost suspended in the air.
descriptions.NUR18739: Nuraghe completely destroyed by agricultural improvement works. Possible location.
descriptions.NUR4805:
Four-lobed nuraghe built of white limestone.

It preserves a magnificent and grand tholos. Is Paras is one of the most elegant nuragic constructions in Sardinia. It consists of a central tower partially enclosed by a three-lobed bastion including a large courtyard. The main tower, circular in plan (diameter 12.50 m x 12.70 m), made of white limestone blocks, 12.70 m high, was composed of two superimposed floors, of which only the lower one remains today.
descriptions.NUR5405: Small complex nuraghe to which a lateral transverse addition was later added
descriptions.NUR5917: Ispiene was part of the territory of Chiaramonti. About 15 years ago we transferred two thousand hectares to the new commune of Erula, along with a certain number of nuraghes, including Ispiene. For this reason "I still feel it is mine," and if you want to find the character of strength, you must come here; but even more so the unshakable, sacred character of the nuraghe, infused with its cells and the sun, which at the zenith during the summer solstice penetrates into it and unites with Mother Earth. mu
descriptions.NUR16201: The probable nuraghe is situated halfway up the slope of Monte "Sa Corona Arrubia". Its structure remains indeterminate: due to the significant presence of fallen stones arranged in a disordered manner; and because of the dense vegetation that obstructs any view. Only a few courses can be seen, arranged in a circular pattern in their original position, likely belonging to the central tower. In the area, on the surface, several ceramic fragments are present.
descriptions.NUR526: The nuraghe is located in the territory of Riola Sardo, adjacent to the marsh; the nuraghe was not recorded and appears even less in the maps.
descriptions.NUR20255:
What is visible is only a small portion. The rest is completely buried and covered by vegetation. Structure with a circular form on multiple levels.

A little lower down, an ancient wall cut from the rocks and composed of very large stone blocks.
descriptions.NUR5697: The structure of the nuraghe is clearly complex; the compact mass of the monument is immediately apparent, dominated by the central tower. To the north-west of the nuraghe, about ten metres away inside the enclosure, stands a large stone which, because of its shape, is thought to be a stele; its presence gives the site its name, and also the name of the Nuraghe Istelai, or "place of the steles". All around, traces of the ancient human settlement are evident, ranging from the pre-Nuragic period back to the Neolithic.
descriptions.NUR4949: The Su Nuraxi di Loceri nuraghe was built incorporating a rocky outcrop. The main tower is well preserved and was constructed with local granite blocks, partly roughly shaped and arranged to form regular courses. Its entrance is raised above the surrounding plain by at least three courses.
descriptions.NUR5097: The Su Nuraxi di Loceri nuraghe was built incorporating a rocky outcrop. The main tower is well preserved and was constructed with local granite blocks, partly roughly shaped and arranged to form regular courses. Its entrance is raised above the surrounding plain by at least three courses.
descriptions.NUR11485: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR2744: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR11486: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR6484: Built with local granite stones, it has a roughly triangular plan and exhibits features blending those of corridor nuraghes (the most archaic type of nuraghe) and tholos nuraghes (an evolution of the former). The central chamber with its tholos roof remains intact, while the lateral chambers are partially collapsed. The structure has two entrances: one in the south-west (the main entrance) and another in the south-east.
descriptions.NUR1347: The nuraghe, of which only a few remains are left, is at an elevation of 599 metres.
descriptions.NUR6436: Located near the municipal pine forest, four km north of the village, the nuraghe Jana is in poor state of conservation. The nuraghe, in addition to having collapsed internally, was previously used as a shelter for shepherds, so that most of its stones were arranged in a radial pattern as a boundary wall.
descriptions.NUR4485: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe near the Nuraghe Arrubiu. It is hidden by vegetation and in the surrounding area there is a small nuraghe, located in the steep hillside: Nuraghe Jana II.
descriptions.NUR12592: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe near the Nuraghe Arrubiu. It is hidden by vegetation and in the surrounding area there is a nuraghe, located in the steep hillside: Nuraghe Jana.
descriptions.NUR6065: "Nuraghe Ianna Bassa, under the Monte Sedda Sos Campos, near good springs, are the remains of the nuraghe, part of the foundation and above, a heap of stones. In Antioco Sanna soil." The Taramelli's description, seventy years later, is still substantially consistent with the current state of the ruins.
descriptions.NUR1709: The sacred area, dominated to the east by the striking granite ridges of Monte Senes (about 862 m a.s.l.), was built in the Nuragic period at the pass of Janna 'e Pruna, currently traversed by the Irgoli–Norghio road and situated at an elevation of about 590 m a.s.l.—a key point of ancient passage along a mountain route that linked the valley of Riu Siniscola with that of Cedrino, important pathways for inland penetration from the coast into the island.
descriptions.NUR8044: Uncertain structure, appears to be a Nuragic foundation.
descriptions.NUR3715: Small nuraghe reduced to a heap of ruins.
descriptions.NUR5619: Monument in poor condition of disintegration. It is located on a secondary summit of the Monte Nibbarone (237 m) at an elevation of 168 m a.s.l., from where it dominates the entire valley below.
descriptions.NUR11527: The complex consists of a nuraghe and a village of about 90–100 huts, spread over five hectares. Due to its extensive size and the number of buildings, the site is considered unique within the Nuragic context of Gallura.
descriptions.NUR3749: The monolith of "La Serra" is named after the nearby nuraghe, a plurimillennial monument shaped like a truncated cone now reduced to a ruin. The massive stone, composed of multiple fragments, dates to the late Neolithic period, although no precise dates are known; it is certain that the monolith predates the nuraghe by a long time. (Pieragica)
descriptions.NUR1447: Single-tower nuraghe in very poor condition, only two courses remain.
descriptions.NUR1536: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe. Destroyed by a excavator to build a restaurant in the years 1980–85. During excavation, a pot and a bronze dagger were found. Built in the Recent Bronze Age (1300–1150 BC).
descriptions.NUR19547: Single-tower in white limestone, situated within an olive grove, the property boundary is tangent to the structure. Three visible courses remain on the eastern and western sides. Covered in vegetation, a tree growing at the centre of the nuraghe compromises its stability.
descriptions.NUR2911:
From the structure a large part of the Irgoli plain is clearly visible; to the north-east Monte Oddie can be seen.

In the surrounding area there are several collapses, and many ashlars from the structure have been used to build the dry-stone walls.

This is a tholos nuraghe partly leaning against the natural rock to the west; it has an inner and an outer wall face, and between them the spiral staircase can be made out; a guard chamber to the east is plausible, and a possible access ramp starting from the west.
descriptions.NUR5907: A careful survey has not revealed any trace of the Lavrone nuraghe, although some old people claimed it must have existed. The site was certainly anthropogenically modified due to the presence of some human artefacts. A curious anecdote is that Giacomino, who is no longer alive, had built more than "a nuraghe", meaning by the piles of stones gathered in the field. "Nuraghe of the large laurel".
descriptions.NUR3699: The nuraghe, located in land used for pastoralism and partly for viticulture, is irrevocably ruined due to illegal excavations that affected the area. Only a short section of the wall remains, which, however, does not allow us to define its further dimensions or the type of construction.
descriptions.NUR528: The quadrilobate complex nuraghe is reduced to a heap of large stones covered by dense vegetation, yet its massive presence can still be perceived.
descriptions.NUR5696: The site consists of the nuraghe, composed of the central tower and two other towers, various structures arranged around it that would suggest the presence of an important settlement in antiquity, and finally a structure that may represent an ancient sanctuary.
descriptions.NUR17377: It is more likely that this structure belongs to the nuraghe "Tanca di Monsignori", mentioned in the nuragographic map by F. Nissardi (published by G. Pinza in 1901).
descriptions.NUR3537: A few hundred metres from the Paddaggiu nuraghe, we find the Li Colti nuraghe. It may be a four-lobed nuraghe. From the main tower, 6 m of height remain, while the bastions show high mounds of debris and only one tower is legible.
descriptions.NUR1486: The little that remains of the nuraghe Li Espi near the Liscia dam
descriptions.NUR8734: Probable proto-nuraghe consisting of a tower section attached to a rock outcrop. Probable entrance to the south-east. From the top of the rock face, the panorama extends over the archipelago to the north-east and over Rena Majori to the north-west.
descriptions.NUR3105: Nuraghe about 9 m high, built with large basalt ashlar blocks. Corridor entrance about 5 m long with stairs on the left and a niche on the right. Intact tholos, diameter 5.30 m.
descriptions.NUR5906:
The site is located at the top of a slight hilltop, in an area currently used for grazing.

The simple nuraghe, standing on a granitic outcrop, shows only its external wall face, measuring about 1.50 metres in length.

The plan of the chamber, roughly circular, is somewhat irregular due to the inclusion, within the wall face, of a rocky spur of approximately trapezoidal shape, slightly projecting into the chamber.
descriptions.NUR5564:
Complex nuraghe, at the main tower a bastion was added, composed of at least three towers, though a fourth tower may have existed, currently invisible due to the dense vegetation covering the entire nuraghe.

It retains the tholos intact.
descriptions.NUR6420: One of the best-preserved single-tower (single-tower nuraghe) in the Seneghe area.
descriptions.NUR3431: Nuraghe built with calcareous white ashlar laid upon a rocky massif emerging from the dense forest. The walls remain to human height.
descriptions.NUR2825: Complex nuraghe of the lateral-addition type. A main tower is visible with a secondary tower alongside it on the east side. The entrance to the main tower, facing south, is lintelled and buried for more than half its original height. The entrance corridor, with the typical ogival section, is about 4 m long and built of perfectly worked basalt ashlars, showing a level of construction skill rarely found in other nuraghi in the area.
descriptions.NUR6248: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe partially eroded, surrounded by vegetation
descriptions.NUR3474:
The particularity of this nuraghe lies in the presence of a short passage on the wall opposite the entrance, opening into a large window with a lintel, topped by a drainage window.

The nuraghe is a single-tower (single-tower nuraghe) and shows no trace of any kind of staircase. The entrance, located in the north-west, features a lintel surmounted by a carefully worked drainage window.
descriptions.NUR2879: Single-tower nuraghe. The corridor leading to the circular chamber, which is without a vault, has on its left a wide staircase about 1 metre in width.
descriptions.NUR2750: Single-tower nuraghe. The corridor leading to the circular chamber, which is vaultless, has on its left a wide staircase about 1 metre in width. Nearby is a nuraghe known as Lobaos II, visible in the photo.
descriptions.NUR5088: damaged nuraghe near a complex of domus de janas
descriptions.NUR3844: It is located within the territory of the comune of Florinas (SS) and is a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe with a singular entrance oriented to the northeast. Very ruined. An old footpath once ran almost beside it, but is now completely abandoned.
descriptions.NUR3003:
Complex nuraghe, with a bilobate bastion.

The central tower is equipped with a mezzanine.
descriptions.NUR3322: The name means "open stone". The monument is in a state of severe degradation.
descriptions.NUR6175:
The nuraghe, situated at an altitude of about 794 m, is of mixed type, featuring elements both of corridor nuraghes and tholos nuraghes. It consists of a central tower to which a three-lobed bastion is attached.

Around the nuraghe is a village of huts, and at a short distance, two giants' tombs and a dolmen.
descriptions.NUR821: Unfortunately, the nuraghe Longu does not differ much from the state of extreme emergency observed in most of the nuraghes of Chiaramonti. Interesting is its study and architecture, which places it at the centre of attention as belonging to those with a subterranean chamber. Mario Unali
descriptions.NUR3504: The nuraghe is a complex structure, consisting of a main tower with two additional towers attached at a later stage, connected by a straight curtain wall. The main tower, built with well-cut basalt blocks (especially in the upper sections) arranged in regular courses, has an entrance in the north-east, topped by a lintel with a drainage window and elevated above the camp level.
descriptions.NUR2639: The nuraghe Santu Antine, also called Sa domo de su Re ("The King's House" in Italian), is one of the most majestic nuraghi in the whole of Sardinia and also one of the most important of those still standing. The entire complex is a major example of prehistoric Mediterranean architecture, and its original height is thought to have reached between 22 and 24 metres, the tallest for that period after the Egyptian pyramids and the central tower of the Nuragic palace of Arrubiu, which measured between 25 and 30 metres.
descriptions.NUR5495: The nuraghe Santu Antine, also called Sa domo de su Re ("The King's House" in Italian), is one of the most majestic nuraghi in the whole of Sardinia and also one of the most important of those still standing. The entire complex is a major example of prehistoric Mediterranean architecture, and its original height is thought to have reached between 22 and 24 metres, the tallest for that period after the Egyptian pyramids and the central tower of the Nuragic palace of Arrubiu, which measured between 25 and 30 metres.
descriptions.NUR4116: The nuraghe has an elongated elliptical plan corresponding to the type of corridor nuraghe, and its structure is built upon the natural rock, adapting partially to it. At several points along the external perimeter, the elevation is preserved up to six courses in height, so that one can observe how the base blocks gradually decrease in size from bottom to top.
descriptions.NUR6272: The Longu nuraghe, as seen in the photos, is an imposing single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe. Unfortunately, there is no detailed description available.
descriptions.NUR4313: It is one of many nuraghes in the Tertenia area and preserves the tholos intact.
descriptions.NUR3392: Site accessible only by traversing a difficult path. The ruined monument, difficult to read, retains a section to the east with 11 irregular courses of the wall.
descriptions.NUR3621: The nuraghe Loppelìe, despite its collapses, still remains in good condition. The entrance, well preserved, is triangular. On the left side of the entrance passage, an internal staircase opens. Moreover, the nuraghe Loppelìe deserves to be visited for the splendid panorama enjoyed from the summit of the structure, which stretches from the village of Triei below to the mountains above Baunei, and from the bay of Arbatax to the peaks of the Gennargentu.
descriptions.NUR1938: Single-tower tholos nuraghe built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The entrance, opening to the south, is lintelled and gives access to the corridor; to its left opens the stairwell of the helical staircase that led to the upper chamber, which no longer exists. The inner chamber is well preserved except for the top of the false dome, which has collapsed. Two facing niches open inside the chamber, oriented respectively east and west.
descriptions.NUR4296: The Lorenzu Origa nuraghe partially incorporates into its curtain wall the pink granite spur. The monument appears as a truncated conical tower with a diameter of about 11 m, preserving at least 2.80 m – 2.50 m of height. The other opening, topped by a lintel, leads into an area that in reality is a sort of covered corridor composed of blocks arranged in steps and may represent part of a staircase chamber.
descriptions.NUR5902: Complex nuraghe of the tancato type, built with polygonal basalt blocks of local origin. The structure is difficult to read due to dense vegetation, including shrubs and climbers, which conceal the structural elements. The main tower, presumably the older, remains standing to a height of almost 6 m. It is connected to a secondary tower located to the south of the first. The secondary tower survives to a height of about 4 m.
descriptions.NUR3551:
The mastio dates to the 15th–13th centuries BC, while the bastion, the outer wall, and the curtain wall date to the 13th–late 12th century.

Already in the Early Iron Age, the findings show a gradual decline in site occupation, though the site was not entirely abandoned.

It was also used for funerary purposes, as evidenced by the remains from the 7th–8th centuries BC.
descriptions.NUR3424: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe with its top missing, of which only a few courses remain
descriptions.NUR6440: Nuraghe Loschiri, located in the territory of Semestene, a small village in the Meilogu (visible in the background to the right of the image). Partially collapsed, it preserves intact its entrance portal and large internal sections.
descriptions.NUR3252: The nuraghe is situated on the summit of a granitic rock massif; it is a small single-tower nuraghe in an advanced state of degradation, and the dense vegetation prevents access for visitors.
descriptions.NUR2420: The abundant collapse of the structure and the vegetation covering the monument make the site difficult to read, it could be a corridor nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR8889: It is located to the north-east along the provincial road near the border with the territory of Ruinas. It stands on a large calcareous foundation and is filled with its own stone masonry, which renders access impossible. According to common belief, it was composed of a succession of three superimposed rooms. Remains of a staircase are visible along a ridge.
descriptions.NUR15807:
Single-tower nuraghe. Four courses survive intact. In poor condition. Built of roughly dressed medium-sized blocks. Signs of human spoliation. Already shown on Filippo Nissardi's nuraghe map (in Pinza G. 1901).

The hillock occupied by the nuraghe includes a stretch of Roman cobblestone paving identified to the north-west of the monument. The dense vegetation covering the site makes it impossible to detect any remains or traces of a possible village.
descriptions.NUR2696: The single-tower nuraghe is equipped with a mezzanine or mezzanine floor, built above the corridor leading to the chamber.
descriptions.NUR5821: Nuraghe whose southern side has collapsed but still retains the tholos intact
descriptions.NUR11538: Complex nuraghe with a main tower and bastions, possibly including a second tower. Nearby are the remains of a settlement and the Giants' tomb of Li Mizzani. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR11592: This nuraghe, already noted in the 1922 EEM, is included in the Archaeological Map of Taramelli at a short distance to the west of the Nuraghe Pischedda. Of the monument, which already in the 1930s appeared almost completely destroyed – “Only the foundation remains, one metre high” – no trace remains today. It was also known by the name of S. Giuseppe.
descriptions.NUR5375:
The nuraghe is largely destroyed. Built on a rocky hill at the outermost eastern edge of the Anghelu Nieddu valley.

Constructed with medium and small stones, it was intended to appear as a single-tower of reduced size.
descriptions.NUR5612: The complex nuraghe is composed of three parts built in different periods: the mastio, whose construction phase dates to about 1000 B.C.; the quadrilobate bastion with the courtyard, built between the 9th and 7th centuries B.C.; and the antemurale with the four external towers, raised between the 7th and 6th centuries B.C.
descriptions.NUR19514: The site is named after the fact that there once stood a nuraghe, of which no trace remains. It was demolished around 1960, during the construction of the present-day road Castelsardo–Santa Teresa Gallura (SP90); the stone material was reused for this work.
descriptions.NUR5807:
Nuraghe with attached village of huts.

The tholos is still intact.
descriptions.NUR5641:
Preserves the tholos intact.

Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe in basalt, about 10.80 m high; from the entrance, about 1.60 m high, access is gained to the corridor, and immediately to the left there is a staircase with 13 steps.
descriptions.NUR2724:
Complex nuraghe.

Of the nuraghe, located on a modest hill (563 m. a.s.l.), only a few courses of the central tower remain.
descriptions.NUR1578: Damaged nuraghe of which the shape is not recognizable
descriptions.NUR1247: It is in very poor condition and surrounded by dense vegetation.
descriptions.NUR2506:
Angius, known as "Macariu 1849. Taramelli. and cadastral record 1883. Also Girillis."

It is a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe built of trachytic stone, whose structure is poorly visible due to the dense vegetation. Inside, the tower's route is partially discernible. Adjacent to the nuraghe are structures likely belonging to the village. In the area, several ceramic fragments are also present.
descriptions.NUR1649: Nuraghe apparently a single-tower, freed from vegetation in 2022. Previously classified as a single-tower, it is now more likely to be quadrilobate. Around the nuraghe a considerable amount of Roman-era pottery (sealed) is present.
descriptions.NUR1652:
The nuraghe is in very poor conservation conditions (only a maximum of two courses remain) and is completely covered by vegetation.

Around it there is a vast scatter of baetyls, laterites, and coppi.
descriptions.NUR5733: It is a complex structure composed of a central tower (or mastio) and two additional towers situated adjacent to the south. Its entrance is partially collapsed, making access difficult.
descriptions.NUR16976:
Structures related to a complex nuraghe of four-lobed type, built with polygonal basalt blocks. The building has undergone considerable dismantling, leaving only two or three courses remaining, depending on the section.  

The bastion, three towers, and part of the curtain wall can be seen, with large accumulations of rubble attached to the structure. In place of the central tower, a large excavation made with mechanical equipment is visible. The entire structure has suffered significant erosion.
descriptions.NUR3690: Located at the top of the hill known as Montes. It commands a wide view of the landscape.
descriptions.NUR4588: Single-tower, collapsed and stripped, with only the ruins scattered on the ground.
descriptions.NUR5654: Structures belonging to a complex tholos nuraghe built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The central tower has its lower chamber intact and the base of the upper one; the northern part of the bastion is visible, with two towers, while the whole southern part is covered by vegetation. The other two towers, not yet located because they are hidden by vegetation, may lie to the south of the central tower.
descriptions.NUR2051: The complex nuraghe, probably three-lobed, is in such a state of degradation that the structural elements are almost impossible to detect. Around the nuraghe over a large stretch, fragments of Punic and Roman ceramics are found, indicating the presence of a settlement.
descriptions.NUR1927:
In a dominant position, just a few metres from the northern bank of the Rio Merchis—marking the boundary between the municipal territories of Borore and Norbello—less than 400 metres to the south-east of the Nuraghe s'Istrampu and about 250 metres to the south of the domus de janas of Ortigosu.

The site appears as a hill scattered with stones and covered by dense undergrowth. The collapse and vegetation make a precise planimetric definition of the monument extremely difficult.
descriptions.NUR2079: Single-tower nuraghe covered by sand. In its surroundings are visible traces of habitation and a well dug into the rock.
descriptions.NUR4953: Nuraghe Maistu Peldu (commonly known as de Su Par e Pelda) has two still-standing towers about two metres high. The vault, collapsed, exposes the interior of the tholos, which is about 1 m deep. The ashlars, relatively large, suggest the presence of a watchtower nuraghe that controlled the entrance to the Chia valley. In front stands a menhir, the menhir that prays, de Su Par 'e Pelda, visible from Provincial Road 72.
descriptions.NUR18100: The position is approximate. The nuraghe is marked on the maps of the former Catasto.
descriptions.NUR5501:
It is a bilobed nuraghe built with large trachyte blocks, roughly worked and arranged in irregular courses.

At the central tower, which survives to a height of about (???) metres, a second tower is attached to the east, slightly elliptical in shape. From above, part of an internal niche of this second tower is visible, its walls lined with precisely squared limestone blocks.
descriptions.NUR3164: Along the road to Erula, the Nuraghe Majore rises prominently, protected by walls and bordered on the north-east by a large cliff. A single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe, still in excellent condition, has a tholos that is almost intact.
descriptions.NUR5498:
The Maiore nuraghe (14th–9th century BC) is a single-tower type, currently standing more than eight metres high, with a clear taper towards the top; it has a single entrance on the south-east side. From the entrance a corridor leads to the central ground-floor chamber, which has a tholos roof, while on the left a stairway gives access to the upper level.

Because the tower suffered a major collapse before the 1980s, restoration work became necessary.
descriptions.NUR2931:
Built entirely of granite, it is of the central-corridor type, with a mixed layout that combines the plan of corridor nuraghi and tholos nuraghi with a central corridor and paired chambers; the structure is massive and irregular. The tholos is intact.

The bastion is reached by a staircase accessible from the courtyard. The entrance leads into a central corridor, covered by an ogival vault, which runs the full length of the building and opens onto a large courtyard.
descriptions.NUR5535: Considering the characteristics of the minimally worked stones, their small size, and the type of collapse that gives them an elongated form, it is possible this structure represents a proto-nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR6421: It is located within a private farm. Surrounded by vegetation, it is partially eroded but still used as a shelter for sheep.
descriptions.NUR20311: It is a simple nuraghe with a typical troncoconical shape, probably a single-tower with a tholos. It is composed of large granitic blocks. At its highest point about seven courses can be counted, but it is clear that there are others below the level of the floor.
descriptions.NUR2840: Nuraghe characterized by a calcareous lintel, white on dark walls. The tholos has collapsed inward.
descriptions.NUR3048: Nuraghe characterized by a calcareous lintel, white on dark walls. The tholos has collapsed inward.
descriptions.NUR3292:
The monument is located in the area of Mandras (Campeda), about 600 metres to the northeast of the nuraghe Mura Sauccu, and less than 300 metres west of the nuraghe Mura Sauccu B.

It is a single-tower (single-tower nuraghe) that survives to a maximum height of about 6.50 metres. The masonry is composed of large and medium-sized stones.
descriptions.NUR1011: A single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe, about 100 metres from the monument, there is a Roman-era underground chamber, partly excavated into the rock and partly built with rubble masonry and a barrel-vaulted roof.
descriptions.NUR5143: The monument is a single-tower nuraghe, of whose external wall only four courses remain.
descriptions.NUR6220: Corridor nuraghe with concentric plan... (a short distance from the nuraghe there is another structure of uncertain nature, which, in my opinion, dates to the Nuragic period – see photo). From the top, the panorama is breathtaking! a 360° view of forest! to the east, the entire Supramonte stretches in the background.
descriptions.NUR6135: From the early photos, the section of the Tolos is visible but partially collapsed. The splendid niche is also evident. It is easily accessible, although it is located on private land. It is situated just a few hundred metres from the Romanesque Cathedral of Sant'Antioco in Bisarcio.
descriptions.NUR3916: Nuraghe Mannu stands on the summit of the beautiful beach of Cala Fuili. The significance of this site is mainly due to the Nuragic village of Nuragheddu, which is one of the largest in Sardinia and comprises more than 200 huts of various shapes and sizes.
descriptions.NUR4853:
It is located to the west of the inhabited centre, along the border with the territory of Villaurbana. It is a simple single-chamber type. It is undoubtedly the best preserved and presumably one of the latest nuraghes in the municipal area.

Local oral tradition claims that this nuraghe was subjected to a dynamite attack in the 1930s; the arrangement of the ashlar stones in the dome and the condition of the western side support this hypothesis.
descriptions.NUR1418:
From IGM. The aerial map suggests the polygon is occupied by a modern cottage.

The nuraghe today is probably destroyed or at least not identifiable.
descriptions.NUR19890: Nuraghe of undefined structure. Unfortunately, only faint traces remain of the nuraghe, as it was completely demolished to make way for a RAI antenna. At the base of the antenna, several stones are piled haphazardly. At the edge of a recess, adjacent to what may have been the base of the nuraghe, remains the probable footprint of a hut.
descriptions.NUR868: Complex nuraghe built of slates (stintino stone). Three towers remain, with a powerful outer wall enclosing the structure. Around the nuraghe, traces of huts and collapses of related structures are clearly visible. It preserves a tholos almost intact, except for some courses.
descriptions.NUR1899: The nuraghe is in a very advanced state of collapse. Only a maximum of two courses of the original tower's perimeter remain intact. Given the few surviving stones still present in situ, it is possible the structure was dismantled to reuse its stones. A few metres away, stones likely belonging to the nuraghe are found, possibly used to build a sheepfold for animal watering. Currently, the nuraghe is completely enveloped by vegetation.
descriptions.NUR4307: Two nuraghe towers very close to each other
descriptions.NUR5791: Nuraghe in excellent condition, although surrounded by vegetation. The internal tholos is intact.
descriptions.NUR579: Complex nuraghe with a central tower and two lateral towers connected by bastions that enclose a courtyard.
descriptions.NUR19469:
The Margone nuraghe stands on the summit of a hill and is largely hidden by dense vegetation, especially prickly pear and wild olive.

Its important function is emphasised by the complexity of the structure: it is a three-lobed nuraghe with a central tower 12 m in diameter. Around it one can trace stretches of polygonal masonry, built of medium-sized limestone blocks, that link three secondary towers to the main tower.
descriptions.NUR4104: Complex quadrilobate nuraghe of considerable size. Never excavated and located within a private property, thus inaccessible. It is distinguished by some particular artefacts placed inside, including a menhir.
descriptions.NUR4158: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe, part of a larger settlement. The central tower is partially collapsed, with a fairly wide terrace that encircles the main tower. It has a secondary entrance located to the north-east. Nearby, at the base of the nuraghe, there are the foundations of huts.
descriptions.NUR4998: Unfortunately, no significant structure remains, as the site was completely destroyed together with the village of the same period. It provides surface evidence of a hilltop settlement belonging to the early phases of the Middle Bronze Age (17th–16th century BC), as fragments of obsidian, Nuragic ceramic shards, and lithic tools have been recovered, indicating the presence of domestic shelters.
descriptions.NUR993: Single-tower made of large white limestone blocks, located in the courtyard of a private dwelling. About three courses remain, with a maximum height of about 3 m and a minimum of about 2 m. Base diameter: about 15 m. The structure is in a state of collapse; conservation state: mediocre.
descriptions.NUR5236: It is one of the many nuraghes destroyed over the millennia due to vegetation, ploughing, land reclamation, and other uses. It should have been quadrilobate, possibly with a double anterior addition. But it is difficult to say for certain without a thorough cleaning and excavation.
descriptions.NUR12069: It is a single-tower nuraghe rising on a rocky outcrop; from the outside it appears in fairly good condition, but from the inside it shows only a heap of rubble, the roof is missing and part of the upper masonry is absent, so the internal chamber is occupied by fallen debris and does not allow for a detailed reading.
descriptions.NUR3905: Structures related to single-tower tholos nuraghes. The building, constructed from locally sourced polygonal basalt blocks, remains for about four courses on the northern side, while it is largely collapsed on the south, west, and east sides. The internal chamber has collapsed at its upper portion, and the rubble from the collapse fills the remaining space. The entrance cannot be identified.
descriptions.NUR4300: It is named after the family that owned the land on which it is situated. The nuraghe is completely collapsed and certainly quadrilobate. It is located 600 m from the palace of Barumini.
descriptions.NUR2599: It is a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe in evident state of degradation. Nevertheless, its mass and the harmony of the construction make it an interesting nuraghe both for its building techniques and architectural features. It rises on a trachyte base with a brown hue, and at times the stones forming its base blend seamlessly with the natural rocks, providing structural strength to the construction. mu
descriptions.NUR3438: Completely buried... and overlooked. In the village it is said that originally it was the largest in the area and that part of the upper tower was removed for building material.
descriptions.NUR18476: The nuraghe is named after the location situated on the south-eastern slopes of the Giara di Gesturi. It is mentioned by Taramelli in his study of the prehistoric monuments of the Giara; however, the census conducted in the 1980s did not record any trace of it.
descriptions.NUR3828: It is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan, diameter 11.20 m, with residual walling of 3.20 m in height, four courses. The masonry consists of polyhedral blocks, roughly shaped. Already at the time of the Taramelli the nuraghe had been destroyed, leaving only the base.
descriptions.NUR2498: Four-lobed nuraghe, with four towers at the corners of the quadrangular bastion and an internal courtyard facing the central tower's entrance. The nuraghe is completely collapsed; remnants of its fortification are visible in the vicinity.
descriptions.NUR11171: Base of a nuraghe near the old fire watch tower, built with schist blocks.
descriptions.NUR11481: Complex nuraghe with settlement; no traces remain on the surface.
descriptions.NUR5452: This nuraghe is arranged longitudinally and features several cavities (likely towers...) of small dimensions. Four can be seen from the aerial photograph, but there are at least five, if not more. It is truly interesting and would warrant restoring the standing sections, currently buried under the collapses of the upper parts, to better understand its original layout; the towers are of small size and it is unclear whether they were access ramps to a superstructure or served some other function.
descriptions.NUR3341: Nuraghe completely collapsed, its shape difficult to define
descriptions.NUR3177: Complex nuraghe, covered by dense vegetation; near the nuraghe, a menhir and several giants' tombs, concealed by the thick vegetation, are observed.
descriptions.NUR8289: Nuraghe destroyed during the times of the local land reclamation. In the area large stones (not found in the surrounding region) remain, used several decades ago to build terraces. In the area, fragments of pottery, probably Nuragic, and pieces of grinding stones from the same period have been found. It remains impossible to determine their exact location and dimensions.
descriptions.NUR4489: It is the best-preserved nuraghe in the Tratalias area and is located in one of the numerous medaus, known as is Cuccus. It is a single-tower nuraghe with a remaining height of about 5 m, built from megalithic blocks of andesite. The internal circular chamber is about 5.50 m wide, features a topless tholos, and is completely free of collapse.
descriptions.NUR8243: Complex nuraghe with uncertain plan layout, featuring a very large tower and a series of wall structures of uncertain function connected to it. The site was also occupied during the Punic and Roman periods.
descriptions.NUR4071: Near the Medau Massidda or Ghisu, two small buildings built with dry-stone walls, circular in plan, occupy two eminences dominating the valley that slopes down towards Porto Paglia: they may represent a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe or a tower-hut and a smaller hut.
descriptions.NUR4597: Near the Medau Massidda or Ghisu, two small buildings built with dry-stone walls, circular in plan, occupy two eminences dominating the valley that slopes down towards Porto Paglia: they may represent a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe or a tower-hut and a smaller hut.
descriptions.NUR510: Nuraghe of undetermined type. The nuraghe features an unusual staircase that, at about halfway along the entrance corridor, projects diagonally from a height of 2.20 metres above the floor level, extending over more than 5 metres with an exceptionally steep vertical rise that breaks out onto the terrace. The ceiling of the chamber remains intact.
descriptions.NUR2786: Single-tower partially collapsed and covered by vegetation
descriptions.NUR2592: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe heavily collapsed, with only a few courses remaining
descriptions.NUR4772: Vittorio Angius calls it Fumìu: "It is a design, about which one cannot form an idea without having it sketched." He continues to state that there are more nuraghe that compose it: "Above the open door facing the sirocco from the leeward side is a small opening, and not far from this is a second open door facing the sirocco and two metres high, although appearing as a window because it is set high above the ground; on one of its sides is an opening in the wall thickness leading to the upper levels or to the terrace."
descriptions.NUR4130: Single-tower enclosed within a bastion. Four courses of massive arenite blocks from the wall are visible, with a height of almost 2 metres. Climbing the wall, the top of the tower is seen to be ruined.
descriptions.NUR4691:
The hill is not easily accessible to visitors due to the Mediterranean scrub. The vehicle must be abandoned at a distance of about one hundred metres from the coastal road between Sarroch and Pula. From there, one ascends on foot to the nuraghe.

It is difficult to determine exactly how many towers surrounded the central one.

However, it is certain that it must have been a four-lobed structure with access to the south-east, whose "mastio" featured the three typical internal niches.
descriptions.NUR2662: The nuraghe Mereu or 'Intro de Padente', entirely built of white limestone with well-cut stones of medium size, is situated on a height that dominates the surrounding area. The nuraghe is of complex type, consisting of a main tower and two additional towers, further protected by straight bastions.
descriptions.NUR3128: Damaged nuraghe, overgrown with vegetation. Likely single-tower (single-tower nuraghe).
descriptions.NUR6473: In total, the ruin still reveals only a few stones that form the basal circle, composed of white, friable limestone. mu
descriptions.NUR5990: It is four-lobed, with a central tower surrounded by a bastion against which the other four towers are built. In places it is quite ruined, yet it still reaches a height of more than ten metres; the ground floor is well preserved, while the upper floor lacks its roof although the masonry survives to a certain height. As often happens in multi-storey towers, the upper floor was characterised by a large window.
descriptions.NUR5007: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe very hidden by vegetation, built on a rocky outcrop that intersects with the stones of the curtain wall. The site is dated to the Middle Bronze Age.
descriptions.NUR10453: It is located in an area containing the Barru nuraghe and the remains of other nuraghes. It appears to be a single-tower nuraghe broken down, fragmented, and buried.
descriptions.NUR15819: Probable location. In a pasture area, hidden behind a large thicket of mastic, in poor conservation state, some stone blocks are visible. Adjacent to the wastewater treatment plant it may have suffered damage during recent installation works of the structure.
descriptions.NUR8547: Nuraghe partially collapsed with an open tholos
descriptions.NUR11729: Located on a rocky spur near the road between Thiesi and Romana, it dominates the landscape below, where in particular the nuraghe Majore is situated.
descriptions.NUR8206: Nuraghe now almost completely disappeared, of which only a few traces remain visible among the bushes, including two rows of stones.
descriptions.NUR5784: The nuraghe is a complex type, consisting of a central tower closed by a three-lobed bastion. It still rises, despite its current residual height of only five metres, above the plain of Birori, offering a breathtaking view. It was the subject of an excavation campaign in 1995.
descriptions.NUR2421: From the remains that emerge from this nuragic structure located beside the church of Madonna della Pace, I am convinced that this is the Nuraghe of Moddorocco, or that there were two nuraghes.
descriptions.NUR8864: Located on a promontory overlooking the municipal road from Villaurbana to the locality 'S'utturu on cardu'. The tower is largely collapsed and inaccessible.
descriptions.NUR4017: Nuraghe completely destroyed by quarrying activities
descriptions.NUR3694: Complex nuraghe of the tancato type, with a central tower and a secondary tower with bastions. On the IGM map this nuraghe is mistakenly identified as the nearby Sa Tiria nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR2822:
The site is located less than 400 metres to the northeast of the village of Sagama, near the southern bank of the Riu Ralzu: beyond the river, about 160 metres to the north-northeast, stands the proto-nuraghe Mulineddu.

It is a single-tower (single-tower nuraghe) with a corridor niche and a chamber bordered by a niche.
descriptions.NUR6428: Structures related to single-tower tholos nuraghe built from locally sourced polygonal basalt blocks. The internal chamber is collapsed at its upper portion; debris from the collapse is found on the O and N sides of the nuraghe. The structure is accessible only through the entrance corridor, about 5 m long, to the left of which opens a partially filled chamber that was intended to provide access to the stairs leading to the upper chamber.
descriptions.NUR5444: The monument must have been a far more complex and articulated structure than one can imagine today, looking at the surviving ruins, which nevertheless still retain a semblance of their original monumentality. The first tower, circular in plan, has its foundations set on a bedrock surface; the inner chamber has an oval layout whose elongated end joins the wall face of what must have been the main tower.
descriptions.NUR1866: Nuraghe composed of a primitive central tower and several towers. The interior of the central tower is filled with earth and fallen stones. On the eastern side, a lintel-covered passage is visible, interrupted by a collapse after a few metres. A short distance from the central tower, a curved wall is present, which probably marked the boundary of a peripheral tower. To the NNW, adjacent to the nuraghe, an oval-shaped area is visible. In the area, on the surface, numerous ceramic fragments from different periods are present.
descriptions.NUR1701:
A particularly striking proto-nuraghe for the beauty of its proto-historic architecture, the original tholos access is preserved, integrated within the rocky mass.  

Outside the granite block, and visible, are depressions that form natural sculptures; inside there is a shelter beneath rock, probably already in use in earlier periods.
descriptions.NUR1692: The nuraghe is located in the MURAVERA COMMUNE. The entire upper complex, four-lobed with some semi-quadrangular towers, extends along a north-west to south-east axis of about 53 m and an east to west axis of about 6–25 m. The external curtain wall can only be traced along its eastern portion and a small southern section: it is an imposing structure with a thick wall that closed the natural rock outcrop gaps.
descriptions.NUR1863: Complex nuraghe. Traces of at least three towers, probably added concentrically, can be identified. The original tower retains its wall outline, broken to the south by a small opening. The interior is partly blocked by soil and collapse debris. To the south and south-south-east there are two triangular corridors whose outlines, interrupted by collapse, are visible for several metres; one suggests the presence of a stairwell. Clandestine excavations are visible.
descriptions.NUR4627: Bronze Age materials (mainly fragments of pottery and shallow bowls), almost entirely belonging to the S. Cosimo cultural phase and recovered from the surface, mostly come from Crastu Mountains, Atziaddei Mountains, Ibera Mountains, Porceddu Mountains, and Acutzu Mountains. Materials from the Monti Mannu phase are found only in the Serrentese locality, which gives the phase its name; further specific studies are needed to fully understand this assemblage.
descriptions.NUR4583: Bronze Age materials (mainly fragments of pottery and shallow bowls), almost entirely belonging to the S. Cosimo cultural phase and recovered from the surface, mostly come from Crastu Mountains, Atziaddei Mountains, Ibera Mountains, Porceddu Mountains, and Acutzu Mountains. Materials from the Monti Mannu phase are found only in the Serrentese locality, which gives the phase its name; further specific studies are needed to fully understand this assemblage.
descriptions.NUR1248: In the immediate area behind the mouth of the Mannu River, the complex nuraghe Monte Aiveghe remains with a height of about 1.2 m, consisting of three courses of calcareous blocks corresponding to the top of the two towers. Surrounding it, the remains of at least three huts are identifiable, likely belonging to the associated settlement. There is also evidence of ceramic material dating to the Roman period.
descriptions.NUR3036: Reduced to an extreme state of ruin. Since the 1970s, a forest fire watch post has been stationed here by the Sardinian Forest Corps. Clear traces of the nuraghe's construction remain, but the structure has been plundered by various local people and treasure hunters (siddados = treasures) of ancient Sardinians.
descriptions.NUR20534: From a first and certainly partial survey, it may be stated that this could be a complex nuraghe, since it is clearly evident the insertion of a peripheral tower on the central body of the nuraghe, although in very poor conservation. It is also possible to note the presence of important curtain walls, which may be interpreted hypothetically as the remains of an outer wall.
descriptions.NUR4920: The complex is located within the territory of Villaputzu and includes two towers known as N.ghe Monte Arrubiu I and II, which should be considered part of the same structure, together with the Nuragic village that develops in the adjacent plain. From the summit, a magnificent view is enjoyed. There are several rocks that take on particularly distinct shapes.
descriptions.NUR4692: It is elliptical, extends for about 30 metres in length, has a diameter of about 22 metres, and survives to a height of about 4 metres. In the north-west section of the curtain wall, an entrance connected to an internal corridor can be observed; this corridor served as a passage between the two main towers and originally had a roof composed of powerful slabs laid flat.
descriptions.NUR1533: It is a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe with a curtain wall, partially embedded in vegetation along almost the entire perimeter; nevertheless, entry to the tholos at the top, uncovered through the southern-eastern entrance, is possible. Inside there are two large niches and another door located in the north-west, half-submerged by soil.
descriptions.NUR11283: Single-tower nuraghe used as a quarry for the construction of walls and "pinnettas". Today, only a partial row of stones is visible.
descriptions.NUR6228: Complex nuraghe, of which the central tower is preserved in good condition and for almost the entire first level. The tholos is accessible via the entrance corridor, cleared of collapses.
descriptions.NUR4522: The building, a complex structure, incorporates within its bastion, at the western end of the rocky spur, a previous structure: probably a pseudo-nuraghe, whose plan cannot be defined due to poor preservation. The external wall face, visible only on the NE-facing side, is composed of basalt blocks arranged in irregular courses that incorporate natural rock outcrops.
descriptions.NUR6319: Single-tower nuraghe, eroded and surrounded by vegetation
descriptions.NUR4577: In the territory of Serrenti, the nuraghes with a transverse frontal addition are those of Cannedu and Monti Crabu.
descriptions.NUR4620: It is presumed that this single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe existed, despite the fact that the remaining remains are very scarce.
descriptions.NUR4180: At the Abealzu phase, only a few known materials have been attributed to the A1 shelter at Monti Crastu, which was used as a burial and was illegally excavated. The size and location of the proto-nuraghes at Monti Crastu and Monti Mannu suggest that these may have been the most important centres of cantons or sub-cantons in the pre-nuragic period of Campidano, or at least that, together with the other proto-nuraghe complexes, they may have controlled a large portion of the area.
descriptions.NUR4739:
It is located in the territory of Muravera, at a short distance from the Cuili Piras menhirs and near the border with the territory of Castiadas.

More specifically, it is a proto-nuraghe.

Of particular interest is an entrance, for which the lintel is well preserved.
descriptions.NUR3002: Reduced to complete ruin, only the base circle remains, where we can observe an opening to the north. No structures are sufficient for a precise classification of its typological affiliation; it is presumed to be a corridor nuraghe. An interesting area due to the presence of large stones arranged in a cut pattern, giving the impression of facing a giants' tomb.
descriptions.NUR12554: Apparently, but unlikely single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe, with some signs of other structures nearby.
descriptions.NUR3823: Very ruined, yet large blocks of hard limestone, roughly shaped, remain, highlighting the construction layout. The entrance to the south-south-east is visible, with a lintel on the ground near the two piers. The type of nuraghe refers to the sacred character of the site, linked to the union with the god, as the monument is seen as an extension of the mountain in the form of a conical trunk. mu
descriptions.NUR5675:
The enclosure has a single entrance; to its right a passage roofed with covering slabs, which resembles a giants' tomb — a rare feature in the Nuragic age, when tombs were always built near nuraghi but never inside them.

The tower standing on the hilltop has a single chamber with a niche, terraces and bastions defending the doorway, and an annular corridor that probably led to the terrace or to an upper floor.
descriptions.NUR14908: It currently appears as a modest height. Likely a complex nuraghe of "tancato" type (two towers with an intermediate courtyard). Remnants of walls remain. Destroyed by the opening of the municipal road.
descriptions.NUR3167:
Throughout the area, there are settlements and remains of huts dating from the Neolithic to the Medieval period.

This nuraghe is in a state of complete abandonment; no recovery works or excavations have ever been carried out to reveal or bring to light any artefacts.
descriptions.NUR5345: Probable proto-nuraghe with only 4 very irregular courses remaining
descriptions.NUR4134:
This nuraghe is located on the edge of the Teulada military zone.

From the geoportal it is known that around the Monte Idu nuraghe there still remain walls, built for some unknown reason. The site is magical, both for the presence of the monuments and for the breathtaking landscape offered to the visitor. Its landscape value is exceptional.

The nuraghe appears to be a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR3737: Part of it is periodically submerged by the level of the artificial basin of Omodeo.
descriptions.NUR2886: Single-tower nuraghe, eroded and enveloped by vegetation, near which a dolmen is reported.
descriptions.NUR4171: There should also be a corresponding Nuragic settlement at the site.
descriptions.NUR6162: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe, with its top missing and collapsed inward.
descriptions.NUR19465: Complex nuraghe of Mont'Elva with attached village. It is in a state of ruin due to works carried out in the 1950s for the high Nurra aqueduct water network. The central tower, partially buried, remains with a residual height of about 2 m; a secondary tower located to the south-west of the main one has been reduced to just two surviving courses, hidden by the dense Mediterranean scrub.
descriptions.NUR1873: Known as Nuraghe de su casteddu de Monte Maria, possibly a strongholds-type nuraghe, built on a granite base. Difficult to access, it was already visited and recorded by Lamarmora in 1830; it is said that a lightning strike reduced it to its present state. The northern and southern towers are accessible; it seems to be a corridor nuraghe adapted over time.
descriptions.NUR4037: The remains belong to a small complex nuraghe. The found debris suggests the presence of a small proto-nuraghe, possibly modified or demolished and then reconstructed as a classic nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR21182: Complex nuraghe of which two towers are still visible.
descriptions.NUR8796: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe, partially collapsed, located on a trachytic hilltop near the Cuga valley
descriptions.NUR14149: The summit of Monte 'E Mesu is formed by a small oval flat area. On one end stands the homonymous nuraghe, built almost perpendicularly against the rock face. In a small natural terraced area, located beneath the nuraghe, traces of huts and other Nuragic period artifacts are found, such as stones with bull-shaped forms, which lie in a state of complete abandonment and seem, even, weary from the millennia of life they have carried upon their shoulders.
descriptions.NUR553: Damaged nuraghe of which only a buried chamber built in masonry can be observed.
descriptions.NUR3452: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe with a damaged tholos. It retains part of the tholos to the west. In the past it was modified to house a sheepfold.
descriptions.NUR15828: The nuraghe remains for about 3 metres on the north side and has a diameter of about 10 metres. Constructed from medium-sized trachyte blocks, it is partly enveloped by vegetation. Dispersal of medium-sized Roman materials on the northeast side of the site.
descriptions.NUR8669: The nuraghe is located on top of Monte Nieddu
descriptions.NUR14885: Single-tower nuraghe no longer visible but noted by archaeologist Daniele Carta in his thesis (ArcheoArte 2012)
descriptions.NUR3930: The monument, with a subcircular plan, is situated almost at the summit of a steep and wooded hillside, currently used for sheep grazing. Three blocks of the left entrance pillar remain, oriented to the north, and two of the right pillar. The nuraghe, built with rough polygonal masonry and frequent use of zeppe, is composed of granite blocks of medium and large dimensions, only roughly shaped.
descriptions.NUR3677: The urban plan of Sassari (11 Dec. 2014) designates it as "Nuraghe Arcone I - Monte Palmas".
descriptions.NUR870: Almost on the top of a small hill is located the nuraghe of Monte Pedrosu. During the first or second world war it was used as a madhouse, as evidenced by the concrete wall added to the summit portion of the archaeological site.
descriptions.NUR15871: Single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan, built with large calcareous blocks shaped and preserved for 6 or 7 courses (height 3.50 m). It has an entrance on the east and a long passage, with two chambers opening to the left and right within the wall.
descriptions.NUR18157: Nuraghe to be verified as it might be a enclosure.
descriptions.NUR8199: Single-tower nuraghe with an elliptical plan. Other wall sections of undetermined function are present. The site was also occupied in Roman times.
descriptions.NUR3908: Reused in the Roman period and as a posting during the Second World War.
descriptions.NUR2165: Remains of a probable quadrangular fortification built by the Nuragic people. It survives as a large megalithic wall running along the eastern edge of the plateau that forms the mountain summit. The wall is broken by an entrance leading to a corridor parallel to the wall and roofed with basalt slabs laid flat. The place name “Sa Rocca 'e su Para” given to this mountain may refer to the use the Camaldolese friars made of the fortress in the Middle Ages.
descriptions.NUR3858:
Only a few of the basal stones remain. They are hard white tuff, still friable. They are located directly above the curved alignment along the mountain ridge, where several domus de janas are visible, extending along the crest of the named mountain and down its slope. www.archeologosardos.it

Nuraghe of the forated mountain. See Mònte pertùsu.
descriptions.NUR3738: It is a nuraghe of which only a few or no traces remain.
descriptions.NUR4198:
It is difficult to interpret as it is unclear whether it was composed of a single tower, in which case it would have had a wide diameter, or of multiple towers on different levels.

All that is visible are high, strongly built walls, constructed from subsquared blocks distributed over a large area.

It also appears that the wall faces of the monument enclose a space already defined by the rocky outcrops, which in many places are incorporated within this space.
descriptions.NUR3670: It was marked on the IM map but is now completely vanished.
descriptions.NUR5588: It is a very unusual nuraghe. The single chamber is set into the ground at the top of a trachytic mountain, so one reaches it by standing literally beneath it. Access is controlled by an outer wall with a main entrance facing west, while the nuraghe itself faces east, opening onto the cliff that naturally forms an inaccessible location—this is a strong defensive feature for those who believe in its defensive function.
descriptions.NUR6432:
The site is located on the edge of a hillside overlooking the Montagna di Sant'Antonio; the nuraghe tower is bounded by the steep rock profile to the south-west, while on the front a quadrangular enclosure opens.

The structure has a circular form, but with a westerly profile tending towards straightness for a length of about 5 metres: the south-south-western sector is not visible due to collapse and dense undergrowth.
descriptions.NUR19591: Few remains of a nuraghe built of limestone.
descriptions.NUR6235: No trace of the nuraghe remains, except for the stone structures that border the properties. Numerous pottery fragments, however, are present.
descriptions.NUR4193: Single-tower nuraghe partially collapsed but with the tholos open. It offers the possibility of climbing to the last remaining course and enjoying the view over Cala Sinzias.
descriptions.NUR4615: The nuraghe consists of a central tower, two additional bodies attached to it, substantial remnants of the outer wall along most of the perimeter, and the remains of some huts. It is in poor state of conservation except for the main entrance, which features an architrave with a drainage window and the remains of a staircase. Nearby, in the north-west direction, there is a cave several tens of metres long, used as a cemetery. The skeletal remains have been studied and date to the Nuragic period.
descriptions.NUR1862: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe with its top missing, built of calcareous stones, whose perimeter outline is interrupted on the southern side due to collapses of the external wall face. The interior of the cell is not visible as it is concealed by vegetation and filled with earth and debris.
descriptions.NUR3742: One of the numerous nuraghes in this region, located near three giants' tombs.
descriptions.NUR3351: Damaged nuraghe, of which only a few courses remain buried and entwined by vegetation
descriptions.NUR3363: Single-tower nuraghe of tuff, with a megalithic wall attached that encircles the promontory. Located within a private farm.
descriptions.NUR2958: Single-tower nuraghe with a nearby Nuragic spring, in good conservation, features a rectangular entrance with an architrave (approximately 0.95 m by 0.90 m). From this entrance, access is gained—via a staircase of four steps, each 24 cm high—into a dromos (length 1.00 m; width 1.06 m; height 1.82 m).
descriptions.NUR14988: Nuraghe completely collapsed and buried, such that its structure cannot be defined.
descriptions.NUR6271: The nuraghe, or possibly a proto-nuraghe, Monte Uri, given its features, appears imposing, built against and thus erected in symbiosis with a granite rock outcrop, preserving its tholos intact and, due to its position, dominating the Oschire countryside. To us it was a great surprise to see it, admire it, and confirm that where this toponym occurs, ancient monuments are generally present. (ArcheoUri)
descriptions.NUR2856: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe that preserves the intact tholos.
descriptions.NUR5241:
The nuraghe, situated on the summit of the hill, is very damaged.

It consists of a circular tower and an elliptical, eccentric curtain wall elongated towards the south-east, where the entrance is presumably located.
descriptions.NUR4232:
It is more precisely a proto-nuraghe.

In the vicinity there are also a special giants' tomb and a domus de janas.
descriptions.NUR615: The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR4532: The proto-nuraghes of Serrenti are mostly of small size and, as observable, have an elliptical or irregular plan. The ones at Monti Mannu, Monti Atziaddei, Monti Crastu, and Sa Corona appear larger; the last two may have been enlarged or restored between BR and BFI. Around this proto-nuraghe there are traces of a small settlement.
descriptions.NUR9877: Complex nuraghe with a central tower and two lateral towers, connected by straight walls, with a courtyard in the centre acting as an integration space. Nearby, the remains of a Bronze Age stone quarry can be observed.
descriptions.NUR13290: This is the nuraghe Monti di Deu, still partly buried, in a good state of preservation; it stands on the summit of Monte di Deu on the Limbara massif, on the Calangianus side.
descriptions.NUR3270: Only faint traces of two towers added tangentially remain.
descriptions.NUR10510:
Nuragic settlement, attested by a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe, now demolished, and by Middle Bronze Age ceramics.

The site is decontextualized and illegible, although it would be desirable to recover the materials found in situ, the associated documentation, and to fully contextualize the findings.
descriptions.NUR4663: Simple proto-nuraghe, of which only very little remains
descriptions.NUR4481: Proto-nuraghe with a village nearby. The size and location of the proto-nuraghe at Monti Crastu and Monti Mannu suggest they may have been the most important centres of cantons or sub-cantons within the Campidano, or at least that, together with the other proto-nuraghe complexes, they may have controlled a large portion of the area.
descriptions.NUR4617: Single-tower nuraghe of which only some traces remain
descriptions.NUR8198: Nuraghe of uncertain type built on the tip of a limestone hill featuring karst caves used from the Neolithic period onwards. Three rows of stones, up to 25 metres long, are clearly visible.
descriptions.NUR4622: Single-tower, of which only a small portion remains.
descriptions.NUR5909: South-west of the hamlet of Lu Bagnu, on the plateau south of Monte Oschiri, stands the nuraghe of the same name. It is completely hidden by soil and vegetation, making the plan hard to read, but it is certainly a complex nuraghe consisting of a central tower and a tower to the north-east; the extent of the hill covering it suggests the presence of other towers. The tholos of the central tower is intact, visible only from above where traces of a second floor are evident.
descriptions.NUR10024: Nuraghe with a central tower and an additional tower facing it. The nuraghe is located near the cemetery where the large statues of Monte Prama have been found.
descriptions.NUR4598: The proto-nuraghes of Monti Proceddu, Monti Tellura, Monti Acutzu, and Monti de su Marchesu were likely positioned to guard the borders of the cantons of Trexenta, whose principal centres would have been located in the present-day municipal territories of Guasila or Samatzai; the site of Sa Corona (Bruncu de is Angionis Birdis) would have controlled at least the proto-nuraghes of Monti Atziaddei (?), Genna su Carru, and those of Monti Cuamnaxi (Coa Margine) and Sa Corona di Villagreca.
descriptions.NUR10617: Nuraghe of undetermined type; only a few remains are left on the site among the vegetation. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR4025: This nuraghe has been completely destroyed, and only traces of a single row of a single-tower (single-tower nuraghe) of about 9 metres in diameter remain. Numerous ceramic fragments and basaltic lava mortars have been found on the surface.
descriptions.NUR4437: In 1788 the communal council of Villaputzu complained that the sea, penetrating into a long and deep cove, was not being monitored. The corsairs hid "behind large boulders behind an ancient Nuracco known as Nuraxi de moros", using it as a base for raids: in 1767 they enslaved two farmers; in 1779 two peasants; in 1781 four; in 1788 two men who were making charcoal for their own use.
descriptions.NUR4046: Damaged nuraghe, with the upper part of the tholos collapsed. Set within a forest.
descriptions.NUR5297:
Complex nuraghe, possibly three-lobed, built with large blocks of local andesite.

Among the vegetation, some stone heaps and traces related to possible huts are visible.

Clear evidence of repeated occupation in historical times, with numerous ceramic fragments—especially Roman period—found on the collapse and in the surrounding soil.
descriptions.NUR4676: The nuraghe is situated on the summit of the hill. Single-tower with a staircase. Completely with its top missing.
descriptions.NUR20336: The nuraghe and adjacent village are situated behind the hill that hosts the Nuragic sanctuary of Santa Vittoria di Serri.
descriptions.NUR2582:
Report: name check:

On the IGM maps it is wrongly called Muggiaglio. The name is Egra e Mele.
descriptions.NUR6468: Nuraghe composed of trachyte blocks; only the lintel remains, the rest has been destroyed, probably its stones were used for the dry-stone walls in the area.
descriptions.NUR4753: The nuraghe is in very poor condition, nestled within the dense forest of Scala Argiolas, an ancient entrance to the high plateau of Giara.
descriptions.NUR3049: Originally built with medium-sized basaltic blocks, it makes use of the rock as a foundation. Currently it is almost illegible due to a conspicuous collapse, retained by vegetation composed of olive trees and Indian figs.
descriptions.NUR12245: Single-tower nuraghe made of granite blocks, with in situ evidence of trachyte ashlar finely worked for decorative purposes.
descriptions.NUR2603: The nuraghe is almost entirely collapsed. Only the entrance with lintel remains.
descriptions.NUR21169: The entire structure makes use of natural rock. The nuraghe is in poor condition of conservation. Part of it has collapsed, leaving a majestic lintel and some walls. There is also a corridor leading to a chamber, of which only a slight raised area remains.
descriptions.NUR20322: Single-tower, difficult to access, partially collapsed, with the tholos destroyed.
descriptions.NUR3592: It is one of three nuraghe that surround the artificial pond along the perimeter of the former Madau estate. The basal circle is formed by cyclopean stones that give it a imposing presence, almost acting as a guardian of the surrounding valley, which itself is heavily anthropized and rich in other notable features. Hill of the deer.
descriptions.NUR3656: As many others, completely ruined. Nevertheless, sufficient evidence of the ancient construction remains, with some basal stones still visible. Unfortunately, in the 1960s several sites in the area disappeared due to land reorganisation works, but above all because of the construction of the artificial reservoir dam, which never fully fulfilled its intended use. Hill nuraghe of the deer hill. See Montìju de chèlvos I.mu
descriptions.NUR6146:
