On a rocky spur stands the corridor nuraghe, rectangular in plan, built of pink trachyte boulders. The interior of the monument is not accessible because of the many collapses.

The giants' tomb lies to the south, about 500 metres from the nuraghe; only part of the inner wall face of the chamber and traces of the peristalith are visible.

On an area of about 2000 sq m around the giants' tomb, numerous structures are visible, of which only the basal courses remain.
descriptions.NUR3461: The Mura Craba Nuraghe is located near a quarry, about 2 km east of Bauladu. It is a single-tower nuraghe built with basalt blocks in good state of preservation.
descriptions.NUR3552: It is the collapsed nuraghe, reference point for the beautiful and nearby giants' tomb.
descriptions.NUR6253: Nuraghe surrounded by vegetation and eroded
descriptions.NUR6125: Single-tower tholos nuraghe built from polygonal basaltic blocks. Despite the dense vegetation, the circular plan can be discerned and about five courses, though somewhat disconnected, on the north-northeast exposed side are visible. The entrance, identifiable to the east, shows a collapsed pillar on the right side and the lintel placed in an inclined position.
descriptions.NUR2517: Complex nuraghe, eroded and enveloped by vegetation. Its outline is difficult to define. It could be four-lobed.
descriptions.NUR11113: Single-tower tholos nuraghe. The structures are covered by a dense ficus grove and thickets of brambles. Despite this, the edifice is in fairly good condition, partly due to its use as a sheepfold, an activity that has led to some internal modifications. The entrance, lintelled, is oriented to the south-east. Along the approach to the entrance, on the left, opens a space for the staircase, currently blocked by debris from a collapse.
descriptions.NUR6183: The nuraghe is probably of a complex type and equipped with an outer wall, although the extensive collapse and the vegetation covering it prevent a more precise assessment.
descriptions.NUR18759: Of the monument, only some base courses remain, while the entrance has been incorporated into a modern hut.
descriptions.NUR6429: The nuraghe preserves the tholos intact, but due to the collapse at the entrance it cannot be visited. The chamber has four niches; it is one of the very few nuraghes known so far to possess this feature.
descriptions.NUR6057: The monument is a single-tower and single-chambered structure. Its entrance and the entire base are severely damaged, although traces of a staircase and a guard niche remain evident. The western-north wall is the best preserved, standing about six metres high and composed of eight courses of roughly hewn stones. Along the corridor, also almost entirely destroyed, traces of two niches facing each other are visible.
descriptions.NUR3173: Only the external perimeter of this nuraghe remains clearly visible. The rest of the structure is barely discernible. Its plan is rectangular with very rounded corners, and its maximum height to the north is 4 m, with six courses of roughly hewn stones. The western façade is formed by a rocky cliff that drops directly into the valley.
descriptions.NUR2633: Single-tower nuraghe, covered by a layer of vegetation, whose tholos is still intact
descriptions.NUR2939: Simple single-tower nuraghe, built with polygonal basalt blocks of local origin. Of the structure, camouflaged in the dense vegetation and overgrown by a stand of Indian figs, only about 6 courses of stacked blocks remain. To the south-east the entrance can be identified, featuring a large monolithic lintel well-cut and squared. The blocks forming the uprights also show a fairly precise craftsmanship.
descriptions.NUR590: Complex nuraghe of the tancato type, with a central tower and a secondary tower.
descriptions.NUR5633:
The main monument is situated on a raised plateau in a dominant position. It is a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe composed of regularly laid trachytic blocks, well-cut and precisely placed. The entrance, oriented S-SE, has been brutally transformed into a sharp arched opening, as the nuraghe has long been used as a pigpen.

Above, the drainage opening remains. A corridor, 4 m long and 1.00–2.00 m wide, with a vaulted roof in the first part and a flat roof in the second, leads into the chamber.
descriptions.NUR5601: Single-tower nuraghe, in poor state of conservation, traces of inter-wall stairs and lateral niches are visible. In the best-preserved section, the nuraghe rises by about 3 m, with six courses of roughly hewn stones.
descriptions.NUR5674:
The nuraghe is surrounded by a square curtain wall, within which circular remains of huts are visible, possibly forming a small settlement.

The perimeter of the enclosing wall, at its upper section, features several stretches of a path carved into the wall thickness.
descriptions.NUR6205:
What strikes immediately is the skill with which the basalt blocks were arranged. Buried by the earth and enveloped by greenery.

The south-east entrance is topped by an enormous lintel, leading to the chamber where access is blocked by the collapsed tholos.

It must have been an elegant single-tower (single-tower nuraghe), in a strategic position and "guarding" a small, lush valley.
descriptions.NUR6314: In the area there is a large amount of pottery fragments. Amidst the dense vegetation, a hut is still intact; a first tower and a second, possibly a remnant of a four-lobed structure; a magnificent well or cistern with a basalt grating at its entrance.
descriptions.NUR3638: The monument, located within the village of Sagama near the parish church, is a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe with a staircase, a corridor niche, and a central chamber surrounded by three niches arranged in a cross.
descriptions.NUR2341: Nuraghe Muromoi dominates a settlement of huts. It is a complex nuraghe of difficult interpretation due to being concealed by a prominent collapse. Nevertheless, a central tower and traces of lateral towers built with roughly shaped andesite blocks can be identified. To the south-east develops a small settlement of huts.
descriptions.NUR3884: The name derives from the toponym of the land, which at the time referred to the bull god's snout present in the nearby domus, but also very likely refers to a more recent medieval or even nineteenth-century period, when the sound of the waterfall, known locally as "su mummuttu de s'abba cando sicche addobat dae punta de sas roccas aintro de sa peschina, faghet unu murrunzu mannu", was heard during winter.
descriptions.NUR1914:
Complex nuraghe difficult to read in its planimetric layout due to dense vegetation and the prominent collapse, composed of large blocks of andesite.

Traces of a settlement of nuragic huts are visible, especially to the south-east, and of a Neolithic open settlement in the area between the nuraghe and the Neolithic underground necropolis of Serra Maverru.
descriptions.NUR12140:
The Nuraghe Murruzzone or Thiortorro is difficult to spot because it is surrounded by brambles, but it is located almost at the valley floor near some springs. A surviving wall measures about 4 m, and inside there is a circular niche whose entrance faces east, accessible from within and measuring about 2 m.

It is most likely that part of it still lies buried.
descriptions.NUR4427: It has been recently restored, although a large part of the complex still needs to be excavated. It clearly appeared as an imposing structure since it originally consisted of as many as five towers around which the village dwellings were built.
descriptions.NUR3684: The main nucleus of the archaeological complex of Pidighi is located within the municipal park of the same name; it consists of two nuraghes (Pidighi and Muru Accas) together with their respective settlements and their respective water supply sources...
descriptions.NUR6184: Complex corridor-type tholos nuraghe with a main tower clearly visible and two additional towers. One is clearly visible, although covered by vegetation, while the other is only discernible beneath the dense undergrowth. The main tower is preserved in good condition and features an architraved entrance oriented to the southeast. On IGM maps the nuraghe is listed as Serra Crastula.
descriptions.NUR3982:
It is a medium-sized single-tower nuraghe. The building style is the one typical of the sites in the area.

It stands on a small rise a short distance from the Pardu river and commanded a good view over the lower part of the valley formed by the same river.

The site is not in very good condition. The entrance side is intact, but the interior has almost completely collapsed. Only the corridor and the internal staircase can be made out. The vegetation is dense, making the site difficult to visit.
descriptions.NUR21135: The structure is completely missing its top and shows only faint traces of wall faces. Illegal excavations have severely damaged the structure.
descriptions.NUR5400: Nuraghe of which only very little remains externally, collapsed and never studied
descriptions.NUR6379: It is a nuraghe with a regular lintel and a relieving window. In the corridor, 4 m long and 1.2 m wide, the stair is on the left while the guard cell is missing. The eccentric chamber, 4 m in diameter, is enhanced by two equidistant niches, narrow and deep… The nuraghe is surrounded by a double concentric wall of two faces, 3 m thick in total. On one side the wall breaks off; on the other it is 5 m high and has a small tower 6 m in diameter with a flat-lintelled entrance facing south-east.
descriptions.NUR3663: It consists of only a few remains.
descriptions.NUR1883: Four-lobed nuraghe with a very complex structure. Central tower with at least four connected towers linked by a curtain wall that encloses a large courtyard.
descriptions.NUR2746: The nuraghe is almost entirely collapsed. Only the entrance with lintel and traces of two corridors remain. A niche is also visible in the rear corridor. The Budas nuraghe is an example of a proto-nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR5901: Complex tholos nuraghe built from locally sourced polygonal basalt blocks. The structures are surrounded by vegetation, but it is possible to discern a main tower and an additional tower with a courtyard, following the so-called tancato type. The additional tower appears to be smaller in scale than the main tower. From the top of the latter, the interior of the chamber can be seen, still well preserved except for the upper part, which has collapsed.
descriptions.NUR10920: In the locality of Scivu, adjacent to the homonymous beach, stands the nuraghe known as Nuraghe Narocci or Cancedda. The nuraghe is situated on the hill of Punta su Nuraxi, at an elevation of 226 metres above sea level, dominating the valley that slopes down to the coast. The structure consisted of at least four towers, covering a large area. Some of the scattered materials have been found even at the base of the hill.
descriptions.NUR3000: The nuraghe, of an archaic corridor type, built from large polygonal basalt blocks of local origin, has a quadrangular–elliptical plan. It features two interconnected entrances, located on the north and south sides respectively. The entrances are linted and have a vaguely trapezoidal shape. The internal corridor is visible and well preserved, with the usual roof formed by slabs laid flat.
descriptions.NUR2827: The monument is a single-tower with a staircase, a corridor niche, and a chamber surrounded by three niches in the classic cross-shaped arrangement. The masonry work is composed of large stones in the first courses and progressively smaller stones towards the top. Around the nuraghe remain traces of the village, to the east, and a section of outer wall to the north.
descriptions.NUR19672: Located on the summit of the same name, from which it commands the Bechida valley and part of the coastal strip extending northward toward the Nuraghe Artora, the structure is poorly preserved and appears as a modest circular wall face, possibly belonging to a large hut built with local granite. Outside the walls, a large amount of rubble is visible.
descriptions.NUR6233: Single-tower nuraghe, surrounded by Indian fig trees and vegetation. It retains the fine entrance portal with a cracked lintel and dangerous condition, the tholos and the staircase leading to the upper level.
descriptions.NUR4451: Single-tower nuraghe surrounded by dense vegetation.
descriptions.NUR4316: Near the remains of this nuraghe there is a sacred nuragic well that has miraculously survived the surrounding quarrying activities.
descriptions.NUR3350: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe eroded, collapsed, and overgrown with vegetation
descriptions.NUR5448: A huge and tall building, constructed from large basalt blocks of a deep, cyclopean dark stone, roughly shaped and worked only enough to allow them to be set together, giving the structures perfect circularity. The central tower, very wide, and two other towers—one in the south-east and one in the north-west—are visible, together with a portion of wall linking the central tower to the one in the north-west. The maximum height visible of the tower walls reaches up to 3 metres. The eastern part of the complex is covered by soil and vegetation.
descriptions.NUR8834: It is 7.50 m high, composed of 21 courses, with an 11-metre diameter; it features a very high tholos with thick walls. Adjacent to it is a Nuragic-Roman-medieval village, later abandoned due to epidemics; to the north-west there is an outer wall possibly extending for about one hundred metres, following a natural cliff face.
descriptions.NUR6119: Located in a picturesque natural rock outcrop near the nuraghe Nieddu. It is partly eroded and difficult to read due to the few courses remaining in situ. The main tower and a smaller secondary tower, likely added at a later date, are visible.
descriptions.NUR5604:
It stands on a small rise from which the surrounding view can be appreciated. It is a single-tower nuraghe about 11 metres high with a tholos roof. Built of large blocks of dark basalt which, together with yellow lichens, give it its characteristic colouring (hence the name: in Sardinian nieddu means black, dark).

The tower has two openings: an entrance at the base, still partly buried, and, almost at the top, a large window.
descriptions.NUR20051: It is located on the summit of the same hill. At first glance it appears to be a single-tower nuraghe partially buried, but it may actually be four-lobed. The lintel above the entrance is particularly distinctive, being slightly curved. The main entrance is pointed. It is also partially buried, as the lintel of the entrance is only a few centimetres above the ground.
descriptions.NUR4762: Of the nuraghe Niu e Crobu, only a meagre remnant remains. Indeed, the monument lies hidden among the vegetation and is cut off from its dignity by a fence that forces it to look beside a reservoir lined with its own material, thus compromising its environmental impact... ignorance knows no limits.
descriptions.NUR3075:
Corridor nuraghe.

The main tower currently preserves the chamber, which has a sub-circular plan, partially filled with rubble from the tholos and the upper part of the wall face; a first block is visible marking the start of the corridor. To the south, at a distance of about 8.50 m, there is a secondary tower that remains standing for 5 courses, arranged with polygonal technique and irregularly.
descriptions.NUR1895: A probably multi-lobed nuraghe whose exact structure cannot be determined; the massive collapse and the dense vegetation on the hill where the monument stands prevent its understanding. To the south, although filled with earth and collapse boulders, an oval chamber is visible, exposed by the action of looters. From NW to NE a curvilinear wall, about 9 m high, set against the rocky ridge, could be part of the central tower's wall face.
descriptions.NUR3068: Part of the nuraghe has been altered and adapted for the construction of a pinnetto.
descriptions.NUR6221: The Nolza nuraghe is a large four-lobed nuraghe, formed by four corner towers joined by straight bastions and a central tower still standing 13 metres high. Archaeological investigations, begun in 1994 and still in progress, have made it possible to distinguish several construction phases, characterised by alterations and adaptations. In a first phase the nuraghe was built of local schist, the material of which the central tower and two of the corner towers still consist.
descriptions.NUR3281: It should have been a perfect three-lobed structure.
descriptions.NUR4049: The Norampè nuraghe is literally almost entirely vanished, only a few stones integrated into the rock remain, testifying to its excellent and prominent location.
descriptions.NUR21109: Damaged and demolished by vegetation encroachment. Difficult to interpret.
descriptions.NUR21108: Damaged and demolished by vegetation encroachment. Difficult to interpret.
descriptions.NUR21103: Damaged and demolished by vegetation encroachment. Difficult to interpret.
descriptions.NUR21106: Damaged and demolished by vegetation encroachment. Difficult to interpret.
descriptions.NUR21104: Damaged and demolished by vegetation encroachment. Difficult to interpret.
descriptions.NUR21105: Damaged and demolished by vegetation encroachment. Difficult to interpret.
descriptions.NUR21107: Damaged and demolished by vegetation encroachment. Difficult to interpret.
descriptions.NUR2594: Complex nuraghe with traces of a village surrounding it, featuring significant collapses on the slopes. From here there is a prominent view and control over the village, which includes a temple at Irru.
descriptions.NUR3887:
Sa Pedra de Nunnale. A picturesque and colossal single-tower, with a bizarre shape, standing at the base of which rises the homonymous nuraghe. Although imposing, this single-tower nuraghe appears astonishingly small in comparison to the immense rock mass that dominates it.

This single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe is built with megalithic blocks only roughly shaped, larger at the base. Around the rocky mass, the huts of a small village can be discerned.
descriptions.NUR5617: The Nuraghe Nuracale is a four-lobed type, consisting of a central tower, or central tower, surrounded by four smaller towers held together by massive straight walls. The main entrance, located in the east bastion, gives access to the internal courtyard, shaped like a half-moon, onto which open the entrance of the central tower and of the south-east and north-east lateral towers, while the other two towers were linked to the courtyard by two long corridors cut into the bastions.
descriptions.NUR4937:
The Nuraghe Nuraceddeu features a peculiar stone shaped and carved in such a way as to form a transition between the straight section of the bastion and one of the nuraghe towers.

It is a true "special nuragico piece" in terms of construction.

This nuraghe, which might hold other interesting features, is located in the territory of Gesturi.

The bastion of the nuraghe is built with masonry composed of well-cut stones.
descriptions.NUR11487: Single-tower nuraghe and settlement, destroyed due to the construction of the railway. The exact location is not known. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR10443: Multi-lobed nuraghe with an outer wall, a straight curtain wall, built of basalt blocks; Roman Republican settlement on the ruins of the nuraghe. Traces of the nuraghe were discovered during road construction works for the pylon foundations of the viaduct: the site has been extensively documented and is now completely concealed.
descriptions.NUR5566: This complex nuraghe consisted of a central tower and three towers joined by a bastion, today only poorly preserved. The central tower, however, is in perfect condition and has a remaining height of 14 m, only slightly less than its original height. It is built on two levels, both intact, and each with a tholos roof.
descriptions.NUR2224: Of the monument, only the first two courses of the base remain. It could belong to the nuraghe Nuradorzu.
descriptions.NUR2849: Nuraghe of which only a few courses remain
descriptions.NUR3234: The structure composed of basalt blocks is rubble and collapsed. The remains are scattered over a wide area covered with vegetation.
descriptions.NUR6340: "Nuraghe Su Nuragheddu, or de Sa Taula, or de Su Coddu 'e Su Nuraghe. It is located near the Rio di Posada, within a narrow gorge between cliffs, guarding a passage; it is ruined, but clear traces of the nuraghe remain. In terrain of Deiana Serafino".
descriptions.NUR12455: Structures related to single-tower tholos nuraghe. It is very difficult to identify amid the dense vegetation, and only about three courses of the base remain, composed of large polygonal basaltic blocks. The rest of the structure has collapsed, and debris fills the lower portion. Despite the poor conditions, the features can be interpreted as a small, simple single-tower nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR1263: Area where ancient maps indicated the location of the nuraghe Nuraghessu; in this area one or more dolmen are present.
descriptions.NUR3979: Built from limestone blocks and erected on a rocky outcrop, it consists of a central tower, an added body where traces of a corridor and remnants of some huts on the western side are visible. It is in poor state of conservation.
descriptions.NUR4105:
The Nuraghe of Nuraxeddu stands on a promontory currently isolated at the centre of a plain used for grazing sheep herds.

The masonry works are made of roughly shaped blocks with parallelipipedal form arranged in fairly regular courses.
descriptions.NUR4209: The megalithic structure is currently located within a sheepfold.
descriptions.NUR16535: The remains of the nuraghe are hardly discernible; it is certain that the structure has been dismantled, and the ashlar blocks may have been reused in the construction of retaining walls and boundary stone walls, which are present in the area where the nuraghe was likely erected. From the brochure “Ritratto di nuraghe eredità di un'isola …” by Sara Muscuso, it is stated: “Of the nuraghe, only a curved wall face remains, composed of one or two courses.”
descriptions.NUR17160: It was indicated on ancient cadastral maps. Probable location, no traces are identifiable.
descriptions.NUR18260:
Marks the boundary between the municipal territories of Serrenti and that of Villagreca.

Recorded in the historical cadastral map.
descriptions.NUR2500:
Complex nuraghe built of the local volcanic rock. Largely covered by vegetation and hidden by collapse, stretches of walling from the towers that made up the building can be made out. One part has been disturbed by illicit excavations.

At the foot of the hill, to the north, a hypogeum, perhaps an air-raid shelter.

It is likely that on the summit of the hill, in the private land enclosed by fences and inaccessible, traces of the protohistoric cluster of huts may survive.
descriptions.NUR4477: Remains of a nuraghe upon which Roman to medieval period settlements have been superimposed.
descriptions.NUR4239: Possible origin of the name: nuraghe della scolca, which in the time of the Giudicati served as a guard post. On a small relief of 70 m.l.m, there are a heap of stones and basaltic boulders, traces of burials and Roman pottery, and fragments of obsidian.
descriptions.NUR5671: The nuraghe was built during the later Bronze Age (1500–1400 BC) on a granite foundation surrounded by a series of massive stones, and adapted to the irregular shape of the hilltop. It is a four-lobed nuraghe, featuring a central tower and four additional towers arranged in concentric addition. Access is facilitated by a ramp leading to the entrance, which in turn opens into a long corridor with walls that slope inward at acute angles.
descriptions.NUR3981: Ruined nuraghe, buried and hard to define.
descriptions.NUR5167: Nuraghe reported, embedded in vegetation and not visible from the outside
descriptions.NUR3771: Single-tower with circular plan (diam. 12.80 x 12) and a maximum remaining height of 2.55 m.
descriptions.NUR3054: It is a nuraghe more than partially collapsed. It appears as a haphazard heap of stones, which, on its least damaged side, retains three courses of the original foundation.
descriptions.NUR3144: It is a corridor nuraghe of difficult detection due to its poor state of conservation and the rubble from collapses that prevent its reading.
descriptions.NUR9632:
Corridor nuraghe with an indefinable plan because of its irregularity, and a profile that juts out and recedes.

The main entrance, facing south-east, is rectangular (height 1.70 m – width 1.40 m) with a sturdy lintel and leads into a corridor that cannot be traversed because of the collapse; a secondary entrance, collapsed and blocked, seems to open to the south-west.

The wall face survives to a maximum height of 3.60 m with six horizontal, irregular courses; the blocks are polygonal and only roughly dressed.
descriptions.NUR1969: Scant remains of a small nuraghe
descriptions.NUR5800:
The nuraghe consists of a main building with a three-storey central tower accompanied by a bilobate bastion arranged on two levels, enclosing a courtyard and two secondary towers. It is surrounded by an outer wall featuring towers and a sacred area.

Its tower is the one with the largest diameter among the known nuraghes.
descriptions.NUR5582: The Ola nuraghe is a single-tower (single-tower nuraghe) with an external diameter of about 12 m and a height of 10 m, dating to the recent Bronze Age. What stands out most is the use of different construction materials: externally, the base consists of 12 courses of granite blocks, while above this, 13 courses of trachyte extend upward.
descriptions.NUR19510: Of the Olai nuraghe in this pile of stones, currently only the foundation is visible.
descriptions.NUR4380: Complex nuraghe, with a frontal addition, surrounded by a village
descriptions.NUR4632: Single-tower nuraghe with an addition not easily legible. Surrounding village.
descriptions.NUR4636: Single-tower (single-tower nuraghe) of which only a small amount remains
descriptions.NUR20232: Only a few courses of the nuraghe remain. Located in a position of observation and signaling, it provides a view spanning 360 degrees over all the surrounding mountains and nuraghes.
descriptions.NUR3650: Particular structure with a staircase on the left and a niche on the right side of the corridor. Nuraghe likely restored in successive phases.
descriptions.NUR3320: It is completely surrounded by dense vegetation, which prevents access. It is a four-lobed nuraghe built with basalt blocks.
descriptions.NUR3217: Nuraghe type undetermined, set amidst dense vegetation, not accessible internally.
descriptions.NUR1029:
The nuraghe is located on the summit of a hill, at a short distance from the homonymous domus de janas and the Nuraghe s'Aspru.

Of the monument, which may more accurately be described as a enclosure than a nuraghe, only about two-thirds of the courses remain along the west and north sides, with an average height of 2 metres, and other stones scattered on the ground. The masonry includes natural rock in its outline and was originally intended to close with a diameter of about 11 metres. The stones are large and only roughly shaped.
descriptions.NUR5651:
It is a complex nuraghe, built of basalt, on a small elevation composed of at least three towers and surrounded by a village.

The bases of the towers and of what were likely the huts can be clearly distinguished. The central tower remains partially standing. Indeed, ascending to the top of the tower allows one to see the internal chamber. However, the debris accumulated both inside and outside prevents access from the base.
descriptions.NUR2995:
The archaeological site stands on a rocky cliff of granitic nature, bounded by three spires lying about 30 and 50 m apart.

The area covers about 2.0 ha; the settlement is hard to read in plan because of the vegetation and its very poor state of preservation.

The site is surrounded by an outer wall that encloses the nuraghe, the two watchtowers and, in the centre, the Nuragic huts, while other huts lie outside the wall on the east side.
descriptions.NUR2782: It is visible from the SS131 and immediately strikes you as a special nuraghe. Special because it combines the features of a nuraghe with an elongated, upturned-boat-shaped chamber and a truncated-cone nuraghe. On entering, you find yourself in the long chamber, which has two large niches and is about 7 metres high; at the far end a doorway leads to a staircase that, plunging into darkness and enclosed by the nuragic walls, spirals up to the upper floor.
descriptions.NUR13372: The Orgono nuraghe of Ghilarza is a unique monument that through the development of its structures tells the evolution of Nuragic architecture: from the proto-nuraghe with a elongated chamber shaped like an upturned boat to the truncated conical tower with a circular chamber and false dome. The consolidation and excavation works carried out so far have allowed for at least partial recovery of the monument, which was already severely destabilized and dangerous.
descriptions.NUR3176: Around it one can see the remains of the ancient village and the granitic rocks in their varied shapes. Near the building, of which only a few courses and the lintel facing Monte Novo remain, the traces of the granite quarries are very evident. Within an area of 1 km there are nine domus de janas; some lie near the Nuraghe, the others, on the same granitic outcrop, lie near the Sau family farmhouse.
descriptions.NUR6448:
The nuraghe is a single-tower built with large, well-cut stones.

The entrance is covered by an imposing lintel and leads into a corridor featuring a niche on the right side and a staircase opening on the left; the latter is largely blocked by debris. At the end of the corridor opens a circular chamber, with the tholos vault still intact, containing three niches arranged symmetrically.
descriptions.NUR19708: Small single-tower nuraghe located at a short distance from the settlement of Siniscola in the northward direction, and likely associated with the nearby village of Ghiramonte. The structure is severely damaged by the presence of a quarry extending from its base. Only a portion of the wall face is visible in the south-east direction; fragments of Nuragic ceramics are found on the ground nearby.
descriptions.NUR2590: It is located on the hill overlooking the commune of Silanus. It is a complex nuraghe, mainly built of granite. The central tower, originally about 12 metres high, remains almost intact and was originally flanked by two or three additional bodies. The nuraghe features two superimposed tholos connected by a main staircase and a secondary, hidden staircase with a mezzanine. At the base of the nuraghe, remnants of other nuragic constructions are visible, still insufficiently studied.
descriptions.NUR5764:
It is a three-lobed nuraghe particularly significant due to its location, size, and state of preservation. It is located in the Marghine subregion, within the territory of the comune of Bortigali, at an elevation of 785 metres, from where a wide expanse of central Sardinia is visible.

The site is situated on the slopes of Monte Cuguruttu (867 m), in a position stretching from the nearby Monte Santu Padre (1.025 m) to the more distant mountains.
descriptions.NUR3460:
The tower, circular in plan (diam. 10.65 x 10.12 m), survives to a maximum height of 4.40 m on the north-east side, while the minimum is 3 m on the south-west. The masonry consists of trachyte blocks roughly dressed with some care and laid in fairly regular horizontal courses. The wall thickness is 3.30 m on the north-east, 4 m on the south and 3 m on the north-west.

The interior of the nuraghe is entered through a rectangular doorway (h. 1.70 m – w. 0.90 m), lintelled, oriented to the south-east and slightly splayed inwards.
descriptions.NUR6096: Nuraghe type undetermined; it features a tower with the tholos still intact, surrounded by remains of collapse within the dense undergrowth.
descriptions.NUR5563: Likely complex nuraghe today partially collapsed and difficult to read.
descriptions.NUR4721: Remains of the base drum of a classic single-tower (single-tower nuraghe) in polygonal masonry, with a maximum residual height of about 4 m, featuring an internal chamber vaulted in a tholos form, equipped with a small subsidiary niche, and a staircase – unfortunately completely destroyed – defended by a counter-facing watchtower. The structure, already dismantled in Roman times, was repurposed, incorporating also five menhir-statue trunks, pre-existing in the area.
descriptions.NUR3506: Due to the collapse, which affects the entrance, access to the chamber is impossible. The polygonal masonry work is composed of well-shaped granite blocks, frequently using wedges of the same lithological material. The foundation, in contrast, shows a very compact structure relative to the upper plane of the monument, with large blocks roughly worked.
descriptions.NUR11739: Due to the collapse, which affects the entrance, access to the chamber is impossible. The polygonal masonry work is composed of well-shaped granite blocks, frequently using wedges of the same lithological material. The foundation, in contrast, shows a very compact structure relative to the upper plane of the monument, with large blocks roughly worked.
descriptions.NUR4267: Damaged nuraghe with multiple towers, undecipherable, part of a larger settlement.
descriptions.NUR663: Damaged nuraghe of which a good height of about 3 metres is preserved.
descriptions.NUR5191: The artifacts indicate that it was used from the Middle Bronze Age until the Recent Bronze Age. It is built with large blocks of limestone and originally contained a chamber with two niches and a staircase. Now the collapse blocks access to the chamber. Nearby the nuraghe, remains of a hut are visible, consisting of a circular room and a courtyard.
descriptions.NUR3295: In very poor condition of conservation, completely ruined, only a few courses remain visible.
descriptions.NUR5843: The Ortei nuraghe is four-lobed, consisting of a central tower still well preserved and two lateral towers, the remains of which are almost completely buried and overgrown by vegetation. The particular feature of this nuraghe is that the circular chamber of the central tower contains three deep niches, especially the central one, which has a large lintel with a window above.
descriptions.NUR4208: It is a quadrilobate nuraghe (Sardara commune) completely demolished, of which only a few courses of the mural basement remain.
descriptions.NUR2398: Semi-diroccato. Twelve courses of stones remain, with a breach to the south-east, possibly the entrance. The prism-shaped stones easily interlock, allowing precise connections between them, though they are not arranged in horizontal layers. The external wall is vertical and difficult to access, making it hard to enter the interior.
descriptions.NUR2376: Semi-diroccato. Twelve courses of stones remain, with a breach to the south-east, possibly the entrance. The prism-shaped stones easily interlock, allowing precise connections between them, though they are not arranged in horizontal layers. The external wall is vertical and difficult to access, making it hard to enter the interior.
descriptions.NUR6376: Around the nuraghe there is an extensive Nuragic village; most of the huts are now reduced to heaps of rubble, while large enclosures remain with walls taller than usual, at times appearing like ramparts—probably indicating a fortified settlement.
descriptions.NUR5740: Situated within a picturesque forest of monumental olive trees, the nuraghe is a complex, quadrilobed, corridor-type structure with a ramped access path located at the upper part and a well from which one descends into a subterranean chamber. The only accessible lateral tower is the one situated to the north and is visible from the upper part of the central tower.
descriptions.NUR12021: Single-tower nuraghe in partial good condition, located on the slope of a small hillock.
descriptions.NUR15904:
Designated by IGM with the nuraghe symbol, it is now disappeared.

It is likely that it belonged to a hut from the village or to a giants' tomb.
descriptions.NUR16879:
A single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe (mainly remains) is located on the slope of Cuccuru S. Eremilis, very close to the road.

Position to be verified
descriptions.NUR15664: Quadrilobate complex nuraghe. Visible are traces of a central tower and three additional towers with bastions, whose foundations remain in very poor condition. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR3145: Complex plan, it is built in basalt with a structure composed of well-cut blocks arranged in regular horizontal courses such that the joints of the upper blocks fall in the centre of the lower ones. The fortress is probably composed of three towers enclosing a small courtyard with an entrance to the south-west.
descriptions.NUR6457: The Ozzilo nuraghe is located in the territory of Aidomaggiore; it is a corridor-type nuraghe, accessed from the top, as it is heavily cluttered with debris due to a collapse. The interior chamber is occupied by the debris of the collapse, which affected part of the "naviform" vault. Nearby are two giants' tombs, one of which is partially destroyed.
descriptions.NUR18858: The Ozzilo nuraghe is located in the territory of Aidomaggiore; it is a corridor-type nuraghe, accessed from the top, as it is heavily cluttered with debris due to a collapse. The interior chamber is occupied by the debris of the collapse, which affected part of the "naviform" vault. Nearby are two giants' tombs, one of which is partially destroyed.
descriptions.NUR18860: The Ozzilo nuraghe is located in the territory of Aidomaggiore; it is a corridor-type nuraghe, accessed from the top, as it is heavily cluttered with debris due to a collapse. The interior chamber is occupied by the debris of the collapse, which affected part of the "naviform" vault. Nearby are two giants' tombs, one of which is partially destroyed.
descriptions.NUR3268: Single-tower with the tholos collapsed inward
descriptions.NUR3521:
The Paddaggiu "pagliaio" is located less than one km "from the elephant".

Apparently a single-tower nuraghe is in fact a complex nuraghe, composed of a central tower and a bastion with two lateral towers barely visible. The particular feature of this nuraghe is the presence of a chamber set above the entrance corridor, originally accessible via a staircase inside the right niche of the main chamber. It retains intact the tholos and the staircase to the upper level.
descriptions.NUR15018: Single-tower nuraghe with a dismantled and buried village, the structure of which cannot be defined.
descriptions.NUR4621: The Paiulu (IGM) or Paiolu nuraghe is located on a basaltic bastion at Costa Pisu, on the western slope of Monte Arci, at the border between the municipal territories of Oristano, Palmas Arborea (Tiria) and Villaurbana.
descriptions.NUR18218:
It has a single entrance oriented to the northeast.

It is now covered with soil and sand, although at the top of the nuraghe the top section remains, from which part of the internal walling is visible.
descriptions.NUR21110: Now only large stones have remained, moved and reused in the nearby retaining walls.
descriptions.NUR3876: Single-tower tholos nuraghe built from polygonal basalt blocks of local origin. Of the monument, only three to four courses of outer wall blocks remain, with a maximum residual height of about 2.60 m. At present, the entrance cannot be identified, partly due to thickets and mastic vines that partially encircle the surviving remains of the nuraghe. The internal chamber has collapsed, and the materials that once formed it now fill completely the remaining parts of the monument.
descriptions.NUR10446: Unidentified nuraghe. Area with finds attributable to a settlement with a nuraghe, the nuraghe has been demolished. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR2419: Completely dismantled. Probably partly still present beneath the vegetation, which shows stones placed without order.
descriptions.NUR9482:
The monument, located in the immediate northern outskirts of Birori, has a circular plan (diameter 12 x 12.30 m) with an average residual height of just 2.75 m and two courses; the stones, polygonal and roughly hewn, are arranged in horizontal courses.

Due to its extremely poor state of conservation, the internal structure of the monument cannot be identified.
descriptions.NUR8488:
Built with limestone and sandstone blocks, it consists of a central body with two towers, an outer wall, and a village of huts.

The oldest structures, dated to the 15th–10th centuries BCE, are the main tower and several huts. The tower, with an entrance to the east-northeast, remains about 8 m high. The internal chamber retains intact the vaulted tholos roof.

In the back wall, an ogival stairwell opening is visible, leading to the upper floor and the terrace.
descriptions.NUR2954: Single-tower that remains half-submerged, completely buried.
descriptions.NUR5433: Present on topographic maps but evidently destroyed in the past. The sheepfold visible in the photo is not a nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR11648: Also known as "nurarchei" according to A. Tarameli (1915).
descriptions.NUR19667: Single-tower nuraghe with attached village. The original tower remains, its interior filled with debris and vegetation. Of the original structure, about four complete courses are preserved. To the south, a curtain wall with an entrance topped by a lintel is present; due to collapses and vegetation, its function cannot be determined. To the north-east of the tower is a cyclopean wall, which abruptly ends, apparently forming the northern wall of a corridor.
descriptions.NUR4281: Complex nuraghe consisting of 3 towers connected together. The structure shows heavy damage caused by tomb robbers.
descriptions.NUR2684: Single-tower nuraghe with its top missing and encircled by vegetation, with a domus de janas located nearby.
descriptions.NUR2270: Single-tower composed of large, roughly hewn limestone blocks with an entrance oriented to south-east. The tower remains up to a maximum height of 2.50 m. To the left of the entrance is a staircase. The visibility of the nuraghe is greatly impaired by the vegetation that covers it.
descriptions.NUR6078: Damaged nuraghe, of which only a small portion remains at the junction of three borders.
descriptions.NUR3868: The monument, in very poor condition of conservation, does not allow the identification of the original layout of the structures; one can only hypothesise, considering the alignment of some wall sections on the south side, where two courses of granitic blocks are preserved, that it might have been a simple tholos nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR8946: The Pastoris nuraghe is of simple type, located to the north-east relative to the inhabited centre, near the municipal water deposit, and in close proximity to which, a few years ago, some structures related to a livestock farming company were built—though in reality these do not harmonize well with the presence of the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR3599: It is a single-tower nuraghe with a diameter of 9.90 metres, whose entrance, still intact, leads into a corridor now uncovered, with the passage niche projecting from it and still preserved. The circular chamber (diameter 3.50 m) is missing its top and stands 3.50 m above the current floor level; it has no niches, and access to the staircase leading to the upper levels was provided from the ground surface.
descriptions.NUR999: The Nissardi in 1901 (map included in G. Pinza's volume) indicated a giants' tomb slightly south-west of the Paule Tolta nuraghe: a nuraghe that is indeed located within the perimeter of the airport.
descriptions.NUR19589: Single-tower nuraghe built of a mixture of calcareous and arenaceous stone, while the lintel is made of trachyte. The chamber is bordered by three niches.
descriptions.NUR8430:
Located on the southern bank of the Rio Berchida, close to the sea, it appears as a haphazard pile of rubble, from which the upper part of the central tower is visible, and it is evident that additional structures were once present.

On one side of the structure, some courses of roughly hewn granite blocks are visible, and clear signs of damage caused by illegal excavation activities can be seen.
descriptions.NUR3791: A few megalithic stones indicating a probable nuraghe, perhaps a circle. Certainly, witnesses report that many stones ended up forming a vespai during the reclamation of the marsh. Marsh nuraghes, wetland nuraghes. See Paùles and Cunvéntu nòu.mu
descriptions.NUR5348:
The tower, conical in shape, shows a prominent structural collapse on the southern side, extending from the entrance to the top of the collapse, affecting also part of the "tholos".

From the entrance, oriented to south/south-east and lacking its lintel, access is gained through a strombed passage leading inward with a partially surviving vaulted roof. On the left side of the corridor, access to the staircase is provided, with a flat-laid roof, of which three blocks remain.
descriptions.NUR4126:
The nuraghe appears as the central nucleus of an elaborate system of enclosures, the first of which is a powerful curtain wall that at several points exploits natural rock formations; within this perimeter, a second courtyard develops in two semicircular arms that extend to meet the tower.

This tower has a slightly elliptical plan and also incorporates natural rock outcrops within its own perimeter wall.
descriptions.NUR1350: Probable complex nuraghe completely collapsed and fallen.
descriptions.NUR6232:
It is a single-tower nuraghe from which most of the underlying plain can be seen.

The nuraghe is completely collapsed and privately owned, though access is not difficult.

The filars beneath the lintel are buried.

The tholos is entirely collapsed inward, but through the rocks the helical staircase placed on the left side relative to the entrance and a second staircase, whose layout is hard to determine, can be discerned.

It still merits a short visit.
descriptions.NUR1813: nuraghe Peddalzos, in the area between this one and the nuraghe Cheas, should be where the famous giants' tombs mentioned, studied and sought by G. Lilliu, are located.
descriptions.NUR3037: When leading visitors to these sites, it is often the historical memory of relatives and friends who generously offer to accompany me physically, sharing with me facts and anecdotes passed down from their fathers and grandfathers. The nuraghe is practically absent, but the assurance of my guide is so strong that I am compelled to believe it, for he himself has had direct experience of such structures.
descriptions.NUR11289: In this case too, I must report the almost complete absence of the site. Only a few stones remain, which nonetheless indicate the ancient presence of the site. It is a place where you can try electromagnetic applications designed for bodily well-being.
descriptions.NUR5942: More precisely, it is a proto-nuraghe, and it is circular in plan.
descriptions.NUR5887:
Small nuraghe, located on a high cliff of Monte Dominigu.

Nearby, to the west of the nuraghe, the megalithic circle of Monte Dominigu. On old cadastral maps it is listed as Nuraghe San Leonardo.

According to the current Regional Catalogue (CTR) of Sardinia, it is now known as "Nuraghe Sa Pedra Pertunta".
descriptions.NUR3894: Unique construction situated exactly on the summit of the rocky Pedras Serradas, barely discernible. It appears to be a semicircular nuraghe. Some consider it a circular nuraghe, while others see it as remains of a nuraghe after the collapse of the underlying ground. Unparalleled views over Giorrè.
descriptions.NUR3630: It is a bilobate complex nuraghe in granite with traces of a wall that encloses the monument. It is situated between the rocks at 245 m, on top of a hill.
descriptions.NUR3259: It is in a state of complete ruin. Some of the basal stones, though barely visible, are discernible and embedded in the natural rock, forming a single unit with the entire structure.
descriptions.NUR3043: Not easily accessible due to its position on a particularly striking elevated ridge, it includes a complex nuraghe. The structure, partially collapsed and difficult to interpret because of abundant debris, shows rows of limestone blocks.
descriptions.NUR6171:
A few courses still visible at the Peidru nuraghe, a probable single-tower nuraghe located on SP8 near the old bridge maintenance station at Oinu.

A notable stone with three holes is observed at the base of the monument.
descriptions.NUR5773: It is the second corridor nuraghe named Peppe Gallu in the Uri area, following Peppe Gallu of Cuga. The attached village, very extensive, has been destroyed by agricultural mechanization. It is a proto-nuraghe of corridor type. It features two elevated entrances, above the farm level, which could be accessed via wooden or rope ladders.
descriptions.NUR11480: Complex two-tower nuraghe with settlement. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR4838: Nuraghe of which only faint traces remain
descriptions.NUR3775: Single-tower tholos nuraghe. Of considerable size, it retains a height of about 5.40 m. Built with polygonal basalt blocks of local origin, it is well preserved in its western portion, while in the eastern part it is partially collapsed and covered by vegetation. The entrance can be identified on the eastern side, though it has collapsed and is reduced to a simple opening.
descriptions.NUR6385: Nuraghe immersed in vegetation, eroded and partially buried. The entrance is visible but buried down to almost the lintel.
descriptions.NUR15009: Complex nuraghe, partially eroded and buried.
descriptions.NUR2120: Complex nuraghe composed of two simple towers added laterally and joined tangentially, oriented SSE and NNW. The SSE tower has its interior choked with collapse; on the south side there is a break in the wall outline. The second tower, oriented NNW, does not preserve its full perimeter, which is interrupted in several stretches by collapse probably caused by the dense vegetation there. Other building masses are present but not clearly definable because of collapse and vegetation.
descriptions.NUR545: The nuraghe stands on the summit of an isolated, modest elevation. The area is covered by vegetation that is almost impenetrable. Some alignments of granitic blocks are visible.
descriptions.NUR980: Complex nuraghe probably surrounded by a ring of walls, with traces of walls around it.
descriptions.NUR3757: The Perda Lada nuraghe is located on a hillside used for grazing and farming, near the Crastutorro nuraghe. What remains of the monument are large granite blocks, which unfortunately do not help in identifying the type of monument or its various features, possibly also due to the work of erosion caused by the elements.
descriptions.NUR2628: Single-tower tholos nuraghe, built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. The internal chamber has collapsed in its upper part, but still survives to a height of about 3 m. Inside it two facing niches can be made out, one to the west, the other to the east. The entrance, no longer existing, must have faced south, as can be deduced from the surviving structures. The outer wall face survives to a maximum height of 4 m.
descriptions.NUR4638: Single-tower (single-tower nuraghe) with its top missing, of which only a few remains are visible
descriptions.NUR3085: It is located in the territory of the comune of Urzulei at an elevation of 1,030 metres. It was a complex nuraghe, of which only a few ruins remain. Nearby are also important giants' tombs.
descriptions.NUR15070: Single-tower with its top missing and buried
descriptions.NUR10873: The tower is missing its top and the perimeter has an irregular shape. The internal diameter varies from 4.2 to 5.6 m. Presence of clandestine excavations.
descriptions.NUR5575: Nuraghe reported on Wikimapia but under deletion. To be verified.
descriptions.NUR5426: There are some subsquared granite blocks, on two courses, attributable to a nuragic structure.
descriptions.NUR5089: Unidentified nuraghe, located on the summit of a hill between two valleys, now reduced to a heap of large ashlar stones.
descriptions.NUR4630: It is located on the left side of the Samatzai–Serrenti municipal road, in the village of the same name, on a slight elevation above the plain. It is a single-tower (single-tower nuraghe) with an external diameter of 10 m and a wall thickness of about 2 m. It retains almost completely, along its entire circumference, the base course composed of large limestone blocks quarried from the surrounding area, rich in such outcrops.
descriptions.NUR5465: The Nuragic village of Perdu Isu (one nuraghe and traces of about 11 huts) and the cistern storage known as "Su scusorgiu" are located at an altitude clearly above 1,000 m a.s.l. The village is situated on the crest of one of the ridges, with visual contact to the well-known site of Serbissi and to the valley where the complex of "Is Tostoinus" is located.
descriptions.NUR1008: It appears as a heap of stones and a few large blocks of red sandstone, located on a piece of land excluded from cultivation and grazing, near the necropolis of Anghelu Ruiu. State of conservation: poor.
descriptions.NUR5486: Erased, buried, little known and never excavated, it is visible while travelling along S.S. 131.
descriptions.NUR5822: This nuraghe has a tholos partially collapsed. Inside, on the left side, there is a staircase leading to the entrance, and three niches with "stipetti" in the central chamber. The niche on the right, at first glance a normal niche, contains an internal staircase that leads to a mezzanine positioned above the main entrance to the nuraghe, with an opening from which the entrance corridor can be seen. The mezzanine has a window facing the central chamber.
descriptions.NUR3817: Nuraghe probably of simple tholos type. The interpretation of the structures is very difficult due to the dense vegetation, poor state of preservation, and the presence of recent structures superimposed on the remains of the building. Some polygonal stones aligned can be observed, while the remaining parts consist of a heap of disconnected blocks, upon which smaller stones are superimposed.
descriptions.NUR3058: The nuraghe is largely invisible due to vegetation, but mainly because its lithic components have been dismantled and reused to build dry-stone structures nearby (themselves now abandoned). Because of this, its location is difficult to determine.
descriptions.NUR2855: It is a complex nuraghe located on the hill known as Pettu 'e Murtas, from which it takes its name. Nearby are the remains of some huts, all of Nuragic age.
descriptions.NUR3743: Single-tower nuraghe today destroyed by agricultural mechanization
descriptions.NUR11146: Single-tower nuraghe greatly modified by agricultural mechanization in the 1950s.
descriptions.NUR3409: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe collapsed. Incorrectly, some refer to the nearby Molafà nuraghe as "Piandanna".
descriptions.NUR1575:
Single-tower nuraghe, preserves almost intact the tholos roof of the chamber.

It is one of the few nuraghes equipped with a mezzanine or mezzanine floor on the entrance corridor.
descriptions.NUR3558: Enormous single-tower, inaccessible, built on a rocky outcrop, with earthbound walls remaining up to 4 m in height. It can be reached on foot via the forest ranger's lookout road. One of the highest points in the area offers a magnificent view.
descriptions.NUR15926: The nuraghe is located on the summit of a high hill, from which the view perfectly extends over the area of S'Adde 'e S'Ulumu,
descriptions.NUR5516: The nuraghe takes its name from "pibiri"/pepe. The monument and its surrounding area have been the subject of scientific investigations at the beginning of the 2000s. The main structure, built of limestone, consists of a central tower and at least two additional towers connected by straight curtain walls. The helical staircase is visible. The main body is enclosed within an outer wall composed of several towers linked by both straight and curved walls.
descriptions.NUR4377: Probably dismantled after the construction of the adjacent houses.
descriptions.NUR2578: The nuraghe is located about 400 metres to the north-northeast of the Nuraghe Biriola, while 350 metres to the east lies a Roman-era cemetery area, evidenced by a dozen cremation urns of different shapes dug into the exposed rock. It is a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe with a niche, a ramp to the top, and a central chamber bordered by two niches. The tower, circular in plan, is missing its top and reaches a maximum height of 5.80 m with 11 courses; a major collapse has affected the perimeter wall facing north-northwest.
descriptions.NUR3543: It is undoubtedly the most imposing and best-preserved nuraghe in the territory of Solarussa. The layout follows that of the corridor nuraghe, featuring a main tower and a secondary tower separated by a courtyard. The main tower is in good condition, with the tholos vault essentially intact. The secondary tower, however, is partially collapsed, while the internal courtyard is blocked by debris from the collapse.
descriptions.NUR3017: During the Nuragic period the area was densely inhabited due to its highly strategic location: near the lake stand numerous nuraghes, including one known as Sa Pigalva.
descriptions.NUR4873: Complex nuraghe of modest dimensions, apparently undisturbed as it is covered by vegetation. The central tower and other aligned curtain walls are clearly visible.
descriptions.NUR5261: As far as can be seen through the vegetation, it is a single-tower nuraghe with a curtain wall; I believe it is well preserved despite the collapsed tholos, though it still requires excavation and cleaning.
descriptions.NUR14825: The area preserved the settlement, which was uncovered in the early 1980s. The land was expropriated and archaeological investigations were launched, revealing a series of residential areas used at least up to the late medieval period, traces of a complex nuraghe, and what has been identified as a sacred well, still to be excavated.
descriptions.NUR3224: Nuraghe apparently single-tower. It could belong to the category of "uncompleted nuraghes".
descriptions.NUR1181: The nuraghe is a single-tower structure on two levels, elliptical in shape, which makes use of natural rock masses in which it is embedded. Due to poor conservation, its form is not clearly legible.
descriptions.NUR3910: Structures related to single-tower tholos nuraghes, of which three to four external courses of the wall remain, with a maximum height of about 2.50 m. The internal chamber has collapsed, and the debris from the collapse fills the space. Built with locally sourced polygonal basalt blocks. The entrance cannot be identified. The structures are largely covered by vegetation.
descriptions.NUR20200: Disappeared from maps and censuses, it has reappeared thanks to the geological mining map drawn by engineer C. De Castro in 1889 and the drone survey carried out by the Assoc. Cult. Limen Sarrabus-Gerrei.
descriptions.NUR5379: A tower remains, its interior collapsed and inaccessible. A staircase appears to have been present. It is surrounded by an elliptical wall with a residual height of about 3 m and 7 courses.
descriptions.NUR6164: Located in the territory of Mara, it draws attention to what appears to be a large monolith visible from the SS292 just before the junction at Bonuighinu. The nuraghe, likely a complex one, is unfortunately almost completely swallowed by vegetation; what strikes me is discovering that the monolith is the remnant of a colossal outer wall shaped like a V.
descriptions.NUR5527: It is a complex nuraghe, composed of a central tower and four attached towers, only slightly evident. The central tower is the only one in good preservation; it has two superimposed levels, the lower one intact, while the upper one lacks its tholos roof. On the upper level there is a large window facing the entrance.
descriptions.NUR12510: Single-tower tholos nuraghe, built from locally sourced polygonal basalt blocks. The structures are almost completely enveloped by vegetation. The stacked blocks on the southern side can be seen, with a residual height of about 2.50 m. The rest of the building is not visible due to poor visibility. Accumulations of fallen blocks can be observed on the small slope to the south of the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR4530: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe built with large blocks, located on top of the hill. On the slopes of the hill there are high curtain walls dating from the same period. The site was used from the Bronze Age to the Roman period.
descriptions.NUR4060:
The monument has a fairly complex plan characterised by successive additions to the main body; the latter has an elliptical plan with a maximum diameter of 13.5 m and is equipped with two entrances located north and south-west, from which access is gained to two corridors that meet at an angle at the centre of the central tower.

Two bodies are attached to the central tower: one is situated on the northern side, while the other, which would have encircled at least two-thirds of the entire structure, is positioned on the opposite side.
descriptions.NUR20415: In the centre of the village, research has shown “the existence of important portions of the nuragic structure still preserved around the water basin constructed on the site in the 1920s. Despite the ancient building having been used as a foundation for the modern structure, excavations have revealed extensive remains of a tower featuring a powerful masonry of polygonal basalt blocks”.
descriptions.NUR1845: The monument is located about 200 metres to the northeast of the Nuraghe Figu and less than 350 metres to the southwest of the Nuraghe Bighinzone. It is a single-tower (single-tower nuraghe) with a circular plan, having a wall thickness of 4.00 m to the east and 3.60 m to the west, and a height varying from 3.05 m to the north-northeast, with 6 courses, to 1.75 m to the south-southwest, with 3/4 courses. The masonry is composed of polyhedral blocks arranged in horizontal courses, not always regular.
descriptions.NUR5934: Nuraghe belonging to the category of "uncompleted nuraghes", relatively common in this area.
descriptions.NUR3796:
Although reduced to a level of great ruin, it is still possible to discern the significance of this emergence, which should be classified within the group of nuraghes with a subfloor chamber, still partially accessible.

Literally "nuraghe of the cows' urine". See Pìsciu 'àccas.

See MAURO MAXIA, I nomi di luogo dell'Anglona e della Bassa valle del Coghinas, ed. Il Torchietto, Ozieri 1994, pp. 73-74 for the entry "Anglona".
descriptions.NUR5068: The Nuraghe Piscu, located within the municipal archaeological park since 1982, lies along the SS 128 towards Mandas. Piscu is the most representative monument of the Nuragic civilization of the Trexenta region.
descriptions.NUR2676: It retains the tholos intact except for a few upper courses.
descriptions.NUR1777: A row of subterranean wall face remains.
descriptions.NUR5482: Four-lobed nuraghe, largely covered by vegetation. The central tower is still accessible from above. It shows to be a much larger complex than it appears at first glance.
descriptions.NUR4909: Four-lobed, whose excavations have yielded many intact artefacts. The lifespan of the nuraghe appears to be very short.
descriptions.NUR15032: Damaged and buried nuraghe, whose structure cannot be defined. Part of it lies beneath a public reservoir.
descriptions.NUR5754: The structure, in a strategic location, stands on the calcareous hilltop of Sas Seas (482 m a.s.l.), from which it commands the surrounding territory. The planimetric development of the nuraghe is not clearly definable due to collapses. Inside the structure, a portion of a rectangular chamber remains, which originally probably closed with a truncated arch. The same chamber-closing system has been hypothesized for the nuraghe Fodde at Bolotana.
descriptions.NUR4730: Almost completely destroyed. The presence of large stones along the sides of the small hilltop indicates the existence of a nuraghe. Dense vegetation covers what remains.
descriptions.NUR4365: Nuraghe completely destroyed. On the small hilltop, small stones are visible, covering together with earth what was once the nuraghe, which no longer exists.
descriptions.NUR3327: Remains of structures related to single-tower tholos nuraghe. The building, now almost completely destroyed, consists of some blocks from the base course and part of what was intended to be the left pillar of the entrance, oriented to the south. The construction material is local basalt. Nearby, there are accumulations of lithic material derived from the nuraghe structures.
descriptions.NUR3857: The nuraghe remains isolated at the top of a rocky massif inside a large quarry.
descriptions.NUR4756: The site includes a central tower, a sub-elliptical structure that likely served as an entrance, and remnants of an outer wall along the entire perimeter. Various rocky outcrops complete the walls and influence their plan. The sub-elliptical structure, located on the southern side, probably functioned as the entrance to the complex and connected internal spaces via a corridor, currently blocked by collapses. In the north-western area, a terraced platform is identifiable.
descriptions.NUR6244: It is a complex structure consisting of a main tower with a staircase, a corridor niche, and a chamber surrounded by three niches arranged in a cross pattern, plus an addition of uncertain typological interpretation. The circular tower (diameter 11 m along the north-south axis) survives to a maximum height of about 6.50 m.
descriptions.NUR5960: Single-tower nuraghe, preserves the tholos intact. The lintel above the entrance measures approximately 3.30 m x 0.90 m x 1.85 m, weighing about 16,000 kg.
descriptions.NUR5629: The nuraghe is a complex type, with a central tower at the centre of a four-lobed bastion with a straight-curved profile enclosing a vaguely rectangular open-air courtyard. The whole structure measures 22.00 x 20.00 m (W-E / N-S axis), while the maximum surviving height is 6.20 m to the south-west and the wall thicknesses are 6.40 m to the south-west and 2.80 m to the north. Of the towers, only the one to the east is detectable, accessible from the courtyard through a corridor with steps visible in the final stretch.
descriptions.NUR4659: Single-tower nuraghe, of which megaliths remain, regularly "arated" in which few cossi of the Late Bronze Age.
descriptions.NUR19694: Located at a short distance from Sa Unta and Sa Tumba, in the area of Sculta 'e Muru, it appears as a heap of stones in complete disuse.
descriptions.NUR5916:
Elliptical corridor nuraghe, built using polygonal masonry with trachytic red stones.

The southern short side is preserved to a height of about 3 m and houses the entrance, topped by a granite lintel, from which access to a small sub-circular chamber leads to a second room via another entrance also featuring a granite lintel.
descriptions.NUR3727: June 2021, report. The foundation has collapsed and the stones have been propped up with iron rods; if you enlarge the image, the rods can be seen.
descriptions.NUR14700: It is a nuraghe left incomplete, notable for the size of the lintel above the entrance.
descriptions.NUR5805: Buried nuraghe, whose layout is difficult to determine. It was certainly a complex and multi-lobed structure. The name suggests its probable function as a watchpost at an embarkation point during the Nuragic period.
descriptions.NUR4019: There is no trace of the nuraghe remaining, apart from a large amount of rubble from the collapse, hidden by vegetation.
descriptions.NUR5320:
Nuraghe situated on the double and secure landing at Porto Pirastru.

Currently, only the walls and a concrete foundation of a recent installation remain.
descriptions.NUR14527: The highest part of the Posada cliff was occupied by a corridor-type nuraghe, and on its southern-eastern slopes, at a significantly lower elevation, there stood also a village, probably arranged on terraced levels. The village began at about 90 m as the crow flies from the nuraghe and extended from an elevation of about 42 m down to about 25 m a.s.l., covering a drop of about 17 metres. (Sanciu 2010)
descriptions.NUR873: The site consists of a three-lobed nuraghe, still mostly buried, and of structures probably dating to the Roman period.
descriptions.NUR3928: Likely location. Today only the megalithic basal structures of the nuraghe remain, although it is possible that much of the stones above have been broken up and incorporated into the walls of Villa La Favorita.
descriptions.NUR5313: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe in good condition, with entrance and tholos partially buried but relatively intact.
descriptions.NUR6018:
Complex tholos nuraghe, of the tancato type, with a central tower, a small courtyard and a secondary tower. The complex is built of polygonal blocks of local basalt, but is distinguished by the extremely careful working of the entrance blocks (jambs and lintels).

The central tower has a maximum surviving height of about 4 m, while the added tower has largely collapsed and survives to a maximum height of just over 3 m.
descriptions.NUR2872: Of the monument, in large part covered by an agricultural access road built directly over it, only some large stones remain, which formed the base row; from these it is possible to infer that the original layout was circular.
descriptions.NUR3913: Structures related to a complex nuraghe of the tancato type, featuring a main tower and a secondary tower connected to the first via a small courtyard. The nuraghe is built with polygonal basaltic blocks. The secondary tower, located to the south of the main one, is currently covered by vegetation and remains visible for 3–4 courses. The entrances cannot be identified and access to the complex is impossible due to collapses and the dense vegetation growing over the ruins.
descriptions.NUR3837: It is a simple tholos nuraghe, whose external plan is not visible as it is completely buried. The layout of the corridor (maximum length 3.40 m) and the nearly circular shape of the chamber, with a niche on the left side, can be understood. The structure is built with courses of granitic blocks, each course being progressively smaller than the ones above.
descriptions.NUR4479:
A nuraghe located in the territory of Ulassai, in the province of Ogliastra, is the second largest after the s'Ulimu nuraghe within the municipal area; it belongs to the complex of the "Neuletta" zone, where, in addition to itself, there are two other nuraghes and a small megalithic village, locally known as Nuragheddos.

The nuraghe was constructed during the period spanning the Middle to Late Bronze Age, approximately between 1400 and 900 BC.
descriptions.NUR2942: Diroccated nuraghe, it is distinguished by its proximity to several other Nuragic megalithic monuments.
descriptions.NUR1882: The nuraghe is completely ruined, reduced to a heap of blocks about two metres high.
descriptions.NUR4943: Nuraghe in basalt blocks. Unfortunately, the high residual volume is not properly exploited and the site is neither legible nor accessible, also due to dense vegetation.
descriptions.NUR786: Only small portions of the wall of the nuraghe remain. The collapse makes it impossible to read the plan.
descriptions.NUR5614: Of the nuraghe, in very poor condition of conservation, only a few large trachytic stones remain, which once formed the first course of the base and which today barely suggest the circular plan of the structure.
descriptions.NUR3891: Single-tower nuraghe. Only visible on the side facing west, the lowermost 3–4 courses of the base remain, constructed from locally sourced polygonal basalt blocks. The structures are completely overgrown with vegetation and are only observable from the agricultural penetration road that runs alongside them.
descriptions.NUR2536: Single-tower nuraghe, in reality a complex with buried structures covered by vegetation. The original tower retains its full perimeter circuit. On the south-east side there may be an elevated entrance. The interior of the tower is blocked by stones and soil. To the south-east a clear sign of illegal excavation is visible, exposing the external wall face of the tower. To the south and north-west circular curtain walls are visible, which may belong to two other towers.
descriptions.NUR3569: Nuraghe in poor state of conservation.
descriptions.NUR2189: Single-tower nuraghe with its top missing, of which only the imposing portal remains.
descriptions.NUR2190:
It is located in the municipality of Bolotana.

Single-tower nuraghe with a chamber.

The nuraghe is cut by a recent wall.

The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR2769: Diroccato, in poor conservation, covered by vegetation and partially buried, remains interesting for its position against the coastal cliff. Some internal chambers are visible but not accessible. Definitely a single-tower (single-tower nuraghe).
descriptions.NUR5169: Proto-nuraghe subsequently restructured into nuraghe. On the summits of the highest hills of Serrenti, overseeing the valleys leading to Trexenta, we find the simple proto-nuraghe of Monti de su Marchesu, Monti Acutzu, Monti Ibera, and Monti Proceddu.
descriptions.NUR5961: Single-tower in excellent condition, with walls 8/9 metres thick, internally inaccessible, with ancient oak trees surrounding it. It offers a magnificent view down to Gallura.
descriptions.NUR3278: It stands on a hilltop, at a panoramic point that dominates most of the Olgiastrino territory. Of the structure, in poor state of conservation, only some courses of limestone blocks are legible.
descriptions.NUR4067: Located in the area of Su Fonnesu (Teulada), at about 300 metres above sea level. It is situated on a pointed promontory, locally known as "punta acuccia", which from a distance resembles a pyramid. The stones used are mainly granitic. The view is excellent, especially over the Gulf of Palmas.
descriptions.NUR2163: Single-tower nuraghe, completely collapsed, still shows the entrance to an internal staircase that once led to the lower level and is now filled with collapse debris. A breach in the wall is also visible on the external eastern side, where perhaps a window had opened.
descriptions.NUR16090: Damaged nuraghe, of which only a few courses of the wall face remain
descriptions.NUR2502: Damaged nuraghe, overshadowed by a firebreak post with only a few visible remains. Excellent panorama stretching from the Seruci nuraghe to the large beach Porto Paglia/Punta S'Arena/Plag'e Mesu/Fontanamare to the Pan di Zucchero.
descriptions.NUR8432: The nuraghe is preserved to a height of about two metres, with an internal diameter of about 7 metres, and features a single opening positioned in the north-east direction, dominating the access path to the terminal part of the valley and the small plateau on which the Giants' Tomb of San Giacomo is located.
descriptions.NUR8634: Small atypical single-tower nuraghe, belonging to the Appiu village context. Located at the end of a path that extends from the village to the Giants' Tomb, two small dolmen, and finally this small nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR17302: On the summit of the hill lie the ruins of a small nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR19710: It is the most imposing monument preserved on the territory. It is almost certain to have been a complex structure, given the prominence of its walls compared to other monuments. Inside the chamber, a niche positioned towards the north-west is still visible, and slightly to the west, a small access chamber appears, which seems to correspond to a staircase.
descriptions.NUR11633: Very buried but identifiable. During recovery work carried out by the Superintendence for Archaeological Heritage, funded by the Porto Rotondo Consortium. The so-called nuraghe, after archaeological excavations, was found to be a coastal watchtower of Punic period (4th century BC).
descriptions.NUR10880: It is a complex nuraghe to which the anti-ship battery Boggio structures were added during the Second World War. From the outside the wall face of the probable main tower is clearly visible.
descriptions.NUR2524: Remains of a complex nuraghe built in basalt.
descriptions.NUR8266: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe overlooking the valley of the Rio Santu Milanu in an area re-used in the medieval period.
descriptions.NUR2752: Of the nuraghe only a few courses remain, barely visible from the area of the subterranean sanctuaries below. The nuraghe rises above a calcareous spur from which it commands the surrounding valleys.
descriptions.NUR3323: The nuraghe was in close topographic and cultural connection with the giants' tombs of Biristeddi, located about 250 metres away.
descriptions.NUR3478:
It is a single-tower (single-tower nuraghe) with a circular plan (diameter 12.50 m), with an entrance oriented to south-east; the tower survives to a maximum height of 4.80 m at south-east, with six courses, while the minimum height is at north-west, with 2 metres and three courses. The masonry is composed of carefully worked blocks arranged in regular horizontal courses.

In the surrounding area, circular structures of numerous nuragic huts are clearly visible.
descriptions.NUR9484:
It is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan (diam. 13.30 x 13 m): the wall thickness is about 4 metres, while the surviving height is 1.75 m with three courses.

The entrance, facing south-east, leads into a corridor (length 4 m – width 1.50/1 m) in which the existence of the stair and the opposing guard chamber can be discerned.

Of the circular chamber only the base diameter (5 m) can be measured, while it is not possible to determine whether it was lined with niches.
descriptions.NUR6331: Complex nuraghe with an irregular plan. Its perimeter wall features a single, continuous mass of rubble, from which westward remnants of the central tower emerge. The complex is enclosed by a megalithic outer wall that protects it to the west and, in part, to the north.
descriptions.NUR3620: Probable nuraghe tower, of which only the lintel of the entrance and the rubble heap remain.
descriptions.NUR14332: Nuraghe located within the urban centre, single-tower, partially collapsed
descriptions.NUR3787: Complex nuraghe. Access to the upper level via a staircase passing beneath the SE tower.
descriptions.NUR2561: Complex nuraghe, never studied, located within a private property, surrounded by vegetation.
descriptions.NUR640: The nuraghe is situated on a hillock where some wall structures of uncertain origin are also visible, part of which ends in a dry stone wall of more recent construction. The structure of the nuraghe is indeterminate due to its poor state of preservation; it might be a single-tower (single-tower nuraghe) built of trachytic stone.
descriptions.NUR15898: The site is difficult to identify due to the Mediterranean scrub. Along the roadside there is a significant scatter of betili, probably dating to the Roman period. Around the nuraghe there are traces of collapses.
