descriptions.NUR4353: A tholos nuraghe whose north tower is clearly visible. The south tower has collapsed on the seaward side. An artificial entrance dug by curiosity-seekers is present.
descriptions.NUR2830: It is well known to the local population because the entrance architrave is particularly striking, being made of white limestone probably from the area of Giombachis or Iscala 'Lvena. In this case, too, one must speak of an advanced state of degradation due to numerous collapses affecting the cyclopean monument. Nevertheless, certain constructive and architectural features are clearly evident.
descriptions.NUR3867: Proto-nuraghe of corridor type. The structure stands on a valley floor just 4 m above the river named Riu e'Sa Tanca, on its eastern bank. It is completely covered by vegetation, particularly obscured by thick thickets of rowan trees growing abundantly along the riverbanks. Large polygonal basaltic blocks are visible, stacked on the northern and eastern sides.
descriptions.NUR3902:
The complex, located on the summit of Monte Colbu, which overlooks the Olbia plain.

The nuraghe, surrounded by a curtain wall that originally reached a height of over 5 metres and featuring two entrances (one to the north and one to the south), is of single-tower type. In the entrance corridor there is a small niche and part of the staircase passage leading to the upper terrace. The central chamber, which contains a small sacred well, had a tholos roof.
descriptions.NUR5749: Complex nuraghe belonging to a much larger settlement, which has never been the subject of archaeological excavations.
descriptions.NUR8431: Located on the side of the canyon of the same name, where during the rains the same named torrent flows, it originally stood on an isolated spur raised above the valley below. Some courses of medium to large stones are present. A few metres downstream, large amounts of rubble are visible, and the structure is now almost completely destroyed.
descriptions.NUR1930: Single-tower nuraghe, with traces of a settlement. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR3925: Single-tower nuraghe consisting of a chamber with an intact tholos roof and an internal staircase connecting the various levels that form the complex structure.
descriptions.NUR2912:
It is a nuraghe of difficult typological definition due to the collapse and the dense undergrowth that covers it.

The masonry is composed of medium-sized stones laid in regular horizontal courses. The few elements identified do not allow a clear understanding of the planimetric layout of this structure, which a excavation might reveal as possibly a proto-nuraghe rather than a classic tholos nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR6417:
Four-lobed nuraghe.

In the vicinity there are also two giants' tombs and a nuragic temple with a sacred well.
descriptions.NUR2999: It is located within the territory of the comune of Pozzomaggiore (SS). It is a large proto-nuraghe, almost destroyed. There is a covered entrance covered in debris and a corridor of about 10 metres in length with a height of 2 metres. At the upper part, a further entrance is still visible. Numerous stones are scattered around the structure.
descriptions.NUR5662: Nuraghe partially collapsed with intact tholos
descriptions.NUR2961: The monument is a single-tower nuraghe constructed with medium and large-sized blocks arranged in regular courses. The nuraghe is not in good condition of preservation. The southern-eastern entrance, collapsed, leads into a corridor whose left wall shows access to a staircase (itself collapsed). The chamber is circular and survives to a maximum height of 9 m.
descriptions.NUR3635: It is a single-tower (single-tower nuraghe) situated on top of a cliff from which the entire area of the Tirso river, below the village of Villanova Truscheddu, can be seen. The tholos has collapsed inward, and the nuraghe is not maintained and has never been investigated.
descriptions.NUR16343: The Ruinas Nuraghe is described by Giovanni Lilliu as the tallest in Sardinia. At an elevation of 1,205 metres, it offers a magnificent panoramic view of the surrounding landscape and of the ruins of numerous circular huts that surround it (at least 200).
descriptions.NUR4648: Ruina Tassa is a single-tower nuraghe. Like Luas and Friorosu, it rests on a calcareous foundation. The entire area shows an unusual abundance of squared stones, used in boundary walls, suggesting the existence in ancient times of a village of considerable size.
descriptions.NUR5737: Single-tower tholos nuraghe. The nuraghe, built from polygonal basalt blocks of local origin, has collapsed in large part in the south-eastern sector, while it remains in good condition to the north and south. The entrance was probably located to the south, but it is no longer visible.
descriptions.NUR5706: The Ruiu in question is an abandoned single-tower nuraghe completely enveloped by vegetation, yet we were able to penetrate through the thick undergrowth to enter it. The tholos is not intact, and unfortunately vegetation dominates the structure.
descriptions.NUR6061: The ground level should have the tholos intact.
descriptions.NUR5734: It is one of many nuraghes scattered across the Torralba area; this one is located near the railway line connecting Mores to the Torralba station. It is a complex nuraghe, consisting of a central tower with a frontal addition of two further secondary towers, connected by a robust curtain wall. It dates to the period between Middle Bronze and Late Bronze (1600–1000 BC).
descriptions.NUR3533: Nuraghe along the road. Partly collapsed. The tholos is open and essentially visible in section, showing its constructional features.
descriptions.NUR3703: It is a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe with a characteristic conical shape and two superimposed chambers…. Access is through the central door facing south-south-east, and the structure includes a central chamber with courses corbelled inwards that close the dome, and three lateral cells arranged orthogonally (90°) relative to the entrance. A spiral staircase, turning clockwise, leads up to the top of the nuraghe directly above the central chamber, where the raised portion of the second chamber is still clearly visible.
descriptions.NUR14208:
The nuraghe is of the single-tower with tholos type, constructed from roughly hewn trachytic stones and has a circular base with an external diameter of 12 metres, a remaining height of about 6 metres, and wall inclinations ranging from 7 to 11 degrees.

The entrance, oriented to the southeast as in most nuraghes, is topped by an architrave composed of two separate blocks and leads into a passage covered by transverse slabs.
descriptions.NUR4170:
More precisely, it is a proto-nuraghe.

Attached to the nuraghe, a boundary wall was built for a villa.
descriptions.NUR6292: Nuraghe with a system of outer walls surrounding it, visible from the adjacent path.
descriptions.NUR3944: It is a complex nuraghe that was demolished to make way for the Roman settlement.
descriptions.NUR5935: The Abba Noa nuraghe, on a granite outcrop at 178 m above sea level, is characterized by mixed masonry: part of the construction uses local granite, while the rest employs basalt obtainable in the surrounding hills. The plan, complex, consists of two towers diametrically opposed, joined by a bastion that is straight to the west and curved to the east, running along the edge of the summit.
descriptions.NUR1255: Location according to ancient maps of this nuraghe, of which today only scattered stones remain.
descriptions.NUR538: Single-tower nuraghe and settlement (Santu Sadurru). The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR539: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe with its top missing, not indicated on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR1864: Complex nuraghe of which the central tower and a bastion, perhaps three-lobed, survive. The original tower retains almost its entire outline. The interior of the tower is filled with collapse and vegetation. To the NNE there is a curving wall that reaches its maximum height to the ENE, where five courses survive; it may be a tower. To the W–SW a wall can be made out, probably belonging to a lateral tower. A further tower was probably located to the SE. Ceramic fragments are present, attributable from the Nuragic period to the medieval period.
descriptions.NUR6413: Built on a slight basaltic outcrop less than 200 metres south of Riu Corte, the monument is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan, now largely demolished along its outer perimeter. Due to the collapse, the details of the corridor and chamber are no longer discernible.
descriptions.NUR3559: Four-lobed, topless nuraghe, partially buried, shows the lintel, which stands out for its considerable size.
descriptions.NUR1896: One of the six coastal nuraghes of the island of Sant'Antioco – a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe, with an attached probable hut or other structure – located on the promontory of the same name, is situated in a strategic position within the cove "Su Portu de su Casu". Of this nuraghe, only some of the original tower's courses and a short stretch of walling located to the east of the tower remain. The internal curtain wall's route cannot be identified anymore, as the space is completely covered by vegetation and collapse.
descriptions.NUR3544:
The nuraghe is a single-tower with a staircase, a corridor niche, and a chamber bordered by two opposite niches. The external plan profile cannot be fully defined due to collapses and dense undergrowth.

The tower, with a diameter of about 12 metres, remains with a maximum height of 5.30 m (8 courses).

The masonry is composed of basalt blocks of medium and large size, roughly shaped with care, arranged in regular horizontal rows.
descriptions.NUR18107:
The nuraghe is situated on the northern edge of a modest trachytic plateau and commands a view over the entire valley below. At a short distance from it lies the Runara dolmen and the Pittigheddu nuraghe.

The nuraghe is in very poor condition, having been used as a quarry for stones used to build enclosures that now rise completely against the structure, making it extremely difficult to trace the original layout of the ancient construction.
descriptions.NUR2725: It appears to be a single-tower nuraghe in good condition with the interior still intact. Surrounding it, traces of a settlement are visible.
descriptions.NUR827: The construction is atypical and difficult to classify: it is not a nuraghe but difficult to categorize as a hut. Human interventions at different historical periods have been found, clearly altering the original structure and thus causing the difficulty of classification.
descriptions.NUR4803: The corridor nuraghe complex Sa Conca 'e sa Cresia originated as a corridor nuraghe in the Middle Bronze Age and was later restructured into a tholos in the Recent Bronze Age. It underwent restoration in the surrounding areas during the 1990s. From the tholos corridors were excavated by tomb-burial workers, leading to the interior tholos chambers. Outside, two elliptical structures are noted to the west and south, some of which are now partially collapsed and of uncertain function.
descriptions.NUR4551: Proto-nuraghe of circular or sub-circular form
descriptions.NUR3318: It is located at the summit of the mountain of the same name. Access is difficult by climbing the slopes from the village of Bottidda below, but it can be reached more easily via the nearby road to Foresta Burgos. From its remains one can enjoy a view of the valley below, known as "Su Campu".
descriptions.NUR16533: Complex structure, almost entirely buried. The nuraghe is surrounded by dense vegetation, and furthermore, a fence has been erected on top of it, preventing view of the eastern part.
descriptions.NUR4578: Mixed nuraghe, of which only little remains, partly covered by vegetation. Possibly enlarged and restored.
descriptions.NUR536: Almost hidden by the dense undergrowth of shrubs.
descriptions.NUR5506: Complex nuraghe, partially collapsed and surrounded by vegetation. The tholos is intact, surrounded by a significant outer wall.
descriptions.NUR19521: Nuraghe on the SSW slope of Monte Arbus, on the hillside facing the S'Acqua sa Canna area. Complex nuraghe with a three-lobed bastion and an internal courtyard. The towers of which traces remain are positioned to the N, SSE and SSW. Because of the collapses and the vegetation it is difficult to make out the outline of the walls clearly. By contrast the outline of the courtyard is well defined; at first glance it appears pentagonal; in some stretches up to three rows of boulders of various shapes and sizes survive.
descriptions.NUR2763: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe; located within a military area. It preserves the intact tholos. The site is now accessible (it is nonetheless advisable to request an "authorization" from the Caserma "Bechi Luserna").
descriptions.NUR15026: Complex nuraghe, partially eroded and buried, for which it is not possible to define the structure.
descriptions.NUR12457: Circular single-tower nuraghe with a southern entrance topped by a stone lintel. The central chamber, elongated, is distinguished by the presence of four niches—an unusual feature—located one on the left side, one at the back opposite the entrance, and two (in pairs) on the right side. All are semi-elliptical in plan; the cross-section is trapezoidal, like that of the access passage. The remaining conical height is about 3 m.
descriptions.NUR3920: Structures related to a nuraghe, presumably of an archaic type, of corridor design. The monument is located within a private courtyard in the northern periphery of the current settlement of Bonarcado. Among the remains visible—between stone blocks and recent concrete structures that adjoin the nuraghe—there are 4 to 5 courses of polygonal blocks in basalt. The construction features of the few surviving elements appear to suggest an archaic character for the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR2765: Single-tower nuraghe located at Sa Cordiola. The condition of the external walls is good, while inside the structure has collapsed. It is characterized by having two names: the first is "Sa Cordiola", the second is "Giustalassa", the name of the adjacent locality.
descriptions.NUR5955:
Single-tower, single-cell. Svettato, with the chamber completely filled with collapsed debris. The southern-eastern side of its outer wall, where the entrance opened, is entirely collapsed. The highest point of the monument reaches about 3 m in height and is composed of six courses of roughly hewn stones.

The lintel of the entrance, well-crafted, is found isolated on the ground a short distance away.
descriptions.NUR1279: The nuraghe is located at the end of a valley on a small rocky spur.
descriptions.NUR4917: Powerful, captivating even under a grey winter sky, the Nuraghe Sa Dom 'e S'Orku rises above a rocky massif amid a magnificent landscape, offering broad views over the entire Parteolla down to the Gulf of Cagliari and the mountains of Iglesiente. Dating back to the 2nd millennium BC, it is the main monument of the Dolianova area, where numerous other prehistoric remains are also present.
descriptions.NUR4802: The Nuragic fortification consists of a tholos tower enclosed in a courtyard which in turn is protected by an outer wall provided with five further towers. The entrance lies to the south and leads into a small courtyard where several rooms are found that were used for metal smelting, as shown by the bronze-smelting waste discovered all around. The central tower has an elliptical plan; inside, on the right, a stairway branches off leading to the upper floor.
descriptions.NUR3711: Located in the valley of the Rio Siniscola, near the mouth of the river, it has a rectangular plan with an internal chamber of elliptical shape, preserved to a height of about 2 metres, and is built with white limestone incorporating slabs of shale.
descriptions.NUR1262: Remains of the nuraghe Sa Domo Ezza
descriptions.NUR8463:
This nuraghe has unique features, such as three distinct helical staircases leading from the ground up to higher levels.

Today, what remains is very little. The height of the central tower and the massive scale of the structure can be inferred from the diameter of the tower, the size of the ashlar blocks, and the surface area of the main body's sediment.

In this case too, a village of considerable size must have developed around it.
descriptions.NUR19665:
The nuraghe is very large and I believe it has more than one tower.

It has suffered numerous collapses; it would be advisable to take a photo from above using a drone.

From the nuraghe one has a wide view of the surrounding territory extending all the way to the sea.
descriptions.NUR3786: Remains of a nuraghe, possibly never completed
descriptions.NUR3356: A short distance from the megalithic circle are the basal remains of a simple circular nuraghe of the advanced Nuragic period, and a little further downhill the Ochila domus de janas, some of them richly decorated with symbolic and architectural elements in relief. The megalithic enclosure consists of ten (plus an eleventh lying overturned in the centre of the area) irregularly parallelepiped megaliths set side by side, forming a semicircle 9–10 metres in diameter.
descriptions.NUR4870: It is a singular corridor nuraghe, complex and irregular, composed of three large megalithic bodies placed side by side and various secondary constructions. It has a surviving height of over 6 metres and was built on a projecting rock outcrop using polyhedral basalt blocks stacked dry in polygonal masonry. The nuraghe dates back, in its initial construction phase, to the early Bronze Age.
descriptions.NUR5355: The imposing single-tower nuraghe Sa Fraigada is located just tens of metres from the summit of Monte Cresia and is the largest in the area. The ancient nuragic structure has suffered significant collapses, making its plan difficult to interpret; the architraved entrance, presumably situated to the east, is not visible. The circular tower has a diameter of about 8 metres and remains visible to a height of 3.70 metres on its southern-western side.
descriptions.NUR10494:
The nuraghe is a complex type, consisting of a central tower to which a bastion has been attached on the front—complete with full enclosure of the structure—containing two secondary towers that enclose a central courtyard.

The main tower (diam. 18.00 m) has an entrance oriented to the southeast (width 0.80–1.20 m), surmounted by a lintel with a drainage window.
descriptions.NUR5073: Single-tower nuraghe with an elliptical plan. Some courses are visible. In the area, large clumps of clay are present, along with other wall structures suggesting the existence of a residential zone inhabited by huts.
descriptions.NUR19526: The area where the nuraghe is believed to have been situated has been completely destroyed, I would say devastated, during the period of the Second World War, when the likely structures, belonging to the monument and the huts of the village, were dismantled/adapted for military use.
descriptions.NUR4575:
The construction is extensive and intricately structured. The area highlighted in red is the highest and most fully enclosed by walls, typically Nuragic, up to one and a half metres thick.

Yet, surrounding it, other walls can be discerned, defining a much larger surface area, with terraced levels sloping down towards the northern catchment.

The building dominated the valley, now completely built up, which is named after the chapel of Santa Barbara.
descriptions.NUR20346: It is located above the Church of Santa Lucia. Only little remains visible, particularly a wall of the tower (I believe it is a single-tower nuraghe) on the northern side and some varied courses.
descriptions.NUR8369: It is a complex structure built with squared limestone blocks, featuring a clearly visible internal chamber whose archaeological deposit has been severely disturbed by illegal activities. Inside, three niches with vaulted, ogival coverings are clearly visible, and the entrance is located in the south-east, to the right of which a short dead-end corridor opens, leading to a small niche.
descriptions.NUR5502: Complex nuraghe visible seasonally depending on the water levels in the Cuga basin. A considerable village once surrounded the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR2858: Near the provincial road 25 to Aidomaggiore stands the corridor nuraghe known as “Sa Jua”, as illustrated here in the fine photographs by Nicola Castangia. Professor Pittau derives its name from the Latin “iuga”, indicating a herd of cattle. I may observe that in ancient Egypt cattle were also called “iwa” (jua), a clear parallel to the Sardinian term “ju o “juale”, which denotes a yoke.
descriptions.NUR2555: Complex nuraghe with a main tower and two additional towers with a courtyard, built of limestone. Traces of a settlement.
descriptions.NUR4136: Given its dominant position over the surrounding countryside, it is presumed to have been a very important and complex nuraghe. Unfortunately, at present only two curved sections of wall remain: one towards the north and the other towards the south. Nearby, many basaltic lava pebbles have been found.
descriptions.NUR3647: Complex nuraghe: the central tower is visible, inside there are three niches. It has been extensively modified due to agricultural mechanization and the constant activity of tomb diggers. It once had an extensive village attached, extending to the giants' tomb of "Sa pedra Longa".
descriptions.NUR4509: Small complex nuraghe, not otherwise definable
descriptions.NUR3328: Damaged nuraghe, of which three courses and the entrance portal remain.
descriptions.NUR6255: Damaged nuraghe, of which only a few courses remain
descriptions.NUR2504: Single-tower nuraghe, built with calcareous stones, of which only one to two courses of stones of the external wall face remain.
descriptions.NUR3680: Single-tower nuraghe partially collapsed. Most of the walling remains on one side.
descriptions.NUR3528: The village consists of several well-built huts, equipped with basins, drainage channels, and ovens. Some scholars believe these huts were used for cultic purposes, while others think they formed part of a residential settlement.
descriptions.NUR1383: The Nuraghe Sa mandra e sa Giua no longer exists; it has been levelled, and its ashlars were used to build dry walls and the Roman settlement.
descriptions.NUR5911:
The archaeological complex "Sa Mandra de sa Jua" – literally "the yoked oxen enclosure", a term broadly indicating a fertile area – occupies a modest elevation overlooking the Rio Mannu of Ozieri.

The site, multi-stratified, was continuously inhabited until the medieval period and has been incorporated since the 1960s into the San Nicola district, located about 4 kilometres from the village of Ozieri.

The Monument
descriptions.NUR3398: The complex nuraghe cannot be fully assessed in its current state due to the entire site having been disrupted by mechanical equipment; although, a few years ago, it was still possible to enter by descending from above. Access was therefore through a long corridor with walls curving inwards, likely a recent earthmoving operation has added more material to the nuraghe and has blocked access to the interior. Hope remains that the burial has protected it from this damage.
descriptions.NUR3849:
Possible single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe; doubt arises from its small size, but it might be a small nuraghe situated on a hilltop with the sole function of a watchtower.

Near the structure are two burials, possibly of Roman period, built with calcareous slabs; inside, two skulls and other human bones can be observed.
descriptions.NUR9274: Single-tower nuraghe made of large trachyte and limestone blocks; the monument retains the tholos, inside which there are three niches arranged in a cross pattern, the tholos being about 5 metres high. Adjacent to the nuraghe is still present the nuragic well, which is still used today by the landowners.
descriptions.NUR15145:
Buried and partially concealed by anti-aircraft installations from the Second World War. Traces of a Bronze Age village between southwest and east.

Chronology: Bronze Age Nuragic (for the nuraghe and the village); contemporary period (circa 1942–43: for the military post).
descriptions.NUR6308: The Murartu or Sa Menta nuraghe is located in the territory of Silanus, about 2.2 km from the village. It is almost completely hidden by vegetation. As a complex nuraghe, a portion of the central tower rises about 2 metres in height.
descriptions.NUR5571: It is characterized by having been built with both calcareous and trachytic stones, as in the nearby nuraghe Corvos; however, while the latter shows a clear distinction between the calcareous and trachytic sections, in the nuraghe Sa Menta stones of different types are intermixed in the wall face without any discernible pattern.
descriptions.NUR3885: A few calcareous white stones at the base perimeter. Only the entrance and a little else are visible, all set within a dense thicket of fetid anagiride (sa giolva). The name should derive from the local topographic term. Collina dei liburni, a leguminous shrub known for its pendulous fruits and for the unpleasant odour exuded by its leaves when touched. Pastoralists believe that the leaves of this plant impart a bitter taste to the milk of goats. See Nuraghe sas giòlvas. mu
descriptions.NUR5508: In total state of ruin, it is named after the toponym of the land or the owner of the land itself. mu
descriptions.NUR3207: Complex nuraghe consisting of a tower with an additional body, built in trachyte.
descriptions.NUR1605: Complex nuraghe heavily collapsed, making it difficult to determine its original form.
descriptions.NUR3939: The nuraghe Sa Murallia gets its name from a wall that has been built against the original structures on the lower side; it is largely hidden by accumulations, strata, and superimposed or adjacent structures built over the centuries. At the same time and in successive phases, alongside these nuraghes, the first settlements emerged, sometimes enclosed by imposing walls with oval or circular outlines, today partially visible (Tradori, Araganzola, Maganzosa). (from the town of Narbolia website)
descriptions.NUR5646: It is located at the border between the municipal territories of Nuoro and Orani, south of the town. Land transformation does not allow for a certain identification of the rest of the settlement, though its existence is remembered.
descriptions.NUR3413: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe belonging to the complex of nuraghi at the site Su Padru.
descriptions.NUR3798: The nuraghe stands on a hillock, next to the church of the same name (17th century). Its state of conservation is modest; it rises about 4 metres, with a southern entrance partially blocked. Inside, two niches with acute sixths can be seen. Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe built of basalt blocks.
descriptions.NUR2943:
It is a single-tower nuraghe with a guard niche, a probable stairwell, and a chamber with three niches arranged in a cross.

The tower, circular in plan (diam. 12.70 m), survives to a maximum height of 5 m on the west side, with 7 courses, while the minimum height is about 2 metres in the section affected by the entrance, to the south-east, which has completely collapsed. The masonry consists of roughly dressed trachyte blocks laid in horizontal courses with numerous packing wedges.
descriptions.NUR3335: Inaccessible with the tholos collapsed inward.
descriptions.NUR3983: A central tower rises up to four courses, over two metres in height, surrounded by a wall. The entire structure is connected to circular and straight walls that emerge from the ground but only at the upper edge of the last course of stones. Most of the complex nuraghe lies buried beneath the soil. To the north-east of the tower, at a distance of about 7–8 metres, there may be a "sacred" well.
descriptions.NUR13682: The single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe Santu Juanni or San Giovanni is located about 1 km north of Villaurbana, in the territory of Siamanna. It is a single-tower nuraghe built from basalt blocks only roughly shaped. The entrance corridor is flat-topped and leads to a chamber where the tholos is still intact. The upper level, now collapsed, is overgrown with shrubs and Indian fig trees.
descriptions.NUR4233: It is a tower with a circular outer perimeter, a maximum diameter of about 10 m, and an internal chamber that is approximately elliptical, as far as can be judged from its present state of preservation. The whole northern sector is badly damaged, and the east and west sides have been affected by illicit excavations that caused further gaps in the perimeter, later patched by an attempt to “restore” the masonry in the eastern quadrant carried out by the Sisters of the Good Shepherd.
descriptions.NUR3370:
The monument consists of a central tower with a second, partially collapsed tower attached to the north-northeast exposure.

The main tower, composed of basalt blocks of varying sizes, survives to a maximum residual height of about 8 metres. A staircase leads to the upper level. A large settlement, indicated on the surface by paving and numerous ceramic artifacts, extended around the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR895: San Leonardo is an ancient village in Gallura, situated near the church of the same name, a typical rural Gallurese church accompanied by a small cemetery. The remains of the San Leonardo nuraghe demonstrate the presence of inhabitants even during the Nuragic period.
descriptions.NUR3948: Nuraghe partially enclosed by the walls of the small church dedicated to San Lorenzo, on the north-east side of the structure (the side facing the village), some remains of the S. Lorenzo nuraghe are still visible.
descriptions.NUR4200:
The Santu Scioni, San Lussorio nuraghe stands in the countryside of Pabillonis, on a hillock from which much of the Campidano plain can be seen towards Monte Linas and above a bend of the Flumini Mannu.

Originally it must have consisted of a central tower and a series of other towers that are now by no means easy to identify, since all the wall structures have been levelled and covered by human activity around the sacredness that the site still retains today.
descriptions.NUR19523: Destroyed nuraghe, of which only a small amount remains
descriptions.NUR3352: Of the nuraghe only the foundation remains.
descriptions.NUR13469: Built from basalt blocks, the structure features a three-lobed layout, with a central mastio and three secondary towers arranged around a courtyard of falcon-shaped plan. The site was surrounded by a powerful outer wall – traces of which are clearly visible – composed of five towers and straight curtain walls, except for the northern side, naturally protected by the slopes of the Giare.
descriptions.NUR4178: At the site of 'su pranu', a complex nuraghe in poor state of conservation, hidden and almost inaccessible to visitors. Nearby, the remains of a village are clearly visible.
descriptions.NUR4729:
Partially uncovered in December 2002, the nuraghe Sanna is named after the nearby furriadroxiu that rises at its base in the countryside between Santadi and Piscinas. The excavations enabled the men of the Soprintendenza to discover a previously forgotten complex nuraghe, preserved in excellent condition and situated in a dominant position over the surrounding territory.

Today it is almost abandoned and damaged precisely by the excavations.
descriptions.NUR5446: The nuraghe has been destroyed, only some traces of the wall face remain observed in different areas of the hillside.
descriptions.NUR4259: The San Nicola nuraghe is considered the oldest in the entire area, dating back to 1600 BC. The nuraghe awaits further study and is still buried up to its summit.
descriptions.NUR4072: All that remains of the nuraghe are some courses arranged in a circular order that formed the base of a single-tower.
descriptions.NUR2647: It takes its name from an old church. It stands on a small promontory on the right bank of the Riu Mannu. The lintel is broken and the whole monument is in a state of complete decay and abandonment. There were two entrances (one has collapsed) and several sacrificial stones. The peculiarity of this nuraghe is that the tholos, perfectly intact, was built with dark boulders formed from agglomerations of fossil shells. A rarity, since no trace of this type of material is found in the area.
descriptions.NUR21148: Nuraghe partially collapsed and invaded by vegetation, located at the edge of the village, near a rural chapel.
descriptions.NUR4871: The San Pietro nuraghe is located on the summit of a hill in the immediate vicinity of the village of Ussaramanna and is named after a church of the same name, now disappeared. It is a complex nuraghe consisting of a central tower and a quadrangular bastion with towers facing the four cardinal points.
descriptions.NUR3946: Three-lobed nuraghe serving as a foundation for the church of San Saturnino.
descriptions.NUR8429: The nuragic complex consists of nine towers, three belonging to the central structures and six to the robust outer wall. Its absolute peculiarity is the direct superimposition on its structures of the ruins of a small country church, dedicated to the eponymous saint and dating to the early 17th century; eleven burials found in the area around the sacred building belong to its period of use. On the hill of San Sebastiano, traces of a Punic occupation are legible.
descriptions.NUR4600: The Church was built upon the remains of a nuraghe known as Nuraxi Mannu, and Nuragic remains are present throughout the village. The decision to build the Church arose from the desire to give a sacred continuity to a specific location. The Church is a small building with a rectangular plan and a single nave. On its white façade, the entrance door is an arch with six voussoirs and a cornice, topped by a small circular window.
descriptions.NUR19697: Located in the San Simplicio valley, on the ground surface only a few fallen stones remain.
descriptions.NUR5816: It is a complex nuraghe, consisting of a main tower surrounded by a quadrilobate bastion that includes four angular towers and an open-air courtyard. In the north-eastern area, the remains of the outer wall and the ruins of an attached dwelling are visible.
descriptions.NUR5660:
The structure, one of the most renowned on the island, is a complex type, consisting of a central tower and a quadrilobate bastion with an open courtyard.

It was defended by an outer wall, identified by General Della Marmora, which today is barely legible on the landscape.

The bastion (height 8.80 m) includes four towers connected by curtain walls with a concave-convex profile, built with roughly shaped basalt blocks laid out on horizontal courses.
descriptions.NUR4697: Almost imperceptible remains of a nuraghe
descriptions.NUR3464: The simple nuraghe was transformed into the "tancato" type. Indeed, a second, smaller building was added in front of the original tower, connected to it by two curtain walls with a broken line, enclosing a courtyard. Noted for the occurrence of the "bull's light" phenomenon.
descriptions.NUR2516: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe with stairs, a corridor niche, and a chamber with three niches arranged in a cross. The tower, circular in plan, retains a maximum height of 12.25 m on 21 courses, while to the south-east it measures 11 m on 19 courses. At the top, the diameter is 10 metres. The masonry is composed of finely shaped basalt blocks arranged in regular horizontal courses.
descriptions.NUR3725:
It is a large proto-nuraghe with a single tower, equipped with some auxiliary structures, built with enormous basalt blocks.  

Due to collapses, access to the interior is possible only partially.
descriptions.NUR4582: In 1942 a stonemason from Donori, while breaking up a granite block to extract building stones, discovered beneath the block 53 coins bearing the image of Emperor Antoninus Pius, Trajan, Empress Faustina, and other rulers with names indecipherable. The nuraghe must have been very large, since despite being heavily damaged and covered by bushes and various debris accumulated in the surrounding area, the number of scattered stones is considerable.
descriptions.NUR6206: The complex nuraghe of Santa Barbara is located about three km from the village. Built in basalt, it is four-lobed and is surrounded by a large settlement. A field survey conducted in 1986 explored part of the settlement, particularly a hut. This hut was circular, constructed from Sinis sandstone; the floor, however, was made of tuff. Near the hut, a rectangular basin with two concave sections, communicating with each other, was found.
descriptions.NUR2990: More precisely, it is a proto-nuraghe or corridor nuraghe; due to an internal collapse, it has become impossible to visit it from the entrance.
descriptions.NUR1249: According to the map shown in the publication "L'Altare preistorico di Monte d'Accoddi" by Ercole Contu, the correct name of the nuraghe should be "Camusina", a name also recorded in the IGM as "Camuscina". It is in very poor condition and completely surrounded by dense vegetation.
descriptions.NUR4428: Currently, the single-tower retains a height of five to six courses and the plan of the lower chambers is fairly easy to discern. On the western side of the corridor opens the staircase chamber, which still preserves eight steps in situ and which originally curved to follow the circular outline of the curtain wall.
descriptions.NUR4791:
Along the road from Samatzai towards S. Pietro.

Collapsed complex nuraghe, located on a slight slope with a central tower and two other smaller towers. It has an elongated plan with the three towers aligned along the same longitudinal axis oriented from north to south. Near the central tower, the basal structures of three circular huts are visible, clearly belonging to a small nearby settlement. The structures are built using marly and basaltic materials.
descriptions.NUR2303: "Almost entirely dismantled, only some ashlar and wall segments remain of the original structure, whose layout is indiscernible due to dense vegetation and widespread decay. R. Ledda notes the discovery of primary fusion residues of minerals, currently no longer in situ."
descriptions.NUR15281: Nuraghe coincident with a medieval settlement
descriptions.NUR4028: The single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe at Santa Lucia di Assolo is located in the countryside, within the archaeological area encompassing the country church dedicated to the same Santa; it has a tronco-conical form and is currently visible only its base, composed of four courses laid dry, made up of large stone blocks.
descriptions.NUR4513: The archaeological area is located on the edge of the basaltic upland of Santa Lucia, east of the Monte Arci massif. The area includes two complex nuraghes with villages, situated about 50 metres apart. The nuraghe to the east is also a complex, in better condition than the previous one, and preserves the mastio chamber, with its top missing, some niches along the walls, and the staircase opening on the entrance passage.
descriptions.NUR4447: The nuraghe belongs to a complex that also includes a second nuraghe located about 50 metres away. It must have been particularly impressive, judging by the extent of the ruins. In the collapse that covers the main tower, a tholos chamber of notable height is identifiable: on the profile of the environment, the upper part of the angular passage, typical of early-type nuraghes, can still be distinguished.
descriptions.NUR11169: The most well-known nuraghe is undoubtedly the one discovered in the Santa Maria area during excavations carried out beneath the sacristy of the rural chapel; the foundations were uncovered in 1843, and some nuraghe stones are incorporated into the fence wall of the church courtyard. www.aserramanna.it/storia/ www.serramanna.altervista.org/storia.htm
descriptions.NUR5903: Single-tower nuraghe with the tholos still intact
descriptions.NUR6390: Single-tower nuraghe with the tholos partially collapsed inward. Located beside a sheepfold.
descriptions.NUR4593: Single-tower located within the private park of the Sardara Thermal Hotel. It is partially buried and access to it cannot be identified.
descriptions.NUR10048:
Nuraghes that have disappeared completely or almost so, among them is this one, and it is located near Morimenta, not far from the Santu Sciori nuraghe of Pabillonis.

In other records it is mentioned as the remains of a small chapel, but there is little evidence of a church.
descriptions.NUR2716: What remains of a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe dating from a period between the mid-Bronze and recent times. Diameter of about 12 m and height of about 2 m.
descriptions.NUR1858: The nuraghe is located within the territory of Villaputzu; it appears as a subcircular structure, with only a few elements visible due to demolitions carried out to extract ashlar stones for use in the construction of the adjacent church. On the northern side is attached a semicircular structure.
descriptions.NUR5939: This complex nuraghe, with five towers and a curtain wall measuring as many as 450 metres, rises prominently at the eastern edge of the Abbasanta plateau. The general plan of Santa Marra nuraghe is complex and three-lobed, with a concave-convex perimeter, typologically similar to Santu Antine of Torralba and Losa of Abbasanta, but reinterpreted in an original manner.
descriptions.NUR2285: It is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan. The nuraghe stands on a basaltic platform at the summit of Monte S. Antonio, south-west of the country church dedicated to the Santo. The monument rests on the edge of a cliff that forms a natural bastion along the western arc of the tower, gradually declining towards the north-northeast where the structure sits upon a plain.
descriptions.NUR4757: Built of calcareous and marly blocks, the nuraghe features a quadrilobate plan with a central tower and four external towers aligned with the cardinal points... surrounded by an outer curtain wall, and the remains of four additional towers. Inside the complex there is a sacred well.
descriptions.NUR10524: The nuraghe once located near the church's sanctuary has been demolished and leaves no trace of its former presence. Some shaped stones have been incorporated into the church dedicated to Santa Petronilla. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR6155: The nuraghe has a base diameter of 12.60 m and, although partially demolished at the upper levels, retains a height of 8.60 m. Through the southern entrance one enters the corridor, on which a rectangular niche is located to the right and a staircase to the left, still walkable, which led to the upper chamber now destroyed. The corridor leads to a beautiful circular chamber, 4.15 m in diameter, with three niches arranged in a cross pattern opening from it.
descriptions.NUR4776: Near the remains of a church dedicated to the saint after whom it is named stands this nuraghe. Built from basalt blocks using polygonal masonry, it has a residual elevation of about 3 metres. It is surrounded by several thickets that prevent the identification of the entrance.
descriptions.NUR21126: It is possible to assume the location of the nuraghe indicated by Taramelli on the slope of the hill. The nuraghe was already demolished at the time of Taramelli and is no longer visible today. Exact location not established.
descriptions.NUR5802: Two single-tower nuraghes placed at a short distance. The second is about 70 m to the north-east.
descriptions.NUR4537:
The collapses affecting the nuragic monument do not allow the identification of the entrance.  

Even at the upper portion, several collapses are visible, making it impossible to see the internal chamber.  

In this area, some stone courses are observed resting against the rock face.  

On the northern side, adjacent to the central tower and a rocky outcrop, there is a structure with an entrance that appears to belong to a courtyard or a nuragic hut.
descriptions.NUR19463:
Located in the inland area of the town of Porto Torres, the Sant'Elena nuraghe is among the best preserved in the municipal territory.

The monument occupies the top of a low elevation covered by dense vegetation.

The central tower has a diameter of about 12 m and a remaining height of 4 m above the current campagna level.

The masonry work is composed of 13 courses of blocks laid one on top of the other, in white limestone, precisely shaped.
descriptions.NUR1531:
The nuraghe is a single-tower with a subelliptical plan, built from roughly shaped trachyte blocks, in a state of collapse to the south and partially buried, and it is completely surrounded by vegetation.

Only faint traces of the staircase and a niche remain from the central chamber.

On the side facing the valley, a feature that was presumably an opening in the outer wall is visible.
descriptions.NUR14946: Damaged nuraghe, of which only a very small amount remains
descriptions.NUR8539:
The complex consists of a nuraghe and a village of huts. The nuraghe is composed of a central tower surrounded by a bastion with a straight-convex-curvilinear profile, which includes two smaller towers located to the northeast and southwest.

The village, dating to the early Iron Age, extends to the north and east of the nuraghe. The dwellings, with a sub-circular and sub-rectangular plan, are arranged in "isolates" with multiple rooms that generally connect to a central courtyard.
descriptions.NUR1703:
The prehistoric settlement is distributed, adapting to the rocky outcrops, across three natural terraces, the first being linear and the remaining two curvilinear.

These natural formations have been enhanced with large stone bastions composed of large and medium-sized ashlar stones, laid in a very densely packed manner. The proto-nuraghe, consisting of ashlar stones arranged in irregular wall courses and densely packed, conforms to the morphology of the rocks.
descriptions.NUR4187: The nuraghe, consisting of a single circular tower, is not in good state of preservation. The structure was built using medium-sized metarrenary (schist) blocks only roughly shaped. The tholos remains with a maximum diameter of almost five metres and a height of less than two. One reaches the nuraghe via a steep uphill path, set within the Mediterranean scrub.
descriptions.NUR8566: The Sant' Uanni site is located on a hill just a short distance from the village of Dolianova; besides the remains of a multi-lobed nuraghe and the basal part of a church that bears its name, some remains attributable to the Nuragic and Roman periods have been found, suggesting the presence of both a Nuragic and a Roman settlement.
descriptions.NUR2030: The nuraghe is built on several levels. The oldest part is the central tower; an outer bastion then surrounds the central tower and links it to a second tower. The boulders making up this bastion are of considerable size. The only accessible part is a corridor on the second floor of the central tower, with a “donkey-back” or inverted ship’s-keel roof, whose south entrance is topped by a huge lintel with its relieving window.
descriptions.NUR2959: The site is located in a hilly area, in a pasture zone about 100 metres south of the rural church of San Giacomo. Originally built on a granitic outcrop, where it is presumed it would have included some parts. It has a sub-elliptical plan, and only a portion of the base wall remains, with a curved outline.
descriptions.NUR2699: Nuraghe eroded and surrounded by vegetation, of which three or four courses remain.
descriptions.NUR2043: Remains of a nuraghe located near the millenary olive tree of "Sa Tanca Manna"
descriptions.NUR3945: The church is located on the right bank of the Temo River; about several hundred metres east of the village of Bosa (OR). Built in the medieval period, it rests on the foundations of a nuraghe, as most early Christian and early medieval churches do.
descriptions.NUR1002: Built on a hillock overlooking the Riu Filibertu, the San Marco nuraghe has been incorporated into a rural farmhouse; during World War II it housed military structures, marked until the 1970s, now no longer visible.
descriptions.NUR2274:
Traces of a nuraghe and a Nuragic village, along with Roman-era findings.

The monument is located on a granite outcrop in a wooded area, about 1.220 metres to the north-east of the settlement of Lei. Around the nuraghe, especially to the east, traces of a village are discernible, and the ground is scattered with remains of various periods. In 1867, traces of Roman-era constructions were found at a short distance.
descriptions.NUR3811: A rural penetration road runs along the hillside, though one must still climb uphill on foot (no paths or trails are present).
descriptions.NUR4715: The Santu Millanu nuraghe is a single-tower nuraghe surrounded by a four-lobed bastion barely discernible.
descriptions.NUR960: It is a ruined nuraghe of which only little remains.
descriptions.NUR5695: It is a ruined nuraghe of which only little remains.
descriptions.NUR2113: Single-tower nuraghe, preserved for only a few courses.
descriptions.NUR4121: Inside a large enclosure at the site of S. Pietro, adjacent to a colonial farmhouse, only a small portion of the nuraghe remains. The building appears to have been constructed upon the nuraghe. The materials used are large blocks of arenaceous rock. From the ruins come hundreds of fragments of Nuragic pottery, lithic tools, flakes and microliths made of jadeite, as well as remains of food.
descriptions.NUR13544: The tombs of the archaeological complex are located on the southern slope of the hill, from its base almost to the summit, where instead the remains of a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe are found. No nuraghe reported. A wall with a doorway of apparent Nuragic period was reported to the Nurnet editorial office by Mauro Tavella.
descriptions.NUR20136: Complex nuraghe with a central tower and an additional tower connected by a wall. The central chamber is bordered by two niches. Around the nuraghe, traces of a settlement have been found. Archaeological excavations have been carried out. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR4032: Complex nuraghe with walls made of dressed ashlar stones and of similar thickness. Damaged, collapsed, and partially buried.
descriptions.NUR3833: Complex-type nuraghe, presumably of the frontal addition type. The nuraghe shows numerous structural modifications carried out after its initial construction. However, it is possible to discern a main tower to which two secondary towers have been added.
descriptions.NUR4827: The original nuraghe was likely quite tall. Currently, the tholos has collapsed inward. Note the presence of two giants' tombs located close to the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR3872: The IGM lists it as Longu, which instead is located slightly further east, some hundreds of metres away. It is composed of several courses of massive, polygonal stones that impress with their remarkable precision and craftsmanship. It features an opening to the north, with an architrave containing the initial form of an arch. The surrounding area is particularly noteworthy.
descriptions.NUR3383: On the maps of the former Catasto, the nuraghe is called "Mesu 'e Tancas Paulis".
descriptions.NUR3859: The nuraghe is located on the summit of a hilltop, from which the view extends over the surrounding landscape and especially over the valleys below and the Rio Mannu river course. It is situated within a cultivated area dedicated to olive groves.
descriptions.NUR2654: Built on the edge of a trachytic bastion, on the edge of a natural fissure, about a hundred metres north of a giants' tomb located downstream, the monument is a single-tower (single-tower nuraghe) with a staircase and a chamber bordered by three niches. To the west, in the area not naturally protected by the vertical rock cut, the remains of a powerful outer wall are visible, while the rocky profile on which the tower stands also appears reinforced by rowed masonry.
descriptions.NUR12297: Nuraghe completely stripped and immersed in vegetation, never studied
descriptions.NUR3824: Noted as a nuraghe, it appears as a large heap of stones. Very useful for hiking purposes, as it marks the turnaround point when coming from Magola, following the edge of the cliff, before descending along the path beneath the cliffs. Caution with shepherd dogs!
descriptions.NUR5962: Around the monument extends the Nuragic village over a large area, with in particular two huts in good state of preservation. To the south-west there is a pond (Paule – from which the site gets its name) that very likely served as a water reservoir.
descriptions.NUR5672: Single-tower nuraghe in relatively good condition with the tholos intact. It is located at the boundary between two fields and is accessible only through a privately owned plot cultivated as a garden.
descriptions.NUR19207: It could belong to the category of unfinished nuraghes, of which there are many examples between Macomer and Sindia.
descriptions.NUR3832: Single-tower nuraghe completely collapsed. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR5211: "Monte sa Perda" – it is thought there may have been another nuraghe dominating the entire Gulf of Palmas, probably destroyed during the construction of "su forr'e sa cracina" (limestone furnace) located in the immediate vicinity.
descriptions.NUR5298: Possible corridor nuraghe, rectangular in plan, entrance to the south-east, helical staircase on the left leading to the second level now collapsed. Studied by Lamarmora in 1830.
descriptions.NUR10868: Small circular structure, built using Nuragic technique and classifiable as atypical nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR6262:
Proto-nuraghe, corridor type. The structure is built on a solid rocky foundation, controlling the southern bank of the Rio Cispiri. The nuraghe is constructed from polygonal basalt blocks locally sourced, with the base courses being notably large in size.

Visually connected to various nuraghes such as Zenna Uda, Muschiu, and Serra Crastula.
descriptions.NUR19413: Nuraghe completely collapsed, of which only a few traces remain on the surface.
descriptions.NUR16110: Complex nuraghe of mixed and trenched type, with a central tower and two additional towers. The central chamber, slightly elliptical in shape, features two niches and a roof of slabs rather than a tholos, which brings it closer to a proto-nuraghe. Built of granite. The exact location of the nuraghe is not confirmed and is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR813: Destroyed nuraghe and today no longer visible
descriptions.NUR6369: Single-tower nuraghe visible only when the waters of the Cuga basin recede. It is one of the 20 nuraghes in the Cuga valley.
descriptions.NUR14948: Nuraghe almost completely disappeared, named by Prof. S. Ghiani in “La Trexenta Antica”. At the base of the hill there is a large rock with artificial cavities.
descriptions.NUR5490: Hidden from view behind a granitic outcrop, the nuraghe appears partially ruined. On site a menhir is present, from which the settlement and the region likely derive their name. Possible presence of a village.
descriptions.NUR4258: Nuraghe dominating the landing points and the area below the coast. Walls in good condition. Open tholos, probably collapsed.
descriptions.NUR5621: Usanis, located at the top of a rocky spur, was a complex structure composed of two towers.
descriptions.NUR9876: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe with its top missing; in the surrounding area traces of a quarry and a settlement can be seen.
descriptions.NUR4295: The Maletta II nuraghe, located at 264 m a.s.l., is now almost completely destroyed due to continuous agricultural activities that have affected the entire area, one of the most intensively exploited regions of the Sinis agricultural zone, and retains only a very fragmented section of the base row.
descriptions.NUR13096: Nuraghe with village almost completely covered by soil and vegetation. The most visible part has been destroyed by excavations. Surrounded by greenery and numerous streams, other nuraghi such as Sa Dom' e S'Orku are visible from here.
descriptions.NUR2523: Nuraghe no longer visible; a house was built on the site in the early 20th century, now in ruin, using basalt blocks from the original nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR5636: It may be a proto-nuraghe, and it is almost square in plan.
descriptions.NUR5854: The Costa nuraghe, commonly known as Sa Reggia, comprises a complex nuraghe, an adjacent village, and a powerful outer wall. The nuraghe consists of a central tower and a bastion with four secondary towers, containing an inner courtyard. The central tower (14 metres in diameter) is built with polygonal basalt blocks in the lower section and finely worked blocks in the upper section.
descriptions.NUR5968: The S'Argara nuraghe is undoubtedly one of the most important nuraghes in Su Pranu; it is a four-lobed nuraghe, with four towers at the corners of the quadrangular bastion and an internal courtyard facing the central tower. From its summit, on days when the sky is clear, one can overlook almost the entire western coast of Sardinia, from Capo Caccia to Capo Pecora in the Sulcis.
descriptions.NUR2164: Fortification or nuraghe also called Staderis or Giolza. It lies in the Montiferru, near the summit of a high spur of bare, rugged rock facing Monte Urtigu, where the remains of an imposing megalithic wall survive with seven courses of roughly dressed basalt boulders. The straight line of the ruin suggests an original quadrangular defensive structure around the level top of the rock, rather than the wall face of a hilltop nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR2076: Nuraghe in very poor condition and hidden by thick undergrowth
descriptions.NUR2078: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe, embedded within the dense vegetation.
descriptions.NUR2077: Single-tower nuraghe, the few remaining fragments are covered by dense vegetation.
descriptions.NUR6332: In good conservation conditions it is possible to visit it, although access to the upper level is not possible due to the collapse of the stairs.
descriptions.NUR5117: Discovered by the great cartographer A. Lamarmora in 1840. It is covered in dense mastic vegetation, has collapsed inwards and filled with earth over time. The stones used for the construction are white with yellow patches of dry moss. The surviving height of the tower exposed to the north is about three metres. If visited in summer, the desert-like landscape of the area adds to the fascination of this imposing megalithic monument.
descriptions.NUR5174: It is largely buried. This allows the identification of a central tower, with an irregularly circular perimeter, featuring a central chamber that is itself circular. Along the external perimeter of the monument, there are traces of walls that suggest the presence of more complex articulations, and for example to the east-northeast, terracing might be hypothesised, if not the presence of huts or enclosures.
descriptions.NUR10436: The nuraghe is located in an area where, for a long time, an Ozieri culture settlement (4th millennium BC) and a lithic cist tomb of Campaniform-Bonnanaro type (late III–early II millennium BC) have been known. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR6203: Near the village of San Salvatore, within a private property, the nuraghe is in very poor condition, but the remains of a significant Nuragic settlement are clearly visible.
descriptions.NUR2216: Only a few remains of the nuraghe are left.
descriptions.NUR2902:
We approach the south-east wall from the inner face of the nuraghe, past the "guardian niche" on the right and the start of the helical staircase on the left.

These two chambers are inaccessible as the interior has completely collapsed and is filled with ashlars. However, the outline of their layout remains clearly visible, with the upper part of the staircase emerging above the access chamber and completing a full circuit around the tower.
descriptions.NUR2720: Single-tower tholos nuraghe built from local basalt blocks, its outer wall face is preserved for about 4 to 5 courses, with a maximum remaining height of about 2.50 m. The interior of the nuraghe is completely filled with collapsed debris. The structure must have been of considerable size (diameter exceeding 13 m) with multiple superimposed chambers. Currently it is situated adjacent to a contemporary building constructed from cement blocks.
descriptions.NUR5616: It is also known as Sas Coas, from the name of the adjacent terrain near Sas Baddes. It is a single-tower nuraghe with its tholos collapsed, exposing the interior of the central chamber with its three canonical niches. There are some features not found in other nuraghes that make it unique.
descriptions.NUR11145: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe at the top of a hill, with only a few stone rows preserved. From this nuraghe, the Nuraghe su Stiddiu, the Nuraghe su Bobboi, and the hill where the Nuraghe di Crabili Simoni stood are clearly visible, along with the megalithic altar at its base. A few hundred metres from the nuraghe lies the Mitza Aramu spring.
descriptions.NUR1921: Located about 300 metres to the northeast of the Nuraghe Su Figu and less than 600 metres to the southeast of the Nuraghe Columbos, the monument is a single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan, having a maximum remaining height of 3.65 m and five courses. The entrance, facing south-east and rectangular in shape, is raised by 0.40 m above the surrounding terrain, supported by a threshold slab, and is topped by a finely finished lintel resting on piers that differ from the rest of the masonry due to their better-cut stones.
descriptions.NUR4015: Of the monument, the wall structures related to the central tower, plus other towers, and possibly one more, are clearly visible. The outer wall, equipped with an entrance lintel, is clearly visible. The mastio retains a structure of as many as seven courses.
descriptions.NUR3799: On the calcareous table at the north-eastern edge of the Sas Cudinas, a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe rises, composed of roughly squared stones, with only a few basal circles remaining. It dominates the entire valley of the Iscanneddu river in the Mamucada plain and the fertile Orria Pitzinna. mu
descriptions.NUR3211: Damaged nuraghe, of which only a few courses remain
descriptions.NUR3204: It retains the tholos intact except for the closure slab.
descriptions.NUR1226: It is a nuraghe with a square chamber that remains unfinished, as only the base has been constructed, and an architrave has been placed at the entrance. Interesting because around it, stones are already ready for use on the nuraghe, making it valuable for understanding the construction techniques employed.
descriptions.NUR1819: location of the remains of the nuraghe Antoni Letzesa sea
descriptions.NUR11237: A few white limestone stones forming the basal perimeter. Only the entrance and a little else are visible, all set within a dense thicket of fetid anagiride (sa giolva). The name should derive from the local topographic term. Pastoralists believe that the leaves of this plant impart a bitter taste to the goats' milk. See Nuraghe sas giòlvas.
descriptions.NUR6192: DIRROCCATO NURAGHE WITH ABOUT FOUR COURSES OUT OF TERRA
descriptions.NUR5389:
It is located within the territory of the comune of Quartu Sant'Elena (CA).

Of exceptional form, the nuraghe is now almost completely destroyed.
descriptions.NUR1499: It may be a nuraghe whose construction was never completed.
descriptions.NUR2572:
Single-tower tholos nuraghe. The structure stands on the summit of a bend of the Rio Cispiri and rests on a solid rocky foundation, partially embedded within the structures, as can be observed on the north-facing side.

The nuraghe is well preserved in the northern and north-eastern sectors, with an external curtain wall constructed from large polygonal basalt blocks, reaching a maximum remaining height of about 12 m; it appears to have collapsed in the southern and western sectors.
descriptions.NUR2611:
Position verified with GPS. The nuraghe is partially collapsed and the entrance is blocked by debris from a collapse.

It still reaches a maximum height of about 8 metres.
descriptions.NUR2577: “Nuraghe Sas Melas, near Monte detto Fruncu Sas Patatas, at the river crossing of Rio Minori. It is the best-preserved nuraghe in the commune; it still has two levels; solid construction, with accessible corridor and lower chamber; used as a shepherd's refuge; the staircase leads to the upper level, which includes a chamber with a domed roof; windows are wider than tall. In the lower chamber, a stone table. On the land of the heirs of Luca Piras, formerly known as Angelo.”
descriptions.NUR5650: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe made of trachyte blocks: only three courses remain, the structure appears destroyed and completely hidden. It is named after the mountain on which it stands, where in remote times there stood a convent for nuns.
descriptions.NUR3822: It is located a short distance from Lake Cuga; as can be seen in the photos, only 2 or 3 courses of stones from the foundation remain, which give a clear idea of the internal layout of this single-tower nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR5956: Single-tower tholos nuraghe. The interpretation is based on the circular plan of the monument, although due to its poor state of conservation and dense vegetation it is not possible to observe any other distinguishing features. The entrance cannot be identified. Many materials from the collapse of the nuraghe have been reused in the construction of modern enclosures attached to the ancient structures.
descriptions.NUR1227: Ruined nuraghe submerged by the floral scrub
descriptions.NUR5121:
The megalithic complex consists of a central body, composed of large stones set in irregular curtain walls; the overall plan is vaguely quadrangular and includes three small circular chambers.

These rooms, enclosed within the wall face (about 2.10 m high) that defines the central body, which has a quadrangular plan, were the subject of extensive excavations carried out at an unknown date by clandestine diggers.
descriptions.NUR8370: The monument, built of limestone, has an internal diameter of about four metres, dimensions relatively small compared to known standards, but not insignificant when considered in relation to the width of the promontory on which it stands, which extends over slightly more than six metres in width and ends at the edge of a cliff.
descriptions.NUR15711:
The nuraghe lies less than 100 metres north-east of Nuraghe Ordari.

The monument is not clearly legible.

The masonry survives on the west side for 3.20 m with four courses of large basalt stones, only roughly dressed and laid in irregular rows.

A better-finished stone, rectangular in shape and measuring 1.90 m long, 0.78 m wide and 0.56 m thick, appears to be the lintel of the entrance, which can no longer be identified in any way.
descriptions.NUR5711: The nuraghe S'Aspru, one of the largest in the Goceano, is in poor condition and partly unstable. It is a complex nuraghe whose central tower stands in the middle of a rectangular courtyard and is enclosed within a circular bastion to which three further towers were later added; these towers are not accessible. Inside the central tower there are three niches and a corridor leading to the staircase that goes up to the upper floor, where a second chamber with a tholos roof is found.
descriptions.NUR15024: The remains of the nuraghe are located inside the Orguglioso Castle.
descriptions.NUR12035: Nuraghe now almost completely destroyed. Only a heap of stones remains.
descriptions.NUR5593: It is located in the territory of the comune of Lodine (NU). Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe reduced to a heap of ruins. It is situated very close to Sos Nuragheddos 1. More details can be found in the book Archeologia in Barbagia by M.A. Mele.
descriptions.NUR2384: Remains on a rocky outcrop from which the valley below is visible.
descriptions.NUR728: The complex nuraghe is completely collapsed and buried. It is likely that the ashlar blocks were removed to build some structure nearby. All around there are traces of a village.
descriptions.NUR6459: Nuraghe named after the locality: "Sa tanca 'e su padru". Of imposing dimensions but completely ruined and not discernible anymore. Until a few years ago it allowed access to the interior.
descriptions.NUR3522: It seems to be one of those nuraghe classified as unfinished.
descriptions.NUR3658: It is in a state of considerable degradation. Covered by moss and shrubbery, it is inaccessible. Constructed of trachyte. From the outside, a small window can be seen, high up, facing east. The walls still standing are about four metres high.
descriptions.NUR14952: Nuraghe completely dismantled according to S. Ghiani in La Trexenta Antica.
descriptions.NUR2962: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe. On the IGM map this nuraghe is mistaken for the nearby nuraghe Molas. Around the nuraghe, traces of a village or settlement are present.
descriptions.NUR5110: Single-tower nuraghe with a small village adjacent.
descriptions.NUR4955: The nuraghe is located on the hill of Cala Francese, in the area “Serra is tres portus”. The nuraghe may originally have been of a complex type, built using limestone blocks. The original tower's outline is preserved only in fragments, its interior being covered by collapse and vegetation.
descriptions.NUR730:
At Sa Turricula the first phase of the Nuragic civilisation is recognised. The site comprises the nuraghe, the village and, a short distance away, two giants' tombs, a well, and the Funtan'e Casu dolmen.

Sa Turricula does not allow an easy reading of the structures. It is choked with vegetation but, once you reach the top of the hill on which it stands, you enjoy a breathtaking view over the whole surrounding territory.

The nuraghe probably belongs to the corridor nuraghe type.

Nearby are
descriptions.NUR16244: It is a place almost inaccessible, visible from a high vantage point, with most of the nuraghes of the Ogliastrina plain. I think it is four-lobed... but it is illegible due to vegetation and rockfalls. The entire structure is hidden among natural rocks and, as a result of collapses, it is not legible. The area is scattered with small terracotta fragments (report by Daniele Murgia, Triei).
descriptions.NUR4948:
Single-tower nuraghe built with squared blocks of andesite, with fairly regular courses, in good state of conservation. The entrance is located to the east, but the chamber is not currently visible due to wall and roof collapses of the monument.

To the south there extends a wall with a straight-curvilinear profile, possibly belonging to a recent sheepfold, now dismantled.
descriptions.NUR1599: Nuraghe that might belong to the category of "uncompleted"
descriptions.NUR8040:
The fortress was built in a strategic location: from its summit on the hilltop, one can see the Campidano plain, the Lina mountain range, and some nuraghes in the territory of Pabillonis. It is of considerable size (covering an area of almost 4,000 square metres) and consists of four towers connected by a curtain wall of rhomboidal shape.

Due to partial collapses of the towers, only one is currently accessible.
descriptions.NUR6092: Single-tower nuraghe with an elliptical plan, the layout of the nuraghe is difficult to read.
descriptions.NUR6075: Single-tower nuraghe with a chamber bordered by three niches, built in basalt. Traces of a settlement.
descriptions.NUR1217: Damaged nuraghe, completely surrounded by vegetation
descriptions.NUR2621: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe situated at an elevation of 250 m a.s.l., it is practically the site that rises the highest above all its "similar" counterparts, probably fulfilling a very important function within its surrounding context because it dominates the Cuga valley, where more than 15 nuraghe are located within just a few square kilometres.
descriptions.NUR5396: The site, besides the nuraghe Iscalas, includes Roman-era and prehistoric menhir structures. The nuraghe, of which only some portions of the walling remain today, had a circular tower constructed with medium and large polygonal stones laid without the use of binding mortar.
descriptions.NUR4415: Built on a high elevation, from which it dominates the surrounding territory, it can be seen by taking the turns of SP 6. It is a single-tower (single-tower nuraghe) with a base diameter of about 10 m, constructed with slabs of slate. Part of the wall to the south has collapsed, and the entrance, also located to the south, is ovoid and provides access to the internal chamber, which lacks the tholos roof; inside, a niche is visible.
descriptions.NUR3816: The quadrilobate nuraghe of S. Caterina is located in the municipality of Osilo, just metres from the ruins of the church of S. Caterina.
descriptions.NUR20367: According to an 19th-century local historical document (Emanuele Atzori), in the centre of Capoterra there stood the remains of a nuraghe (which probably was completely destroyed by the 19th century), and today not a single trace of it remains, not even in memory. In this public document (dated 23 September 1844), a ruined nuraghe is noted to have existed at Sa Gruxi Santa (appearing to be roughly where today's named piazza now stands).
descriptions.NUR3057: Structures related to a complex nuraghe of mixed type, consisting of a proto-nuraghe of corridor type connected to a tholos nuraghe of single-tower type. The complex, overall very imposing, is composed of a large elliptical – slightly quadrangular – building with rounded corners, about 22 m long and 17 m wide, slightly more than, oriented N–S.
descriptions.NUR1901: The complex nuraghe, of which only remains of the central tower and two curtain walls, situated at two different levels, are left. The original tower preserves almost intact its perimeter. The two curtain walls are visible in the northern-eastern section, relative to the central tower; they extend along a curved route of several metres, interrupted from north-east to north-west by a substantial collapse originating from the central tower.
descriptions.NUR636: The nuraghe, likely of a complex structure, is currently covered by dense vegetation and preserves only a few courses of the original structure. Associated with the nuraghe is a circular cyclopean wall with a diameter of about 10 m. The state of conservation is very poor.
descriptions.NUR1830: The nuraghe is located on Monte Perdas de Fogu at an elevation of 230 m. It is a complex nuraghe, of which only the wall face of the central tower remains. To the south-southeast lies a trapezoidal entrance to the monument. There is a narrow passage with an ogival cross-section that leads directly to the chamber of the central tower.
descriptions.NUR16025: The nuraghe is partly collapsed and likely destroyed during the works for the construction of the municipal road.
descriptions.NUR15314: The structural element of the building, with the top of mastio A and some wall profiles emerging for several metres, is basaltic andesite. A thick mass of mastic wraps around the exposed part of the structure, revealing a curved profile of the bastion that, from satellite images, appears at least four-lobed due to the addition of at least two secondary bodies.
descriptions.NUR4667: The nuraghe has been completely levelled for the construction of the Church of Santa Greca. In aerial views, the circular outline at ground level is still clearly visible and likely represented its original foundation.
descriptions.NUR5708: Corridor nuraghe, also known as Runalgalva.
descriptions.NUR4414: The nuraghe, built from basalt blocks, is in fairly good condition. It consists of a central tower and two others attached to it, though the structure of one of them is not discernible due to collapses. Access to the main tower is via an entrance featuring a lintel. Inside the tower, a niche and the remains of a staircase are identifiable. From the nuraghe, one enjoys a magnificent view of Cea Bay.
descriptions.NUR5657: Single-tower nuraghe in good condition near a small agricultural farm
descriptions.NUR5828: From the old road to Sorradile, turning left, about 1 km from the village, near a bend of the Riu Binzas, the remains of a circular nuraghe of about 12 m in diameter can be found: only the base course is visible, composed of large trachytic stones, not yet shaped.
descriptions.NUR5874: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe with its top removed, of which only half the perimeter wall remains, spanning seven courses.
descriptions.NUR5958: It is a nuraghe that is particularly dear to me, not only because it was the site of a discovery of an object that I donated to the Sanna Museum in Sassari, an object that has unfortunately disappeared. I have monitored the nuraghe over the years and reported its imminent collapse. I have visited it inside and believe I am one of the few to have ever known the full extent of its internal equipment.
descriptions.NUR13375: The nuraghe is located in a dominant position above the wide valley of Modolo, in the region of Planargia, in north-eastern Sardinia. The structure, of particular interest and grandeur, is of the corridor type. It has an irregular elliptical plan, crossed longitudinally by a central corridor passage with opposite entrances.
descriptions.NUR5484: The Senis Mannu nuraghe is reached from the Church of San Giovanni after about one kilometre of road. This nuraghe, built at an elevation of 302 m a.s.l., is a megalithic structure featuring a tower constructed thousands of years ago by stacking sedimentary rock blocks. The tholos has collapsed at its centre. From the top of the nuraghe, there is a good view: to the south the tabular profile of the Giara and to the north the Santa Vittoria hill.
descriptions.NUR16861: Not recorded, it is located on private land.
descriptions.NUR15764: From the aerial photograph it appears to be one of those nuraghes belonging to the category of "uncompleted" ones.
descriptions.NUR4324: Complex nuraghe composed of a central mastio and two towers with a courtyard.
descriptions.NUR3080:
It is likely a corridor nuraghe to which, in more recent times, elongated huts and numerous dry stone walls have been added, making its detection particularly difficult.

From this pile of stones, invaded by vegetation, a circular tower (diameter 11–12 m) emerges, with a remaining height of 4 m.

At the top of the structure, short segments of corridor are discernible, though it is not possible to define the full layout due to collapse.
descriptions.NUR4366: It is located within a military zone, access to which is forbidden to the public.
descriptions.NUR659: A place of rare beauty. The site, particularly evocative, includes a complex nuraghe with an attached village, a cave with two entrances, two giants' tombs, and two single-tower nuraghes.
descriptions.NUR4346: Nuraghe almost completely destroyed, of which only a single course remains visible. Almost entirely covered by the collapse and vegetation, its plan cannot be established.
descriptions.NUR6256: Single-tower nuraghe in excellent condition, with its tholos intact. Surrounding traces of other towers and huts are visible.
