descriptions.NUR3588: Single-tower nuraghe reduced to ruins. Only a single circular wall section remains, about 4 metres high and featuring seven courses. The monument is almost completely destroyed, and the materials have been reused for the construction of animal enclosures and sheepfolds in recent times.
descriptions.NUR1285: We are confronted with only a few basal circular elements of the construction, consisting of stones arranged in courses, some of which have been broken and affected by collapses. Several interesting construction features further highlight the local expertise of those who commissioned its building.
descriptions.NUR3011: The nuraghe "Serra de Chigulas" was formerly known as "Su Tangarone" and is mentioned in the book of Canon Spanu. The monument has a complex plan.
descriptions.NUR5301: Some courses of large stones can be seen, together with part of the summit, which includes a blocked access. At 40 metres to the east, the remains of a "sacred" well.
descriptions.NUR537: Nuraghe "a tancato", with a central tower and an additional tower connected by bastions. Traces of a settlement. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR20140: This nuraghe represents a unique case in the Padadese area, as it was built with stones considerably smaller than the average, except for beams and lintels. Its structure suggests it belongs to a proto-nuraghe (1800–1600 BC).
descriptions.NUR3987:
The overall plan of the structure must have been quite irregular and adapted to the natural contours of the rock, which was incorporated over large stretches in the construction.

The remaining structure extends along a north:south axis of 7.35 m and an east:west axis of 0.78 m, and preserves a high point reaching up to 1.90 m above the camp level.
descriptions.NUR6101: USAI (2014, p. 42) includes it within the typology "the 'small nuraghes' probably unfinished".
descriptions.NUR5985: The largest nuraghe in the territory of Illorai, mentioned by Taramelli, G. Lilliu and Angius-Casalis, consists of a central tower probably of two storeys with its tholos still intact; on the south side is the courtyard with the entrance partly collapsed; on the north-east and north-west sides are the two lateral towers (with collapsed tholoi) but their internal walls are in excellent condition. Collapses inwards are minimal, while those outwards are substantial. Contact AGRIS for access to the area.
descriptions.NUR4655: This singular monument, composed of two towers stacked one above the other, rises alone on an extremely high and impressive cliff dominating the vast valley of the Rio "S'Acqua Callenti", right at the junction with the valley of the Flumendosa.
descriptions.NUR4003: Nuraghe of the same name, near the singular monument composed of two superimposed towers, stands alone on an extremely high and impressive cliff dominating the large valley of the Rio "S'Acqua Callenti", right at the junction with the valley of the Flumendosa.
descriptions.NUR6216:
The nuraghe stands on the summit of a high watershed, whose northern and eastern slopes are steep, while to the west, just a few metres from the nuraghe, the hill ends in a high cliff.

It is a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe with a circular plan, having a diameter of 10.30 m. Very little of the nuraghe remains due to significant collapses that have affected it throughout the centuries.

For further details:

Bibliography: E.E.M. 1922, p. 04; MERELLA 1996-97, vol. V, pp. 770–773, fig. 37, tav. XXIII.
descriptions.NUR5312: Remains of nuraghe or nuragic huts
descriptions.NUR5637: Single-tower nuraghe completely collapsed and looted. Only some stones of the outer wall face and the circular base alignment remain; no other elements are detectable.
descriptions.NUR1900: Complex nuraghe composed of a central tower and possibly two other towers. Unfortunately, the original structure is hidden by a conspicuous collapse and the presence of dense vegetation. Adjacent to the central tower, in front-facing position, two possible towers can be glimpsed. To the north-east a rectangular room built in cyclopean masonry is visible, featuring a flat-laid roof.
descriptions.NUR19661: Nuraghe in a very advanced state of collapse, making it difficult to define its structure. To the north-west, some courses are still in their original position, but these do not help in establishing its overall form.
descriptions.NUR5151: Remains of a probable single-tower (single-tower nuraghe)
descriptions.NUR15803: The area of Nuragic and Roman-era lithic fragments at Serra Ona can be defined as east of the nuraghe, in the surrounding fields used for agriculture. These are fragments of small and medium size, dating from the Nuragic and Roman periods, with a medium degree of fluting. They are distributed in an uneven manner and, due to agricultural use, they are especially concentrated in the areas where the plow turns.
descriptions.NUR1888:
The Nuragic complex at Serra Paulis now appears as a ruin, with four wall structures, already identified by Struglia in the 1980s.

Its dominant position over the entire landscape allows for a 360° panoramic view.

The site was probably reused in Roman times as a forge, given the substantial remains of burnt and fire-deformed materials found in situ.
descriptions.NUR3492: A ruined nuraghe, not easily reached, stands on a hill at as much as 982 m above sea level. The Serra Pirisi cave is an area that is not particularly extensive, measuring about 1.5 km in length, located in the Su Canale area, in the Supramonte of Baunei. Despite its small size, compared with other areas, it contains a considerable number of cave entrances, among them Lovettecannas, the deepest in Sardinia with a vertical drop of -520 m.
descriptions.NUR2941: Complex nuraghe, apparently four-lobed with the tholos of the central tower intact
descriptions.NUR6111:
It appears as a large heap of rubble covered by dense shrub vegetation that in no way allows the ground plan of the monument to be read.

The surrounding ground is strewn, over a wide area, with the remains of the Nuragic settlement, which was also reused in Roman times, as shown by the potsherds scattered on the ground and several cippi.

The nuraghe was defended by an outer wall that still survives for about sixty metres in length and to a height of about 1/1.50 m.
descriptions.NUR2604: The monument, partly hidden by dense vegetation, is of corridor type with an elliptical plan, built with granite stones of medium and large dimensions and survives to a maximum height of 4 m on the northern side.
descriptions.NUR1907: Very little information is available about the Serra Su Parone nuraghe, as the nuraghe has been almost entirely dismantled. Possibly a single-tower nuraghe, only faint traces remain, with the tower's curtain wall preserved in fragmented sections, consisting of two courses of trachyte stones. The state of conservation is very poor.
descriptions.NUR3682:
Of the nuraghe only a few base courses remain, with a maximum height of about 2 m, composed of large polygonal basaltic blocks arranged in a circular pattern.

The internal chamber is completely blocked by debris from collapse and covered by a thick layer of vegetation, including brambles and shrubs. The entrance, now invisible, was oriented to the south.
descriptions.NUR3445: Structures related to single-tower tholos nuraghes. The building stands on a modest elevation in a dominant position over the surrounding plain. Three to four courses of the external curtain wall, constructed from locally sourced polygonal basalt blocks, are visible, while the internal chamber is destroyed and not observable. The maximum remaining height is about 2 m.
descriptions.NUR5970: Among the numerous nuraghes in the region, Serrese is particularly notable for having the tholos in good state of preservation.
descriptions.NUR6689: The nuraghe is four-lobed, that is, it consists of a central mastio surrounded by five towers, some of which are in good state of preservation. The towers have their tops collapsed; originally, the summits of the towers were to be crowned with stone parapets, which have since been recovered at the bases of the structures during the most recent archaeological excavations carried out on the site.
descriptions.NUR3076: Nuraghe with staircase in good state of conservation.
descriptions.NUR575: Complex nuraghe with a central tower and two lateral towers connected by bastions and featuring a courtyard. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR862: The nuraghe is hidden beneath an impenetrable layer of vegetation.
descriptions.NUR5775: Complex nuraghe with frontal addition and lateral extension: the added bodies are arranged not only in front, but also laterally relative to the main tower. The smaller towers are two, connected to the main one by curtain walls; in the centre lies the courtyard as an integration space.
descriptions.NUR4999: Of this nuraghe only a small portion remains: the first two courses of the foundation on the northern side, and the upper part of the basaltic ashlar courses arranged in curved lines at the other cardinal points. Clearly, the nuraghe bears no blame. What can be documented is documented.
descriptions.NUR3989: It was a smaller tower (diameter of about 8 m) compared to the Susu nuraghe. It probably served as a watchtower. It was certainly repurposed during the Roman period, as evidenced by terraces, pit tombs, and lithic material found in the area. After the bulldozer operations during reforestation, very few traces remain.
descriptions.NUR4195: Very little or almost nothing remains standing, and it is possible to distinguish a portion of the external curtain wall on the south side, as well as a large number of scattered stones scattered around, derived from collapses. It is classified as a single-tower (single-tower nuraghe) with a circular base of an external diameter of about 11 metres.
descriptions.NUR4280: The nuraghe, built of stone, constructed with square blocks arranged in regular courses and bonded with a layer of ochre clay, consists of a central tower and an adjacent chamber connected to the first by a short curtain wall. On the inner wall face of the tower, several voids are visible, which were likely used to house a wooden subfloor. Adjacent to this nuraghe, at its base, are the huts of the Nuragic village.
descriptions.NUR3425:
The monument is located less than 900 metres south of the Nuraghe Suerzu.

It is a single-tower (single-tower nuraghe) with a circular plan, slightly compressed, with a surviving height of 2.15 m on 4/5 courses of medium and large stones, roughly hewn and laid in irregular courses.

Due to its poor state of conservation, the collapse, and the undergrowth, it is not possible to determine the position of the entrance.
descriptions.NUR5905:
It is a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe with a tholos in trachyte, with some granite elements, having a circular plan of about 11 m in diameter, preserved to a maximum height of 5 m.

The monument features an entrance topped by a lintel, a trapezoidal light corridor with a niche and a staircase opening, plus a central chamber with two opposite niches; however, access is extremely difficult due to collapses.
descriptions.NUR5738: One of many nuraghes, hidden beneath the earth, in the Oschiri area.
descriptions.NUR4841: Nuraghe currently undergoing excavation. It is hypothesised to consist of a central tholos and four surrounding towers, with an inner courtyard. Around it extends a large settlement composed of numerous huts used also in Punic and Roman times, protected by a massive system of walls up to 6 metres thick. Great significance is attributed to the discovery within the settlement of a glass-working workshop. The site is not open to the public.
descriptions.NUR2817:
Located 500 m from the village along the road to Sarule, the circular-plan nuraghe was probably of single-tower type.

Today only the base course, composed of squared trachyte blocks, is visible, and to the north, a portion of the second course.
descriptions.NUR19896: It is in complete state of abandonment, enveloped by vegetation, with some parts buried but mostly collapsed, partly due to the actions of tomb-bearers. Nuraghe with at least two rooms or smaller towers attached to the main tower and an entrance certainly oriented to the South/East. It is mentioned as a nuraghe with a furnace. Visually connected to the nuraghes S'Omu 'e S'Orku, Monte Eghedda, and Brandanu.
descriptions.NUR5540: Of the nuraghe tower only very little remains. The lintel and three courses. Around the ruins of a small village.
descriptions.NUR4238: Together with the nuraghe Cabonu, it lies at the border between the territories of Ussaramanna and Turri.
descriptions.NUR8195: Nuragic structures are difficult to read as they are either stripped or covered by more recent construction phases at Medau Canè. The site was inhabited during the Bronze Age, in the Nuragic culture.
descriptions.NUR3242:
Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe in the basaltic upland of 'Su Gollei', in the area of S' Iscampiatorju. It is a perfect tholos. The south-facing entrance, with a staircase on the left and a 'garitta' on the right, leads to the central chamber.

Traces of a first semi-lunar outer wall are present to the east, attached directly to the nuraghe; moving further east, a second outer wall surrounds the Nuragic village.
descriptions.NUR6327: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe with giants' tomb nearby
descriptions.NUR3657:
At present a circular tower (diam. 1.50–2 metres) can be seen at the centre of an irregularly quadrangular fortified bastion that follows the rocky contour of the hill.

The entrance to the bastion, on the south-east, has a rectangular opening (width 0.80 m – height 1.05 m above the fill) and is topped by a massive lintel. This doorway leads into a short corridor (depth 2.50 m – height 2.05 m – max. width 1.75 m) that turns left and then stops where it has collapsed.
descriptions.NUR19549: Three courses of roughly dressed limestone blocks survive. The stair opening and perhaps the chamber roof are visible on the summit. The south-east side of the entrance has collapsed. Military structures lean against the north and north-east sides. Partly enveloped in Mediterranean scrub, the nuraghe is in a good state of preservation. It is a single-tower nuraghe, originally accompanied by a village. Structures currently reused are also reported in the immediate vicinity.
descriptions.NUR988: On a hill composed of a central tower and a bastion, featuring a large village hidden almost entirely by dense vegetation. Two large huts remain, one identified as the 'meeting hut', and at least four others are visible in the undergrowth.
descriptions.NUR4574: The Sisini nuraghe stands on the summit of a hillock in the countryside at the entrance to the homonymous hamlet. It is characterized by an original and rare plan, which reinterprets the model of temple with a well. Indeed, it consists of a circular tower preceded by a massive bastion of square form.
descriptions.NUR6427:
Impressive four-lobed nuraghe with two towers partially collapsed, but with the main tower in good condition, although largely buried. It was intended to serve as a defensive structure for the nearby village, with the Pettu 'e Murtas nuraghe, just 200 metres away by air distance, and as a watchtower over the valley below, Badde.

For further details:
descriptions.NUR634: Located about one hundred metres north of Rio Merchis and less than 300 metres west of the proto-nuraghe known locally as “Nuraghe Magossula”, the monument is a single-tower (single-tower nuraghe) with a circular plan (diam. 13.70 x 11.70 m) that remains standing to a maximum height of 2.00 m, with 4 courses to the north; to the south-west there is only one course, and to the south-east, where the entrance would have been, the wall face is entirely absent.
descriptions.NUR16022: Damaged nuraghe of which it is not possible to indicate the form
descriptions.NUR19581: Single-tower nuraghe with a chamber bordered by at least one niche, built in trachyte.
descriptions.NUR3227: The central tower, almost completely destroyed (maximum remaining height of 2.70 metres), is composed, like the rest of the visible structures, in polygonal masonry with blocks exclusively in granite. On the southern side a trilithic structure remains, which might be interpreted as the remnant of a staircase entrance leading to the terraced space of the tower or to an adjacent secondary chamber.
descriptions.NUR5717: Complex nuraghe with village. Damaged and difficult to read due to being covered by collapsed walls. Occupies an area used for agriculture and pastoralism. Built from granite blocks; only the central tower and the two lateral towers are visible.
descriptions.NUR5027: "Nuraghe s'Omu e s'Orcu", is located near Santa Giusta. The nuraghe fortress consists of a bilobate central tower, characterized by a lateral tower and a second tower situated in the central part of the complex; the towers are circular, with a diameter of about 7.50 m, and are composed of quadrangular and polyhedral ashlar stones of medium and small size, arranged in a tightly packed manner according to regular wall courses.
descriptions.NUR5290: The site is partially eroded. Only the entrance corridor and part of the staircase remain. It is thought that the use of the nuraghe may date back to 1550 and continue until 900 BC.
descriptions.NUR4474: The site stands on a gentle hill at the edge of a plateau where sherds of pottery from various periods abound. We are at 194 metres above sea level and seven other nuraghi are visible all around. The structure is undoubtedly complex: the central part, although damaged, preserves an almost intact niche, a room filled with collapse debris, and some wall remains that suggest further rooms and structures around it. The building material is granite.
descriptions.NUR5730: Characterized by a large Nuragic settlement to which several archaeological excavations have been carried out.
descriptions.NUR6208: The tower, circular in plan (13.20 x 13.50 m at the top) and with an entrance facing south-east, survives to a maximum height of 9.30 m, while the average height remains at 8.50 m. The masonry is composed of carefully worked trachyte blocks arranged in regular horizontal courses with some slight buttresses.
descriptions.NUR5969: The nuraghe apparently composed of three towers; inside, three niches can be seen. On the left, a staircase leads to the upper levels, and surrounding it are the remains of the Nuragic village, with some red stones from the area. To the left of the nuraghe lies a small necropolis.
descriptions.NUR3672: Nuraghe never excavated, almost completely buried
descriptions.NUR3206: Single-tower nuraghe, the entrance is not visible; its diameter is about 9 metres. It belongs to the complex of nuraghes at Su Padru.
descriptions.NUR1007: Single-tower nuraghe in limestone, almost half-covered by vegetation, stands at the edge of a cultivated area within a bend of the Riu Filibertu. State of conservation: good. It is suspected that a village once surrounded it.
descriptions.NUR6044: Remains of the nuraghe Sos Iscaledos, greatly damaged.
descriptions.NUR818: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe belonging to the complex of nuraghi at the site Su Padru. Partially destroyed
descriptions.NUR5808: Among the nuraghes in the Mores area, this one is the best preserved and most intricately structured, thanks to its three towers connected by a bastion. Surrounding it, traces of the ancient village are visible.
descriptions.NUR6141: It is a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe that still has the tholos intact. It almost certainly belongs to the type featuring a subterranean chamber, which is easily detectable. The entrance has collapsed, but access can be gained with care by sliding over the lintel spanning the small chamber.
descriptions.NUR6247: In total ruin, only some of the basal circle stones remain, which help identify its belonging. The stones are of large dimensions and the chamber has collapsed together with numerous debris that have accumulated over time. Fichidindia plants and thorny shrubs have colonized the site.
descriptions.NUR6089: The exact name of the nuraghe (with the mezzanino above the entrance corridor) should be S'Olteri.
descriptions.NUR5382: Nuraghe destroyed by the scolopi fathers in 1730 for the construction of some buildings in Chia. Eighties-era construction further erased all traces.
descriptions.NUR4738: The oldest nuraghe in the territory of Villa Sant'Antonio is the Nuraghe Spei, a corridor nuraghe with a central body composed of an elliptical structure measuring 22 x 7.5 m. On its eastern side, three architraved entrances lead to the internal tholos chambers, which are interconnected by inter-wall passages. On the opposite side, a second, wider elliptical body is attached, also featuring three architraved entrances, now blocked.
descriptions.NUR8749:
It is striking that the monument is not signposted in any way, in an area where, moreover, there is a sign for every sheepfold. The wall looks out over the Boncaminu plain, and from it one can see the village of Lu Brandali and the site towards La Colba.

The wall looks out over the Boncaminu plain, and from it one can see the village of Lu Brandali and the site towards La Colba.
descriptions.NUR2485: Remains of a simple single-tower tholos nuraghe built with basalt blocks from Montiferru. The structures are preserved to a height of 5–6 courses. The nuraghe stands on the summit of a dune that, until the 1950s, was part of the desert of Is Arenas. It has a direct line of sight to the large quadrilobate nuraghe at Tradori, located on the opposite side of the road.
descriptions.NUR3909: Built with polygonal basalt blocks of local origin, only a few courses remain, with a maximum height of just under 2 m. The entrance, trapezoidal in shape and equipped with a monolithic lintel oriented to the south, can be observed. The nuraghe is located near the crossing of the Rio Strampadorzu, where this stream forms a small waterfall.
descriptions.NUR11156: Only a few stones remain, yet they clearly indicate the presence of the structure. Subjected to looting like most sites in our commune, it testifies to the intense anthropization of the landscape. Part of the surrounding area is known by the same name as the nuraghe. m.u
descriptions.NUR2873: The few remaining fragments of the nuraghe have been lost, as a result of land clearing and agricultural improvement works, now covered by brambles and other shrubs, and behind a wire fence. Nevertheless, traces of the monument are still visible through large basal circle stones. mu
descriptions.NUR6066: In this case, too, without concrete evidence of foundations or anything else, we must rely on historical memory passed down orally by those who heard it from their ancestors. Concretely, it must be admitted that during the 1970s and 1980s of the 20th century, numerous land reform and improvement projects took place, involving many sites reduced to heaps of unsorted stones. Probably nuraghe of the scapolo type. See 'Ajanu'.
descriptions.NUR2894: The nuraghe is situated on a modest hilltop, in an area currently used for grazing and crop farming. Its poor state of degradation prevents determination of its type and architectural development. Only a section of the outer perimeter wall remains, forming a semicircle. The stones that compose the walls are granite, roughly shaped and of medium to large dimensions, appearing in irregular courses over the short visible stretch.
descriptions.NUR4808: The area around the Nuraghe Su Angiu is further enriched and distinctive due to the nearby Punic and Roman villages, the remains of which are still visible today.
descriptions.NUR587: Single-tower nuraghe, near which traces of a settlement and a sacred well are found.
descriptions.NUR2501:
Complex nuraghe, of which only some of the curtain walls of the towers and possibly a outer wall remain evident. The collapse and dense vegetation make it difficult to interpret the spatial layout of the complex.

A modest Neolithic village develops to the south-west.

The complex shows interesting superimpositions, including the remains of an old medau with buildings constructed with dry stone walls.
descriptions.NUR6163: Sub-trapezoidal in plan, it rises on a granite outcrop. It is built with large granite blocks arranged in polygonal masonry. The only well-crafted block is the lintel, with a sub-triangular cross-section shaped to deflect the lateral thrusts from the superimposed structures onto the piers. On the more accessible sides, namely west and east, the nuraghe is enclosed by a curtain wall, of which about 17 m of the western side remains preserved.
descriptions.NUR11260: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe partially destroyed at Su Billianu in Uri
descriptions.NUR12817: Of this nuraghe only a small amount remains, just a few large stones arranged in a circular form. Perhaps the first course of stones from the foundation.
descriptions.NUR11150: The shape of this single-tower nuraghe is still clearly visible, although only a few stone blocks have survived.
descriptions.NUR5972: Known locally also by the name of the terrain, "serra porcheddos". It appears to be a single-tower (single-tower nuraghe) although the surrounding area shows a significant and richly documented probability of exploration, with abundant evidence. – Three-legged nuraghe. For other nuraghes whose names refer to objects of use or cult-related items, compare Nuraghe Trìbides, Cogàlzos, Manos d'òro.
descriptions.NUR19714: The nuraghe is easily identifiable as it is located near the reservoirs of the hydro-voro system of the Central Sardinia Irrigation Consortium. On the eastern slope of this hill, large slabs of shale emerge from the ground; however, a more detailed assessment of the site is not possible due to its very poor state of preservation.
descriptions.NUR3067: The nuraghe is now reduced to a heap of massive ashlar stones, though the base circumference is still discernible.
descriptions.NUR6201: The toponym dates back certainly to the medieval period and is due to the fact that the nuraghe rises above the most extreme promontory, directly jutting over the valley below. There are still several circles of stones, variously fallen. The interior can be visited, and the entrance, strictly oriented towards south-south-east, is clearly visible.
descriptions.NUR3365: Nuragic hut. It is circular, built of flat stones of various sizes laid one on another in courses that corbel inwards towards the centre. The wall is conical: about 60 cm wide at the base and about 40 cm wide at the top, with a surviving height of about 130 cm. To the south-east the wall breaks off for about 100 cm (perhaps the entrance) where the structure has collapsed, probably because of wild olive and mastic trees.
descriptions.NUR6381: Nuraghe partially buried with a special lintel, worked and currently broken into two. Nearby is also a dolmen of the same name.
descriptions.NUR5833:
The building is a single-tower nuraghe that retains its chamber, accessible via a corridor with a stair and a niche, and provided with three subsidiary chambers.

The tower is built in its lower courses with large blocks; above these are set smaller boulders, carefully dressed and laid in regular horizontal courses.

Several light openings, triangular or quadrangular, arranged almost in a spiral, are visible on the outer wall face.

A short distance from the nuraghe a domus de janas has been cut.
descriptions.NUR3359: It has a well-preserved tholos and features, at a height of about four metres, two niches that undoubtedly communicated with the staircase leading to the first floor. The boldness of the construction is evident, as the two niches would likely weaken the vaulted structure, which instead appears solid and strong. Part of the first floor, accessible from the outside, is also visible. mu
descriptions.NUR4613: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe incorporated within the Medau Su Conti. In recent times it has been used as a support point for the walling of a dwelling. It is partially stripped of its outer stones but overall retains a good state of preservation. It is the only nuraghe in Carbonia still accessible, although located within a fenced-in area.
descriptions.NUR2545: Something cyclopean stands before something magnificent. The site is known as a nuraghe, but not all the features of the structure are present that could definitively identify it as such. It could be a ceremonial circle. The stones are about 5.00 m long x 0.90 x 0.90. Because the correct curvature of joint between one stone and the other could not be achieved, they were regularly beveled. I believe I have identified the quarry not too far from the site. mu
descriptions.NUR4388:
It is set on a high rocky spur, the shape of which has strongly influenced the overall appearance of the monument; in its remaining portion, it shows a partial internal space with a sub-rectangular plan and rounded corners.

The remaining wall segment of this space measures about 3 m in length and 1.55 m in height.

The rest of the nuraghe is reduced to a large-scale collapse, mainly concentrated on the southern slope.
descriptions.NUR5428: the rock that is visible at the site) and a landslide of medium to small stones
descriptions.NUR5162:
The structure is severely damaged and remains only a circular alignment of large stones set directly on the natural rock, with a maximum diameter estimated at 11 m; it is not possible to determine any further details or planimetric features.

The remaining base course is composed of large, roughly shaped blocks, with dimensions reaching a maximum length of 1.04 m and a height of 0.41 m, down to a minimum of 0.35 m by 0.17 m.
descriptions.NUR3538: Proto-nuraghe of corridor type, with an ellipsoidal–sub-quadrangular plan, built with polygonal basalt blocks. Only a few courses of the base remain, less than 2 m in height. The nuraghe is built upon a solid rocky foundation that emerges and forms an integral part of the structure.
descriptions.NUR6196: It is also known as Matzone (Maxia records Massone). Su crastu covaccadu probably comes from the presence, not far away, of a giants' tomb that had a trilithon and a cist covered with a flat lintel, hence su crastu covaccadu. It is a single-tower nuraghe and its features cannot be made out because it is completely covered by plants and bushes. However, the Nuragic spring that supplied drinking water (so the owners told me) until a few years ago is noted.mu
descriptions.NUR10641: Single-tower nuraghe, whose shape is difficult to determine due to collapses and the dense vegetation present. Nevertheless, the external wall of the central tower can be identified. In the western part of the central tower, a possible infill remains, with partial traces of about two-thirds of the courses still visible.
descriptions.NUR4487: On the main summit of the rocky ridge, beneath the remains of a modern rectangular structure, the ruins of a probable nuraghe are visible, almost unrecognizable.
descriptions.NUR6384: Single-tower nuraghe with access to the collapsed tholos.
descriptions.NUR3266: Significant difficulty discouraged by the ascent. Several abrupt drop-offs. At certain points, walkways and ropes are provided to serve as handholds.
descriptions.NUR4945: Built from squared limestone blocks, it rises for at least six courses and features a well-defined and clearly visible façade even from a distance. It was investigated in the 20th century through unsystematic excavations carried out by the then Honorary Inspector Cornelio Puxeddu. Approximately 25 m to the west of the nuraghe and at a lower elevation, a modern structure of uncertain purpose was constructed, featuring a stone wall cemented and equipped with an iron door and a top lantern.
descriptions.NUR10883: It is an archaic construction of presumably oblong shape extending on a north–south axis for a presumed length of 20 m and a width of 13.40 m. The building is erected entirely on the pre-existing bedrock with a steep slope towards the north. The south façade consists of two courses of large, rough granitic-marl blocks without any dressing, of uneven size and superimposed with an irregular archaic technique without any alignment on horizontal planes...
descriptions.NUR6435: The single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe Su Cuttu is located on the provincial road Alghero Ittiri. It is a single-tower nuraghe that has undergone considerable damage. Only a few stones remain in their original positions. It belongs to the complex of nuraghes in the Cuga valley.
descriptions.NUR3098: Nuraghe belonging to the complex of nuraghes in the Cuga basin. Apparently bilobate, but a third, partially destroyed tower submerged beneath the lake cannot be ruled out. All around the remains of a large Roman settlement are clearly visible.
descriptions.NUR2946: The Su Guzzu nuraghe is a single-tower (single-tower nuraghe) built with calcare blocks and later modifications in basalt. It is located about 7 km south of Paulilatino and, together with the Forreddos, De Mesu, and Codas nuraghes, forms a quadrilateral between the territories of Zerfaliu and Paulilatino. Very interesting is the lintel that provides access to the internal chamber, which features an intact tholos, though unfortunately it is blocked by a large amount of collapsed debris.
descriptions.NUR10511:
Single-tower nuraghe destroyed during the clearing of the field used for cultivation, although traces of ceramic finds are still detectable during reconnaissance.

The site is difficult to read due to the presence of ongoing cultivation; it would therefore be advisable to recover the materials found at the site and document them for a partial reconstruction of the site.
descriptions.NUR15214: Indeterminate nuraghe, only a few courses remain buried within the dense vegetation, which makes it difficult to read the shapes of the structures. In the area, several wall fragments are present, likely belonging to huts. Various ceramic fragments are also found in the region.
descriptions.NUR3220: Someone knows it by the local toponym "runda de suerzones" but also "de sa paghes", as at that site in ancient times two families ended a feud. The monument is in advanced state of degradation. Nevertheless, important features can still be identified that make it a "unique" example in the archaeological landscape as far as I have information. The surrounding area is also noteworthy. mu
descriptions.NUR3936: Corridor nuraghe particularly eroded. The corridor is composed of a flat band with stone slabs. Transversal niches have been carved.
descriptions.NUR19703: Located in the channel between Monte Alibertu and Cammeddare, the nuraghe appears almost destroyed and further data cannot be recorded.
descriptions.NUR3564: A single-tower nuraghe built on a spur of granite rock, following its contours and in places incorporating it. The interior of the nuraghe is filled with backfill earth and large blocks that belonged to the masonry. The nuraghe stands in a commanding position on the coast with a broad view over Tavolara and Capo Ceraso. It is a watchtower of which five courses of stone survive on the outside and about two metres of masonry inside.
descriptions.NUR3871: Single-tower tholos nuraghe. The nuraghe is constructed from polygonal basalt blocks of local origin and remains as a circular arrangement of 2–3 courses, reaching a maximum height of about 2 m. The entrance, featuring a finely worked monolithic lintel, is aligned to the east, just as the stem blocks. Between the internal chamber and the entrance, a passage is discernible, although the upper portion of its roof is missing.
descriptions.NUR6347: The monument stands on the basalt plateau that extends at the southern foot of the Marghine chain, south of the Rio Tossilo. It is a single-tower nuraghe with a niche, a corridor staircase, and a central chamber flanked by two opposing niches. The tower, circular in plan, survives to a height of 2.90 m on the north-west side, with 6 courses, and 2.20 m on the north-east side with 5 courses. The masonry consists of medium and large blocks, carefully worked and laid in regular horizontal courses.
descriptions.NUR2567: Located about 300 metres from the Sas Casas and Columbos nuraghes, respectively to the west and southeast, the monument is a single-tower (single-tower nuraghe) with a niche and a ramped staircase, featuring a central chamber bordered by three niches arranged in a cross. The tower, circular in plan, survives to a maximum height of 4.70 m with 7 courses to the southeast, while the minimum height is recorded to the south with 0.40 m and barely one course; the wall thickness ranges between 4.25 m and 4.75 m.
descriptions.NUR1174: Single tower of irregular shape in basalt and porphyry (Inglese)
descriptions.NUR4138:
It is nevertheless a particularly strong towered structure. This tower is offset with respect to a kind of “curtain” wall, which appears to have been of substantial thickness and is attached to the northern side, while a wall facing composed of large blocks extends over the western sector.

Another external wall is visible from north-west to south-east, almost doubling the perimeter of the tower.
descriptions.NUR5897: The monument, built with polygonal masonry using granite stones, is of the corridor type and has a subcircular plan; the entrance leads through a small flat-laid corridor to a central circular chamber without a roof, which once connected to two other rooms, now inaccessible due to collapses.
descriptions.NUR6029: It is a good example of a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe where the tholos is still intact. Proceeding up the stairs, in clockwise direction, some constructive features similar to those found in other sites in the Chiaramonti area become evident, a distinction that exists today but did not exist three millennia ago, when the territory was merely an adjacent extension of that of Ploaghe. m.u
descriptions.NUR5504: Spends most of the year underwater in the Lake of Cuga. Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe destroyed, only a few courses of the original structure remain visible. During earlier excavations prior to the dam construction, archaeologist Contu discovered here an important nuragic boat.
descriptions.NUR3679: Complex nuraghe, completely buried and destroyed; only three courses of about 1.20 m in height remain of the main structure, with a diameter of about 9/10 metres.
descriptions.NUR568: Poor visibility and the vegetation cover prevent a proper reading of the monument. Part of the east and north sides can be seen, with a wall face built of large polygonal basalt blocks laid in four to five courses to a height of 3–3.50 m. The whole building is buried to a considerable depth, especially on the western side. The inner chamber has collapsed and the surviving part is filled with collapse debris, as can be seen from the top of the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR3232: The tower, almost completely destroyed, can be easily accessed from the inside, where there are three niches; the most intact part of the tower is about 4 metres high. Accessible from the road, it is located about 300 metres away. Around the nuraghe there is a magnificent garden of Indian fig trees.
descriptions.NUR4075:
It stands imposing in the locality of Pauli on a limestone plateau. The monument consists of a central tower almost 7 metres high, against which two further added structures lean, now almost completely collapsed. From the entrance you enter the main chamber, partly covered by collapse debris.

The nuraghe is surrounded by an outer wall and the remains of a village, whose huts are used as goat shelters. A few hundred metres away lie the remains of two giants' tombs.
descriptions.NUR2739:
The S'Ulivera nuraghe is of mixed type, as it features corridor structures, and above it rises a tholos chamber with niches, though partially collapsed.

Around the nuraghe, some remains of what was once a village are still visible; at a short distance, several basalt stones well-cut remain, which likely formed part of a culturally significant building.
descriptions.NUR3166:
It is a single-tower (single-tower nuraghe) in a state of severe deterioration. The term "single-tower" may be inappropriate, as these structures seem to speak and shout like living beings. The story of our ancestors, of a great people who managed to express a culture of peace and solidarity among small pastoral kings united into a single great state. This applies as noted elsewhere to the numerous emergences in the Chiaramonti area.

(foto mario unali)
descriptions.NUR3203: Single-tower nuraghe, attached to a colonial-era farmhouse. Very close to the asphalted road.
descriptions.NUR9750: The Su Mamuccone nuraghe is today completely ruined, standing on a calcare monolith near the homonymous sheepfold, located in a position optimal for having an elevated view of the entire area.
descriptions.NUR12621: Partially destroyed and located near the industrial zone of Portoscuso.
descriptions.NUR6430: It is a complex nuraghe in poor state of conservation.
descriptions.NUR15861: The nuraghe located on a rocky cliff to the west of the Domus de janas is completely hidden by dense vegetation. However, the mastio's course is difficult to identify, though some visible filari suggest its structure was that of a single tower.
descriptions.NUR2812: Simple-type nuraghe, completely ruined, reduced to a heap of rough blocks, about two metres high.
descriptions.NUR5881: It is reported in historical memory of those who worked on the construction of the artificial basin at Madau in the second half of the 1900s. There are no on-site evidences of other types of constructions or foundations.
descriptions.NUR19212: Single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan and a remaining wall face reduced to 2–3 courses.
descriptions.NUR1297: Like the Oes nuraghe, it does not have a traditional tholos roof but one made with wooden substructures.
descriptions.NUR2280:
It is a nuragic structure with courses that rests on the rugged profile of the hilltop, which determines its irregular plan. At the top, a small space filled with debris from collapse is visible: no entrances or other structural elements are discernible.

It must be noted that the construction of a building on this rocky outcrop is difficult to comprehend, and movement on such terrain is extremely hazardous and perilous: more than a defensive structure, it appears to have functioned as a watchtower.
descriptions.NUR17157: In the historical dictionary by Goffredo Casalis, the nuraghe is listed as Sa Corti deis Bacus.
descriptions.NUR8618: Nuraghe/proto-nuraghe characterized by a robust and wide central tower and the remains of two other towers barely visible. The nuraghe is situated on top of a hill, in a natural rocky outcrop from which it offers a magnificent view, allowing the naked eye to easily spot the ruins of the Las Plassa castle... traces of Punic/Roman ceramics suggest the superimposition of multiple civilizations.
descriptions.NUR3542: On a hillock along the provincial road Atzàra-Belvì, blocks of granite, almost entirely buried and arranged in a circular pattern, have been found, which are presumed to belong to a nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR2021: The nuraghe is completely collapsed and only some residual stones remain of the entire structure.
descriptions.NUR736:
Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe.

Located within a private plot, it is partially in good condition.
descriptions.NUR3751:
The monument appears as a large sub-circular enclosure (diameter about 18 m), with a wall thickness of about 2.50–3 m and a maximum remaining height of about 1.50–2 m, featuring two courses.

The masonry is composed of large polygonal blocks arranged in horizontal courses.

From what can be seen, it is most likely a corridor nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR14956: Nuraghe now completely vanished but studied by Silvestro Ghiani in the 1940s. S. Ghiani in “La Trexenta Antica.”
descriptions.NUR6095: Complex nuraghe, the architecture cannot be determined due to the poor state of the structure.
descriptions.NUR4102: The Su Nuraxi nuraghe of Gonnosfina is located about 400 metres east of the village, near the industrial area. It is a single-tower nuraghe, largely destroyed and covered by its own debris and vegetation. Only a few courses remain.
descriptions.NUR4591:
Single-tower nuraghe known today as "Su Nuraxi", while in the past it was better known as "Cocconi".

It is suspected that a second tower once existed. A particular feature is that within the central tower a Byzantine funerary complex has been revealed: a sacred use that evidently has never been abandoned. Indeed, another known name for this structure for a long time was "Sa Parrocchia".
descriptions.NUR11472: Remains of the Nuraghe Su Oi. Currently only the base course remains.
descriptions.NUR5439: Very eroded nuraghe with a tholos and collapsed walls
descriptions.NUR3471: The nuraghe, located on a pastoral area atop a granitic outcrop, is irrevocably ruined. Its entrance, marked by a lintel, can still be observed, within which debris from the collapse remains. As for the chamber, due to the collapse that has affected the entire structure, only a short section can be identified on the northern side.
descriptions.NUR15225:
Popular memory reports the existence of a complex nuraghe beneath the Forte Su Pisu.

In the regional reconstruction of the Sulky Fenicia, a Nuragic village is reported situated at the top of the dominant hill, overlooking the port and the ancient city.
descriptions.NUR2308: Proto-nuraghe of sub-triangular form, built of basalt. It is located a short distance from n.ghe Su Pranu in the westward direction.
descriptions.NUR6045: It is in a state of ruin quite advanced, yet the monument retains some features that make it a particularly notable construction. Indeed, in our territory there are a few other nuraghe with an opening to the north. "Nuraghe del Gallo" or "di Pullo", a Latin name. In popular belief, the gallo represents an apotropaic image of the devil.
descriptions.NUR5505: Almost nothing of the tower remains.
descriptions.NUR9246: Proto-nuraghe with multiple towers, almost completely destroyed. With its height it dominates the entire area of "Su Padru". The name derives from the fact that the nuraghe is situated on a very sharp hilltop, from which Punzu Rudu is seen.
descriptions.NUR9630:
It is a single-tower with a circular plan (diameter 9.60 m) reduced to a heap of ruins. The wall face, composed of medium-sized stones laid in horizontal courses, survives to a maximum height of 2.20 m with 3 to 4 courses.

Due to the collapse, the internal structure of the monument cannot be known.
descriptions.NUR5522: Complex nuraghe consisting of a central tower and four lateral towers, enclosed within a large outer wall featuring ten towers, for a total of at least 15 towers. Of the nuraghe, seven of the outer wall towers are visible, while the others are buried beneath the soil layer. In recent excavations, structures related to the complex nuraghe have been identified, including two of the lateral towers.
descriptions.NUR18066: Nuraghe with a sub-rectangular plan (13.40 m long along the NS axis and 10.60 m wide along the EO axis), characterized by straight long sides and convex short sides. The nuraghe is completely destroyed and practically illegible. It is located in the territory of the comune of Ittiri.
descriptions.NUR3954: Destroyed nuraghe and no longer visible
descriptions.NUR2060: The nuraghe is completely ruined, reduced to a heap of stones about two metres high. Inaccessible due to the dense vegetation present. Complex structure with a settlement from the Bronze Age and remains of Punic-Roman houses.
descriptions.NUR5712:
The nuraghe stands on the edge of the Corte plain, south-west of the town. You follow the Nuoro–Orani farm track and stop at the little bridge that crosses the Rio Su Saju.

On the left, about 200 metres away (near the shepherd's hut), lies the nuraghe. The site occupies a dominant position over what was a possible access route to the Corte plain and made use of the water from the nearby stream, which in ancient times was much more abundant.

Altitude 510 m a.s.l.
descriptions.NUR5158: We find it listed in the map of the 1844 State General Census, as Nuraghe Numassi.
descriptions.NUR4916: The nuraghe, built with blocks arranged in courses of different shapes and sizes, is a complex type characterised by the fusion of the central tower, originally single, with six successive buildings connected by curtain walls that surround it.
descriptions.NUR14921: Nuraghe. It is located on top of a hill near a pond, adjacent to a building. Covered with stones and vegetation.
descriptions.NUR2869: Nuraghe built into a stone masonry and tholos structure between emergent rocky masses.
descriptions.NUR4813: It is possible that the natural terrace had some chambers at higher levels, integrating natural cavities, which were later demolished. The nuraghe rises over the present-day village of Morgongiori, guarding the valley. For this reason, it is reasonable to attribute to it the function of territorial control and visual connectivity with the adjacent basaltic bastion of Funducarongiu, where the cave of Scaba 'e Cresia opens, the subject of this study.
descriptions.NUR1823: Complex nuraghe, probably of the "tancato" type with courtyard and an added tower, built of limestone. Most of the magnificent wall faces of the main tower remain intact. Internally, on the SSE side, a trapezoidal lintel opening is visible, preceded by a passage whose outline is interrupted due to the collapse of the structures. Clear signs of clandestine tampering are evident.
descriptions.NUR6309: Complex nuraghe with a unique plan. Known in the IGM incorrectly as "Giaga 'e Puliga" (which is the name of a nearby nuraghe).
descriptions.NUR16020: Single-tower with tholos, built in basalt
descriptions.NUR3941: Nuraghe on an acrocoro from which the Coros is seen. Single-tower, built with local limestone ashlar, its tholos has collapsed inward.
descriptions.NUR3314: Single-tower nuraghe belonging to the complex of nuraghi at the site Su Padru. Currently very modified.
descriptions.NUR5388:
The construction, although appearing very crude, is fragmentary and reduced to as many as three courses of base in the best-preserved sections.

Other ruins and wall alignments can be observed as one moves deeper into the dense vegetation from the road.

In general, a very rough building technique is evident, using large granitic blocks only roughly shaped into elongated parallelepipeds, arranged in irregular courses that, at present, are highly disjoined.
descriptions.NUR4249: Complex nuraghe with three towers, probably added. Calcare ashlar. Nearby are the remains of a village and two giants' tombs.
descriptions.NUR4250: The Bruncu Mannu Nuraghe at Villa Sant'Antonio is located on a hill at a short distance from SP 37. At first glance it appears to be a single-tower nuraghe whose top is missing and overgrown with the foliage of various shrubs. Along the perimeter, the entrance can be identified, surmounted by an interesting lintel. The interior is cluttered with debris from collapse.
descriptions.NUR1175: Complex nuraghe with a central single-tower nuraghe and a quadrangular perimeter wall with four towers.
descriptions.NUR5466: Complex nuraghe, only a few remains of the central tower and bastions are left; the structure was demolished to build the nearby state road. Many Roman and high-medieval artifacts testify to the continued use of the monument during these periods.
descriptions.NUR2947: The monument, of simple type, is located at the edge of a short clearing, on a granitic outcrop that extends over large parts, within the walls. Its external plan is roughly elliptical, with an architraved entrance leading into a corridor about 3.50 m long; to the left of this, another architraved access leads to a presumed staircase, or at least to a raised floor level that in antiquity must have led to a terraced space.
descriptions.NUR5872: Single-tower nuraghe with a tholos, unfortunately in advanced state of degradation, protected by a large outer wall with a deep underlying drop, of which today only a fortress remains inaccessible.
descriptions.NUR2583: With the filling of the artificial basin at Oliai, it is found on the summit of a small island.
descriptions.NUR3311: The complex consists of a proto-nuraghe, a village, and a giants' tomb. The proto-nuraghe, of the "corridor" type, has a roughly elliptical plan and is built against a granitic outcrop. The masonry is composed of large polygonal granite blocks.
descriptions.NUR12182: Inside there is a flat-laid corridor, a semicircular niche, a staircase leading to the upper level, and a central chamber; originally vaulted in tholos form but now without a roof, it has the classic circular plan with three niches arranged in a cross. The external wall, up to 4 m high, is composed of medium to large trachyte stones.
descriptions.NUR18933:
The monument, a complex structure, consists of a central tower and a bilobate bastion.

Access to the central tower is via an entrance with a lintel. The bastion likely enclosed two towers, one to the east and one to the south-west.
descriptions.NUR3593: It is located within the municipality of Nuoro. It is not the only Nuragic site in the city, but it is the only one that has been systematically excavated. Around the nuraghe, remains of a village dating to about 1600 BC (early phase of the Nuragic period) are visible, originally composed of more than 200 huts. Historical records nevertheless indicate the presence, along the hillside, of some domus de janas.
descriptions.NUR3803: Nuraghe site located just a few metres from the cliff formed by the Rio Carrabusu. The state of conservation is precarious and the structure is partially buried.
descriptions.NUR4923: More precisely, it is a proto-nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR17939: Within a farm, it is in good conservation condition and access is possible from the top.
descriptions.NUR3926: Structures that are hard to read because of the dense vegetation, probably belonging to an archaic corridor nuraghe. A few blocks of the upper part can just be made out among the vegetation. The plan appears vaguely elliptical, with a straight section facing south, in which a doorway with a monolithic lintel opens onto a flat-roofed corridor about 4 m deep. The nuraghe is built of polygonal blocks of local basalt. A
descriptions.NUR2719:
Single-tower tholos nuraghe built of polygonal basaltic blocks.

The structure is completely covered by brambles and climbing vegetation, such that only parts of the external wall face can be observed. From above, the filling of collapsed materials inside the chamber can be seen. Modern and contemporary structures, enclosures and storage facilities, are attached to the nuraghe on the west side.
descriptions.NUR11484: Complex nuraghe with settlement, village. If this designation is incorrect, it might refer to a nuraghe without a name, listed as number 480 by van Dommelen. The nuraghe is not marked on the IGM map.
descriptions.NUR6367: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe eroded and enveloped by vegetation. Five courses of the wall remain.
descriptions.NUR4647: Currently, in the site we can observe an old stone enclosure, below which several stones belonging to the nuraghe are visible.
descriptions.NUR3013:
The site is located on the summit of a steep hilltop, whose lands, partially covered by a dense forest, are used for sheep grazing. The simple-type nuraghe has suffered a collapse on the eastern side, obscuring the entrance.  

It remains standing to a maximum height of 5.50 m and a minimum of 1 m, with wall facings constructed from granite blocks arranged in irregular courses.
descriptions.NUR3809:
Reduced to a state of complete ruin, likely due to road excavation works and land improvement projects. It is confused with the one slightly farther away at Pedru Canu.

Nuraghe of the smilace (Smilax aspera). It is very likely a paleo-Sardinian term. It indicates that at the time the name was first used, the monument was covered with smilace, a thorny climbing plant.
descriptions.NUR5620: The nuraghe Thorra, similarly to the nuraghe Sas Melas, stands on a low hill rising at the valley floor, surrounded by higher elevations; from its position, it overlooks a significant river crossing along the course of the Rio Torra, a tributary of the Rio Mannu. At a distance of 300 metres to the west, there is a giants' tomb of the same name, listed by Taramelli, who strangely omits any mention of the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR2543: The nuraghe is a complex structure consisting of a central tower to which a bastion has been attached, the bastion featuring three secondary towers connected by a curtain wall with a concave-convex profile: two towers are positioned on the front, the third is offset to the south (towards N). The bastion has a curved eastern face (height 5.00 m), at its centre where the entrance opens (width 1.10 m; height 1.60 m), today partially blocked.
descriptions.NUR1241: Nuraghe situated atop a mass of granite dominating the Gulf of Arzachena Cannigione
descriptions.NUR5739: Reduced to a great ruin, it still shows some constructive features of that period. Clear traces of the foundations and part of the masonry apparatus remain. Land improvement works have significantly contributed to its disappearance through the piling up of stones.
descriptions.NUR3614: The Tinteriè nuraghe appears to be a single-tower nuraghe with very irregular masonry. It has a circular plan with a diameter of 12 m and retains its entrance, which leads into a curved passage 4.50 m long, covered by a flat lintel. On the left side of the passage is the space for the staircase, while the interior is blocked by rockfalls.
descriptions.NUR5589: Four-lobed, rock-cut. The upper and lower chambers are visible through a breach in the upper surface layer. Surrounding them, traces of the settlement are visible.
descriptions.NUR9808:
The remains of this nuraghe are located on a trachytic outcrop guarding the Rio Tossilo, near the curve that the Birori–Cobercada road follows at the level of the Urighe nuraghe.

Unfortunately, only a few large stones are left, arranged in scattered patches, in just a few sections, in double rows. Any surveying is not possible.
descriptions.NUR2775:
Reduced to a level of ruin, only some circles of roughly shaped and disordered stones remain scattered in the courses. The remains poorly show the original construction features, despite some courses still being arranged in order.

Info: www.archeologosardos.it

Nuraghe of the site of Ginestroni, in Logudorese Tiria. See Tiriàles.
descriptions.NUR6063: The “Tittiriola” at Bolotana is a single-tower nuraghe built of basalt blocks, bounded by an outer wall and set within a village whose traces are still appreciable. It has an internal stair chamber that is currently impassable because of collapses, and on the upper part, corresponding to the entrance, a large window surmounted by a lintel is clearly visible. Near the structure a sacred well is visible that appears to have been covered over in relatively recent times.
descriptions.NUR5855: It is located within the territory of the comune of Pozzomaggiore (SS). Partially destroyed, about 2 metres high, covered with debris.
descriptions.NUR5820: Of the monument, in very poor condition, only some fragments of the first base course are visible, in pink trachyte.
descriptions.NUR3042: Single-tower nuraghe on top of a basalt outcrop, a natural fortress. Inside, a shelter for shepherds was built. Today it is abandoned.
descriptions.NUR5577: The Tolinu nuraghe, located in a fine position on a plateau overlooking the Tirso valley, is an imposing complex nuraghe consisting of a large central mastio with a truncated conical shape, surrounded by a bastion that encloses several smaller towers.
descriptions.NUR3283:
Complex nuraghe considerably buried.

The central tower, which retains intact the tholos, reaches a height of about 10 metres on the northern side.
descriptions.NUR5669: It preserves the intact tholos covered by a large slab. It is a complex structure with a lintelled entrance and a partially collapsed stairwell. On the left an opening leads to another tower in good condition but with the ashlars fallen from the tholos inside it. To reach the upper floor one must use the side facing north-east, from which to admire the 360° panorama over the village with huts still distinguishable amid dense vegetation and among the various collapses.
descriptions.NUR17857: Only a few traces of the nuraghe remain, as the stones were removed to build a road.
descriptions.NUR6191: The nuraghe is built with blocks of soft trachyte, not very large. The foundations rest directly on the rock, which also forms a natural bastion later refined and completed by the nuraghe builders, who added large blocks. Nearby, the base of a nuragic hut is visible. Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe with village and outer wall, possibly with seven towers.
descriptions.NUR3041:
The monument is located less than 200 metres to the south-east of the giants' tomb at Santu Bainzu, which would have formed the reference funerary area.

It is a single-tower (single-tower nuraghe), situated at the centre of a large settlement bounded by an outer wall that is only partially discernible. The tower, circular in plan (13.12 m x 2.75 m; diameter at the top 11.90 m), with wall thicknesses of 4.30 m to the east and 3.60 m to the north-west, survives to a maximum height of 7.25 m and 12 courses to the south-east.
descriptions.NUR3237:
The single-tower nuraghe, set within the Mediterranean scrub, is a prehistoric building constructed with dark basaltic stones of fairly regular dimensions.

The internal chamber, accessed through a well-preserved corridor, features two lateral niches and a terrace situated at about eight metres in height, reachable via a staircase ramp.
descriptions.NUR6263: The Tradori Nuraghe is built of black basalt. The entrance features a pointed arch and is very low. The chamber, from which two low corridors extend, is circular with a high, intact pseudo-hipped (tholos) vault. Outside the nuraghe, a section of curtain wall composed of large stones is present, and on the external face—oriented towards south-east—a tunnel opens, descending deeply and apparently reaching beneath the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR4963:
In the territory of Gonnosnò there is the nuraghe Tramatza, which, together with the Emmauru nuraghe, watched over the course of the Rio Figu, a winding watercourse between the hills at the foot of the plateau.

Only faint traces of the nuraghe remain; the original structure, a single-tower nuraghe, had a truncated conical shape, built by stacking stone blocks, and housed a main chamber connected externally by a narrow corridor.
descriptions.NUR4880: Embedded within the vegetation of this nuraghe, only a few courses remain. It has never been excavated or studied.
descriptions.NUR5218: It is a complex, three-lobed nuraghe, featuring a central tower, three peripheral towers arranged in a triangle connected by curtain walls with a straight-curvilinear profile, and an internal courtyard with an entrance facing south-east. Finds of incense-burners with female heads, draped figures, and anatomical votives indicate a probable cult dedicated to the goddess Demetra.
descriptions.NUR620:
Nuraghe composed of two towers and a courtyard on the southern slope. Built with large, roughly shaped blocks of red trachyte. From the nuraghe a double-walled megalithic curtain wall extends to the south, with about 35 m of the base courses still remaining. To the north, and partially to the east and south, extends a village of huts, with various circular foundations still visible.  

A few metres to the west of the nuraghe lies a well now completely blocked by rockfalls.
descriptions.NUR6059: Likely a three-lobed nuraghe, if not even four-lobed; the planimetry is almost impossible to read due to the poor state of preservation.
descriptions.NUR2546: The name would suggest a possible three-lobed structure, almost entirely destroyed, of considerable dimensions. Above the main tower there is an entrance covered by bushes.
descriptions.NUR3046:
The site appears as an artificial hill, at its base where debris from the excavations that affected the surrounding lands has been accumulated.

The severe state of ruin, the burial of parts of the structure, and the rubble that partially covers it prevent a clear planimetric reading of the building, which, nevertheless, must have been grand and complex, as suggested by the very name given to it—Tresnuraghes.
descriptions.NUR1344: It is located within the municipal territory of Nuoro. The area is known as Intranuraches because, on three rocky outcrops, three powerful nuraghes are present. Unfortunately, the nuraghe is in poor conservation conditions and appears more as a fortification, built fully exploiting the granitic outcrop.
descriptions.NUR2323: Covered with stones gathered from a collapse.
descriptions.NUR3484: Unfortunately, the nuraghe is covered by vegetation. It is believed to have a well-preserved tholos.
descriptions.NUR17385: Single-tower nuraghe with a circular plan, of which only a single row of calcareous blocks remains, arranged in a curved line, about 4 metres long. In the north-northeast direction, a section of wall is visible, composed of blocks laid in a line for a length of about 3.20 metres.
descriptions.NUR3963: It is submerged beneath the waters of Lake Omodeo.
descriptions.NUR3700:
It consists of a few basal circles that nevertheless define its construction character precisely; this character belongs to a broader human context in the surrounding territory with numerous other features close by. Its function as a lookout, or if you prefer as a defensive post, is paramount.

- Nuraghe del mestolo. In the matter of kitchen utensils it is curious that this nuraghe lies about one kilometre as the crow flies from Nuraghe Cogàlzos (see entry) which means "spoons (of bone)". See Truddàriga.mu
descriptions.NUR2754: The possible staircase is visible. The tholos has collapsed.
descriptions.NUR6102: Quadrilobate nuraghe, the central tower (with a mezzanine) retains intact the tholos roof of the chamber.
descriptions.NUR717: Submerged nuraghe in the basin of the lake on the hillside
descriptions.NUR6365: Damaged nuraghe, with three courses remaining. Likely nuraghe belonging to the category of "uncompleted" nuraghes.
descriptions.NUR5610: It is a tholos nuraghe with an outer wall, located near the village and in a precarious state of conservation.
descriptions.NUR5792:
The Tunis nuraghe is in poor conservation conditions, especially in the central tower and in the southern parts of the quadrilobate bastion; here, the two northern towers with fragments of the three adjacent curtain walls are visible, as well as the eastern boundary wall of the courtyard with the window connected to the direct staircase leading to the parapet.

Around the remains of the bastion, linear walls and parts of circular buildings emerge.
descriptions.NUR5397: The nuraghe of Tuppedili, located along the road to Mandas, is of particular archaeological significance. Still awaiting a complete study, so far excavations have yielded a large number of artifacts datable to the Nuragic and Roman periods.
descriptions.NUR3821: Structure of uncertain interpretation built with local polygonal basalt blocks. The building stands on a small natural rocky outcrop and has an elliptical plan. It measures about 17 m in length and about 11 m in width at its central point. The northern, western, and eastern sections are composed of 1–2 courses of large and medium-sized polygonal blocks, while the southern section has three courses constructed with the same technique.
descriptions.NUR3199: Single-tower nuraghe, with part of the tholos remaining and the access portal restored.
descriptions.NUR6423: It is a single-tower nuraghe with its roof collapsed.
descriptions.NUR5895:
Although the current state is entirely characterized by collapses affecting the entire site, I must admit that it evokes interest and respect for the grandeur of the cyclopean stones, only a few of which remain in situ. The state of devastation is evident.

Nuraghe della Tortorella. mu
descriptions.NUR792: Nuraghe in good condition, built of red granite stones. Equipped with a spiral staircase. Likely part of a complex nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR5409: The Tutturuddu nuraghe is located on the first promontory after the Nuridda nuraghe, guarding a path descending towards the village of Tuili. Of this Nuragic testimony, only faint traces remain. The name Tutturuddu derives from the Sardinian word tutturu (mattarello), referring to the shape recognizable in the remains of the ancient structure.
descriptions.NUR5728: Un ruined nuraghe never studied, of which only a few courses remain. A singular and remarkable stone worked near the proto-nuraghe, above a few rudimentary remains entirely indeterminate, might be interpreted as a fragment of a mound originally shaped and placed above a domus with a façade, or alternatively as a covering element of a giants' tomb.
descriptions.NUR10197: It appears to be a single-tower (single-tower nuraghe). Surveying is difficult due to thorny shrubs that have completely overtaken the structure. Clear traces of nuragic village huts are visible, scattered around the central body within a limited area, not as erroneously reported by others.
descriptions.NUR2097: Nuraghe of uncertain type built on a rocky spur, utilizing its elevations; characterized by a powerful collapse, particularly located to the north-northeast. Situated at 418 m.
descriptions.NUR3600: The Tuvurunaghe nuraghe, built of trachytic stone at the edge of a rocky plateau, features a single-tower layout with a nearly intact tholos roof. It has a "classical" plan: three niches arranged in a cross, and an open spiral staircase to the left of the access corridor, partially blocked by fallen stones. Nearby, circular hut bases are visible, indicating the presence of an inhabited settlement.
descriptions.NUR3239: Single-tower nuraghe, built with local basalt blocks. The external wall face is preserved to a maximum height of about 4 m. The entrance can be identified to the south-east, based on the remains of the passage, with an opening for the staircase on the left and a niche on the right, leading to the internal chamber. This chamber is preserved to about half its original height and features a large internal niche facing south.
descriptions.NUR5624: It is a "corridor nuraghe" located at the centre of a large outer wall within which the ruins of a vast settlement are found. The monument is situated on the basaltic upland extending between the settlements of Dualchi and Borore. About 180 metres to the northeast, the remains of the corresponding giants' tomb are preserved, while to the north-northwest lies the giants' tomb of Putzu Iu.
descriptions.NUR3280: Nearby are also some nuragic huts.
descriptions.NUR2622:
Other towers are attached to the central tower, possibly five in number. The entire structure is hardly discernible due to the presence of dense vegetation and thorny bushes that block access (good thing!). Internally, almost the whole structure can be visited and one appreciates the harmonious development of the powerful and majestic construction.

The word ùi, which probably is paleosardinian, mu
descriptions.NUR6348: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe, with its tholos collapsed and enveloped by vegetation
descriptions.NUR3004: Structures related to proto-nuraghe of the corridor type. The building is constructed from large polygonal basalt blocks of local origin. The plan is roughly quadrangular, though an accurate interpretation of the monument is not possible due to the complete vegetation cover.
descriptions.NUR3861: Single-tower tholos nuraghe built from locally sourced polygonal basalt blocks. Almost completely destroyed, it appears as a heap of basaltic stones. The first two courses of the base are visible on the south side.
descriptions.NUR3736: Single-tower tholos nuraghe, presumably of a single-tower type, although poor conservation conditions and intense vegetation cover prevent a complete reading of the monument. Built with polygonal basalt blocks, the external wall on the west side is preserved to a maximum height of about 3.50 m. The nuraghe has undergone intense clearing operations, as evidenced by the large blocks piled on the northern plain adjacent to it.
descriptions.NUR9159: Through a gap between the large ashlars of the upper part of the outer wall face, one enters the corridor that housed the helical staircase giving access to the upper part of the tower. In fact, the corridor ends against two large lintels that are completely buried. The nuraghe is in very poor condition. It is partly enveloped by mastic shrubs and prickly pears, the cause of the collapses and the burial, up to about two metres from the floor level.
descriptions.NUR2614:
It is a single-tower with a circular plan  

(axis SE-NO 11.75 m; axis East-West 11.50 m) with a thickness of 2.70 m to the north-west and 3.85 m to the west; the maximum remaining height is in the north-west, measuring 3.60 m on 8 courses of basaltic stones, well-worked, of medium and large dimensions, laid in regular horizontal courses.
descriptions.NUR2984: The monument was demolished by a bulldozer. What remains is a spread of ashlar fragments belonging to the wall masonry.
descriptions.NUR3777: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe that features 10 courses of stone still in situ, in porous basalt, is located in the Sorradile area (OR). Its current position is particularly noteworthy, as a result of the construction of the artificial Omodeo reservoir, it now lies along the lake's shores, subject to continuous fluctuations in the lake's water level.
descriptions.NUR4972:
The Urceni nuraghe complex was built at 900 m on the summit of a rocky spur.

A well-preserved architectural monument of great merit for the skilful symbiosis between the built element and the natural element. Several holm oaks grow in the area.

One is faced with a well-preserved architectural monument of great merit for the skilful symbiosis between the built element and the natural element. Several holm oaks grow in the area, partially obscuring the view of it.
descriptions.NUR15924: It is located on the summit of a hill, precisely at the intersection of two watersheds. From this fortunate and strategic position, the nuraghe dominates the entire surrounding plain.
descriptions.NUR2985:
It is a circular single-tower nuraghe (diam. 13 x 13.50 m) with a corridor niche and a provisional chamber of two niches; the existence of a staircase is probable but not certain.

The tower survives to a maximum height of 5.54 m and is built of medium-sized blocks, roughly dressed and laid in horizontal courses that are not always regular.

A corridor 4.25 m long leads into the circular tholos chamber (diam. 4.20 x 4 m), now reduced to a maximum height of just 3.10 m with 7 courses.
descriptions.NUR11587: Of this monument, noted by Lamarmora and other authors, but not by Taramelli, no trace remains. It seems to have been located near the railway and destroyed during the works related to the construction of the Borore railway station.
descriptions.NUR6411: In Florinas, among cultivated fields, we find this small proto-nuraghe known as Urzeghe, "characterized by a corridor-like structure with parallel corridors attached to a small circular tower."
descriptions.NUR2658: Usanis, located at a short distance from Osidda and situated at the top of a rocky spur, was a complex structure composed of two towers.
descriptions.NUR3126: Nuraghe partially collapsed, with a dozen courses still standing, located beside two rural buildings
descriptions.NUR5497: Single-tower nuraghe and traces of a settlement.
descriptions.NUR8747:
At the head of a dominant ridge overlooking the beds of two watercourses that fed the pond behind the harbour, before it was transformed by the present buildings.

Remains of Nuragic towers beside the abandoned house.

There were probably two towers, contiguous, one of them built on a granite outcrop, exactly like all the other Nuragic towers of Santa Teresa. The perimeter of the tholos is clear, collapsed inwards and filled with ashlars for at least three metres in height.
descriptions.NUR5770:
The nuraghe, of complex type, consists of a central tower around which a three-lobed bastion has been built, enclosing a courtyard of disengaged space.

The towers have a curved form, as seen in the Santu Antine nuraghe of Torralba.
descriptions.NUR3829: Corridor nuraghe. The structures are completely covered and hidden by dense palustrine vegetation. The building stands on a small alluvial elevation between the Rio Cispiri and a parallel stream. As regards the structures, only a few courses of polygonal basaltic blocks can be observed.
descriptions.NUR12843:
Destroyed nuraghe located on the summit of the hill of the same name.

Unfortunately, little remains of this monument, but it is still of considerable significance.
descriptions.NUR573: Nuraghe "a tancato": on the front face of the main tower there is a wall of irregular shape that encloses a smaller tower and a courtyard situated between the two towers.
descriptions.NUR4076: Oral sources insist that a nuraghe stands on the summit of Bruncu Zinnibiri, without specifying whether it is a single tower or a more complex structure. Immediately below the few ruins of the “nuraghe” the village extended, also the target of continuous illicit digging; one of the surveys carried out led to the discovery of a cultural deposit near which charcoal remains were observed and where abundant ceramic material was collected.
descriptions.NUR505: Oral sources insist that a nuraghe stands on the summit of Bruncu Zinnibiri, without specifying whether it is a single tower or a more complex structure. Immediately below the few ruins of the “nuraghe” the village extended, also the target of continuous illicit digging; one of the surveys carried out led to the discovery of a cultural deposit near which charcoal remains were observed and where abundant ceramic material was collected.
descriptions.NUR534: Nuraghe in very poor condition and completely covered by undergrowth.
descriptions.NUR617:
Zinnuri in a rural municipal park characterized by the presence of ancient olive and oleander trees, together with a rural refuge. Around the spring there is an area equipped for outdoor refreshment, with wooden tables and benches, and a parking area for vehicles.

Here are located the Zinnuri nuraghe and the homonymous spring.
descriptions.NUR17032: Marks the boundary between the municipal territories of Siamaggiore, Solarussa, and Tramatza.
descriptions.NUR3574: Single-tower nuraghe, around the traces of a settlement. At this site the famous bronze tablets of Tzricottu were discovered.
descriptions.NUR3971: Single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe in advanced state of degradation.
descriptions.NUR2557: Complex nuraghe of quadrilobate type, the central tower is surrounded by bastions with four towers enclosing a courtyard. Around it, traces of a settlement and a wall remain.
