descriptions.NUR3721: Complex nuraghe consisting of a central tower with a body added comprising two lateral towers connected by a curtain wall and an intermediate courtyard from which access to the central tower is obtained.
descriptions.NUR3246: Complex nuraghe with an adjacent giants' tomb and a spring source known as "Roia Zrighidanu", which flows into the Riu Pizziu further downstream. It is an occupation site used up to the imperial Roman period, and the rectangular structures in the area of the nuraghe are likely from this latter period. At 500 metres from the nuraghe, researchers Dyson and Rowland report a Roman cemetery with at least 32 cist tombs.
descriptions.NUR5687: The Zuanne Orane nuraghe is located about 5 km north-west of Norbello, near the road leading to the church of Sant'Ignazio. It is a single-tower nuraghe built with basalt blocks in good state of preservation.
descriptions.NUR6312:
The nuraghe has been dated between the 14th and 12th centuries BC.

It is notable for the use of large basalt blocks carefully squared, in particular the jambs and lintel of the entrance.

At the entrance, on the left, is the ramp that led to the upper terrace, while on the right there is a niche in the walling. In the chamber one can see the three large ogival niches in the walls, the central hearth, and the tholos that forms the ceiling, still intact.
descriptions.NUR3634: Nuraghe probably unique because composed of two adjacent towers similar in type and dimensions.
descriptions.NUR5208: Single-tower, of limited architectural value but of significant strategic importance, as it allows control over the entire Gulf of Palmas.
descriptions.NUR4404:
Nuraghe today completely demolished, with only a fragment of the foundation remaining.

Among the evolved nuraghes of Serrenti, this one belongs to the type with concentric additions: it is located at Nuraxi, four-lobed, in shape similar to Su Nuraxi of Barumini (Lower Nuragic I phase of Lilliu) and to that of Bruncu Siliqua, featuring a central tower 14 m in diameter and at least three secondary towers.
descriptions.NUR13635: This nuraghe was identified through a letter sent to Nurnet by a reader of the page. The nuraghe appears to have been destroyed and incorporated into a large rural building. This is the origin of the name "Medau Mannu".
descriptions.NUR4118: Destroyed by the construction of modern buildings.
descriptions.NUR4394: Of this nuraghe no traces remain as it was completely destroyed during the construction of a vineyard.
descriptions.NUR10339: It is a millennial olive tree, certainly the oldest in the Chiaramonti area. In summer hundreds of sheep rest beneath its branches, and at night hundreds of birds and other animals take shelter there. Personally, I reported it to the Sardinian Forests Authority, which has placed it under its care. I am its guardian.
descriptions.NUR714: Its position relative to the terrain's topography is truly odd! Or rather, it is clear as the sun, since the fortified wall facing it on the Zennaru hillside clearly indicates its function as a control and surveillance post.
descriptions.NUR1551: It is an acrocoro surrounded by a wall, probably of Nuragic period, partially buried and never investigated, near which stands the baetyl (warrior's head of Bulzi). From it, all the numerous nuraghes that existed in the surrounding area are monitored.
descriptions.NUR9214: The sources available to us indicate that the proto-nuraghe was studied by the archaeologist Ercole Contu prior to the construction of the Cuga dam, in the 1950s/60s. Unfortunately, the same texts mention that the body of the nuraghe was dismantled in order to be studied, precisely because of its unusual forms. Subsequently, with the approval of the Ministry, it was used as a foundation for the Cuga dam. The tower's height was 6 metres.
descriptions.NUR6843: In the countryside around Samatzai there are several scattered menhirs. Many of them, once standing, now lie overturned at the edges of paths and farmland; some have become and are used as boundary stones between one village and another, like the one still visible on top of the hill Bruncu sa Furca, where a prehistoric village may have stood. This standing stone is 1.30 m high, with a quadrangular section, rounded at the top, and without any particular signs of working.
descriptions.NUR12847: Nuragic village with remains of Roman-period dwellings, most of which were destroyed by the commune during the eucalyptus reforestation.
descriptions.NUR13499: Inscribed stones, petroglyphs with concentric circles and cups
descriptions.NUR19421:
A spring located atop a travertine limestone wall produces a continuous dripping along a vertical wall plunging into the bed of the Flumendosa. The constant flow of water has formed calcareous deposits and allowed the growth of a lush vegetation of capelvenere.

This unique waterfall flows into a pool suitable for bathing during the summer months. The dripping is intense in winter and quiet and calm in summer.
descriptions.NUR8513: Vast and complex archaeological site, comprising at least two villages, a probable necropolis with an associated building that may have been of cultic use, and nearby also a furnace.
descriptions.NUR17274: Nuragic gate that leads to the rock above the cliff.
descriptions.NUR16903: It is located within the territory of the comune of Uras; given the construction technique used, it is likely that the structure dates to the Nuragic period.
descriptions.NUR19607: The well located south of the cave and at a short distance from it has an oval shape. The well was cut into a rocky outcrop that forms the northern side and, partially, the eastern and western sides. A masonry structure made of parallelipipedal stones completes the eastern and western sides and fully encloses the southern side.
descriptions.NUR19229: The monument, in good state of conservation, consists of a rectangular entrance with a lintel, from which access is gained via a four-step staircase to a dromos. The ceiling of the dromos is covered with a flat band of calcareous slabs; the lateral walls, instead, exhibit a dry-stone masonry. On the back wall of the dromos is the opening leading to the chamber housing the sacred well, which is constantly full of water.
descriptions.NUR13049: Well of undefined period, often indicated as Roman but possibly Nuragic.
descriptions.NUR16967: The nuragic well/spring was built at the edge of a rocky outcrop using trachyte ashlar; it has an ovoid shape and extends to a depth of approximately 2.50 m. The northern wall continues from ground level up to a height of about 2 m, with the same width. In recent times, a livestock water trough has been constructed nearby.
descriptions.NUR15788: Well located a short distance from the nuraghe Unia, along the catchment of a stream, of probable Nuragic origin
descriptions.NUR17002: Nuragic well concealed. It has been completely sealed with bricks and cement to make it undetectable.
descriptions.NUR16834: Nuragic sacred well currently under study and excavation. The reconstruction is hypothetical.
descriptions.NUR12566: It is located within the municipal territory of Pula (CA) inside the archaeological area of Nora.
descriptions.NUR11028: Sacred well of probable Nuragic date and probable sacred use, located at 70 m east of the quadrangular tower. The well is built with well-shaped ashlar blocks of limestone and basalt, and has a notable depth of about 30 m, having yielded a large amount of material dating to the Nuragic, Punic, and Roman periods.
descriptions.NUR20286: Probable Nuragic well in poor condition and relatively isolated. It still has an active perennial spring. Noted and photographed by Sergio Melis.
descriptions.NUR8645: Remains of two sacred wells of the Nuragic period, set about 150 m apart. The first well is almost entirely buried. The second is in excellent condition, with an entrance formed by a semi-buried staircase. Its cylindrical shape has a diameter of about 2 m and a depth of about 3 m; it is built of stone blocks laid in horizontal courses. The presence of two sacred wells suggests a sacred centre of considerable importance.
descriptions.NUR8644: see sacred well Bau Crabas I
descriptions.NUR11928: The sacred well was excavated by diggers using a backhoe, and they found numerous bronze objects sold on the black market. The current state of the well is very poor, covered by moss and mud.
descriptions.NUR10424:
Sacred well, located inside the Romanesque chapel of the 13th century dedicated to Sant'Antonio da Padova.

Access is via a hatch leading to a series of stairs that lead to the sacred well, which is perfectly positioned directly beneath the Christian altar.
descriptions.NUR10004:
The monument stands in the marly basin of Coni at the foot of the Valenza hill, in the historic region of Part'e Alenza, between the Marmilla and the Sarcidano. The sacred well of Coni, built of basalt blocks in pseudo-isodomic masonry, although lacking a vestibule, follows the classic architectural scheme of Nuragic wells.

The monument consists of a descending staircase protected by a corridor (2.60 m long) and an underground chamber that encloses the spring vein.
descriptions.NUR8161: The village consists of three sacred wells and a series of circular huts. The best-preserved well lies in the northern sector of the area. Built of local schist blocks, it abuts a small natural rock face to the south-west. The entrance to the chamber is off-centre relative to the axis of the tholos. The latter has collapsed on its northern side. The area in front of the well's entrance chamber is bounded by a series of curvilinear walls at different levels.
descriptions.NUR10849: The village consists of three sacred wells and a series of circular huts. The best-preserved well lies in the northern sector of the area. Built of local schist blocks, it abuts a small natural rock face to the south-west. The entrance to the chamber is off-centre relative to the axis of the tholos. The latter has collapsed on its northern side. The area in front of the well's entrance chamber is bounded by a series of curvilinear walls at different levels.
descriptions.NUR11536: From Tharros.info. Position not precisely defined
descriptions.NUR2666:
Dated to the 11th century BC. Temple built with isodomic calcareous ashlar, an achievement of refined architecture. The external walls are decorated with rows of carved notches on the ashlar. Water is channeled into the well through gutters and then into an external basin.

It shows some similarities with the well at Predio Canopoli in Perfugas.
descriptions.NUR12846: The sacred nuragic well at Is Molineddus is located in a valley rich in springs. From the limited information that Spano was able to gather, it consisted of a rectangular structure with an entrance on the western side, built with large stones laid dry and closely joined. Behind the building, a spring emerged from the rock, collecting in a round well also constructed of large stones.
descriptions.NUR11026: The "roundhouse" at Sa Corona Arrubia in the Genoni area, also known locally as "Santa Maria S'Ungroi", is a rare sacred structure of Nuragic age, located at Sa Corona Arrubia–Genoni. The monument, mentioned by Taramelli who considered it a Nuragic sacred well, retains intact its base ring composed of isodomic masonry in basalt, with two and in a few places three courses preserved, including a small niche and some blocks likely belonging to a quay.
descriptions.NUR12657: Built by the Sardinian Nuragics, the well is estimated to be about 2,700 years old; it was discovered in 1883 during land clearing for railway tracks, and it is believed that valuable artifacts were lost. Of the original 40 steps, only 22 remain. Various artifacts, including rings and coins, were found and are now preserved at the Archaeological Museum of Cagliari.
descriptions.NUR20022: The sacred well of Nanni Ecca is located in a private property, a fence taller than 2 metres from the ground protects a large private area; within this, in a thorny area, the remains of the well are found, preserving the entrance and part of the chamber, but lacking the "dome".
descriptions.NUR13616: Pozo temple, one of the most refined Nuragic sites in Sardinia, features a vestibule that leads into a staircase connecting to the well chamber. The building is constructed with precisely cut limestone ashlar laid in regular courses. The vestibule, rectangular (width 2.70 m; depth 1.88 m), has a perfectly laid floor, and on the walls two bench-seats are formed by two worked blocks.
descriptions.NUR8697: The Sa Linnarta complex, a three-lobed nuraghe with numerous associated huts and a beautiful sacred well, is, according to experts, one of the most important Nuragic sites in the Baronia.
descriptions.NUR13310: The archaeological site is located just a few dozen metres from a Christian-medieval settlement, set within the greenery of ancient olive trees. It is divided into two nuclei: in the first you will find a temple with a sacred well, dating to the Late Bronze Age (12th century BCE), surrounded by a sacred enclosure (themenos) shaped like a 'lock'. Built with finely worked basalt ashlar and precise techniques, the temple is a masterpiece of perfectly geometric forms.
descriptions.NUR13620: The well consists of a rectangular, paved atrium that leads to the stairwell through a strongly tapering trapezoidal passage; the stairwell, about 6 metres long, leads down to the underground chamber, which is sub-circular and covered by a tholos, where the water table is intercepted. The structure is built of local marl blocks, regularly squared, bush-hammered and laid in staggered courses with earth inserted between the bedding planes.
descriptions.NUR8615:
Built of granite blocks, it consists of a circular courtyard, a vestibule – a small space linking the courtyard and the well – and the well itself, reached from the vestibule by several steps; the spring lies 17 steps down.

Excavated completely in 1938, the sacred well of Sa Testa has an overall length of 17.50 metres. It was a place of worship for spring waters. Numerous finds came to light during the excavations, such as Punic-period incense burners.
descriptions.NUR12964: Caves frequently used and modified during the Neolithic. Nearby are the remains of a Nuragic village. Sacred well dismantled using mechanical tools. Some arenaria blocks and T-shaped ashlar stones remain. Where the well or the temple once stood, there is now a crater.
descriptions.NUR20122: “Su Posidu”, meaning treasure. A very unusual well set between two enormous granite boulders, about 60–80 centimetres apart and 5–6 metres high. A series of schist steps, set between the two rock spurs, deliberately worked and cut, form a double staircase that allowed easy access to the central part of the well, where the precious liquid was found: water, what treasure was as precious to the people of that time as water?
descriptions.NUR17300: Located in the same locality, in the countryside of the village, a Nuragic well temple, of which only some remains are visible today. The monument is isodomic in type and thus exhibits very refined craftsmanship. Numerous blocks of the sacred structure are scattered near a recently constructed well, which in fact has replaced the ancient one.
descriptions.NUR8115:
Romanzesu represents one of the most important complexes of domestic and ritual architecture in Nuragic Sardinia, featuring about a hundred huts, five cult buildings, a well temple and four "megaron" temples, plus a large ceremonial enclosure. It is built with local granite.

The area extends around the well temple, constructed into the rock from whose fissures spring the spring water. It has a staircase of access and a circular chamber built with regular courses of precisely worked blocks.
descriptions.NUR10744: The sacred well or well temple represents without doubt the most striking example of a sacred building among those so far discovered and studied in the Mediterranean basin. This type of building, belonging to the rich Sardinian civilization, dates back to the long and diverse Nuragic period. It was conceived as a place for carrying out various rites related to the cult of water.
descriptions.NUR7034:
Composed of domus de janas of the type with horizontal projection and well (1, 2, 3, 4), the other consists of domus with well (5, 6, 7).

Particularly notable is tomb 1, the result of several construction phases: originally of the type with well and antechamber and large chamber, later equipped with a long corridor replacing the well, and extended to the right of the large chamber, attaching three burial chambers to a neighbouring burial site.
descriptions.NUR21001: Interesting site in the territory of Villa Sant'Antonio. Located about 2 km to the south-east of the village, it shows probable remains of domus de janas, canaletas, coppers, basins, and a symbol that the locals believe refers to fertility. All these elements together suggest a possible pre-Nuragic cultic area.
descriptions.NUR19819: Remains of a megalithic circular structure with an apparent entrance portal.
descriptions.NUR20253: Likely domus de janas, currently used as a dog kennel. It is probable that other domus de janas existed in the area, now destroyed due to building activities.
descriptions.NUR20142: Reported by a resident of Osilo. The domus is not photographable, hidden by brambles and shrubs. To be verified.
descriptions.NUR21163: Fountain whose architectural form recalls several clearly nuragic analogies
descriptions.NUR17888: On site the carved stones belonging to the nuragic fountain still remain, presumably the nuragic fountain was destroyed during the works for the construction of the water trough complex.
descriptions.NUR21172: It consists of a façade and a small courtyard. On the façade there is an architrave lintel opening for the collection of water. The space has a semicircular plan and walls that gently slope inwards.
descriptions.NUR21179: Generally known as Su Corrazzu dessu Estiu, it is so large that its circuit measures no more than a hundred ordinary paces, and it is built of enormous stones with the wall about 30 palms high on one side and half that on the other. Inside and around there is a great mass of ruins. The simple folk who live there believe an evil angel dwells within, so many fear to approach it, and only the most courageous dare go there in September to search for some marvellous flower of prodigious virtue that benefits whoever picks it. But all who have gone have laboured in vain, because the spirit of the place hides it. This place and this spirit are the subject of wondrous tales among the people of Fluminimaggiore, and anyone who tries to dissuade them speaks in vain.
descriptions.NUR3169: A small isolated hill in the middle of ploughed fields. Many believe that within it there is a nuraghe completely covered in earth. This view is supported by the stone ashlar cap at the top.
descriptions.NUR20343: It is located about two hundred metres from the Church of Santa Lucia. At first glance it appears to be a single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe, but it could simply be the summit of a large, buried nuraghe complex hidden within a hill formed over millennia. What is visible is somewhat ruined: some courses, and a cavity that may represent the top of the central tower or the end of a staircase.
descriptions.NUR14925: Well, probably belonging to a Nuragic village. It is located on the top of a hill, inside a vineyard.
descriptions.NUR19605: South of the nuraghe and near the village huts, there is a rectangular structure cut into the ground to a depth (visible) of about 150 cm, about 120 cm wide and 250 cm long, surrounded by trachyte stones of varying sizes. The interior is almost completely filled with fallen stones and vegetation, making it difficult to accurately determine its dimensions and structure.
descriptions.NUR21140: Giants' tomb destroyed, from which two lateral walls remain; traces of excavation by tomb diggers are evident.
descriptions.NUR20350: Piles of ashlar characteristic of an ancient settlement abandoned and covered by dense forest vegetation, and various fragments of walls, most of which are circular: on the southern side there is a wall about 5 metres long, almost straight, and a smaller circular wall lower down, while on the western side of the settlement there is a circular wall made of large blocks of 2 to 3 courses, suggesting a Nuragic origin.
descriptions.NUR21141: It is an unidentifiable structure without an appropriate archaeological excavation. Limestone slabs set vertically, adjacent, tall but not very thick, are visible; a semicircular structure emerging from the ground, built of limestone blocks and with two openings. A long circular row, perhaps delimiting the structure, at the top of which cavities covered by a few slabs can be seen. Further west, a structure with two adjacent vertical limestone slabs positioned to the north, with another slab to the right while to the left there is a wall of ashlars. Traces of tomb-robbers' digging are evident.
descriptions.NUR2672: It has a quadrangular plan with a rounded profile and a maximum remaining height of 3.65 m to the south-east, with five courses, while to the north-west it reaches 2.00 m with four courses. The masonry is composed of large stones, only roughly shaped, stacked in horizontal rows that are very irregular. The structure features two co-axial entrances, one in the east-southeast and the other in the north-west, connected by a corridor that runs orthogonally to the main axis of the structure.
descriptions.NUR12270: Located on the edge of a cliff, less than 400 metres north of the "Pattada" nuraghe, now reduced to a heap of rubble, it is covered by shrub vegetation.
descriptions.NUR14235: The nuraghe has an irregular elliptical shape, with a total circumference of about 50 m; the powerful construction is crossed longitudinally by a corridor 15.2 m long, with opposite entrances and delimited on both walls by wide openings leading to niches, i.e. cavities, or to a stairwell that leads to the upper level. The straight corridor has a trapezoidal cross-section with a flat ceiling made of 11 slabs.
descriptions.NUR2980: The proto-nuraghe Su Cannuju (ex S'Alzola Trigale) has a quadrangular plan, with a single longitudinal corridor.
descriptions.NUR1250: Known as Coarittos nuraghe, but there is no trace of that type of monument.
descriptions.NUR20116: The structure is built upon a natural rocky outcrop and forms a enclosure measuring about 50 by 32 metres with an average height of about 3 metres. Access to the interior occurred through two side portals, north/south. These entrances are followed by a stone corridor. Inside, a large granitic block, which some believe resembles a mother goddess, suggests a possible temple function for the site.
descriptions.NUR1939: It is described as a nuragic enclosure by A. Moravetti.
descriptions.NUR3761: Located about a hundred metres south of the Provincial Road Borore-Sedilo, the enclosure of Pedru Feghe has a vaguely circular shape, with a remaining height of 2.45 m to the north-west and 2.05 m to the south-east, respectively, with 4 and 3 courses; the wall thickness varies from 1.45 m to 0.46 m. The masonry is composed of polyhedral blocks of medium and large size arranged in fairly regular horizontal courses.
descriptions.NUR20132: It is difficult to say whether this was a village. The site, being on a steep slope, has been covered by sedimentary deposits that have buried the existing structures. The area has never been the subject of excavations. Large walls, dozens of metres long and very thick, descend into the valley bottom down to the river; others run parallel to it. In particular, a long wall composed of two parallel rows of walls separated by a ditch about two metres wide has struck us.
descriptions.NUR21160: The reliefs at Sa Icu in Dorgali are on the basalt cliff overhanging the Cedrino, 1.2 km east of provincial road no. 38, and are attributed to the Chalcolithic. They consist of 57 geometric figures covering an area of 10 x 12 m, carved mostly in high relief (only one is incised) on three basalt blocks that protrude on average 30 cm above ground level. The figures depict: simple parallelepipeds, truncated terraced pyramids of three tiers with simple rectangular plans or with a semicircle on the longer side of the base parallelepipeds.
descriptions.NUR19917: Natural monument, eroded into columns and protected by rock overhang.
descriptions.NUR8234: Cave currently blocked by a collapse that prevents access. Inside, some ceramic fragments have been recovered, assignable to the culture of Bonu Ighinu.
descriptions.NUR8232: A shelter characterized by various rooms, one of which was inhabited from the Early Neolithic, later used for funerary purposes. The artifacts found can be attributed to the Cardial culture.
descriptions.NUR19647: Cave that may have been used, in prehistoric and protohistoric times, as shelter/residence for human families. In this case, as in others, the man-made wall structures are evident, designed to reduce the opening. Nearby, at least two more are found, similar and in comparable conditions.
descriptions.NUR19649: Tafone/luttoni – rock shelter probably used in prehistoric and protohistoric times, possibly as dwelling for human families. There is no certainty regarding its identification due to the lack of in-depth studies, and thus information is very limited. The only indications suggesting its identification as such are other rock shelters located nearby (exactly three) and a giants' tomb at a short distance.
descriptions.NUR12969: Su Scusorgiu: "The Treasure". In this storage room, 40 complete pre-Nuragic swords were found. They are now on display at the Archaeological Museum of Cagliari.
descriptions.NUR7363: The underground cemetery of "Sa Perdra Pertunta", better known as "The Elephant Rock", consists of two domus de janas: the first is located at the top of a large trachytic boulder and only traces of three chambers remain; the second tomb, opening slightly below on the same boulder, is composed of four small chambers and is particularly notable and well known for the presence of carved bull's-head protomes on the walls of the first chamber.
descriptions.NUR11032: Comprises two large stones protruding near the State Road 131. They may date back to the Ozieri culture, when these stones were used as a "sacred stone" for the smallest of the roccioni that form Perda Longa, as evidenced by the cups practiced in this area and the remains of tools made of chert and ceramics found nearby. Extract from: Biddas e nuraxis de su sattu de Serrenti de su Brunzu de mesu a su Ferru I, by Daniele Carta
descriptions.NUR3767: The I.G.M. lists it as a nuraghe, yet strong and well-founded features raise doubts about classifying it as such. It stands at the border between the territories of Chiaramonti and Ardara, in the area known as Pittiri, at an elevation of 440 m a.s.l., and at the boundary with the territories of Truncu Nieddu and Serra di Monte Pittu. The structure is atypical and difficult to classify: it is not a nuraghe, but difficult to categorize as a hut.
descriptions.NUR19679:
The cave, about 30 metres long, has two entrances aligned north-south.

Inside, traces of wall structures and numerous ceramic fragments are visible. The archaeological deposit shows continuous occupation from the Bronze Age.
descriptions.NUR12863: Megalithic enclosure with inside a toppled menhir.
descriptions.NUR12848: Nuragic village almost entirely covered by debris, vegetation, and stones from cleared lands.
descriptions.NUR8474: Remains of about twelve huts and a perimeter wall.
descriptions.NUR1935: The nuraghe is subterranean, probably a single-tower and single-cell structure. The external wall has parts that project. The internal wall retains three courses that completely close the circular space. The lintel at the entrance was inserted into a dry-stone wall.
descriptions.NUR8088: The giants' tomb Sa Dom 'e S'Orku is one of the best-preserved Nuragic monuments. Built on a slight rise in the terrain, it is of the type with an exedra front and coursed façade. The tomb's body, apsidal in plan, is aligned along the SE-NO axis and is 15.20 m long. The masonry work is composed of medium-sized basalt blocks well-cut and arranged in regular courses. In certain parts of the wall, the use of alletting wedges is observed.
descriptions.NUR9868:
There are no features sufficient to classify it as a nuraghe. It appears to be a simple megalithic wall composed of roughly squared stones, possibly serving as a rudimentary fortification for a watchpost (?)?

Nuraghe of the ruins. The ruins referred to here are those of the nuraghe that gives its name to the locality. See Carràlzu. Ardu Pinzone = cardinal axis. mu
descriptions.NUR14129: The site has yielded a two-chambered hypogeum burial cut into the southern wall of the plateau, whose upper part shows a slab of natural rock that, seen from the front, gives the monument a megalithic appearance; a small dolmen; a giants' tomb; a spring; a megalithic wall with traces of later adaptations; and a corridor nuraghe. The corridor wall includes boulders of considerable size, some of which bear linear incisions.
descriptions.NUR7997: The site dates back to the Bronze Age and was entirely constructed using finely worked basaltic stones. The structure consists of a curtain wall almost completely destroyed: only the base of the well remains, as it lacks the covering of the tholos (its typology is difficult to establish), although the chamber itself remains intact. There are 9 steps descending to the water level, located about two metres below ground.
descriptions.NUR8708:
The temple of Sant'Anastasia is located near the church of the same name, in the upper part of Sardara, at the foot of the escarpment rising towards the Pran'e Cuaddus hill, in central Campidano.

The sanctuary, one of the most important Nuragic sites in Sardinia, is centred on the temple with a well.

The temple, dating to the Late Bronze Age (13th–12th century BCE), is part of a complex settlement with both civil and religious functions, still under excavation.
descriptions.NUR7106:
The site dates back to about 3000 BC and was used for about 1500 years, from the Ozieri culture to the Bonnannaro culture.

It derives its name from the large number of skeletons (over 200) and the rich military assemblage—dated to about 1650–1600 BC—comprising copper arsenical swords and daggers (a total of 19). The swords, with triangular blades, vary in length from 27 to 66 cm and show some similarities with swords from the El Argar culture (Spain).
descriptions.NUR8265: Sacred area of probable Nuragic origin, reused in Punic and Roman periods, where abundant building materials and ceramics are found.
descriptions.NUR11927: It consists of the remains of a megalithic sanctuary located at the centre of the saddle, about 100 metres from the other site to the east. Currently, the dense vegetation allows access to only four or five standing menhirs laid on the ground, spaced only a few metres apart. From a visit I made to this site many years ago, I remember that there were far more menhirs back then; now, the thick vegetation prevents any assessment of whether there may be others.
descriptions.NUR12888: The excavation has revealed a rectangular building divided into two rooms, set within an enclosed area. It is hypothesized that the building had a religious function. The excavations have yielded artifacts datable between the 8th and 7th centuries BC. The context is bleak and typical, featuring abandoned military structures (built within the sanctuary), an abandoned restaurant, and a large tar-covered parking area.
descriptions.NUR17761: Comprised of a Nuragic village, a circular temple, and a megaron temple, and upstream a series of springs, wells, and channels for the collection, gathering, and channeling of water towards the sacred area located downstream.
descriptions.NUR11041: In the fissure there is a stone staircase, squared and one metre wide, composed of three ramps, two visible, the third covered by debris, separated by two landings. All the steps are made of two squared basalt blocks 'to size', assembled by inserting between them a wedge-shaped block. In some steps circular recesses have been cut, interpretable as basins for lustration, while on others there are projecting mammillary reliefs.
descriptions.NUR14230: The archaeological site was discovered in 1985, entirely by chance, during land clearing works for the installation of a vineyard. Investigations, continued until 1988, allowed the identification of the main nucleus of the sanctuary, consisting of the sacred well, a round structure that characterizes a portion of the large building constructed in isodomic masonry, and two cylindrical structures, interpretable as altars.
descriptions.NUR9171: This, as it seems, is the area where initially the Castle of Burgos was being built at Sa Pattada, Illorai, before abandoning this site to finally construct it at Burgos, ... but for me it is not so! ... to me it suggests something more ancient, perhaps Nuragic, ... some ritual area!
descriptions.NUR8333: In good state of preservation are two nuragic huts; the rest of the village is now in ruins. On the south-western edge there is a pond (Paule – from which the site gets its name) that probably served as a water reservoir.
descriptions.NUR20375: "On the site, some large slabs are found partially embedded in the ground, partially fragmented and not in situ, which might be related to a dolmenic structure. Although no archaeological material is found on the ground, the shape and dimensions of the blocks suggest the site should be included among areas at risk." The name recalls other toponyms of dolmen.
descriptions.NUR6833:
There is a popular tale that these stones are a pair of petrified spouses, frozen by the deity for having mocked the sound of the church bells from the nearby church of Masullas during the festival of Sa Gloriosa.

It seems that in ancient times, these rocky statuary blocks—geologically nothing more than subaquatic basalt outcrops—were venerated by the proto-Sardinians as fertile deities.
descriptions.NUR19417: Its entrance was narrowed and adapted in the Nuragic period to make it difficult to detect and extremely easy to defend in the event of an external attack. The rather steep descent, ending with a final drop of 8 metres, was modified by the addition of a retaining wall and the creation of a narrow, steep staircase of 18 steps for access. Inside, traces of Nuragic-period occupation are clearly visible.
descriptions.NUR19681: The cave is accessible via a staircase constructed using Nuragic technique, with an architrave lintel spanning sixteen steps, very similar to those found inside the nuraghe. The cave consists of two large chambers and a small single-cell room located at the upper part of the cavity. On the base of the cave, fragments of Nuragic ceramics are present. The site is generally classified as either a subterranean temple or a refuge.
descriptions.NUR10129: Inside a lentisco trunk, probably ready for transport to the client, the sarcophagus (2.00 x 0.90 x 0.90 m) is made from a single monolithic brown trachyte of considerable size.
descriptions.NUR19894: North-west of the nuraghe Sa Scrocca Manna, on the ground surface, lies a probable menhir of prismatic form with a triangular base. The stone has its anterior face flattened, likely through surface carving. The two posterior faces show signs of working and smoothing.
descriptions.NUR19892: In the area of Monte Sa Scrocca Manna, at the border of the municipalities of Sant'Antioco and Calasetta, there are several structures that, originally, very likely formed part of a Phoenician and/or Roman settlement. Unfortunately, during World War II, military works severely damaged the curtain walls. Some walls remain, still fairly well preserved, and various squared and moulded ashlar stones, used in military constructions.
descriptions.NUR10195: It is named after the terrain's toponym. Like most of the nuraghes and other features in Chiaramonti, it is in a state of degradation almost irreparably compromised. Several features stand out that lead me to consider its belonging to the nuraghe type with a flat floor.
descriptions.NUR1501: It is a sarcophagus similar to those of Su Cannau and sos Terrelas. Ready for burial, or simply ready to be carried to the deceased? Roman period or merely medieval? Or belonging to the period of the Giudicati, as part of the personal or family heritage of one of the judges or kings of Torres or of Logudoro.
descriptions.NUR5262: The Giants' Tomb at San Liberno – which, moreover, is perfectly oriented towards dawn at winter solstice – is just one of many archaeological features present in the municipality of Sarroch. Unfortunately, the monument has been damaged by an electrical pole.
descriptions.NUR8671: Nuraghe with remains of a village and a Roman settlement.
descriptions.NUR19683: The monument located at a short distance from the Giants' Tombs of Su Piccante and Su Ittichinzu and from the nearby village of Lettu Rucratu is situated at the foot of a hill where it appears as a small well carved into the ground, where presumably the water table naturally emerged, and lined with rough basalt blocks.
descriptions.NUR7038: The domus de janas of Pranu Efis or S'acqua Salida, at Pimentel, are easily accessible. After travelling about two km along the road connecting the village to Guasila, one turns left onto a dirt track that, after 300 metres, leads to the necropolis. Some of the burials still show traces of red ochre painting, and one in particular contains a profile similar to a bull's-head protome.
descriptions.NUR10026: Local folk belief, mixed with clear memories of old ancestors and confirmed by the regional newspaper "l'ISOLA" of that time, reports that in a small village some tombs were found. Among the artifacts was a statuette in the form of a woman (an ocarina, or Mother Goddess?). MU
descriptions.NUR832: It is the only one in the entire territory inaccessible due to environmental incompatibility: the monument is presumed to have disappeared entirely. mu
descriptions.NUR5209: Site completely eroded and buried. It is evident that a village, probably Nuragic or pre-Nuragic, once occupied a large area. Apart from a few scattered ashlars, only a few hut or nuraghe walls remain visible.
descriptions.NUR14671: The site includes an undefined structure (WHAT COULD IT BE?) located at the edge of a cliff face, featuring (now missing) a cut stone resembling a water cistern, a small domus de janas, the giants' tomb of Pascaredda; a dolmen, the Nuraghe Monti Di Deu, the Nuraghe Agnu, and the nuragica spring of li Paladini. Access to the tomb of Pascaredda and the Nuraghe Agnu is easy, while the rest of the site is abandoned and largely inaccessible, difficult to locate and reach.
descriptions.NUR12958: Settled village already in the iron age. According to the report, the site continues to be affected by quarrying activities, particularly by a large dump of equipment and inert waste. Quarry where approximately 10,000 tonnes of toxic waste from Portovesme S.r.l. have been illegally dumped.
descriptions.NUR6806: Tall three metres, broken transversely at mid-height and cracked at the base from the impact of a mechanical vomer, it features at the top a kind of smooth sub-oval mask. The design extends linearly along the sides, and at the apex appears almost crowned by a distinct bull's head ornament. The monument represents a unique example on the island, but possibly also in continental megalithic sculpture.
descriptions.NUR6790:
Within an agro-pastoral farm and at the centre of a circular sheepfold enclosed by a dry stone wall, stands a singular and exceptional proto-anthropomorphic menhir. The pillar, 1.77 m high, features a rudimentary representation of a head distinct from the underlying body, separated by a short collar, and may symbolically echo the phallic motif.

It is located 500 metres to the north-west of the underground cemetery of Monte Ozastru.
descriptions.NUR11035: In Serrenti, nuragic villages are often located near a nuraghe, as in the case of the site of Bruncu Pubusa; in other cases (Giuanni Acca, Sattu Divisu, Bruncu Abis, and Sa Serra) they are located without any nearby nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR18711: Stele with an arched stele placed at the post for a metal gate
descriptions.NUR6793: Menhir / carved stele with concentric circles
descriptions.NUR10863: Elliptical building, slightly raised on an artificial platform. Function to be verified.
descriptions.NUR4726:
On the summit of the limestone outcrop at 191 metres above sea level stands a monumental Nuragic complex that makes use of the natural rock ledge to the west and a sheer drop on the eastern slope.

The monument covers an area of about 1000 sq m and extends in plan along a longitudinal axis oriented north-west–south-east, with a probable entrance to the north.

From north to south the following can be identified: a tholos; a sub-rectangular block; a semicircular room; walls following a curvilinear course.
descriptions.NUR10857: Archaeological trace corresponding to the area of the trigonometric point.
descriptions.NUR6838: Su Putzu Nuragic village, composed of about one hundred huts surrounding a well temple, exactly Su Putzu.
descriptions.NUR13565: The slow retreat of water, due to drought, reveals what is normally submerged beneath the waters. Around us, clear nuragic traces are evident, such as sacred huts and other typical period environments. On a small promontory stands another nuraghe, "Sa tanca 'e sa Mura", and moving a little further, a third nuraghe, "Tudera Alto", of which, unfortunately, only some of its cyclopean stone courses have reached us!
descriptions.NUR12616: Remains dating to the Nuragic period located on the Red Island, about one kilometre from the coast of the commune of Teulada. The area falls within the Capo Teulada military zone.
descriptions.NUR8276: The site, dating to the late Bronze Age (1300–1000 BC), is a complex nuraghe consisting of a central tower to which eight additional towers were later attached to form a bastion. The bastion is surrounded by a megalithic curtain wall featuring five towers equipped with loopholes. For its construction, mainly granite stones were used, a material available on-site.
descriptions.NUR19915: In the area, where a Nuragic site probably once existed, a calcination oven has been built, which in recent times has been repurposed as a dwelling. Adjacent to it are the remains of a recently constructed house. The oven's construction, likely, dates to the end of the 1800s or early 1890s: many other ovens of the same period were erected in Sant'Antioco.
descriptions.NUR19911: From the second giants' tomb, moving 50 m westward, one finds an area containing polyhedral stones of various sizes, only roughly shaped, suggesting the presence of a cultic zone.
descriptions.NUR19913: From the second giants' tomb, moving 450 m north, one finds an area where the presence of polyhedral stones of various sizes, only roughly shaped, suggests that it was a site dedicated to cult practice.
descriptions.NUR19909: Adjacent to a probable Nuragic enclosure, there is a trachyte block of red stone that appears at first glance to be a door or an entrance slab. This block, irregular in shape and resembling a parallelepiped, has a plane on two offset levels visible in the exposed section. At the upper level, and at the ends, there are two holes: one circular and the other rectangular.
descriptions.NUR19907: About 200 metres from the second TdG there are nuragic constructions whose use cannot be defined, mainly due to overlapping interventions carried out in different periods (including recent ones) and also because of the lack of archaeological studies. The remaining structures of probable nuragic origin consist of a enclosure featuring cyclopean walls built with roughly hewn stones, and the remains of two possible huts.
descriptions.NUR19903: In this area there were two giants' tombs, one of which has been completely dismantled. In the area where the burial structure presumably stood, scattered ashlars remain within a stand of mastic trees. Due to the local ground elevation, part of the tomb may still be buried.
descriptions.NUR19905: In this area there were two giants' tombs located about 100 m apart. The second one is the one that is best preserved, although, for most of its extent, it is covered by vegetation and its walls are blocked by collapse. The tomb that shows its structure with the greatest difficulty most likely has a rectangular chamber built with large stones of varying sizes, only roughly shaped.
descriptions.NUR8099:
The monument consists of an atrium and the actual spring source from which springing water emerges.

The atrium is a rectangular space measuring 5.15 m by 1.80 m, bordered on the sides by two seating areas of equal length, constructed with basalt blocks, and on the left by a wall measuring 2 x 0.3 m built with well-cut ashlar stones laid in regular courses. The floor is paved with slabs of the same type.
descriptions.NUR19931: Between 1950 and 1960, a calcination oven was built, whose structure was very likely constructed using stones belonging to the village.
descriptions.NUR19927: To the south-east of the village lie the remains of 2 or more tombs, likely of Punica or Roman origin. In one of these tombs, the landowner had observed a dozen small human skulls, exposed by illegal excavation. Inside the tomb, human bones are still present. The funerary structure has been completely destroyed, and most of the worked stones have been repurposed for other uses.
descriptions.NUR19924: The probable Nuragic village, located about 200 m west of the nuraghe, consists of about 10 huts, two of which are rectangular and the rest round. Unfortunately, all the structures are in very poor condition and in some cases barely distinguishable. The huts were built using small and medium-sized polyhedral stones, set together without mortar. Several ceramic fragments are found in the area.
descriptions.NUR8755:
The nuraghe has preserved an extraordinary Nuragic altar. Three construction phases can be identified.

The first, possibly from the Middle Bronze Age I (XVI–XV centuries BC), featured the layout of a bastion and an outer wall with corridors and cells.

In the second phase, Middle Bronze Age II (XIV century BC), a three-lobed sinusoidal bastion and a new outer wall with four towers connected by irregularly straight curtain walls were added.

In the third phase, the outer wall was equipped with another tower and additional curtain walls.
descriptions.NUR14793:
Of this monument nothing remains, as it was buried over time and subsequently covered by houses and roads.

Some sewer excavations and local narratives indicate the presence of a complex nuraghe and a settlement. The site is also about 300 m from the location of the tomb of the warriors of Sant'Iroxi, known for its two hundred skulls and swords.
descriptions.NUR5867: Site located in the Su Pranu area, on top of a hill with a truncated pyramidal shape. Here the remains of a nuraghe or more likely a temple are found, attested by votive material discovered at the base of the site and along the ridges of the small hill; on its southern-facing slope there are subterranean tombs that are extremely difficult to access.
descriptions.NUR4974:
The site exhibits a planimetric and architectural layout among the most remarkable produced by the Nuragic culture. It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1997.

The complex shows various construction phases characterized by the use of local stone: basalt from the Giara, which predominates, and calcareous marl.
descriptions.NUR8556: Excluding the central tower, the complex is extensively buried, making it difficult to interpret the components that make it up. In the area surrounding the nuraghe, several circular rooms are detected, possibly remnants of a village. In its vicinity, an area that could be a sacrificial site is also noted, known among the Samatzesi as “Sa piscedd' 'e su casu” due to its distinctive shape, which resembles that of a type of cheese.
descriptions.NUR11735:
Su Nuraxi Serra Manalgiu, about one kilometre from the old railway station of "Ortuabis", in the territory of Meana Sardo.

Around the nuraghe there are many fallen stones and many leccio plants, which grow alongside it.

One can observe an interesting wall built with rows of stones of the same height and a chamber with a collapsed vault.
descriptions.NUR19751: The pond located to the north of the Noccus nuraghe and about 200 m from it was excavated using a natural depression in the terrain, roughly circular in shape and bordered by rocky outcrops along about two-thirds of its circumference. The northern and south-western banks show clear signs of human intervention: by placing large stones along the bank, the waters were contained and at the same time the pond's capacity was increased.
descriptions.NUR12834:
Site where a proto-Sardinian healing god was worshipped.

Rectangular-plan temple built of large blocks, with a spring that collected in a round well. Taramelli judged that all the elements of a sanctuary with a healing character were present: a therapeutic spring and a temple to the healing deity, where the most remarkable find in Sardinian archaeology came to light. The bronze column base with inscriptions in Greek, Punic and Latin dedicated to the god Eshmun.
descriptions.NUR13502: Probable Nuragic water source from a perennial stream
descriptions.NUR19568:
The name is linked to a legend: after the discovery of a human skull inside the cave, it is believed that the skull belonged to one of the "mother girls" (it is said) who, as a punishment, were confined inside until they died of asphyxiation.

Recently, anthropological remains have been found, accompanied by pottery fragments made of clay. It is evident that Su Secretu is a natural cave that must have been used for funerary deposits.
descriptions.NUR8480: Neolithic period - Ozieri culture. Entrance to the western shelter - asset identification code: 95059055
descriptions.NUR19624: "The presence of humans on the island of Sant'Antioco is attested from the 5th millennium BC, in rock shelters, caves, lithic stations, and burials." A tafone, due to its size, was used as a rock shelter. Human use is evident, also from stones of various sizes, some in original position and others in considerable quantity in the immediate surroundings, which probably formed part of a partial wall closing the entrance.
descriptions.NUR19781: Cave that, due to its size, was probably used as shelter beneath rock. Several stones of varying dimensions, some still in original position and others at the edges of the cave, suggest the presence of a partial enclosing wall at the mouth. Nearby, some small ceramic fragments of undefined use are found. The present vegetation prevents visibility of further traces.
descriptions.NUR19626: “Human presence on the island of Sant’Antioco is attested from the 5th millennium BC in rock shelters, caves, lithic scatters and tombs.” A tafone which, because of its medium-sized opening and its not very large interior surface, as well as its volumes, may have been used as a pantry, considering that it lies near a hut. Here too some stones remain in their original position forming the wall that partly closed it off.
descriptions.NUR19759: A tafone of very particular construction, probably used as a burial, considering the presence of several stones beneath it, which likely formed part of the closing wall. A popular legend tells of a chest hidden/enclosed within it, containing a treasure, a "Scrixoxiu".
descriptions.NUR1327: It is an interesting Nuragic structure featuring the corner junction between the perimeter walls. Experts describe it as a megaron Greek type.
descriptions.NUR12714: The structure, likely Nuragic, features straight wall traces defining a rectangular plan aligned along a north-south axis. It is plausible that stones removed from the ancient building were reused in subsequent enclosure and hut constructions; the original building, by shape and visible features, resembles a megaron temple.
descriptions.NUR19900: Located within the municipal urban plan. There are no authoritative studies on the structure. Local oral traditions state that it has an entrance on an inclined plane/slope for a few metres, leading to a base, after which one descends vertically by about 20 to 25 metres. The landowners of that area sealed the entrance with a large stone/ slab.
descriptions.NUR19736: Well constructed with stones of different sizes; the external structure is completely ruined, probably belonging to a temple of a spring-water well.
descriptions.NUR8489: The monument is built at the foot of a rocky outcrop where a spring vein is present. The structure is made of trachyte boulders of various sizes expertly worked. Access to the well is through a vestibule leading to a staircase that ends in the well chamber; this has a façade preserving a rectangular entrance opening surmounted by a lintel. Because of collapses and its precarious state the site has been fenced off.
descriptions.NUR14575: The temple of Antas is a Punic-Roman temple dedicated to the worship of the god bearing the Sardinian name Sardus Pater Babai (Sid Addir for the Carthaginians). It is located about ten kilometres south of the village of Fluminimaggiore, in an area where Carthaginians and Romans settled, attracted by the abundant deposits of lead and iron present in the region.
descriptions.NUR14805: Temple dedicated to Astarte, the Phoenician goddess of love, fertility, and war. What made their places of worship notable was the fact that they were associated with a particular practice: sacred prostitution.
descriptions.NUR12446: The main sacred building is composed of two rooms: an atrium with a sub-rectangular plan (originally equipped with a bench), probably protected by a double-sloping roof, and a chamber accessible directly from the atrium, with a circular plan and likely originally covered by a tholos (false dome). The chamber features the remains of a hearth in the central position, showing various phases of use, and a bench-massive along the wall face.
descriptions.NUR10788:
Domu de Orgia di Esterzili is the largest known Nuragic "megaron" temple to date.

The building is enclosed within an elliptical enclosure (48.50 m x 28 m; wall thickness of 1.50 m), reduced to only the base course, with entrance to the north.

These and other details:
descriptions.NUR11967: The temple, built with irregular granite, porphyry, and more rarely limestone blocks, is composed of two square chambers opening into a circular space that once housed an altar reproducing two nuraghe towers. Outside, an irregular rectangular structure has preserved an extraordinary deposit of votive bronzes dedicated to the deity during religious ceremonies.
descriptions.NUR15758: Discovered in 1881, it was buried and then rediscovered in 1982 by the Superintendent.
descriptions.NUR10637: To the north-east of the nuraghe there is a well whose masonry consists of polyhedral stones of various shapes and sizes. The north wall's masonry is hidden by vegetation and appears to have collapsed at first glance. Around the well, several stones are present, likely part of the original structure.
descriptions.NUR10638: To the south-east of the nuraghe, attached to a rocky outcrop, lies the structure of a well dug into the rock. It appears as a long cavity executed in a semicircular form with stones of various shapes and sizes. Around it, stones of collapse are visible, likely part of the original well structure.
descriptions.NUR19817: To the east of the nuraghe a structure is visible that, at a cursory analysis, appears to be a well, though highly degraded. Its interior is completely covered by fallen stones, and what remains of the masonry appears to be composed of polyhedral stones, mostly small in size.
descriptions.NUR10097: In the Nuragic period, during the final Bronze Age, a small temple with a well was built, dedicated to the cult of water. The structure follows the planimetric layout typical of this type of monument throughout the island, being organized into a vestibule, a staircase chamber, and an underground cell. The circular cell, originally covered by a tholos, and the staircase chamber, which retains six steps, both have wall faces constructed with isodomic ashlar blocks of sandstone, perfectly interlocking with one another.
descriptions.NUR10448:
Nuragic well in the territory of Guasila, for which no significant information is available.

It is noted simply that the structure is built of isodomic masonry and features on its upper surface a T-shaped ashlar course, a feature observable only in more renowned and highly significant monuments.
descriptions.NUR12619:
Nuragic temple with sacred well and circular chamber, originally covered with a tholos vault, now lost, preceded by a staircase of which seven steps remain.

The underground structure is built with andesite blocks arranged in concentric courses, eight of which remain.

Water from the groundwater table still accumulates at the bottom of the chamber. The monument is currently located within a small enclosed area.
descriptions.NUR10654:
It was built in the Nuragic period for the water cult. Situated in the locality of Is Pirois, this Nuragic sacred well has the peculiarity of a single-tower nuraghe erected on its summit, built on the false dome that closes the well chamber.

The vestibule is defined by two wall faces composed of granite blocks. From the lintelled entrance one enters the stairway leading down into the well chamber, which is closed at the top by a false dome.
descriptions.NUR10777: The sacred well of Sa Brecca is located in the area of Sàrrala é Sùsu, Marina di Tertenia (Ogliastra). The site is named after the river Sa Brèca (in IGM Sa Brècca) and the associated sheepfold (Coìli 'e Sa Brèca) which stands on the remains of the proto-Sardinian settlement. The river is one of the most significant in this region and flows into the beach of Fògi Mànna.
descriptions.NUR19603: It is a sacred well almost entirely buried and partially damaged by illegal excavations. It can be identified in the midst of a dense and invasive vegetation, which nevertheless does not prevent the recognition of masonry structures forming the upper part of the tholos of the well and the upper structures of the vestibule.
descriptions.NUR10780: The temple with well is the most important site within the entire sanctuary, recognized first and immediately subjected to excavation. Dated to 900 BC by the archaeologist Anati in 1985[2], the site was constructed using cyclopean technique, the same method used for the nuraghes, but unlike the nuraghes, it employed carefully shaped stones, not roughly hewn. In antiquity, the temple was covered.
descriptions.NUR10708: Set within the dense vegetation lies the sacred well "Su Presoni", so named because in past centuries it was traditionally used as a prison. The sacred well is a structure linked to the cult of water, composed of a subterranean section (the well chamber) and an above-ground section (the atrium) connected by a staircase ramp. The Cardedu monument is in good state of preservation, with the lateral walls of the atrium still clearly visible to a height of more than one metre;
descriptions.NUR11381: Sacred well of the Nuragic period, of which only the vertical shaft remains.
descriptions.NUR10763: Su Putzu Nuragic village, composed of about one hundred huts surrounding a well temple, exactly Su Putzu. The temple features a long ramped vestibule; there is no staircase leading to the spring source.
descriptions.NUR12218: Lacking any visible structures or vestibule. It is composed of a linear sequence of steps (28–29 steps) and a water chamber that together form a rectangular void measuring 8.12 m in length and 1.25–1.10 m in width. The bottle-shaped section of the well, elliptical in plan (1.82 m x 1.25 m, height 5.12 m), distinguishes it from the well temples of Sardinia. The internal masonry is of polyhedral type.
descriptions.NUR4793:
Cuccuru Nuraxi is the hill on whose summit a grand complex nuraghe once stood, now largely destroyed.

Even the earliest studies made it possible to grasp the nuraghe's structure. It was the first archaeological excavations, in the early 1960s, however, that gave a more precise definition of the monumental complex. The building consisted of two megalithic towers joined by a curtain wall. Inside, it comprised at least three chambers, one of which formed the main chamber.
descriptions.NUR4142: The nuragic sacred well is a special structure attached to the spring vein; the sacred spring structure is usually composed of a chamber enclosed by stone slabs.
descriptions.NUR11528:
It consists of a temple, a nuraghe almost completely collapsed, a large circular hut, and a series of tombs "a tafone".

The temple at Malchittu undoubtedly represents the most interesting building in the complex, both for its excellent state of preservation and for the uniqueness of its construction, comparable to only a few other examples in Sardinia.
descriptions.NUR12954: A Nuragic temple on Nulvi territory, almost completely collapsed. At the summit a worked lintel remains, which once covered a door, and access to it was via a spiral staircase, inaccessible from the inside; only the last few steps and a single large slab of roof, set as a monolithic block, remain. From the surviving fragments it appears the gable resembled that of the giants' tombs. Nearby are various remains of nuraghes, a village, and a curtain wall encircling the summit of the promontory.
descriptions.NUR20236:
The building dates from the 11th century. The remains of the wall enclosing the precinct are visible. The most precious part lies at the centre of the area, with the basin altar. The building was constructed of large, fine isodomic ashlars. Many are T-shaped.

Two "circular rooms" were joined by a sort of trapezoidal vestibule, provided with lateral stone benches. Like the nuraghi, it possesses the triad of internal perimeter niches, the western one larger, the northern and southern ones smaller and symmetrical.
descriptions.NUR17369: Third domus of the S'incantu complex
descriptions.NUR17373: The underground chamber of the arcosolio type with a rectangular basin, dug into the limestone cliff like the domus, has revealed two distinct levels of deposition; the upper level with remains of eight inhumations; the lower level with five inhumations. The nuraghe has not been identified.
descriptions.NUR7242: It was a tomb of the "architectural façade" type. The façade is completely ruined and hidden by vegetation. Currently it lies beneath the viaduct of the new Uri-Scala Cavalli road. Source: Wikimapia
descriptions.NUR11539: Mixed-structure tomb composed of an ancient pre-Nuragic multicompartmental underground chamber modified according to the plan of Nuragic period giants' tombs by the addition of a monolithic arched stele (height 3.60 m) featuring a central door and an exedra formed by shaping the rock bench.
descriptions.NUR6997: The tomb opens just a few metres from the remains of a small single-cell domus de janas (Tomb III); it is very likely that Tomb II was originally a small domus de janas, later transformed into the form of a tomb with a façade. The stele is currently missing its upper part, including the lunette border, which lies on its side just a few metres from the entrance.
descriptions.NUR1475: We are facing yet another immense damage inflicted upon the community and history, perhaps in order to recover just a few square metres of arable or grazing land. The emergency has reduced to a state of ruin, and only a few features of the construction remain discernible.
descriptions.NUR17736: The funerary structure shows its wall faces only with difficulty due to collapses and the vegetation present at the front and rear ends. From the visible portions it appears to have been built with finely finished calcareous stones of considerable size. The abside wall, though covered by vegetation, retains two-thirds of the courses of polycylindrical stones. The front part of the tomb is incorporated into a dry stone wall, where a parallelepipedal stone is identifiable, possibly the lintel of the tomb.
descriptions.NUR17738: The funerary structure is indeterminate; the few remaining courses that once formed the tomb do not provide sufficient evidence to define its structure or dimensions. Vegetation that has grown in the burial site and the probable impact of unauthorized excavations are the factors that have contributed to its complete disintegration.
descriptions.NUR12015: What remains of a giants' tomb located in the wooded area of Santa Barbara's pic nic zone
descriptions.NUR11464: Giants' tombs not easily identifiable near the sheepfold Presethu Tortu
descriptions.NUR11465: Giants' tombs not easily identifiable near the sheepfold Presethu Tortu
descriptions.NUR14582: This dolmenic giants' tomb is easily accessible because it is situated alongside the road and near the larger Aidu complex.
descriptions.NUR17698: The tomb is covered by vegetation and can only be found by following the dry stone wall on the western side.
descriptions.NUR8633: Small Giants' tomb, belonging to the Appiu village context. Never excavated, it appears to belong to the cyclopean type of giants' tomb, despite being located in an area where dolmens with arched stelae are predominant.
descriptions.NUR8132:
The tomb of Barrancu Mannu, or "Sa Tuerredda", presents the classic planimetric layout of giants' tombs: an absidal tomb body, a covered corridor, and an arched exedra.

The external wall face is composed of large granite blocks of yellowish-red hue, roughly hewn and topped by irregular rows of polyhedral stones of large size and coarse texture.

Of the absidal arc, originally ending in a regular row of dentilled ashlar, only two or three courses remain.
descriptions.NUR10562: The tomb is not in good conservation. However, it is possible to see in its original position the large stele, of which only the lower part remains, in trapezoidal shape, while the central arched crown is missing, with only a fragment of it having fallen inside the chamber. As for the exedra, practically nothing remains. The burial chamber, also poorly preserved, is constructed with slabs set vertically into the ground.
descriptions.NUR10640: The tomb, still buried, clearly shows the violations it suffered at the hands of looters. The chamber is rectangular, built of boulders of various sizes, only roughly dressed, laid dry with packing wedges. The entrance, facing ESE, has its doorway completely buried, topped by a lintel shaped like a rectangular block whose sides appear perfectly smoothed. The tomb was preceded by an exedra, of which some boulders remain in situ to the north of the tomb body.
descriptions.NUR14084: The tomb is of the coursed type, built with slabs of slate, about one metre long, of which six courses of the external wall of the chamber and eight courses of the exedra remain in situ. The central portal of the exedra is constructed in a dolmenic style, with two slabs placed edge-to-edge and one slab above; the drainage opening is missing. The exedra is joined to the external wall of the chamber by a concave line.
descriptions.NUR12597: In the area of Funtanazza, within the lands of the Lampis family, lies the giants' tomb of Bruncu Espis, a site where in ancient times a Roman village stood. Well preserved and maintained by the landowners, it features a corridor about ten metres long and slightly more than one metre wide, and is completely covered by soil, upon which some ancient constructions still appear.
descriptions.NUR11732: It is in poor conservation. At the Sassari Museum the closure door is on display, but the tomb is incorrectly named Mesu e Rios.
descriptions.NUR10871: The actual location of the site needs to be verified.
descriptions.NUR13517: Giants' tomb with a bilitic stele, of which only the lower part remains; the monument damaged over the years by clandestine diggers and vandals.
descriptions.NUR15051: Dolmen with a collapsed and buried structure, whose layout cannot be defined.
descriptions.NUR10392: It is a masterpiece of architecture and harmonious, sacred construction. In front of the tumulus, turned upside down from both above and below, frequently visited by tomb-bearers, there extends an exedra in two rows of roughly hewn stones. From the arms of the exedra emerges a circle of single stones with a diameter of 15 m.
descriptions.NUR10537: They are two distinct collective burials that share the same exedra. They are located at a short distance from the homonymous nuraghe situated at the top of the plateau.
descriptions.NUR12960:
The corridor tomb has been attributed to the Nuragic period.

The baetyls recovered during surface surveys date to the Roman imperial and late antique periods. Repeated surface surveys have led to the discovery of baetyls and laterite, likely belonging to a necropolis.
descriptions.NUR19638: Near the homonymous nuraghe on the slope descending towards the Stupàra stream there is a giants' tomb built with flat slabs of shale. The tomb is about 7 metres long and about 2 metres high. No exedra is visible. However, the state of conservation is nonetheless good.
descriptions.NUR21133: The olive trees growing in the burial corridor are destroying what remains. Debris, leaf litter, and eolian sediments have covered the cavities. On the anterior side of this TdG, someone had built a sort of hut using part of the ashlar blocks from the exedra. Today, however, due to thorny bushes, the tomb is hardly accessible.
descriptions.NUR16151: The tomb shows a rectangular chamber completely blocked by fallen stones and covered with vegetation. In the space immediately in front of the tomb are stones clearly belonging to the exedra wall, some in their original positions. Given its current state, it is difficult to determine its dimensions.
descriptions.NUR12614: A prehistoric burial of the Nuragic period. Unfortunately, the tomb has been partially demolished by herders to build a sheepfold.
descriptions.NUR11738:
The burial is located on the southern slope of a gentle declivity. Part of the funerary chamber is visible, and about 3.50 m from it, two blocks partially buried, likely elements of an exedra, are discernible. The tomb has unfortunately been disturbed by unauthorized excavations that affected the rear section.

This section, as far as it can be seen, is composed of granite slabs of medium size, well-shaped on the exposed wall face, arranged as orthostats.
descriptions.NUR9875: In an advanced state of abandonment, the curtain wall oriented east-west is still visible, constructed with medium-sized stones set in cut joints. Only faint traces of a possible exedra remain. Notably, a baetyl stone is present, bearing several holes whose meaning is unknown, if not linked to a female essence. mu
descriptions.NUR18918: Of the tomb only the dentilled ashlar and a monolithic arch belonging to the apsidal section remain.
descriptions.NUR8292: On the site there are as many as two giants' tombs of modest size, largely stripped of the stones that originally composed them. The exedra and the burial chamber are still discernible.
descriptions.NUR12233: Of the aforementioned tomb, only a few foundation stones remain, together with a nearby stele, suggesting that there may have been a giants' tomb.
descriptions.NUR9867: Very ruined: vertical orthostats (with transverse cuts) and the tumulus closure and part of the exedra can still be identified.
descriptions.NUR11972: The burial, located near two nuraghe and a village, still preserves the tomb structure. It includes a burial chamber constructed with granite blocks of various sizes, shaped obliquely on the exposed face and arranged in irregular courses using wooden wedges for support.
descriptions.NUR12395: Coursed (coursed) giants' tomb, located in the south-western part of a hillside. Of the tomb, only the external wall face, the entire funerary corridor including the floor slab and a head slab with a door (stele?), most of the eastern arm of the exedra, and a stone with circular recesses placed outside the masonry remain.
descriptions.NUR20297: The cemetery consists of three corridor tombs and two giants' tombs without stelae. Further details are provided in the document "Recovery of archaeological sites in the territory of Castiadas".
descriptions.NUR9869: Although reduced to ruin, some basic elements can be identified that highlight the structure of the emergency. The cist is formed with a varied stone masonry, fairly squared, upon which some covering elements are placed. The presence of the exedra, composed of stones set in a cut, is also evident, although some of them have been destroyed and lie on the ground. mu
descriptions.NUR1479: It is located on the slope to the north-east of Monte Sozu, directly beneath Su Casteddu where the homonymous nuraghe stands. It is the largest giants' tomb in our Chiaramonti area. The lithic burial cist is about 15 m long and is composed of stones of various shapes, roughly shaped, and is covered by large trachytic slabs laid flat. Mu
descriptions.NUR10189: Few remaining walls and many uncertainties: frequent help from the historical memory of the elders and the presence of only a few basal remains of the homonymous nuraghe. mu.
descriptions.NUR16146: It has a particular form, because part of it is built upon a huge stone that has been partially cut out and adapted to a funerary function.
descriptions.NUR15228: Dated to the 13th century BCE. Belongs to the Albucciu nuraghe. In this tomb, the rectangular body, composed of flat slabs, is surrounded by a tumulus of rubble. The exedra reduces to a series of blocks and small slabs, which diminish the monument's grandeur typical of other megalithic burials. Notable is the wall thickness of the tomb, about 6 metres. The structure has undergone modifications in different periods and has been reused several times.
descriptions.NUR20111: It is probably a coursed giants' tomb in very poor condition: it is almost indistinguishable from the surrounding rocks; only the ashlar stones at the sides of the central door, the funerary corridor, the courses on either side of this corridor, and part of the outer walls are discernible. It is clear that many of the stones that formed the central body and the vault have been removed and scattered around the tomb or dropped into the central corridor.
descriptions.NUR20009: The orthostats of the large exedra without a stele stand out. It is broken and lies scattered on the ground in front. In place of the stele, an olive tree has grown. A small fragment of the exedra remains at the back, set on a pedestal, which allows an understanding of the monument's original scale.
descriptions.NUR998: The Nissardi in 1901 (map included in G. Pinza's volume) indicated a giants' tomb slightly south-west of the Paule Tolta nuraghe: a nuraghe that actually lies within the perimeter of the airport.
descriptions.NUR12420: From the tomb, the slabs of the burial chamber and a small portion of the external wall face on the east side are exposed; the chamber has been partially excavated by unauthorized individuals, who also carried out a digging in the burial fill between the left wall of the burial chamber and the row of stones of the external wall, mistakenly believing that the two walls enclosed a second adjacent burial chamber.
descriptions.NUR10130: Only faint traces of the original perimeter outline of the cist remain, but unmistakable evidence of its former presence. Many of the stones were transported to Castelsardo for the reconstruction of the ancient Medieval Cathedral. mu
descriptions.NUR10342: Giants' tomb dating to the Middle Bronze Age (14th century BC). In very poor condition of conservation, located very close to the homonymous nuraghe, better known as N.ghe Gorroppu.
descriptions.NUR12419: About 500 metres from the homonymous nuraghe
descriptions.NUR6458: Known as a nuraghe, it is instead an excellent example of a giants' tomb with an associated ceremonial circle. Facing east is the dolmenic exedra that opens into a rectangular lithic cist. From the sides of the exedra extend large stones cut to form a circular arrangement used for ceremonies.
descriptions.NUR12593: Or at least what remains. During the reconstruction of the Sibiri road, the structure was partially destroyed to allow a more direct route. In practice, the curves of the original alignment were removed and the tomb was destroyed. Today, only a section of about two metres remains. In short, a victim of "progress".
descriptions.NUR18425: It is located within the territory of the comune of Collinas. The Regional Commission for Cultural Heritage of Sardinia, by its own Decree no. 155 of 14 December 2017, has declared the site known as "Nuragic tomb of Sa Terra de Su Muru" of particular archaeological interest.
descriptions.NUR10190: A few but clear remains of a giants' tomb. The mound still partially in situ, together with two pillars embedded in a dry-stone wall. The surrounding area is rich in Nuragic remains. mu
descriptions.NUR10132: Reduced to a level of ruin like so many other cases of neglect. I regret repeating myself, but the disappointment of facing a cultural heritage that is not protected and that is not taken seriously places upon me a civic duty to publicly denounce this disregard.
descriptions.NUR10133: Few remains of TdG. The site, heavily anthropized from distant epochs, is presumed to be very rich, like the nearby Pisciu Accas. mu
descriptions.NUR10234: A burial of the Nuragic period built of polygonal trachyte blocks. Little of the tomb is visible because of the vegetation; the corridor and part of the exedra survive. From what the remains and the vegetation allow one to see, the mound has walls of roughly dressed blocks and a final cut stone. It is of interest as the only one of its type known so far: the ashlar with three holes in which three small baetyls were placed during religious ceremonies. mu.
descriptions.NUR10233: The area is heavily anthropogenically modified from ancient times. The site's significance is evident from the numerous surface exposures and the distinctiveness of these features, which are not found elsewhere on the island. Currently, a project focused on the architecture of the Giants' Tombs is under study, with researchers preparing a specific book on the subject.
descriptions.NUR16569: In poor state of conservation, the corridor and several squared stones that originally were meant to form the entrance are still visible.
descriptions.NUR10193: A burial of the Nuragic period constructed with polygonal trachyte blocks. Of the tomb, little visible due to present vegetation, only the corridor and the exedra remain. From what can be seen through the remains and the vegetation, the two arms (in straight alignment) that border the exedra are composed of two overlapping curtain walls of different widths, with a bevel that presumably served as a seat. mu.
descriptions.NUR10188: The surrounding territory has always been heavily anthropogenically modified, and sites are numerous throughout. Often, and this is the case in the few visible remains, it is difficult to determine the exact typology.
