The proof remains of the historical memory of the elders, who retain an indelible recollection of their existence. mu
descriptions.NUR12639:
Important giants' tomb near Sant'Antonio di Santadi.

It appears to be in good condition.

I do not know its name, but it is certainly of great historical significance. Discovered by cross-referencing data from several maps.
descriptions.NUR21111: Feature whose plan is not easily interpretable
descriptions.NUR10199: Modest in overall scale, almost a little treasure; it consists of two walls of nearly squared stone masonry and has a roof made of large natural trachyte slabs.
descriptions.NUR16896: We find it at about 30 metres perpendicular to the secondary road of SS 131, in a state of complete abandonment.
descriptions.NUR18877:
The giants' tomb lies to the south, about 500 metres from the nuraghe; only part of the inner wall face of the chamber and traces of the peristalith are visible.

In an area of about 2000 sq m around the giants' tomb, numerous structures are visible of which only the basal courses remain; in particular a wall stands out that encloses a roughly rectangular area, inside which there are traces of various types of rooms, some semicircular but mostly quadrangular.
descriptions.NUR11723: The Giants' tomb is located about fifty metres to the south of the Nuraghe Figu. Part of the tomb's structure and a small portion of the exedra are visible.
descriptions.NUR21178: Very damaged and difficult to read. Probably dolmenic. It is likely that on the stele there was a dentilled stone typical of the TDG, placed on top of the entrance.
descriptions.NUR11935:
The T.d.G. is covered by a dense layer of stone slabs, and outside only one covering slab resting to the north can be seen.

A rock shelter opening into a massive granite boulder and featuring a spacious cavity with a wide main entrance, bordered on the sides by two orthostats and already partially closed. The main interest arises from geometric figures in the exposed rock forming the floor of the shelter, schematic anthropomorphic figures on the back wall.
descriptions.NUR20330: Next to the provincial road remains a low row possibly belonging to a giants' tomb, whose typical structure is clearly visible.
descriptions.NUR9180: Located on a small elevation in the countryside of the commune, not far from the new provincial road "Ussana, Donori, Barrali". It is a prehistoric wall structure discovered during a survey beneath a heap of debris. The wall segment is straight, 4 metres long and 80 centimetres wide, built with large stones, of which only the highest course is visible. It could also be a side of a tomb of the same period.
descriptions.NUR21177: Circumferential giants' tomb with an acute vaulted corridor, of red granite. The slabs closing the vault are missing. Nearby, the ashlars appear to belong to the abside. The exedra has been destroyed.
descriptions.NUR10870: Two blocks of the exedra are visible, the inner right wall of the chamber. Illyscavated illegally and damaged.
descriptions.NUR8101:
Also known as "Sa Domu 'e s'Orku", it is built of local granite blocks laid in "cyclopean style". It has the unique feature of being oriented exactly to the north.

This giants' tomb is of the "coursed façade" type, typical of the giants' tombs of southern Sardinia; the façade and the exedra, 10 m wide, are built in megalithic masonry; on the right-hand side of the exedra there are three "ritual hearths", circular in shape.
descriptions.NUR13949: The giants' tomb of Iscrallotze is particularly eroded. In appearance, what remains suggests it belongs to the category of dolmenic giants' tombs.
descriptions.NUR11635: Giants' tomb, nuragic, with a corridor and a partial portion of the exedra.
descriptions.NUR13994:
An interesting monument in the territory of Villanova Monteleone, oriented south-west; part of the exedra is still visible, but unfortunately no trace of the stele remains. The well-preserved corridor, built of well-squared trachyte blocks, is 7.10 m long and 2.80 m wide; two slabs laid flat still survive of the roofing.

To the left of the monument a setting of stones covered by a slab can be seen, perhaps a dolmen.
descriptions.NUR9487: The monument, aligned NW–SE, has a rectangular body (length 15.90 m; width 4.60 m), vaguely apsidal at the rear, with a funerary corridor flanked by two pairs of facing niches; of the exedra (chord 5.60 m; arc about 15 m) only the left wing survives in part. But the most interesting feature of this tomb is the presence of the four niches in the corridor, which probably served to hold funerary offerings.
descriptions.NUR8738:
Practically unknown and inside a private property. The monument, excavated and cleared in recent times, is perfectly legible and defined in all its components: the corridor, which preserves its intact floor of granite slabs, the apse and the two wings of the exedra.

It lies to the west of Santa Reparata.

The structure is built on a very slight rise with the exedra clearly raised. A linear bench is present in the front part of the exedra, a feature often found in other giants' tombs.
descriptions.NUR2650: Giants' tomb completely collapsed, with only a few ashlar stones remaining and its location difficult to determine.
descriptions.NUR15382: Around the structure extends a large settlement of circular huts, while at a short distance two giants' tombs are present. There is also evidence of an ancient well, of which today no trace remains.
descriptions.NUR12177:
A burial of the Nuragic period.

The monument is in very poor condition of conservation and it is not possible to define its constructive type. On the ground a line of stones (probably belonging to the exedra) is visible, while the final section of the corridor is barely discernible, buried under a thicket of brambles.
descriptions.NUR8739: The Lu Brandali complex nuraghe consists of a nuraghe with an outer wall, a village, a giants' tomb, a series of "tafone" tombs, and shelters beneath rock. To reach the Archaeological Site of Lu Brandali from the traffic light on Via Nazionale in Santa Teresa Gallura, one turns left towards Capo Testa, after about 700 m; on the left-hand side, the main entrance is accessed.
descriptions.NUR11622: Only the base of the tomb is visible, and what remains is almost entirely covered by vegetation.
descriptions.NUR20373: Giants' tomb marked in an article by Gallura Oggi, already included in the Geoportal, alongside which a windmill has been erected.
descriptions.NUR10917: Collective burial of the Nuragic period. Of the monument, hidden beneath the thickets of Mediterranean scrub that cover it, only the corridor, the exedra, and inside this the dentilled ashlar stele that once adorned the front remain identifiable.
descriptions.NUR13390: Circled giants' tomb heavily collapsed, with part of the corridor and lintel remaining. The monument features a "filari" type, consisting of a burial constructed from courses of stacked blocks, with a elongated burial chamber in rectangular plan, preceded by an entrance, followed by a dromos, and ending in an abside.
descriptions.NUR13334: A striking dentilled ashlar with three teeth is visible, upon which, likely, the three baetyls representing an unidentified Sardinian triad were set.
descriptions.NUR20299: The TdG consists of two walls, each about 15 m long. Destroyed by tomb robbers. Location uncertain.
descriptions.NUR9181: Giants' tomb located within a large olive grove.
descriptions.NUR9483: Nearby, and in close association with the nuraghe Miuddu, just a hundred metres to the south-east, lies a giants' tomb that exhibits the typical funerary architectural layout: a semicircular exedra (arc m. 10.05 – arrow m. 2.25), a slightly apsidal rectangular body (length m. 9.75 – width m. 0.25), and a rectangular burial chamber (length m. 4.60 x width m. 0.80 x height m. 0.75 on filling).
descriptions.NUR13674:
It is a burial with a rectangular corridor cut into the rock and equipped with a calcareous slab flooring.

The chamber walls are built with marl ashlar, originally bonded with mud mortar, arranged in horizontal courses, which on the upper part of the wall face show an oblique exposed surface. No trace of the semi-circular exedra remains.
descriptions.NUR11726:
Giants' tomb of the orthostat type in the region of wall ramparts, Muracalzos.

A nuraghe is also present nearby, Muracalzos.
descriptions.NUR14728: The arched stele of this giants' tomb, lacking an entrance lintel, must have rested directly on the posts that mark the entrance. Alternatively, it could have rested on a lintel, which would have added greater grandeur to the monument.
descriptions.NUR20020: Giants' tomb, of which only a very small portion remains, almost completely destroyed.
descriptions.NUR12159: It is a tomb with a rectangular burial chamber clearly in a state of degradation, almost entirely covered by moss and difficult to identify; the chamber is about 15 metres long.
descriptions.NUR12821: Partially hidden by the Mediterranean scrub, the tomb is oriented in a north-south direction, with an exedra facing south, of which about three courses remain, composed of large granite blocks in a quadrangular form arranged in alternate rows, with a surviving height of 90 cm.
descriptions.NUR9485:
The tomb, of dolmenic type and oriented to south-east, features a semicircular exedra (arc m. 9 – arrow m. 3) delimited by orthostatic slabs, a rectangular apsidal body (length m. 6 – width m. 4), and a modest funerary corridor (length m.  3.70 x width 0.75).

Currently, the northern side and the right arm of the exedra are incorporated into a dry stone wall.
descriptions.NUR9486: Of the megalithic tomb, very well preserved until the 1970s, only the northern façade and the right arm of the exedra remain, partially; a short section of the burial chamber is also discernible, while at a few metres' distance some enormous slabs, which formed the flat-laid roof of the tomb, are visible.
descriptions.NUR19743: The tomb, because of the collapse of its side structures and the lush vegetation that covers most of it, does not clearly show its layout. However, some ashlars still in their original position suggest a rectangular plan. At the sides and in the surrounding area there are heaps of earth mixed with boulders and rubble that probably belonged to the tomb structure, clear signs of the violation carried out by clandestine diggers.
descriptions.NUR21125: Random location. Tomb mentioned in the Master's thesis by Annalisa Uccheddu 1995, UNICA, located within the Villa Siotto Park. The tomb is svettata and buried. Original length probably about 10 m. Illegally excavated with removal of the covering.
descriptions.NUR21127: Random location. Tomb mentioned in the Master's thesis by Annalisa Uccheddu 1995, UNICA. Situated on land bordering the Villa Siotto Park. The tomb has no cover, is partially buried and devoid of vegetation. Length of about 7 m.
descriptions.NUR9480: The lower border of the stele, slightly trapezoidal (dimensions: 1.02 – 1.05 m, height: 0.98 m), features a border that runs along three sides (width: 0.16–0.18 m, top line; from 0.18 m to 0.13 m on the vertical sides), raised to a height of 0.35–0.15 m. The slab's thickness varies on the two sides: on the left, along the lower edge, it measures 0.34 m; 0.40 m at the top and 0.56 m in the middle section; on the right, it decreases from the base (59 cm) to the top (32 cm).
descriptions.NUR15064: Tomb with corridor and semicircular exedra
descriptions.NUR9635: The tomb is almost buried under a substantial mound of earth and stones. The basal orthostats follow almost the entire perimeter: a semi-circular exedra (arc 10.40 m – chord 3.80 m) flattened on the south-east side with arms surviving for 6.66 m on the right and 4.45 m on the left; a rectangular body 10.60 m long and 4.20 m wide where it meets the exedra wings; a burial corridor (length 7.20 m – width 1.10 m) bounded by upright slabs.
descriptions.NUR9481: The tomb follows the usual architectural layout: elongated and apsidal body (length 14.50 m – width 4/4.30 m), a wide curved exedra (current arc 11.70 m – arrow 3.25 m) and a rectangular corridor (length 11.55 m – average width 0.10 m and 0.55 m at the entrance). In summer 1982, excavation and partial restoration of the monument were carried out.
descriptions.NUR21010: A burial of the Nuragic period. Of the monument, in poor condition and partly hidden by vegetation, only the funerary corridor, the exedra and numerous shaped ashlars remain, showing that the tomb was of the coursed type in isodomic masonry. The ashlars, very carefully made, include the so-called dentilled stele of considerable size, and an element of uncertain definition on which one face has a framed, raised boss.
descriptions.NUR11434: The tomb currently features only a corridor aligned along the SE-NO axis, bordered by orthostats and open on the shorter sides, now destroyed. Although no secure elements remain to determine the entrance's location—only a trench excavation could clarify whether it opened on one or the other side—it is plausible to assume that the entrance, in line with typical features of such tombs, faced south-east.
descriptions.NUR9631:
Of the megalithic burial, of isodomic type and oriented to south-east, the funerary corridor (length 4.20 m – width 1.05 m) can be measured, consisting of four blocks per side and one per headpiece, all finely worked; the design of the exedra and that of the tomb's body, however, remain indistinct.

Among the scattered stones in the area of the exedra there is a dentilled ashlar: it has a trapezoidal shape (dimensions 1.85 x 1.15 x 0.75 m in height), slight beveling, and the usual three vertical recesses.
descriptions.NUR20033: 'Perdas de Fogu' on the slope of a small hill contain the remains of a giants' tomb built with large calcareous stones. The burial chamber is polygonal with an entrance to the south where part of an exedra with a 12.10-metre circumference is visible. The chamber is preserved for a length of 6 metres, a width of 1.20 metres, and a height of 0.50 metres.
descriptions.NUR15741: Of the monument, largely destroyed, the funerary corridor is visible, composed of polygonal blocks finely finished on the exposed sides.
descriptions.NUR21150: Only the central corridor of the structure remains. Surrounding it are scattered ashlar stones, but not immediately assignable to the tomb.
descriptions.NUR10879: The tomb is set into a rocky slope. The funerary corridor is 7.65 m long. Lacks an exedra. Excavation revealed artifacts dating to the Roman period and below the Nuragic period.
descriptions.NUR19651: The tomb shows clear signs of illicit excavation; its structure is hard to make out because most of it is covered by vegetation and soil. The chamber is rectangular and partly buried at the rear; an apse may be present. On the sides and at the back of the tomb there are fallen boulders that certainly belonged to the tomb. Even though it is hidden by the scrub, the wall of the exedra is visible, following a curved course.
descriptions.NUR12236: The site is located in the territory of the comune of Nuoro, in the industrial zone of the city. The structure is partially ruined, but some stones that likely formed the exedra and part of the burial chambers are still visible. The characteristic "U" shape of the megalithic tomb is still discernible.
descriptions.NUR21146: It is a report by an enthusiast, verified by an archaeologist. It appears to be a giants' tomb or a corridor dolmenic, hitherto unknown.
descriptions.NUR13527: The site is located at the centre of a livestock farm. It is a dolmenic tomb arranged along a north-south axis with an entrance to the south-east; the burial chamber tapers towards the back and is open at the front in a large semicircular exedra.
descriptions.NUR1336: The cista is formed by medium-sized stones set vertically into the ground. There is a single stone that closes the cista; previously, the presence of a baetyl is noted.
descriptions.NUR8658: Also known as "Sa Grutta de Santu Giuanni", it presents the classic planimetric layout of giants' tombs. The burial chamber (22.10 m²), arranged along a north-south axis with an entrance to the south, is surrounded externally by rows of granite blocks of varying sizes. The façade remains partially excavated and cluttered with rubble.
descriptions.NUR10874: The tomb was built with large blocks still partially buried and with exposed faces mostly straight. The exedra is no longer visible and the position of the door can only be hypothesised.
descriptions.NUR20149: Unfortunately, very little of the tomb remains: today the central corridor of the burial chamber can still be made out, its walls once formed by courses of stones laid neatly as in nuraghe corridors; the stones that framed the central doorway are also present, together with many other stones scattered all around. Finally, a single stone slab (or orthostat) survives which, set in a row with many others, formed one of the two wings of the exedra.
descriptions.NUR12077:
The megalithic burial is located less than 200 metres to the south-east of the Nuraghe Pattada, which stands at a higher and more dominant elevation on the edge of a steep cliff overlooking a vast trachytic formation.

The monument, built with isodomic masonry, features an exedra with courses and an architrave entrance, repeats the common planimetric layout typical of burial monuments: a rectangular body with an apsidal rear section and a semicircular exedra in front.
descriptions.NUR9815:
About twenty metres north-west of the large tomb described in record no. 50 lie the remains of a second megalithic burial that has been largely destroyed by a dry-stone wall cutting across it transversely.

Only a short stretch of the rectangular body can be measured (4.30 m long – 3.20 m wide); the construction technique uses orthostats, while several large overturned slabs inside show that the roof was flat-laid.
descriptions.NUR8760:
A few kilometres from the village of Uri, a tall stone stele stands in the middle of a field, giving the site its name: Sa Pedra Longa (The Long Stone). In the past it formed the front of a Nuragic giants' tomb, dating to the Middle Bronze Age (about 1700–1350 BC).

Of the original monument only the monolithic arched stele (cut from a single block of rock) survives; its type and relatively modest dimensions suggest an early date.
descriptions.NUR6890:
A semi-circular exedra oriented to the south-east, bounded by large orthostatic slabs; an elongated body (length 6.15 m – width 3 m at the junction with the exedra – and 2 m in the terminal section) with a burial chamber 4.43 m long and 0.55 m wide.

In the centre of the exedra the lower part of the bilithic arched stele is visible, truly majestic (width 1.10 – thickness 0.22) with a trapezoidal doorway (width 0.24 – height 0.20).

Another arched fragment of the stele lies overturned on the tomb.
descriptions.NUR12307: Only the floor, composed of large stones, a few peripheral stones, and clearly visible exedra remain.
descriptions.NUR9633:
The remains of the megalithic tomb lie next to a dry-stone wall that follows the railway line, just 200 metres south-east of Birori station.

Seven surviving slabs of the semicircular exedra (chord 9 m – rise 2.40 m) are visible on the ground, as is part of its outer perimeter (length 9 m – width 4.50 m); nothing can be said, however, about the burial corridor and the arched stele, whose existence can be considered certain.
descriptions.NUR9634: The only evidence of this megalithic burial is the presence of numerous shaped ashlars of various forms incorporated into a dry-stone wall for a length of about 200 metres. All these monoliths are remarkable for being perfectly worked and shaped, indicating that the destroyed tomb was of isodomic type. Among these stones, most of which have lifting recesses, a monolithic arch is of particular interest (arch span 1.72 m – rise 0.80 m – height 0.68 m).
descriptions.NUR21132: Uncertain location. Illegal excavation. The excavation extends for about 5 m. An apse is visible at field level.
descriptions.NUR11642: Arched stele of a Giants' tomb known as “S'Artare de su Moro”; the base of the stele remains in situ, while the upper part has been broken and incorporated into the wall of the hut.
descriptions.NUR19685: Located at a short distance from the small church of San Giacomo, this tomb is severely damaged due to illegal activities; however, some particularly monumental features are evident in the way the material was worked. The structure is completely built with isodomic granite blocks.
descriptions.NUR8977: Giants' tomb dating to the Middle Bronze Age with a likely Bilitic stele belonging to the giants' dolmenic tomb, partially buried
descriptions.NUR15614: Completely dislodged structure, the original form of which is barely discernible.
descriptions.NUR12762: This dolmenic tomb, from the pre-Bronze period, is in excellent state of preservation, as it retains almost intact the funerary corridor with a flat-laid roof, i.e., composed of stone slabs laid horizontally along the corridor walls. The large stele is a monolithic arched structure, with a small access opening cut into it to reach the burial chamber. The exedra still retains some stones set in place as they originally were.
descriptions.NUR9812:
Of this megalithic tomb, which must have been closely associated with the homonymous nuraghe, only a fragmentary upper portion of the arched stele remains.

The monolith, currently embedded within one of the many dry stone walls interweaving near the Serbine nuraghe, measures 1.68 m in height and 1.15 m in maximum width; the outer border defining its profile is 0.11 m wide.
descriptions.NUR19797: The tomb is hidden by vegetation, blocked by fallen boulders and earth. Despite the collapse, the entrance can be identified and faces east. The exedra and the apse are hard to make out, also because of the violation by looters. For the exedra, the few clues are some semi-worked stones still in their original position at the sides of what remains of the probable entrance. To the rear, boulders arranged in a semicircle formed part of the apse.
descriptions.NUR19799: The tomb has a rectangular apsidal chamber, with the exedra and entrance facing south. The chamber was built of boulders of various sizes, only roughly dressed, bonded dry with packing wedges. The tomb has certainly been violated by looters; the burial chamber is covered by vegetation and filled with collapse stones and earth. On the east side of the tomb there are collapse boulders that certainly belong to the monument. The west wall is hidden by vegetation.
descriptions.NUR18120: The giants' tomb is located in the municipality of Romana; the remains of the burial are visible today embedded in a dry stone wall.
descriptions.NUR13439: The giants' tomb S'iscra and Lottoni is of dolmenic type, from the pre-Bronze Age period, and is in good state of preservation, as it retains almost intact the funerary corridor with a flat-laid roof, i.e., composed of stone slabs laid horizontally along the corridor walls. The large stele is a monolith with an arched form, in which a small access door has been cut to lead into the burial chamber.
descriptions.NUR12436: Giants' tomb completely embedded in the undergrowth, never apparently excavated and totally collapsed. Only a few isodomic ashlar stones remain from the inner wall of the corridor...
descriptions.NUR9048:
The burial — of the coursed type with an arched stele — partially preserves the apsidal tomb oriented to the east and built with medium-sized polyhedral granite and porphyry blocks. The short internal corridor, rectangular, has walls composed of orthostats at the base upon which three courses of roughly hewn blocks are placed; the floor is formed by exposed rock.

The burial dates to about 1500 BC.
descriptions.NUR9844: Almost certainly present up to the 1960s, when major land improvement and land reorganization works were carried out. The toponym of the area, "su crastu covaccadu", suggests the presence of a trilite or a set of flat slabs forming a possible cover for a burial tomb. mu
descriptions.NUR14239:
The Written Boulder, carved.

Giants' tomb at Santu Micheli whose stele is framed, precisely, by a low-relief border.
descriptions.NUR19688: The tomb is small in size and built using an orthostatic technique. It was destroyed by illegal excavations; during the excavation and restoration works carried out in 1996, fragments of a uniquely shaped, carved bowl were recovered, a type not previously known in Sardinia. In 2008, several vitreous paste beads were also recovered.
descriptions.NUR10067: In this case we are once again confronted with traces of a dolmenic structure, though it is preserved only in the memory of the elders. On the site remain clear traces of construction resembling a dolmenic structure. The cyclopean stones involved are disordered and registered in a haphazard manner as a result of land improvement works.
descriptions.NUR21137: Giants' tomb of Deruta. Located just 50 m from another Giants' tomb in better condition, on which the municipality has carried out minor interventions for cleaning and improved accessibility.
descriptions.NUR20264: Giants' tomb of Deruta. Located just 50 m from another Giants' tomb in better condition, on which the municipality has carried out minor interventions for cleaning and improved accessibility.
descriptions.NUR8306: The giants' tomb Su Niu de su Crobu is located on a rocky elevation, not far from the sea, in the area Sa corona de su crabì. The burial, of the "coursed" type, consists of a funerary corridor with an apsidal end, about 10 m long and averaging 1.20 m wide; the stones forming it are only minimally worked, arranged in irregular files and consolidated with numerous pegs.
descriptions.NUR21124: The tomb without a cover has an external profile of the central body with concave wall faces. The exedra has curved arms. The burial chamber is oblong. A row of infill stones along the apse is visible.
descriptions.NUR8334: Located on a plateau adjacent to the Rio Caddare, the tomb is situated at a short distance from the site of Lettu Rucratu. The burial, which prior to excavation and restoration work showed significant damage caused by mechanical equipment that had removed parts of the chamber and exedra, was constructed using an orthostat technique. The site has yielded materials datable to the early BM period.
descriptions.NUR11964: Giants' tomb with a cyclopean corridor in good condition, while the exterior appears buried and partially eroded.
descriptions.NUR12212: The giants' tomb Su Pranu est is not in an optimal state of preservation, but its fundamental components can still be made out. In the facade only a few blocks of the exedra remain in their original positions; at the centre stands the monumental monolithic arched stele, which has the peculiarity of lacking a doorway. The stele is now broken in two, uprooted and lying overturned on the remains of the chamber. The tomb can be dated to the beginning of the Bronze Age, about 1800 BC.
descriptions.NUR20281: Tomb built of roughly hewn calcare ashlar. Part of the exedra and the corridor remain. The lintel above the door is still in situ.
descriptions.NUR19965: The tomb is completely covered by vegetation; some blocks aligned can be seen through the grass. The presence of another tomb at the site is noted, possibly belonging to a heap of blocks visible among the vegetation.
descriptions.NUR8567: The Giants' Tomb is located beside a river and is largely destroyed. A portion of the open corridor is still visible. The area is interesting because it is rich in springs. Nearby the Giants' Tomb are several nuraghes. It is situated at the foot of Bruncu Salamu, where there are numerous springs, sacred wells, and the Nuraghe Sa Dom'u S'Orku.
descriptions.NUR21173: Three metres of approach, a lintel at the west, a row of external blocks; particularly interesting is a block with a large cup. There would be another section of approach, but it is not accessible and even less documentable due to trees.
descriptions.NUR6897: The walls are composed of rubble masonry of varying and medium-sized stones, roughly shaped, with cyclopean stones cut and embedded in the ground closing one end. The coverings are megalithic, some of which remain in situ while others have been removed due to land improvement works.
descriptions.NUR16899: Simple to find and difficult to understand, due to its cover in REINFORCED CONCRETE, which only the local administrators can comprehend, plus its pitiful state of abandonment. It appears the giants' tomb was used as a powder magazine during the construction of SS131; hence, it was equipped with a reinforced concrete cover and a metal door, now no longer present.
descriptions.NUR14174: The great burial at Zanchia shows the lower part of the bilitic stele still intact, while the upper part lies reclined upon the other stones of the tomb corridor.
descriptions.NUR12959: It was a large stone cist, dug into the ground, oval in shape, with walls lined by stone slabs; inside it contained the remains of 15 inhumations and various items that formed part of the funerary equipment, typical of the Early Bronze Age (Bunnannaro culture).
descriptions.NUR8925:
Giants' tomb dating to the Middle Bronze Age. Located in the immediate vicinity of the Sa Sinèpida equipped area.

With a possibly Bilitic stele of the giants' dolmenic tomb, partially buried
descriptions.NUR11752: Collective burial of the Nuragic period. The monument is built in isodomic masonry with basalt elements finely squared and finished, found both in their original orientation and incorporated into the dry-stone walls of the surrounding enclosure. The burial chamber is visible through its corridor, with the terminal slab at the end, the exedra with the central slab through which the entrance portal is cut, and the dentilled lintel.
descriptions.NUR11753: Collective burial of the Nuragic period. The monument is adjacent to the tomb of Battos I and repeats both its typology and the high quality of its basalt elements, which are well-cut and finely finished, though the site is not equally well preserved. Among the fallen stones, the corridor and the exedra can still be identified, while in the apsidal area two monolithic arches are present. On the ground, dentilled ashlar is visible.
descriptions.NUR11754: Collective burial of the Nuragic period. The monument, of large dimensions, is barely legible in plan as it is almost entirely buried. Parts of the orthostatic structure visible include the external wall face and the exedra, together with fragments of the large arched stele scattered over the monument.
descriptions.NUR18895: Less than 100 metres south of the nuraghe lies a small giants' tomb, of which only the funerary chamber remains, composed of large granite orthostats, together with traces of the external wall face and the peristalith.
descriptions.NUR18897:
The second giants' tomb, located 100 m to the south-west of the nuraghe, instead features a narrow corridor 6.5 metres long, without a roof, with only part of the peristalith visible, and to the left of the entrance, an orthostat about 1 m high and traces of an exedra.

About 500 m to the west of the nuraghe there is an area where fragments of curtain walls and surface material emerge, probably dating to the Roman period.
descriptions.NUR12205:
A burial of the Nuragic period.

Of the monument, almost destroyed, only the funerary corridor remains, composed of two parallel alignments of ashlar stones projecting from the ground. Other ashlar stones are visible in the immediate surroundings.

The construction technique of the tomb was isodomic, made with finely shaped ashlar stones.
descriptions.NUR11755: The Giants' tomb at Brebeghenieddu is located about 400 m north of the Nuraghe Columbos at Sedido. The lower part of the stele has been repurposed as a wall of a cottage now collapsed and roofless. Behind the stele, part of the funerary corridor is visible.
descriptions.NUR18743: Of the monument, currently destroyed, only some worked ashlar stones remain, indicating that the tomb type was coursed in isodomic masonry.
descriptions.NUR18735: Of the monument, currently destroyed, only some worked ashlar stones remain, indicating that the tomb type was coursed in isodomic masonry.
descriptions.NUR11318: Structures belonging to a giants' tomb built of local basalt. The funerary structure stands on a small rise overlooking a small river valley, between the nuraghi Campu Scudu and Piricu (Santu Lussurgiu). Some blocks of the funerary corridor and part of the outer wall face remain visible. The tomb is oriented east–west and survives for a total length of about 8 m. In the front part a few displaced blocks can be seen that originally must have formed part of the exedra.
descriptions.NUR17910:
A burial of the Nuragic period constructed with polygonal blocks in limestone laid in courses.

Although partially covered by vegetation and fill soil, the plan is clearly visible, including the apse and the exedra, whose arms have a straight configuration. On the front, at the entrance portal, a rectangular slab lies on the ground, which may represent the lintel of the entrance.
descriptions.NUR15645: Giants' tomb, cut-down, belonging to the same named nuraghe and village
descriptions.NUR12190:
A burial of the Nuragic period. The monument, though partially concealed by vegetation, retains a discernible external profile, the funerary corridor, and the right arm of the exedra.

The construction technique involves regular courses using polygonal blocks that are slightly squared.
descriptions.NUR6761: Very little of the tomb remains. The baetyls are five and are located in the territory of the comune of Dualchi (NU).
descriptions.NUR10005: The site is located in the Planu Is Ciaexius plateau, in the Sarcidano, central-southern region of Sardinia. The megalithic tomb of Aiodda, which follows the classic layout of giants' tombs, was discovered during agricultural works. The entrance, facing east, is preceded by a large semicircular exedra composed of calcare orthostats, about 6 m in width.
descriptions.NUR12410: "Giants' tomb of Araene, in the long chamber the side stones are visible and large slabs form the roof. In Carta Luca, it was Luigi." From Taramelli's description, the giants' tomb of Araene must have been the best preserved among those in the territory of Lodè; unfortunately, the monument was destroyed in relatively recent times, as a result of the usual agricultural land reclamation works, which spared nothing.
descriptions.NUR11082: Giants' tomb in very poor condition; the chamber is still clearly visible, the exedra is partially incorporated into the boundary wall. Located inside a small enclosure a short distance from the country church of Santa Cristina. Easily accessible.
descriptions.NUR14688: Located at a short distance from the Durane river, the tomb features a burial chamber about 9 metres long and a large exedra along its length measuring 14 metres. It is entirely built of granite with ashlar laid in regular courses. The central section has an entrance portal topped by the so-called "dentilled ashlar". The large exedra, equipped with bench-seats for pilgrims to rest, contains, to the east, a small baetyl, which must have been the object of cult practice.
descriptions.NUR18889: About 150 m from the Bigozzi nuraghe, in a north-western direction, lies the giants' tomb, bearing the same name. Built on a small platform made of small stones, the burial preserves the funerary corridor composed of granite orthostats; the roof is missing and the apsidal slab lies on the ground, while only a short section of the exedra, located outside, remains visible.
descriptions.NUR16990:
A collective burial of the Nuragic period.

Of the monument, hidden beneath a mass of mastic trees, only the apsidal area and the terminal section of the corridor remain visible.
descriptions.NUR11526: It is located in the area of Capichera (Arzachena – OT), near a winery producing the fine Vermentino wine. In the immediate vicinity lies the complex nuraghe of La Prisgiona.
descriptions.NUR10721:
It is located in the territory of Goni (CA).

Although signage highlights the presence of a giants' tomb, the architectural type (the monument features two opposing apses) is not well attested in funerary contexts.

It could be a cult enclosure.
descriptions.NUR17768: Only some stones remain of the tomb.
descriptions.NUR11958: Funerary structure of the Nuragic period. The monument is fairly well preserved and still reveals its various components: corridor, apse, and exedra.
descriptions.NUR18900: 100 metres to the south-east of the nuraghe, traces of a giants' tomb are present: some slabs emerge from the ground belonging to the burial corridor.
descriptions.NUR19078: The layout is quite imposing: it measures a total of 22 m; the exedra has a circumference of 18 m and almost all the stones remain, set in a sharp, pointed fashion, some of which are very tall. The funerary corridor is 16 m long, 1.30 m high, and 1.40 m wide; it is covered by horizontal slabs, one of which is missing, revealing the interior of the tomb, which has a rectangular cross-section.
descriptions.NUR11741: The burial is located at the south-western edge of a plateau used for agriculture and grazing. It is situated about 1.50 metres to the north-west of the homonymous nuraghe and a few hundred metres to the south-east of the open-air station at Ruinacchèsos. The monument has an entrance facing north-west, with some blocks of the exedra located nearby. The funerary chamber is about 3.55 metres long and has a rectangular plan.
descriptions.NUR19341:
1. Of the monument, unusually close to the reference nuraghe, only a fragment of the burial corridor emerges from the soil.

2. The monument, currently destroyed, reveals only some worked ashlar stones, indicating that the tomb type was coursed in isodomic masonry.
descriptions.NUR12632: The tomb, located beside a narrow path and built with courses of large stones, features an exedra facing south and a gallery partially damaged. Nearby, scattered stones and large rubble heaps are visible.
descriptions.NUR11439: Described by Lamarmora and Mackenzie, who had seen it almost intact, at least in plan, and defined by Pinza as “the façade of the most beautiful giants' tomb known in Sardinia”, the giants' tomb at Imbertighe is now reduced to only the arched stele and the arms of the exedra composed of three rows of stones.
descriptions.NUR10800: Giants' tomb completely collapsed, with the most significant elements missing. It retains the burial corridor.
descriptions.NUR11488:
The tomb was built in several phases. The first dates to the Early Bronze Age, when the Bonnanaro culture was widespread in Sardinia (about 1800 BC). At that time the tomb must have looked like a cist dolmen covered by a mound.

In the Nuragic period the site was reworked into a giants' tomb by enlarging the burial chamber and adding the exedra, composed of 14 slabs among which the central stele, with its entrance, stands out at almost 4 metres high.
descriptions.NUR11537:
The tomb is built with coursed masonry. The tomb body contains a rectangular funerary corridor, closed at the far end by a single shaped head slab with an arched top.

The exedra survives only in part: the hemicycle is bounded by orthostatic slabs of reduced size, at the base of which runs a low bench-seat, also incomplete, intended to receive offerings.

The rear wall face of the exedra joins the tomb body without a break.
descriptions.NUR18515: Located in a position somewhat detached from the funerary complex of Madau, despite the few visible structures and modest dimensions, it appears to retain the characteristics (and thus possibly also the construction period) of the "larger sisters". Of the tomb, currently partially buried by sediment, only the exedra and part of the corridor are visible.
descriptions.NUR11618: Giants' tomb completely collapsed, with only faint traces remaining
descriptions.NUR10619: The tomb is in excellent state of conservation, both internally and externally; its façade, built with medium-sized blocks precisely squared and laid with accuracy, features at its centre a low rectangular access door (about 50 cm wide and 60 cm high). The burial chamber, reaching a height of about 1.80 m at its highest point, is very well preserved, including the apse that closes the back of the chamber.
descriptions.NUR16356: Currently it has been largely buried prior to carrying out interventions for its preservation.
descriptions.NUR10632:
The site located at 520 metres above sea level, Sa Murta 'e Pizzus, is beautiful and picturesque, being nestled in the greenery and quiet of a region scarcely disturbed by human activity. Numerous granitic rocks of a grey-pink hue have been carved by the passage of time, and from the hilltop one can see the Gulf of the Angels.

Near this funerary complex there are some stones marking the circular perimeter of some nuraghic huts.
descriptions.NUR10458:
The distinctive features:

the complete absence, at the entrance of the tombs, of the exedra; the resemblance to an upturned ship's keel that can be seen or compared with funerary monuments called "navetas", typical of the Talayotic civilisation of Minorca and the Balearic Islands.

These large structures are built of limestone slabs laid in courses that corbel progressively further inwards towards the top, and the roof was formed by a series of slabs serving as lintels.
descriptions.NUR10459:

the complete absence, at the entrance of the tombs, of the exedra; the resemblance to an upturned ship's keel that can be seen or compared with funerary monuments called "navetas", typical of the Talayotic civilisation of Minorca and the Balearic Islands.

These large structures are built of limestone slabs laid in courses that corbel progressively further inwards towards the top, and the roof was formed by a series of slabs serving as lintels.

The distinctive features:

the complete absence, at the entrance of the tombs, of the exedra; the resemblance to an upturned ship's keel that can be seen or compared with funerary monuments called "navetas", typical of the Talayotic civilisation of Minorca and the Balearic Islands.

These large structures are built of limestone slabs laid in courses that corbel progressively further inwards towards the top, and the roof was formed by a series of slabs serving as lintels.
descriptions.NUR16214: Of the monument, currently destroyed, only some worked ashlar stones remain, indicating that the tomb type was coursed in isodomic masonry.
descriptions.NUR18791: Of the monument, currently destroyed, only some worked ashlar stones remain, indicating that the tomb type was coursed in isodomic masonry.
descriptions.NUR17909: Tomb of which the orthostats of the corridor emerge from the ground. No stele or exedra are visible.
descriptions.NUR8294: The tomb was restored in 1993, using and repositioning the exedra and other orthostats, some of which were deteriorated or broken but still in situ. The monument, which shows two distinct construction phases, was built during both phases in the Early Bronze Age and was used for funerary purposes only during the first phase of occupation.
descriptions.NUR11626: Interesting giants' tomb with a bilitic arched stele, of which only the lower part with a door remains. The exedra and the burial chamber are also present.
descriptions.NUR11877: Dug in 1996–97. Nearby, numerous menhir statues were found, some of which are partially preserved at the Samugheo textile art museum.
descriptions.NUR12206: It is a giants' tomb with a collapsed structure and in relative abandonment.
descriptions.NUR12533: At the foot of the hill, once used as a stone quarry, within the inhabited centre of Monastir, in the south-western area, near Via Progresso no. 80, a giants' tomb was discovered during archaeological excavation, yielding numerous human bone remains.
descriptions.NUR11613: The tomb, of dolmenic type and aligned along a west-east axis, preserves only the burial chamber and part of the exedra with the large arched stele; the external profile of the tomb and thus its thickness are not discernible. It was noted by Lamarmora, who in the Atlas documents the already broken stele as it currently appears.
descriptions.NUR17167: Remains of a giants' tomb, of which the base courses remain.
descriptions.NUR11646: Nuragic dolmen burial, with the funerary corridor remaining, composed of finely finished basalt slabs, without steles.
descriptions.NUR17265: It is in poor conservation condition. Position verified with GPS.
descriptions.NUR11722: The burial is located on the flat summit of Planu Borgolo, about 50 m east of the SS131 road, which separates it from the surrounding settlement context. Of the tomb, only the burial layout and the funerary corridor—formed by several large orthostats, especially at the terminal end—are still visible; only some elements remain of the exedra.
descriptions.NUR11925: Giants' tomb, dolmenic, completely exposed, with only a trapezoidal stele and part of the original exedra remaining
descriptions.NUR12203: A burial of the Nuragic period with isodomic masonry. Of the tomb, partially demolished, only the burial corridor, the apse, and some elements of the left arm of the exedra remain.
descriptions.NUR10647: Remains of the megalithic construction were revealed during a survey at the nearby Perdu Lodde nuraghe by a local shepherd.
descriptions.NUR19474: Giants' tomb Sa Canna, in the Sàrrala area of Tertenia but administratively belonging to one of the many enclaves in the zone (39.61237 N 9.63864 E). This was my first encounter with a tomb built of schist, a stone used only sporadically for this type of monument. It is of the coursed type, considered more recent than the 'dolmenic' or 'arched stele' type, and has an elegant exedra — although it lacks the dentilled ashlar characteristic of the more refined examples — standing 2.55 m high at its apex. The tomb shows some gaps due to clandestine disturbance (the missing ashlar from the left arm of the exedra is clearly visible), which prevent the exact width of the semicircle from being determined, though it can be assessed as having a slight curvature. The chamber, not very large, is 6.75 metres long measured at the outer threshold and 6.40 metres at the inner threshold, and is distinguished by a perfect ogive with a descending height from 1.95 m at the entrance to 1.40 m (presumed, since the clandestine excavation has disturbed the basal paving) at the rear, where traces of ancient plastering seem to be detectable (unless this is due to a neoformation of clay caused by the loss of the corridor's waterproofing — which, on the other hand, remains intact for almost its entire length). The entrance doorway is trapezoidal (50 cm wide at the base and 60 cm at the top), 57 cm high, and easily passable. This is therefore one of the tombs in which it is clear that access from the top of the corridor was not possible, as most island archaeologists maintain (on the other side of the 'barricade' stood the great Ercole Contu, who in my opinion took a more scientific approach to the question), since there is no possibility of removing any ashlars from the corridor to allow such hypothetical access. The tomb almost certainly belongs to a settlement located about 500 metres away as the crow flies, on another saddle of the same ridge, of which only a few remains can be identified today: a non-canonical type of nuraghe and a few surrounding traces attributable to huts (the area is also known as Serra 'e Mari, and a boundary stone — the municipalities concerned are Lanusei and Arzana — was placed on the nuraghe in 1953).
descriptions.NUR10346: Collective burial of the Nuragic period. In very poor condition of conservation.
descriptions.NUR11460: Right next to the village of the electric company there are two nuraghes and this exceptional giants' tomb, belonging to the site known as Pira Onne. Here too there is a stele with three recesses for housing the three figures of the Trinity, which usually stood on the exedra of a wall composed of horizontal courses; the stones are slightly squared.
descriptions.NUR9751: The giants' tomb Sa Fache e s'Altare is a corridor tomb with an arched stele.
descriptions.NUR12175:
The tomb was part of a funerary complex originally composed of four megalithic burials placed in close proximity to one another and near the nuraghes Ilòi and Logula.

The present road alignment has divided the small necropolis of giants' tombs, built according to the villages along a transhumance route. It is a dolmenic tomb, originally equipped with a bilitic arched stele with a door at its base, placed at the centre of the exedra.
descriptions.NUR12176:
The tomb was part of a funerary complex originally composed of four megalithic burials placed in close proximity to one another and near the nuraghes Ilòi and Logula.

The present road alignment has divided the small necropolis of giants' tombs, built according to the villages along a transhumance route. It is a dolmenic tomb, originally equipped with a bilitic arched stele with a door at its base, placed at the centre of the exedra.
descriptions.NUR16871: Giants' tomb in miniature, very small
descriptions.NUR11442:
Located at a short distance from the rural chapel of S. Gavino and about a hundred metres to the north-northeast of the Nuraghe Toscono, with which it shared close cultural ties, the tomb of Santu Bainzu is of dolmenic type with a monolithic arched stele, arranged along the SE-NO axis and featuring an entrance to the south.  

Detected by Lamarmora, who in his drawing still shows the orthostats of the exedra in situ, whereas they are no longer present in a later planimetric sketch made by Mackenzie.
descriptions.NUR18118: Giants' tomb in a state of complete abandonment, located just a few dozen metres from the nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR10588: Of the two giants' tombs, both relatively eroded, the burial chamber and the exedra are identifiable.
descriptions.NUR10587: Of the two giants' tombs, both relatively eroded, the burial chamber and the exedra are identifiable.
descriptions.NUR11715: Of this burial only the stele and part of the exedra remain.
descriptions.NUR12411: The giants' tomb at Sas Melas is located about 200 metres by air distance from the homonymous nuraghe. The tomb is completely buried and is in very poor conservation condition; only a few orthostats emerge, barely a few centimetres above the surface.
descriptions.NUR11029: The giants' tomb of "Sa Sedda 'e Sena", known as "Sa Tanchitta", is notable for having been built in the Nuragic period and later adapted to an even older funerary structure dating to the Early Bronze Age (1800–1600 BC) of the "Covered Alley" type. Of this funerary monument, the burial chamber, about 10 metres long, can still be observed today.
descriptions.NUR11372: Two giants' tombs adjacent, from two different construction periods. The first is of dolmenic type, the second is coursed (with opposed courses).
descriptions.NUR11373: Two giants' tombs adjacent, from two different construction periods. The first is of dolmenic type, the second is coursed (with opposed courses).
descriptions.NUR11881: Apart from the two monumental giants' tombs, unique and clearly visible and of exceptional craftsmanship, three other tombs have been identified. For those familiar with nuragic buildings and urbanism, this means the existence of a community of several hundred people who had the need to multiply their cemeteries.
descriptions.NUR11880: Apart from the two monumental giants' tombs, unique and clearly visible and of exceptional craftsmanship, three other tombs have been identified. For those familiar with nuragic buildings and urbanism, this means the existence of a community of several hundred people who had the need to multiply their cemeteries.
descriptions.NUR21003: Feature covered by vegetation of indistinct nature
descriptions.NUR11742:
Dimensions: h. 1.50 m; len. 10.50 m; wid. 1.40 m;

The tomb is situated on a small elevation whose gentle slopes are currently used for vine cultivation. The left side of the exedra remains, composed of large blocks decreasing in size from the entrance towards the lateral ends. The missing portion of the stele features an interesting device for its insertion, namely, a granite block shaped to have supported the stele.
descriptions.NUR12396:
Hidden among the vegetation, only a small part of the tomb remains.

The filar type and the walls of the burial chamber employ isodomic masonry technique; the monument, oriented to south-east, has a total length of 7.60 m, measured to the edge of the exedra, and a maximum width of 3.15 m. Partially visible are a portion of the tomb and the exedra.
descriptions.NUR11736: The tomb, located about 300 metres to the north of the homonymous nuraghe, is in good state of preservation. The entrance, facing east, provides access to a rectangular chamber about 10 metres long and 1.20 m high, composed of well-shaped ashlars laid in regular courses.
descriptions.NUR8637: The monument is named after the ancient name of the area where it is located (Nixias) and the unusual hole positioned on the right side of the large stele, which was believed (perhaps incorrectly) to have been used in historical times to tie horses. The monument is of great interest as it represents a rare example of a giants' tomb with a centinated stele in central and southern Sardinia.
descriptions.NUR11627: The construction was carried out in two phases. In the first phase, dating to the Bonnanaro culture period, a covered allée tomb—a type of elongated dolmen—was built; subsequently, around 1600 BC, it was transformed into a giants' tomb with an exedra and stele, some traces of which you can admire.
descriptions.NUR15762: A burial of the Nuragic period, only faintly legible in its plan. Only a fragment of the arched stele remains.
descriptions.NUR11643: What remains of a dolmenic giants' tomb completely collapsed, mainly consisting of the vertical elements and the surrounding foundations.
descriptions.NUR12413: "Giants' tomb of Torrà, near the tributary Rio Torrà of Rio di Posada; few remains of a large cist or corridor can be seen, almost completely dismantled. On land belonging to Antonio Nanu, it was Giovanni." With this brief description and some geographical inaccuracies (the Riu Thorra is not a tributary of the Posada but of the Mannu, which is in turn a tributary of the Posada river), Taramelli reported the presence of the giants' tomb of Thorra, without however mentioning the nearby nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR18192: Apart from a large worked slab, nothing of the probable tomb remains, except a heap of stones.
descriptions.NUR12204: The burial of the Nuragic period is currently crossed longitudinally by a dry stone wall and is not fully legible in its planimetric development. Nevertheless, the western perimeter and the lower division of the bilitic stele can be identified.
descriptions.NUR10709: The tomb extends along a north-east/south-west major axis 5.50 m long and has its entrance opening to the south-west at the centre of a semicircular exedra that has almost entirely disappeared. The rear apse was probably straight-sided, but the closing masonry has not survived. It should be noted that the tomb is still largely buried, giving the impression that what is currently visible is actually the uppermost courses, lacking their covering.
descriptions.NUR11466: A burial of the Nuragic period. Of the monument, partially hidden by vegetation and collapse debris, only the outer perimeter, the funerary corridor, and part of the exedra remain visible.
descriptions.NUR6800: It consists of three baetyls of truncated-conical shape, about 1.5 metres high and with a diameter of about 60–80 cm, located on the right side of the tomb. The central baetyl, from an undated period, was overturned and transformed into a basin.
descriptions.NUR15657: A burial of the Nuragic period, almost completely destroyed. On the ground surface, the base profile of the tomb is visible, along with some worked ashlar stones. In particular, a short distance away, two monolithic arches belonging to the apsidal section of the tomb are present.
descriptions.NUR15660: Only traces of the structure remain, as it has been completely dismantled.
descriptions.NUR18703: The tomb retains only a small section of the first base course along the side of the colonial house; in the vicinity of the monument, two granite slabs of small and medium size are found, suggesting fragments of a stele.
descriptions.NUR12191: The tomb, of dolmenic structure, is now only discernible in the funerary corridor, the entrance, and the right arm of the exedra. Just emerging from the ground, a row of medium-sized stones forms the left side of the burial chamber.
descriptions.NUR18812: Of the monument, currently destroyed, only a single ashlar with a curved profile belonging to the apsidal area remains, indicating that the tomb type was coursed in isodomic masonry.
descriptions.NUR16987: Collective burial of the Nuragic period. The structure has been largely destroyed. Some alignments of stones relating to the corridor and the exedra help to identify the layout of the monument.
descriptions.NUR16985: Collective burial of the Nuragic period. The monument is completely covered by a layer of mastic but the terminal section of the corridor is still visible.
descriptions.NUR16982: A collective burial of the Nuragic period. The structure is hardly observable because, in addition to being embedded within the usual lentisco soil, it is also covered by small stones resulting from the erosion of the surrounding terrain.
descriptions.NUR16981: A collective burial of the Nuragic period. The structure has been largely destroyed, as well as covered by vegetation and rubble.
descriptions.NUR18652: The monument is almost entirely destroyed and very little of its planimetric layout remains visible on the ground. Nevertheless, evidence of the tomb's existence is confirmed by a fragment of the arched stele found in the dry stone wall adjacent to it.
descriptions.NUR12338: Giants' tomb, dolmenic, partially collapsed, with only the perimetral orthostats and a lapidary lintel remaining.
descriptions.NUR12337: Giants' tomb, dolmenic, partially collapsed, with only the perimetral orthostats and a lapidary lintel remaining.
descriptions.NUR8580:
It consists of an apsidal corridor set on an exedra with a narrow bench. In the centre is a small lintelled doorway with jambs and a threshold. The roof is a pointed vault.

Excavations have uncovered the remains of numerous human skeletons, deposited one on top of another, evidence of its use as a collective burial, whose size is also the origin of the name. Tradition holds that these burials must have belonged to gigantic beings.
descriptions.NUR18921:
A burial of the Nuragic period in very poor condition of conservation.

The corridor and, with difficulty, the exedra are visible in the isodomic masonry type.
descriptions.NUR11889:
A burial of the Nuragic period. Of the monument, the external profile, the funerary corridor, and the exedra can be observed.

The construction technique is regular courses using polygonal blocks slightly squared.

The tomb is notable for its unusually south-western orientation, as well as its very close proximity to its reference nuraghe (about 25 m away).

The monument is located within the territory of the comune of Villagrande Strisaili (OG).
descriptions.NUR11025:
It is also known as Sa Pinnettedda.

The circumstances of its discovery and the materials recovered place the monument chronologically at the end of phase II of the Nuragic civilization (1500–1200 BC),
descriptions.NUR10875: The tomb is svettato and consists of an orthostatic structure in courses. Part of the exedra, the architrave portal, the funerary corridor, and part of the apse are visible. Length about 12 m.
descriptions.NUR10862: A burial chamber of about 11 m in length remains. The tomb is missing its top. The exedra and the abside are still visible.
descriptions.NUR11021: The Giants' Tombs of Mont'Ollastu (Villamassargia) have been the subject of past archaeological excavations and have yielded ceramic artifacts visible at the Archaeological Museum of Cagliari.

descriptions.NUR15347: Man-made structure submerged by the artificial lake
descriptions.NUR15351: Man-made structure submerged by the artificial lake
descriptions.NUR15353: Man-made structure submerged by the artificial lake
