descriptions.NUR15357: Man-made structure submerged by the artificial lake
descriptions.NUR1943: The remains of the funerary structure are completely covered by a layer of mastic. A circular hut built in the contemporary period on top of the tomb's remains is visible, with part of an exedra composed of five basalt stones arranged in a semicircle.
descriptions.NUR14771:
The tomb is in poor state of conservation, hidden by vegetation, and only recently has a fire partially revealed the structure.

The most visible component is the exedra, particularly the lower division of the bilitic stele, while the corridor is marked by several stones emerging from the ground and a covering slab.
descriptions.NUR10861: The tomb is missing its top; it has a rectangular plan and shows no traces of the apse. Its length is about 12 m. Currently, some blocks of the left arm of the exedra, the entrance, and the perimeter wall can be identified.
descriptions.NUR10860: Svettated tomb with walls emerging only a few centimetres. Width of about 4.50 m, calculable length of about 7 m. A burial chamber, an apse, and an external perimeter wall are discernible.
descriptions.NUR18646: A burial of the Nuragic period, of dolmenic type, built with lithic orthostats inserted vertically and covered with horizontal slabs. The tomb's corridor is visible, while the elements of the exedra are likely incorporated into the dry-stone wall built along the front. On the front, lying upside down and, unfortunately, fragmented, is the beautiful arched stele.
descriptions.NUR17208:
Only shaped ashlars of the monument can be identified, from which it can be established that the tomb was of the coursed type in isodomic masonry.

Some of the ashlars (perhaps those belonging to the exedra) are incorporated into the walling of a recent hut, and others lie scattered nearby, hidden by vegetation. In particular, the so-called dentilled stele of considerable size is present.

The baetyls now placed in the forecourt of the Church of Santa Caterina appear to come from it.
descriptions.NUR17210: It is in poor conservation state, severely damaged by excavation and earth movement. It retains in the apsidal area a baetyl with a single "ocular" opening, not fully defined.
descriptions.NUR17225: Of the monument, in isodomic masonry in courses, the funerary chamber, a corridor defined by some dentilled ashlars well connected, the apse and part of the exedra remain. A dentilled ashlar, though probably damaged, might constitute the so-called "dentilled stele".
descriptions.NUR11639: Part of the monument retains the funerary corridor; six courses of stones remain on the right side and only two on the left, with a maximum length of 7.70 m and a width of 1 m.
descriptions.NUR15743: There are three giants' tombs, of which the first is the most important and in the best state of preservation.
descriptions.NUR14241: The tomb is built in isodomic masonry with a faceted wall of courses. The funerary body is thick and symmetrical, apsidal, and slightly tapers to a semicircular exedra marginated by seats, exposed to the SSE. Of the monument, in local basalt, the following remain: the base course of the funerary chamber, parts of the base slabs of the façade and the seat bench, and a good portion of the external vaulted cover composed of monolithic arches.
descriptions.NUR11645:
Funerary structure of the Nuragic period.

Entry form to be completed.

The monument is located in the territory of the comune of Norbello (OR).
descriptions.NUR11638: Of the monument only the corridor tomb remains, which has five courses of stones to the west and six to the east, with a maximum length of 7.40 m and a width of 1 m.
descriptions.NUR18914: Two giants' tombs, probably associated with the nearby Prizzada nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR16979: Collective burial of the Nuragic period. The monument, like the other tombs in the area, is in very poor conservation conditions. It is possible to identify the corridor formed by two parallel rows of stones and to detect, in some sections, the external profile. Some regular ashlar stones, inserted into the dry-stone walls surrounding it, may belong to the tomb.
descriptions.NUR15736: Almost entirely destroyed, the monument's external outline and the exedra are still visible on the ground. On the ground, some dentilled and shaped ashlar stones are present, with their faces exposed, indicating that the tomb type was coursed in isodomic masonry. During the last visit to the site (January 2012), it was noted that the two so-called dentilled stelae that previously stood adjacent to the burial have disappeared.
descriptions.NUR11968:
A burial of the Nuragic period. A monument of considerable dimensions, in good state of conservation, fully legible in all its components except the entrance area, which has now been restored and contains two residual fragments of the original stele.

The construction technique is of the coursed type, using polygonal granite blocks.
descriptions.NUR11971:
The monument is in a fair state of preservation despite the roots of the holm oak that overshadows it undermining its stability.

The burial corridor, built of polygonal blocks in courses, still retains almost all of its roofing, while the tomb body is defined by the mound that covers it. The exedra of dolmenic type is more clearly legible, although it lacks the stele; it consists of orthostats set vertically into the ground.

enclosed by a dry-stone wall.
descriptions.NUR11969:
A burial of the Nuragic period. Of the monument, the tomb structure, partially covered by surface soil, the funerary corridor, and the exedra are identifiable.

The construction type is coursed, using polygonal sub-squared granite blocks.
descriptions.NUR11970: A burial of the Nuragic period. The monument, of small size, is identifiable only by the funerary corridor, while the other parts (still buried or destroyed) that composed it are not visible.
descriptions.NUR10919: Giants' tomb Sa Grutta 'e Su Bandiu
descriptions.NUR11653:
A burial of the Nuragic period. The tomb is completely embedded in a lentisk thicket, but among the vegetation the terminal section of the burial corridor can be identified.

The monument is located in the territory of the comune of Sedilo (OR).
descriptions.NUR15732:
Of the monument, practically destroyed, only the funerary corridor remains, consisting of a depression in the ground, and numerous shaped ashlar stones that indicate the tomb was of a coursed type in isodomic masonry.

Among the ashlar stones, carefully worked, one can observe the so-called dentilled ashlar of considerable size, and a monolithic arch related to the apsidal area.
descriptions.NUR17726: The giants' tomb is located in the south-west direction relative to the homonymous nuraghe, of which only the tomb corridor remains.
descriptions.NUR15754:
The monument is located about twenty metres from a second giants' tomb and about 200 metres from the homonymous nuraghe; it is not detectable in the external perimeter due to its poor state of conservation.

A fragment of a coursed stele (height 0.46 m; width 1.25 m) with a relief border, 12 cm wide on the left and 15/17 cm wide on the right, was probably used in this tomb and has been repurposed in the pavement of the nearby church of Santa Sabina.
descriptions.NUR15751:
The site is located about 200 metres from the homonymous nuraghe.

The tomb has been partially dismantled with the removal of all the dressed ashlar that once lined the burial chamber.

Nevertheless, despite its poor state of preservation, the planimetric layout typical of this type of tomb can still be discerned on the ground: a rectangular body with an apsidal end at the back, a semicircular exedra at the front, and a rectangular burial chamber.
descriptions.NUR10916: Collective burial of the Nuragic period. The monument, adjacent to a nearby road that may have caused its damage, is covered by vegetation, but the corridor and the stone wall structure—composed of sub-squared granite ashlar in courses—can still be observed.
descriptions.NUR11649: Giants' tomb immersed in vegetation and eroded
descriptions.NUR12300: The giants' tomb at Sa Presone 1 features a semicircular exedra with a front of courses. On the right side of the burial chamber, raised and covered by slabs, there is a small niche above the floor, used for placing offerings or a deceased person in a curled position.
descriptions.NUR12299: Sa Presone 2 today preserves only traces of the chamber. Among the scattered stones around it, a dentilled ashlar with three recesses has been identified.
descriptions.NUR12298:
It is practically destroyed. The few remains that allow it to be identified consist of two courses of stones, just emerging from the ground, that define the tomb corridor. In the area of the exedra (itself more guessed at than actually present) lies the so-called dentilled ashlar, not in its original position; its presence indicates that the burial was built with squared ashlars laid in courses, like the nearby Sa Presone II.

The monument lies in the municipality of Bultei (SS).
descriptions.NUR17720: The monument retains a large portion of the internal corridor. It is possible to identify what was the external wall face up to the exedra, whose right side is visible, while on the left only two vertical stones remain near the entrance. At a short distance lies the megalithic stele, unfortunately cut, and what appears to be the closure portal.
descriptions.NUR15616: Giants' tomb, of which the base ashlar stones remain, one slab of the stele, and one from the abside.
descriptions.NUR15618: Coursed tomb, the shape of which is difficult to determine.
descriptions.NUR21184: Giants' tomb built of basalt ashlar
descriptions.NUR20332: The tomb is covered by enormous flat lithic slabs, including one longer than four metres.
descriptions.NUR18816: Collective burial of the Nuragic period. The monument has recently been uncovered after the vegetation that had covered it was cut away. In addition to the corridor, composed of stone courses, the lower partition of a large stele remains.
descriptions.NUR11030:
A burial of the Nuragic period. The monument is almost entirely destroyed. On the ground surface, a row of stones that formed the funerary corridor and blocks related to the exedra can still be distinguished.

The most visible element is the terminal slab of the funerary corridor, still in its original position. The construction technique was of the coursing type, using polygonal blocks.
descriptions.NUR18568:
The megalithic monument, 13.5 m long according to 2005 surveys, does not deviate from the traditional model. Access to the long corridor was through a doorway carved in a generally arched stele, flanked on either side by stelae of decreasing height joined together (exedra).

Despite the collapse of the roof, the corridor has been preserved, while the tomb's entrance is covered by a thick layer of mastic, which prevents verification of the stele's integrity.
descriptions.NUR18925:
The monument is in very poor condition of conservation and on the ground only the terminal part of the corridor can be observed.

The construction type was isodomic, with squared and dressed ashlar stones, worked on the sides to be visible.
descriptions.NUR21013: The Nuragic construction lies in a striking area above Lake Flumendosa. It is hard to reach for two reasons: you must find the path that links the Sa Scala e Trinched'assu waterfall to the Sa Ucca 'e is Canis giants' tomb and, above all, locate the tomb's exedra, which is literally submerged by extremely dense vegetation. Almost the entire corridor of the Nuragic construction survives in good condition, except for the final apsidal stretch, which is missing its covering slab.
descriptions.NUR19562: The monument appears to have been severely and indiscriminately destroyed by a highly successful and ruthless dismantling. Below the numerous ashlars stacked and covering the structure, it seems possible to distinguish the corridor and one arm of the exedra. Among the ashlars—crafted with great care and indicating that the tomb type was coursed in isodomic masonry—one can observe the so-called dentilled ashlar and some curved-profile elements related to the absidal zone.
descriptions.NUR11714: A burial of the Nuragic period of the so-called isodomic type. Of the tomb, practically destroyed, only the external wall face and the terminal stone of the corridor remain visible. A few other squared and well-finished stones, visible in the surrounding area, are scattered nearby.
descriptions.NUR12936: The tomb, of dolmenic structure and now very ruined, preserves only part of the funerary corridor and the external outline, as well as some orthostats from the exedra, which is entirely destroyed. Among the stones lying overturned in the area of the semicircle, one slab measuring 2.50 m in length, 1.25 m in width, and 0.80 m in thickness stands out for its dimensions: it is possible that this slab forms part of a stele with an arched top.
descriptions.NUR18922: Collective burial of the Nuragic period, of dolmenic type. Of the tomb, now completely destroyed, only part of the exedra and the apse remain legible, while some fragments of the arched stele are present both on the front and in the surrounding area.
descriptions.NUR12036: Of the monument, of the coursed type made of polygonal granite blocks, the corridor and part of the external profile of the burial chamber are visible.
descriptions.NUR10762: Near the nuraghe Arrubiu are located two giants' tombs, one of which yielded a sword.
descriptions.NUR10710: It was built right at the base of the rocky outcrop on which the nuraghe Is Berritta stands. The only visible portion is perhaps the apsidal section, while the exedra has not been identified.
descriptions.NUR11459:
A burial of the Nuragic period.

Almost no description is needed as it is clearly visible in the satellite image.

The construction technique is of the coursing type and it should be noted the alignment towards south-west, a feature not very common among the domus de janas.
descriptions.NUR18911:
At the foot of the hill on which the nuraghe Su Gattu stands, the remains of a granite burial are visible.

Of the giants' tomb only a portion of the apse and part of the rectangular chamber, bounded by large granite stones, remain, while externally the remains of the peristalith project.
descriptions.NUR15393: Giants' tomb belonging to the same named nuraghe. Very poor state of conservation.
descriptions.NUR7511:
A nuraghe, a menhir, a wall, and finally a domus de janas with façade.

Ivano Sotgiu, devoted to his own village, wandering through asparagus fields, signals this site where, within a short stretch of just a few hundred metres, monuments dating to the Abealzu culture, 2700 and 2400 BC, possibly predating the menhir, appear in the early Bronze Age with the nuragic wall, through the Bronze Age, and up to the Roman period, marked by probable tombs.
descriptions.NUR7144: The tomb consists of a single chamber with a central pillar, while various niches and a funerary bed with powder deposits at each end are carved into the walls. It is believed to date back to the late medieval period. Currently, the tomb is undergoing consolidation work that prevents access.
descriptions.NUR6842: Three menhirs of decreasing height and size, representing a triad or "a family". The menhirs are set upon a lapidary circle.
descriptions.NUR10192: During excavation works for the road connecting Santu Miali to the church of Santa Maria de Aidos, further down, a burial was destroyed, which may have been a giants' tomb or possibly a medieval tomb. Still visible in its original position is a lintel in dark trachyte.
descriptions.NUR15994:
It is in very poor condition.

Probable location.
descriptions.NUR10464: The exceptional nature of the Pranu Siara site lies particularly in the fact that the tomb is not isolated but forms part of an extensive necropolis perfectly aligned for several hundred metres, and surmounted, at the elevation change, by a kind of fortified curtain wall that appears to protect the plain, following settlement patterns known in the north-western area of the island, particularly in the regions of Olmedo and Castelsardo.
descriptions.NUR18884: The megalithic tomb is located further ahead, in a small open area. Of the monument, composed of a short funerary corridor made of rose trachyte slabs, only the base course remains; the entrance is marked by two carefully worked rectangular slabs, while the external wall, following the profile of the funerary corridor, is built with vertical slabs and a fill of small stones.
descriptions.NUR11934: Giants' tomb. It is a giants' tomb with dolmenic cover.
descriptions.NUR8690: A singular funerary monument, a prehistoric burial entirely carved into the rock. Discovered only a few years ago, archaeologists consider it a collective burial belonging to the end of the middle bronze age and thus classify it among the giants' tombs of the Nuragic period. Its structure, however, is completely different from the usual types of giants' tombs, whether coursed or with stelae.
descriptions.NUR20536: Catalogued as a probable Roman-period burial, with a facing. A surface portion of the monument is visible alongside a depression in the ground, featuring a granite lintel and, beneath, three walls composed of small and medium-sized ashlar stones forming a dry masonry. It resembles the shape of a well.
descriptions.NUR12859: Only known burial in the Dolianova area belonging to the Bonannaro culture and dated to 2200–1800 BC. Here, ceramics, two tripods, and a cup were found. The tomb was destroyed during quarrying operations.
descriptions.NUR20067: "On the Luras terrain there are giants' tombs, indeed, there are four of them in the same area, a rare and unique occurrence. This site has been known for a long time; one tomb was almost completely destroyed over the years, and both the superintendence and the municipality were notified, but no one ever took any action" (report).
descriptions.NUR8354:
Collective tombs of the Nuragic period, 1600–1800 BC, built in the final phase of the Middle Bronze Age, 1500 BC, and used until the Final Bronze Age phase, 1100–900 BC.

The elongated burial chamber has side walls of limestone blocks laid in corbelled courses, closed at the far end by a slab set on edge. The outer wall face is apsidal at the rear. The entrance, facing east in Tomb no. 1 and south-east in Tomb no. 2, is preceded by a semicircular exedra space.
descriptions.NUR2251:
A true necropolis of giants' tombs – comprising 4 or possibly 5 burials, two of which have "a stele centinata", all still preserved in good condition.

The main burial features a broad arched exedra – with slightly suggested wings – placed directly on the tomb's body, with no break in continuity, and a wall face with a concave-convex profile.
descriptions.NUR13623:
Four giants' tombs, placed close to one another and in varying states of preservation. They are built with local limestone blocks and measure slightly more than 10 metres in length, except for one.

Due to illegal excavations, an undisturbed stratigraphic context has not been preserved. However, a sequence datable between late Middle Bronze Age and recent Bronze Age has been identified.
descriptions.NUR12537: Site where the oldest human skeletons in all of Sardinia have been found (8500–9000 BC).
descriptions.NUR12188:
It is in poor state of conservation.

This is a proto-nuraghe; the tower survives to a maximum height of 5.50 m.

Within a radius of 400 m there are 3 giants' tombs, one nuragic spring, and 5 baetyls.
descriptions.NUR15770: Two giants' tombs located a few tens of metres apart.
descriptions.NUR10801: The ashlars making up the tomb, largely buried, are of various types: limestone, basalt and even granite can be seen. A hole lets us see several metres of the side walls and a couple of limestone roofing slabs placed to the west. The right-hand side of the exedra is visible, though not clearly because it is buried; I have tried to document it as fully as possible. To the east, beyond a few trees, stands one of the stelae that were placed at the entrance of giants' tombs, at the centre of the exedra.
descriptions.NUR12382: Two giants' tombs located near the homonymous nuraghe and the nuragic village. A dolmen is attested nearby.
descriptions.NUR16881: Of the monument, currently destroyed, only two alignments of sub-squared sandstone blocks emerge from the ground, marking the corridor. The frontal section and the apse are not currently visible.
descriptions.NUR12634:
It is located in the territory of the comune of Decimoputzu (CA).

I° Giants' tomb with stele, dated to the Middle Bronze Age I (XVI–XV)

II° Neolithic tomb

III° Punic burial
descriptions.NUR12235: Two opposite dolmen tombs. One has been excavated and consists of two chambers, with the entrance facing south. The other tomb remains unexplored; the covering slabs are visible, and the entrance faces north.
descriptions.NUR12885: Eneolithic burial discovered accidentally during public works for the construction of the new Cagliari aqueduct. Three furnaces-type tombs were identified and investigated: the first, located at the lowest part of the hill on which the site is developed, left only the excavation chamber carved into the sandstone bed; 5 m to the west of the previous burial, a second tomb preserved intact the vertical well and the furnace-type chamber with an elliptical plan.
descriptions.NUR15000: irregular and buried, whose structure cannot be defined
descriptions.NUR14986: It is located near the Nuragic spring on Musuleu. It appears to be a Nuragic-period structure.
descriptions.NUR19236: In this sacred well, of which no further information is available and which probably went completely out of use, some bronze figures of great importance were found, including the banner above the votive sword and the warrior with a shield and four daggers.
descriptions.NUR19984: A rocky acrocoro, dominating the promontory of Villasimius, Capo Boi, the valley of Campus, Is Cuccureddus, where the Nuragic village once stood, and the Temple of Astarte. Among the recesses, dry-stone walls were built, typical of Nuragic construction. Around, it is easy to find remains of terracotta furnaces and a few Nuragic fragments.
descriptions.NUR8639: Archaeological site of Mont'e Prama, where statues, baetyls, and the linear necropolis of pozzetto tombs have been found.
descriptions.NUR19629: Area where nuragic huts are found
descriptions.NUR19415: Located in the Bèrchida valley, it shows use and occupation from the Nuragic period, with a significant area of surface fragments dating to the medium to late imperial era. The site was inhabited until the 1950s. Among the habitation remains, the ruins of a small religious building stand out; this structure is documented as early as the 14th century.
descriptions.NUR19545: The village, located to the east of the two nuraghes, occupies a large flat area and is composed of several structures. A huts with a gabled roof, of rectangular form, with a vestibule at the front, is in good preservation; a probable circular hut and two enclosures are also present. Currently, the area affected by the village is undergoing excavation, which is uncovering further structures. The structures were certainly reused right up to recent times.
descriptions.NUR19645: In this site the remains of an extensive settlement with an associated cemetery are clearly visible. From the material recovered in this settlement it appears that it was inhabited from the earliest periods of the Bonnannaro, Ozieri, Monte Claro, Campaniforme vessel, and then by the Nuragic, Phoenician-Punic, and Roman peoples. It seems the village was inhabited until about 500 AD and was later abandoned after a fire that caused its destruction.
descriptions.NUR19734: De Chirigu Village, the one to the north-west of the nuraghe of the same name, even though immersed in dense vegetation, shows several clearly distinguishable wall stretches belonging to probable huts, mostly rectangular in shape. At the far end, to the north-north-west, there is a circular structure (diameter about 10 m) that probably served as a meeting hut, against whose south side a rectangular structure is abutted. Numerous pottery fragments from various periods are present.
descriptions.NUR19810:
Sa Pedra de Nunnale – Orune. Village built around the picturesque and colossal tower, with an odd shape, whose base is occupied by the homonymous nuraghe. Although imposing, this single-tower (single-tower nuraghe) appears astonishingly small in comparison to the immense rock that dominates it.

This single-tower (single-tower) nuraghe is constructed with megalithic blocks only roughly shaped, larger at the base.
descriptions.NUR14796: Ugas mentions this site as a probable village and workshop of the pre-Nuragic period. Along the regular furrows of ploughing, still today, fragments of pottery, obsidian, and remains of lithic hammers are found.
descriptions.NUR2407: Single-tower nuraghe and remains of huts and giants' tomb.
descriptions.NUR14881: Nuraghe and village, of which only faint traces remain
descriptions.NUR16203: Among the scattered structures in the area, some remnants of a probable village are visible, consisting of a few courses in certain cases, pseudo-walls, with stones in their original positions and collapses occurring within the perimeter. Unfortunately, due to collapses and the dense, flourishing vegetation composed of olive, mastic, and filarea trees, it is not possible to determine the type or dimensions of the structures. On the surface, numerous ceramic fragments are found.
descriptions.NUR19727:
Located at the base of a hill along the course of the Rio Caddare, in an area characterized by dense vegetation, several remnants of masonry belonging to the settlement emerge from a section of the hill eroded by atmospheric agents; these, however, are not the only testimonies relating to this settlement.

Indeed, by penetrating the vegetation, one can identify on the ground numerous circular structures.
descriptions.NUR17569: Village attached to the nuraghe Lu Padru
descriptions.NUR12864:
At the north edge of Selargius, in the area of Su Coddu, there is an important Neolithic settlement where remains of over 150 huts and village artifacts have been found, suggesting the village extended over 10 hectares.

This represents traces of a Neolithic settlement (about 3,000 B.C.), composed of about thirty archaeological units belonging to the Ozieri/Monte Claro culture.
descriptions.NUR3750: The Nuragic complex of Tamùli is an important archaeological site dating to the Middle Bronze Age (1500–1200 BC). The site was already well known in the first half of the nineteenth century, primarily due to the description provided by the Genoese scholar Alberto Della Marmora in his Voyage en Sardaigne, published in 1840. In the accompanying atlas, he illustrated in detail with numerous drawings the nuraghe, two of the three giants' tombs, the baetyls, and some of the orthostats found on site.
descriptions.NUR5492: The nuragic settlement comprises a hundred circular huts distributed without any apparent order, at regular distances from one another. It is built with regular courses of limestone blocks; the rare trachyte blocks probably come from the nearby Monte Imberi. The huts, circular (diameter about 6/7 m), are mostly currently covered by debris and invaded by dense Mediterranean scrub.
descriptions.NUR14840: It is a hilltop settlement, located near a natural spring, inhabited by Nuragic populations of the Recent Bronze Age (1300–1200 BC), almost completely destroyed due to agricultural works. Surface remains have revealed evidence of metallurgical activity, documented in a storage area containing fragments of panels and copper ingots shaped like bull hides (oxhide), originating from the island of Cyprus in the Eastern Mediterranean.
descriptions.NUR11356:
On site and in the surrounding area there are several alignments composed of large basaltic blocks and at least two large tumuli resulting from the destruction of structures due to past agricultural works carried out in the area.

Oxidized obsidian fragments appear along a path, and in the exposed section corresponding to the left side of the path, north of the Temannu nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR12865: The settlement is characterized by the presence of a settlement, documented by sacks and foundations of huts, attributable to the Nuragic period, particularly the Middle, Recent, and final Bronze Ages, and the early Iron Age. The Recent Bronze Age phases are mainly attested by numerous finds of grey-ardesia pottery made in the 1980s, coinciding with the initial discovery of the site.
descriptions.NUR14819: The pre-storico settlement at Via Monastir-Via S. Giovanni di San Sperate extends over an area in the current north-eastern sector of the modern Campidanese settlement. Identified at several points within the same UGAS; it developed along the inter-fluvial strip between the north bank of the Riu Flumineddu and the south bank of the Riu Mannu, at elevations not exceeding 46 m a.s.l.
descriptions.NUR9529: Likely corridor nuraghe and remains of a Nuragic settlement
descriptions.NUR1889: Village of which only little or nothing remains due to construction, down to the immediately surrounding areas.
descriptions.NUR19412: The village is located on the slope of Capo Su Moru, northwest of Torre Canai. The area is scattered with trachytic stones of various sizes, and in some patches, where the Mediterranean scrub is less dense, fragments of rectangular and circular walls can be seen, indicating the probable presence of a village, if not a temple.
descriptions.NUR18115: SSE from the nuraghe Chentugheddas, at a distance of over 200 m from it, remains of foundations of various circular huts are preserved, forming a settlement whose total surface area cannot be estimated. On the surface, near the huts, a considerable amount of Nuragic period pottery material is observed.
descriptions.NUR15643:
The presence of the village, belonging to the nearby homonymous nuraghe, is attested by the existence of some circular huts and other alignments of stones emerging from the ground.

The settlement is located within the territory of the comune of Macomer (NU).
descriptions.NUR3494: Approximate area of the Nuragic village Codula Manna
descriptions.NUR19538: A village composed of numerous huts, almost all overgrown with dense vegetation that nevertheless allows their partial structure to be seen. In several cases parts of the huts' perimeter walls are visible. On the plateau at the top of the hill there are a few buildings, one of which in particular preserves a rectangular room with a circular enclosure; given its state of preservation it has been used in recent times as an animal shelter. Pottery sherds are present.
descriptions.NUR19732: The adjacent Nuragic village cannot be defined in terms of its layout due to the massive collapse. To the north-west, and about 350 m from the nuraghe, there is a village, which despite being immersed in vegetation and facing a significant collapse, is still visible: it features several huts whose wall structures are clearly visible; it also has numerous cyclopean wall segments defining enclosures of various sizes. Numerous ceramic fragments from different periods are present.
descriptions.NUR16153: To the south-south-east of the homonymous nuraghe stands the village, of which remnants of enclosures and walls are visible. In some cases, what remains of the masonry is rectangular, while in others, the outline is barely defined, appearing circular. It should be noted that almost all the structures are situated under a dense thicket of olive trees.
descriptions.NUR11926:
It is a large settlement, presumably of Monte Claro culture (Cagliari), which spread across Sardinia around the second half of the third millennium BC. At the centre of the area, where land reclamation work took place, only scant remains of the settlement's curtain wall remain; at the two extreme sides, traces of rectangular and circular huts are still visible.

The planimetry in photo no. 6 was provided by the archaeologist who supervised the excavations.
descriptions.NUR14850: Nuragic village of the recent and final Bronze Age I period
descriptions.NUR11309: Mural alignments and remains of structures, among which a hut with a sub-rectangular plan is discernible, remain standing to a maximum height of about 1 m. Constructed from small basaltic blocks laid dry, it features a small arched lintel window. In the area affected by the concentration, modern and contemporary enclosures are present. The area that presumably once housed a settlement extends around the Marzacche nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR16326: According to legend, it was one of the seven villages destroyed because of the beautiful Maria Cadelana.
descriptions.NUR10808: Nuragic village where 32 dwellings were found, excavated deeply into the ground, a nuraghe, a silver mine, and pre-Nuragic artifacts. The site was covered with concrete in the 1980s to create a reservoir for irrigation, which has never functioned.
descriptions.NUR17766: It is a large village, showing a spread of ruins, with nuraghe walls covering an area of about eight thousand square metres.
descriptions.NUR17759: Very little of the village remains, only the ruins of huts are visible, and I believe this was the regular settlement; at a short distance lies the Sanctuary and Temple of the same name, with adjacent the Hut Settlement of nuraghe huts, partly still standing. I think these latter were (Cumbissias), inhabited only during periodic festival days or pagan rituals.
descriptions.NUR20127:
The village is located a few metres south of the homonymous nuraghe, on top of "Su Monte 'e Subra". Once you reach the summit, you are faced with an enormous expanse of stones and ashlar blocks, covering at least two hectares.

As you approach the various mounds, circular, rectangular, and complex structures, long walls and curtain walls begin to emerge. The site has never undergone any excavations.
descriptions.NUR8160: The village includes three sacred wells and a series of circular huts. The best-preserved well lies in the northern sector of the area. Built of medium-sized blocks of local schist, it abuts a small natural rock face to the south-west. Access to the chamber is off-centre relative to the axis of the tholos. The tholos has collapsed on its northern side. The area in front of the entrance chamber is bounded by a series of curvilinear walls at different levels.
descriptions.NUR14875: Today, in the territory of Serrenti, there are at least 12 sites with evidence of the Late Bronze II - Iron I periods (S'Urbale and Genna Maria facies)... Except for one, all the others are settlements that were already active during the Recent Bronze period. Only at Is Arruinalis, Monti Angurdu, and Monti Crastu do we find evidence extending into the Orientalizing and Archaic phases (7th–6th centuries BC).
descriptions.NUR17873: Currently, nuragic huts remain with very little, only heaps of stone in circular and square shapes, probably the result of clearing works.
descriptions.NUR1593: The Nuragic village of Neulè is located in the area of the same name, a few kilometres from the settlement of Dorgali. The site includes numerous intact huts, a sacred well, and a nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR10697: Nuragic settlement at Pidighi, on the rocky hillside around the nuraghe Pidighi, within a radius of at least 50 metres, the remains of the nuragic village are clearly visible among the basalt outcrops and the forest.
descriptions.NUR14978: The village of Sa Muralla, named after the late medieval walls built around the settlement and the castle constructed in 1365, may be linked to the ancient toponym "NURAGONNOS" located at the northern edge of Sanluri's settlement; this latter name likely referred to the hills on which the current village stands, possibly already inhabited during the pre-Nuragic phase of Monte Claro, as suggested by the underground chamber at Cukkuru Poddinis.
descriptions.NUR14833: It is a vast area of archaeological interest and is located near the ruins of a rural chapel, which are visible in the territory of Sanluri just beyond the border with our village. It has witnessed successive settlements from the prehistoric Middle Bronze Age (16th–14th centuries BC) to the Iron Age (9th–8th centuries BC).
descriptions.NUR20356: Village without a nuraghe. From the same area comes a Neolithic dagger with a leaf-shaped blade, as well as a trachyte rose basin with a diameter of 70 cm at the mouth. A bronze storage chamber is noted at Sant' Elia, reported by Giuseppe Atzori, now dispersed.
descriptions.NUR20108: It is located in the same named locality, about 1.5 km by air from SP165. Easily accessible via rural roads, the village covers an area of about two hectares. As one moves through the ruins of the village, various structures are found that occupy the entire territory bounded by the apparent limits of the complex. Some appear to be huts, while others are more extensive and resemble enclosures.
descriptions.NUR2343: The Nuragic complex at Seruci consists of a multi-lobed nuraghe composed of five towers with a central courtyard and a village of about one hundred huts extending over five hectares, located in a strategic position relative to the Gulf of Leone. The village is organized into small quarters connected by pathways and central squares. A particularly noteworthy structure is a large hut, likely used for family head meetings.
descriptions.NUR542: Complex nuraghe consisting of three towers erected in a linear arrangement, built on the rocky tip of Monte Sirimagus, one of which features a well dug into the rock. Surrounding the site is a village with dozens of huts, enclosed by as many as three curtain walls. The site has been extensively disturbed by excavators. At the foot of the mountain is a perennial pond used during the Nuragic period.
descriptions.NUR20036: STESSEI, indeed, almost adjacent to the nuraghe on the eastern side, the remains of a Nuragic village are clearly visible, extending over an area of at least ten thousand square metres, composed of numerous huts partially hidden among stone heaps. Among the huts there are at least three wells (or cisterns).
descriptions.NUR11965: It is a large Nuragic village, currently only a small amount remains; only the presence of mounds and scattered stones around the homonymous nuraghe can be observed.
descriptions.NUR18380:
Comprises one hundred reoccupied nuragic huts in Roman period.

Near the village there is also a nuragic well and it appears that there are some menhirs.
descriptions.NUR11930: Beautiful village surrounded by a megalithic wall.
descriptions.NUR14861: Nuragic village inhabited in Final Bronze II and Iron I, without any nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR19631: The Nuragic village of Grutti acqua is located in the plain facing the complex nuraghe and consists of numerous circular and rectangular huts. Unfortunately, only ruins remain of the huts, and furthermore, almost all are completely overgrown by dense vegetation, which nonetheless allows partial identification of their layout.
descriptions.NUR13475: nuraghe belonging to the type of those from the 14th century BCE; a few dozen metres away lies the funerary zone; the village is divided into two sectors: one residential and the other artisanal. Dozens of circular huts are interwoven among the natural rocks.
descriptions.NUR8745: Possible uninvestigated Nuragic village. The TdG area contained 80 skeletons.
descriptions.NUR19721: Giovanni Lilliu, still a student, reports the presence of twenty huts of circular and elliptical shape, some of which were later excavated, yielding various ceramic materials such as large jars, dishes, copper beads, and a bronze figurine depicting two oxen, found during agricultural work. Despite ongoing surface damage, some wall fragments, large pieces of household goods, and large basalt fragments remain exposed.
descriptions.NUR12736:
Nuragic village near Monte Maiori, located in the territory of the comune of Guspini.

A fascinating site because it is set within the natural landscape. It is undoubtedly adapted by the local shepherds, yet it retains a living history.

It is not the only one in this comune.
descriptions.NUR19855: The probable Nuragic village occupies an area situated to the south-east of Monte Oliena. It consists of various structures, likely reused over centuries. In particular, a structure, heavily damaged, is noted, composed of several rectangular rooms. A number of circular and rectangular huts are also identified, with traces remaining in some cases, including one or two, or even three, rows of perimeter walls.
descriptions.NUR19747: Located at the foot of the named nuraghe – in the south-eastern area – partially hidden by the undergrowth, remains of wall structures are visible, likely belonging to a village. Distinctly visible are: the entrance to a fenced enclosure; the remains of a rectangular hut; and cyclopean walls adjacent to the huts' structures and to those of the nuraghe itself. These structures were almost certainly reused in relatively recent times.
descriptions.NUR5667: An inhabited space is present within the site, on the inner face of the wall, and a so-called dentilled stele from a giants' tomb. The stele, finely carved, was reused in Roman times and attests to the existence of a Nuragic funerary structure of the coursed type, in isodomic masonry, whose original position has not yet been located.
descriptions.NUR21152: Large area belonging to a probable Nuragic village. In the surrounding areas, fragments and other surface finds are easily recoverable. The village extends over a considerable distance to the south from the indicated point and towards the west stream.
descriptions.NUR19670: The probable Nuragic village consists of several huts, from which only fragmentary remains survive. In some cases, walls composed of multiple courses (3–5) of stones of varying sizes remain. Most of the structures are overgrown by vegetation, which has compromised their integrity through growth; when the structures are located in open field, the remains are indistinguishable to the naked eye.
descriptions.NUR14893: Nuraxi – Pauli Onigus shows only a few and uncertain signs of a settlement in its immediate surroundings, while remains of a village are observed at Pauli Onigus, a site located about 200 m to the south, separated by the Riu Cardaxu stream. The extent of the villages, based on surface materials observed, varies almost always between 7,000 and 10,000 m², except in the case of the village of Is Arruinalis, whose remains are mostly from the BFII-FI period and occupy an area of about 4 hectares.
descriptions.NUR12019: Through a wild gully carved by a stream in the porphyritic granite, access is gained to the Nuragic village of Praidas. The remains are in severe disrepair and have significantly collapsed.
descriptions.NUR17280: The village was enclosed by a megalithic wall.
descriptions.NUR16965: The village lies at the foot of Monte Perdas de Fogu, in the locality Sa Costa de su Lurdagu. The structures survive as disordered wall remains; in some cases two rows of boulders are arranged in a pseudo-circular form. All the structures contain fallen boulders and rubble inside, making it difficult to determine their original perimeter and shape. Numerous potsherds of various kinds are visible on the surface throughout the area.
descriptions.NUR12521: Nuragic settlement area. A nuragic station has been identified with clear signs of human presence (about 1300 BC).
descriptions.NUR14981: Around the parish church the remains of an important settlement have come to light, including three wells and Hut 5, interpreted as a council hall. The discovery of terracotta casting moulds in the area outside "Hut 4" proves that metal artefacts were produced on the spot. By the threshold of "Hut 1", also of the Final Bronze Age, a clay bowl containing ox-hide ingots was found, deposited in the Iron Age.
descriptions.NUR15219: Nuragic village located to the south-south-east of the homonymous nuraghe. In the area, cyclopean wall courses and remains of at least one possible hut are detectable. The abundant vegetation growing there, mainly composed of lentisk, makes it impossible to determine the layout of other possible wall structures. Nearby, on the ground, ceramic fragments are visible.
descriptions.NUR20339:
In some publications it is distinguished from the village and the necropolis of Porcili Mannu, but the area actually lies in Sa Sucraxia and the inhabitants of the region refer to it as such.

Almost camouflaged among the large trees, clearly visible remains of a large stone village with various buildings, some dwellings, tomb remnants, and other structures of unknown function can be observed.
descriptions.NUR14897: There are 22 Nuragic villages known within the municipal territory, both large and small, and not all of them were inhabited simultaneously. Often they are located near a nuraghe, as in the case of the Bruncu Pubusa site; in other cases (Giuanni Acca, Sattu Divisu, Bruncu Abis, and Sa Serra) they are located without any nearby nuraghe.
descriptions.NUR5542: The complex, consisting of the nuraghe and its village, is today fully incorporated into the existing settlement, surrounded by a terraced park rich in fruit trees, aromatic herbs, and Mediterranean scrub. It was built during the Middle Bronze Age (circa 1700–1350 BC) on a small hilltop overlooking the valley of the Rio Carrabusu.
descriptions.NUR10715: Attached to granitic rocks are visible the remains of a Nuragic village near an abandoned old courtyard.
descriptions.NUR19764: The probable Nuragic village consists of several structures that were almost certainly reused up to the last century. The huts, whose remains can be glimpsed, were probably originally circular and rectangular in shape. Parts of the walls survive, built of semi-worked stones of varying sizes. The very dense vegetation, which in places has grown inside the structures, has contributed to their collapse. About 200 m to the east lies the Noccus pond.
descriptions.NUR19866: The probable Nuragic village occupies a large area on the eastern slope of the channel called S'ega Langonis. Despite the dense vegetation, more than 30 circular and rectangular huts can be counted. All have collapsed or imploded, partly because of illicit digging; even so, several courses of the perimeter walls survive on some of them. All the structures were built of small- and medium-sized polyhedral boulders, laid dry in more or less regular courses.
descriptions.NUR19762: The probable Nuragic village consists of several huts, from which only linear wall remains are preserved, composed of multiple courses (in some cases up to five) of stones of varying sizes. These structures were likely rectangular. Unfortunately, the dense and tangled vegetation conceals most of the structures. To the north, and about 100 m away, lies the Noccus pond, a water reservoir serving the villages in the area.
descriptions.NUR19535: In the area, remains of numerous huts belonging to a Nuragic complex are present; some of these may have been reused in more recent, though distant, times. Most of the huts are circular and show only minor remnants of their original structure, with some having 2/3 of the courses broken, others only a single course composed of polyhedral stones of various sizes. In the NE area, there is a enclosure housing one rectangular hut, which consists of two rooms.
descriptions.NUR8716:
The complex, one of the most important and best preserved Nuragic sites in Sardinia, includes a village-sacred sanctuary with about one hundred huts, two temples with attached enclosures, and two megalithic burials.

The village consists of isolated huts and groups of huts clustered around central open spaces. There are six groupings, some of which feature cisterns and wells connected by water channels. The huts, circular in plan, are dry-stone constructed with irregular courses.
descriptions.NUR19253: It is located in the territory of Pozzomaggiore (SS), near the proto-nuraghe (proto-nuraghe) Sinadorzu or Scale e Ozzastru; there are several huts and curtain walls. Nearby, some probable remains of giants' tombs and possibly a sacred nuragic well can be seen, although the entire site is in very poor condition.
descriptions.NUR12567: Submerged Nuragic village noted by Pierluigi Montalbano in public conferences
descriptions.NUR20064: Hundreds and hundreds of ruins, huts, and towers, joined together by narrow paths, transport us back millennia, showing how imposing and significant this site was during the Nuragic period. Two things stand out in particular. The first is a kind of amphitheatre, a majestic construction in the form of a horse's iron; the second is the well.
descriptions.NUR19656: A village composed of several circular huts of which only a few courses and the collapsed structure in the centre remain, plus two of complex structure. Of these two, the first, rectangular, consists of five rooms: four roughly circular ones at the four sides and one rectangular one in the centre, perhaps a courtyard; the second, oval, has four rooms, three of them round and the fourth formed by the wall joining the three rooms, perhaps a courtyard. Enclosures with cyclopean walls are present.
descriptions.NUR16077: Village – scattered throughout the area are several stretches of wall that could belong to the huts of a village; unfortunately, the dense vegetation prevents a clear view of the area and makes it difficult to identify the structures.
descriptions.NUR19654: The probable Nuragic village occupies an area extending from the edges of the plateau towards the northeast slope of the mountain. Remains of various circular huts are present, with only one or two courses and partial collapses at the centre. The best preserved hut is oval in shape and likely reused in more recent times. There are enclosures with cyclopean walls.
descriptions.NUR11737: From the excavations carried out in 1997, several huts of different plans were found, delimited by orthostatic slabs and featuring attached hearths. The archaeological layers have yielded abundant ceramic fragments, some metal objects, and bone artifacts, now preserved in the Archaeological Museum of Teti. The site dates back to the Middle Bronze Age III period and the early Iron Age phase.
descriptions.NUR19718: On a small relief located on the eastern bank of the Rio Monte Ozzatru, which joins the Rio Caddare just a few dozen metres away, there are numerous stone accumulations likely the result of a collapse; in the immediate vicinity, fragments of Nuragic pottery and a fragmented granite mill emerge from the ground.
descriptions.NUR11931: Here there was a Nuragic village, of which only faint traces remain.
descriptions.NUR12030: Nuragic village composed of about 30 huts, and at a short distance there was a sacred well.
descriptions.NUR11458:
The village of "Cuccuru Ambudu" extended over a broad hilly area (61 m a.s.l.) on the north-eastern outskirts of Serramanna, between the roads leading west to Serrenti and east to Villagreca.

The characteristics of the village, reconstructed through careful analysis of the finds, suggest it was already occupied in the pre-Nuragic period, in a phase datable between the Late Neolithic (Ozieri Culture) and the Chalcolithic (Monte Claro Culture).
descriptions.NUR15127: Adjacent to the area where the corridor nuraghe of the same name rises, there are dozens of quadrangular huts, sometimes divided into multiple rooms and featuring apsidal ends, surrounded by blocks arranged in a knife-like pattern. Occasionally affected by illegal excavations, these fragile pre-Nuragic dwellings are located both within the wooded area of municipal property and, more frequently, outside it, in a large area used for grazing.
descriptions.NUR11033: At the end of the Geometric phase the number of occupied sites continues to fall: evidence for the 7th and 6th centuries BC is found only at Monti Crastu, Is Arruinalis and Monti Angurdu, where decorated sherds of the Archaic phase have been observed. In this later phase it is likely that the centre of Is Arruinalis grew to a “proto-urban” level, as is known to have happened at other settlements in the Campidano and Marmilla (Tuppedili, San Sperate).
descriptions.NUR1868: In the area, remains of more than ten huts belonging to a nuragic complex are present. The village area was completely destroyed, I would say devastated, during the second world war, when the structures, belonging to most of the huts, were dismantled/adapted for military use.
descriptions.NUR1800: The nuraghe is located on the Gullei. It is a single massive lava flow extending for several kilometres. Access to the village is difficult due to thick undergrowth. The nuraghe is a three-lobed structure, with its walls visible. For at least one area of two hectares surrounding it, the village extends, including furnaces, a sacred well, and other features. From the top of the towers, the entire territory and coastline can be seen, down to the cliffs of Mariolu to the south and up to Cala Ginepro to the north.
descriptions.NUR18947: Nuragic huts possibly associated with both nuraghes in the vicinity
descriptions.NUR8111: Nestled in the Lanaitto valley, the village of Sa Sedda e Sos Carros (literally “the crossing point of the carts”) dates from a period between the Recent Bronze Age and the Early Iron Age (12th–9th centuries BC). It is particularly important for the presence of traces of metal smelting and working in the Nuragic period. It consists of numerous huts, with circular and oval plans, among which one is of particular interest for its ritual religious function.
descriptions.NUR19723: On a mountain terrace located at the base of the Ischiriddé pinnacle, the village of Sas Funtanas stood, at a very short distance from the Duas Vuccas cave. Lilliu reports the discovery of fragments of grinding stones and grinders, and of a white-ware jar containing a copper chisel, and notes the presence of a small village now no longer visible due to dense vegetation.
descriptions.NUR18807: In literature, as indeed observed on the ground, Su Padrigheddu is closely linked to the complex nuraghe S'Uraki, first mentioned as such by A. Taramelli in 1935. The materials recovered were immediately attributed to a village inhabited during the Nuragic period and continuously active right up to the Republican Roman era.
descriptions.NUR20007: From the upper level of the nuraghe in the north-east, a view of the village is visible, with huts still discernible amid thick vegetation and among the various collapses.
descriptions.NUR12860: Nuragic settlement with particular attention to lithic industry. Here, among other finds, axes, hammers, and stone mace heads have been discovered. One of the most remarkable discoveries is a depiction of a dagger on ceramic.
descriptions.NUR1818: Location of the remains of the Tattari Pizzinnu nuraghe, of which only the foundations remain, a Roman villa built with stones from the nuraghe, and the remaining Roman-period settlement.
